# http -> https for your name (Caddy's own redirect would say "Server: Caddy")
http://game.example.com {
	header -Server
	redir https://{host}{uri} 308
}

# any other name (Host: the bare address, or a name a scanner made up): the
# connection is closed without an answer.  On 80, Caddy's own catch-all
# redirect would name it; on 443, a request for another Host over a connection
# made for your name would get Caddy's empty answer.  (A TLS handshake for
# another name, or for none, fails already: Caddy has no certificate for it.)
:80 {
	abort
}
:443 {
	abort
}

game.example.com {
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8080 {
		# the address that connected, whatever CF-Connecting-IP a client sent (the server reads that header
		# with --real-ip-header cf-connecting-ip)
		header_up CF-Connecting-IP {client_ip}
		# one connection to the server per request in progress, at most this many: fewer than the 16000 the
		# server takes with the unit's --max-peers 2000 (8 per player; 1024 with --max-peers 128 or fewer, then
		# lower this too).  The server itself holds each client address to 64 requests at once.
		transport http {
			max_conns_per_host 15900
		}
	}
	# say nothing about the software: not on answers, nor on errors
	header -Server
	header -Via
	handle_errors {
		header -Server
	}
}

# NFS Underground 2 in the browser: the server bundle

This folder runs the game's web server on a Linux VPS, with HTTPS in front, so
friends can play with you in Chrome, without Docker.

It holds the server, the page and the game module. **It does not hold the game.**
You copy your own NFS Underground 2 folder to the VPS yourself.

1. **Nothing to install first.** The server is one static binary, `nfsu2-server`, for
   the VPS's processor: the bundle's name ends in amd64 (Intel, AMD) or arm64.
2. **The bundle.**
   `sudo mkdir -p /opt && sudo tar -C /opt -xzf nfsu2-web-<rev>-<arch>.tar.gz`
   This gives `/opt/nfsu2-web`.
3. **The game folder.** This is the one with `SPEED2.EXE`. From your own computer, inside that folder, copy
   only the game's own files (the server serves nothing else), then make them readable on the VPS:
   `rsync -rlt SPEED2.EXE server.dll server.cfg CARS CREDITS FRONTEND GLOBAL LANGUAGES memcard MOVIES NIS pfdata SOUND speech SUBTITLES TRACKS root@<vps>:/srv/nfsu2/game/`
   `ssh root@<vps> chmod -R u=rwX,go=rX /srv/nfsu2/game`
   The other languages' voices and movies, if you built them (`LANGPACKS`), the same
   way: `rsync -rlt LANGPACKS root@<vps>:/srv/nfsu2/game/`, then the `chmod` again.
   Before you copy any packs (`LANGPACKS`, `VINYLPACKS`, `MODPACKS`, `TEXPACKS`), check them as the game reads
   them, from the repository: `python3 tools/packcheck.py "<your game folder>"`. It names each file that is wrong
   and exits with 1; copy them only when it says `all good`.
4. **TLS**, in one of these ways:
   - Caddy in front: `deploy/Caddyfile`. Simplest: a Let's Encrypt certificate,
     renewed by Caddy.
   - The server itself on port 443 with a certificate: `deploy/nfsu2-web.service`,
     variant B.
   - A Cloudflare Tunnel: `deploy/cloudflared.yml`, and the service's variant D.
5. **The service.**
   `sudo cp /opt/nfsu2-web/deploy/nfsu2-web.service /etc/systemd/system/`
   Pick its `ExecStart` line (A, D or B) and put your name in `--host`, then run:
   `sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now nfsu2-web`
   Its log: `journalctl -u nfsu2-web -f`.
6. **Play.** Open `https://<your name>/` in Chrome.

**Who can play:** the server has no accounts or passwords. Anyone who can reach
it can play, and can download the game files from it. Your firewall decides who
that is. Behind Cloudflare's proxy, let only Cloudflare's addresses reach 80 and
443, and turn on Authenticated Origin Pulls (SSL/TLS, Origin Server): any
Cloudflare customer connects from those addresses too, so Caddy (its Cloudflare
variant, with `deploy/cloudflare-origin-pull-ca.pem`) or the server (variant B
with `--trusted-proxies cloudflare`) asks them for Cloudflare's certificate.

**SSH:** log in with a key only.

{"id": "AT001506", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/deploy/cloudflare-only.sh", "originalBytes": 2511, "originalSha256": "3cefd428b92a8ef5cd71502e84753daf1abe43484a867139689588706645a421", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 2511, "utf8TotalBytes": 2511}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Only Cloudflare's addresses reach the server's TLS port (compose.origin.yml): a table of its own in
# nftables, so nothing else on the VPS changes (Docker's rules, ufw's, other ports).  The server also asks Cloudflare's
# addresses for its origin-pull certificate; this keeps everyone else from reaching it past Cloudflare.  Run as root;
# again when Cloudflare's list changes (www.cloudflare.com/ips).
#
#   web/deploy/cloudflare-only.sh [port]          the port (default 28443) for Cloudflare's addresses only
#   web/deploy/cloudflare-only.sh --off           the table gone: the port open to all again
#
# At boot: nfsu2-cloudflare-only.service (next to this file) runs it from /srv/nfsu2.
set -euo pipefail
table=nfsu2_cloudflare
if [ "${1:-}" = --off ]; then
  nft delete table inet "$table" 2>/dev/null || true
  echo "cloudflare-only: off"
  exit 0
fi
port="${1:-28443}"
case "$port" in '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "cloudflare-only: not a port: $port" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
list() { curl -fsS --max-time 20 "https://www.cloudflare.com/ips-$1" | tr -d '\r' | sed '/^$/d' | paste -sd, -; }
v4=$(list v4) v6=$(list v6)
[ -n "$v4" ] && [ -n "$v6" ] || { echo "cloudflare-only: no list from www.cloudflare.com" >&2; exit 1; }
# one transaction: the table made if it is not there, then dropped and made again, so a second run replaces the first.
# The port's packets also go untracked (notrack, before connection tracking looks at them): Docker's NAT rules on the
# VPS turn tracking on for its whole network, and the server's ~16000 connections would each be tracked, every packet
# through its hooks, for nothing (no rule here or Docker's asks about them; the same cost on cloudflared's hop was a
# twentieth of the server's kernel time, nfsu2.xyz 2026-11-05).
nft -f - <<EOF
table inet $table
delete table inet $table
table inet $table {
  set v4 { type ipv4_addr; flags interval; elements = { $v4 } }
  set v6 { type ipv6_addr; flags interval; elements = { $v6 } }
  chain untracked_in {
    type filter hook prerouting priority raw; policy accept;
    tcp dport $port notrack
  }
  chain untracked_out {
    type filter hook output priority raw; policy accept;
    tcp sport $port notrack
  }
  chain input {
    type filter hook input priority -10; policy accept;
    tcp dport $port ip saddr @v4 accept
    tcp dport $port ip6 saddr @v6 accept
    tcp dport $port drop
  }
}
EOF
echo "cloudflare-only: port $port for Cloudflare's $(tr ',' '\n' <<<"$v4,$v6" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') ranges only"

# compose.yml with Cloudflare's proxy (orange cloud) straight to the server: no Caddy, no tunnel.
# The server does TLS itself, with a Cloudflare Origin CA
# certificate, on NFSU2_TLS_PORT of the VPS's own network (an Origin Rule in Cloudflare sends https://NFSU2_HOST
# there); it believes CF-Connecting-IP only from Cloudflare's addresses, and those must show Cloudflare's origin-pull
# certificate or their handshakes fail.  So turn Authenticated Origin Pulls on (SSL/TLS, Origin Server) BEFORE
# starting this: until then every page gets Cloudflare's "SSL handshake failed" (525).  The VPS's firewall lets only
# Cloudflare's addresses reach NFSU2_TLS_PORT.  The server's plain port stays on 127.0.0.1, where the image's health
# check asks.  Without cloudflared, the CPU the tunnel took (about 3/4 of the slice at 4,300 players) is free.
#
# In .env, besides NFSU2_HOST, NFSU2_DATA and NFSU2_MODULE (compose.yml):
#   NFSU2_TLS_DIR=/srv/nfsu2/tls     origin.pem and origin.key: the Origin CA certificate and its key, readable by
#                                    the container's user (uid 1000) only: chown -R 1000:1000, chmod 700 the folder,
#                                    600 the key
#   NFSU2_TLS_PORT=28443             the port the Origin Rule names (default 28443)
#   COMPOSE_FILE=compose.yml:compose.origin.yml     so that plain "docker compose ..." uses both files
# then:  docker compose up -d --remove-orphans && docker compose logs -f server
# (--remove-orphans: from the tunnel, it stops and removes cloudflared and net.)
services:
  caddy:
    profiles: [off]          # not started: the server does TLS itself
  server:
    command:
      - --port
      - ${NFSU2_TLS_PORT:-28443}
      - --tls-cert
      - /tls/origin.pem
      - --tls-key
      - /tls/origin.key
      - --trusted-proxies
      - cloudflare
    environment:
      NFSU2_REAL_IP_HEADER: cf-connecting-ip
    volumes:
      - ${NFSU2_TLS_DIR:-./tls}:/tls:ro

# compose.yml with a Cloudflare Tunnel in front instead of Caddy: cloudflared
# connects out to Cloudflare, so the VPS needs no open port for the game at all.  cloudflared and the server
# share one network namespace (a Docker network, not the VPS's): cloudflared reaches the server there, nothing
# else can, and the client's address comes from Cloudflare's CF-Connecting-IP.  In Cloudflare's dashboard the
# tunnel's public hostname is NFSU2_HOST and its service http://127.0.0.1:8080 (the dashboard refuses the
# server's socket, unix:@nfsu2-http, that a tunnel with a config file of its own could take).
#
# In .env, besides NFSU2_HOST, NFSU2_DATA and NFSU2_MODULE (compose.yml):
#   TUNNEL_TOKEN=<the tunnel's token>
#   COMPOSE_FILE=compose.yml:compose.tunnel.yml     so that plain "docker compose ..." uses both files
# then:  docker compose up -d && docker compose logs -f server
services:
  caddy:
    profiles: [off]          # not started: cloudflared is the front
  # holds the namespace, so that cloudflared and the server can each restart on their own (with the server in
  # cloudflared's own namespace, a restarted cloudflared got a new one and reached nothing until the server
  # was restarted too)
  net:
    image: registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10
    restart: unless-stopped
    cgroup_parent: ${NFSU2_SLICE:-nfsu2.slice}
    # Docker's own bridge, not the project's network: on a network of its own Docker answers names at 127.0.0.11
    # through NAT rules inside this namespace, and with them Linux tracks every connection and runs the firewall's
    # hooks for every packet here, the ~12000 between cloudflared and the server on 127.0.0.1 too: a twentieth of the
    # server's kernel time and of cloudflared's on that hop (nfsu2.xyz, 2026-11-05).  On this bridge the namespace has
    # no rules at all, and names come from the VPS's own servers.  Nothing reaches this namespace by its name.
    network_mode: bridge
    # the receive buffers of this namespace's sockets at most 128 KiB, not Linux's 32 MiB: what a player's path does
    # not take then waits at the server, which leaves out free roam's snapshots for it, instead of unread at
    # cloudflared, out of the server's sight (nfsu2.xyz, 2026-10-22: 132 MB there, up to 1 MB for one player).  The
    # localhost hop is fast enough with that for anything (a download goes on as fast as cloudflared reads).
    sysctls:
      net.ipv4.tcp_rmem: "4096 65536 131072"
  # five copies of the tunnel, 4 connections to Cloudflare each: a connection to a far or lossy Cloudflare site
  # slows every player on it (nfsu2.xyz, 2026-10-22: two of one copy's four went to Amsterdam, lost ~100 times
  # the packets of the Helsinki ones, and ~600 of 2,950 players got the others' cars seconds late), and one that
  # drops (every few hours) drops its players; with 20, each is about a twentieth of them (at 16000 players 800 a
  # connection; the Helsinki ones carried ~740 each that day without trouble).  Restart only the copy that has a bad
  # one (docker restart nfsu2-web-cloudflared-N; docker compose restart restarts them all).
  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.9.3
    scale: 5
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: service:net
    command: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run"]
    # in the game's share of the CPU with the server (web/deploy/nfsu2.slice): it pays for each message too
    cgroup_parent: ${NFSU2_SLICE:-nfsu2.slice}
    environment:
      TUNNEL_TOKEN: ${TUNNEL_TOKEN:?set TUNNEL_TOKEN in .env, the tunnel's token}
      # four threads of Go each, 20 for the five copies: with one for each of the slice's cores, Go's scheduler
      # woke idle threads that found nothing to do for a fifth of a copy's CPU (nfsu2.xyz, 2026-10-30, a copy's
      # profile at 5,800 players: findRunnable 18 %, futex 8 %)
      GOMAXPROCS: "4"
    logging: { driver: local }
  server:
    network_mode: service:net
    environment:
      NFSU2_REAL_IP_HEADER: cf-connecting-ip
      # HTTP on a Unix socket too, a name in the namespace (no file): a tunnel's service unix:@nfsu2-http
      NFSU2_HTTP_SOCKET: "@nfsu2-http"

{"id": "AT001512", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/deploy/compose.yml", "originalBytes": 6086, "originalSha256": "43db89eb14d978f9165f2c193482711986ddc5df8db1451e437fa9a5997f6c88", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 6086, "utf8TotalBytes": 6086}

# NFS Underground 2 in the browser on a VPS, with Docker: the server's image (Dockerfile)
# and Caddy, which does HTTPS with a Let's Encrypt certificate it gets and renews by itself.  Both use the VPS's
# own network, as Caddy and the server do without Docker: Caddy on ports 80 and 443, forwarding to the server on
# 127.0.0.1:8080, which nothing outside the VPS can reach.  So Caddy sees every player's real address, over IPv6
# too, and the VPS's firewall (ufw, nftables) decides who can play.  (Ports published from a Docker network
# would pass by that firewall, and would give every IPv6 player the same address, which the server's
# per-address limits then count as one.)
#
# In .env next to this file (or the environment):
#   NFSU2_HOST=game.example.com      the name players open (one name); its DNS record points at this VPS
#   NFSU2_DATA=/srv/nfsu2/game       your NFS Underground 2 folder (default ./game), readable by everyone
#   NFSU2_MODULE=/srv/nfsu2/module   nfsu2.wasm and nfsu2.json from web/build.sh (default ./module)
#   NFSU2_IMAGE=<image>              the server's image (default ghcr.io/th0mk/nfsu2-web-rs:latest)
#   NFSU2_HTTP_PORT=8080             the server's port on 127.0.0.1, if 8080 is taken on the VPS
#   NFSU2_THREADS=12                 the Rust image's worker threads (12 when not set; the image alone takes half
#                                    the cores, 2 to 8); with more than about 3000 players in free roam, 8
#                                    workers keep them at fewer friends each
#   NFSU2_SLICE=nfsu2.slice          the systemd slice every container here runs in (nfsu2.slice: its CPUQuota
#                                    keeps the rest of the VPS its share)
# then:  docker compose up -d && docker compose logs -f server
# Port 80 taken by something else on the VPS: compose.443.yml.  A Cloudflare Tunnel instead of Caddy:
# compose.tunnel.yml.  Cloudflare's proxy (orange cloud) in front of Caddy: compose.cloudflare.yml.  Cloudflare's
# proxy straight to the server (no Caddy, no tunnel): compose.origin.yml.
name: nfsu2-web
services:
  caddy:
    image: caddy:2.11-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    configs: [{ source: caddyfile, target: /etc/caddy/Caddyfile }]
    volumes: [caddy-data:/data, caddy-config:/config]
    cgroup_parent: ${NFSU2_SLICE:-nfsu2.slice}
    logging: { driver: local }
  server:
    image: ${NFSU2_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/th0mk/nfsu2-web-rs:latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    command: ["--behind-proxy"]
    environment:
      NFSU2_HOST: ${NFSU2_HOST:?set NFSU2_HOST in .env, the name players open (game.example.com)}
      NFSU2_HTTP_PORT: ${NFSU2_HTTP_PORT:-8080}
      NFSU2_REAL_IP_HEADER: ${NFSU2_REAL_IP_HEADER:-x-forwarded-for}
      NFSU2_THREADS: ${NFSU2_THREADS:-12}
      # the room for keyphrase saves, in GB (50 when not set, 0: none)
      NFSU2_VAULT_GB: ${NFSU2_VAULT_GB:-}
      # Cloudflare Turnstile's keys for claiming a name (none: no check)
      NFSU2_TURNSTILE_SITE: ${NFSU2_TURNSTILE_SITE:-}
      NFSU2_TURNSTILE_SECRET: ${NFSU2_TURNSTILE_SECRET:-}
      # a Last.fm API account's key and shared secret (last.fm/api/account/create) for scrobbling the songs (none: off)
      NFSU2_LASTFM_KEY: ${NFSU2_LASTFM_KEY:-}
      NFSU2_LASTFM_SECRET: ${NFSU2_LASTFM_SECRET:-}
      # the server's own race bans of cars past these numbers (kw=<n>,rating=<n>; none: off), and a Discord webhook
      # each is posted to (web/server-rs/src/app/autoban.rs); keep both in .env only
      NFSU2_CAR_BANS: ${NFSU2_CAR_BANS:-}
      NFSU2_BAN_WEBHOOK: ${NFSU2_BAN_WEBHOOK:-}
    volumes:
      - ${NFSU2_DATA:-./game}:/game:ro
      - ${NFSU2_MODULE:-./module}:/module:ro
      - state:/state
    # what the systemd unit (nfsu2-web.service) allows the server, as far as a container goes: nothing to write
    # but its state, no capabilities, no swap, 262144 open files (the Rust image's 24000 players take up to 192000
    # connections, 8 each, and 131072 left too few for its files besides); 16 GB of memory (about half a GB a thousand
    # players: 4.9 GB at 13,163 on nfsu2.xyz, 2026-11-05), not the unit's 3 GB
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    mem_limit: 16g
    memswap_limit: 16g
    ulimits: { nofile: 262144 }
    # the game's share of the VPS's CPU, with Caddy's (or cloudflared's): web/deploy/nfsu2.slice.  A cgroup of its
    # own (no `cgroup: host`): the server does not see the slice, so a full slice never gives players fewer friends
    # (the console's "CPU quota" line at the start says "none seen"); only its own workers over 85 % busy do
    cgroup_parent: ${NFSU2_SLICE:-nfsu2.slice}
    # the console, kept by Docker in files it rotates (5 of 20 MB), so the log never fills the VPS's disk
    logging: { driver: local }
configs:
  caddyfile:
    # web/deploy/Caddyfile for NFSU2_HOST.  Caddy names no software (no Server or Via header, also not on its
    # redirects and errors), closes a connection for any other name (the bare address, a scanner's made-up name)
    # without an answer, and opens at most 191900 connections to the server (the Rust image takes 192000 with
    # 24000 players).  It believes no proxy in front: the client's address is the one that connected, and a
    # CF-Connecting-IP a client sends is replaced by it (behind Cloudflare's proxy: compose.cloudflare.yml).  The
    # admin API (127.0.0.1:2019) stays off: nothing reconfigures Caddy while it runs.
    content: |
      {
      	admin off
      }
      http://${NFSU2_HOST:-} {
      	header -Server
      	redir https://{host}{uri} 308
      }
      :80 {
      	abort
      }
      :443 {
      	abort
      }
      ${NFSU2_HOST:-} {
      	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:${NFSU2_HTTP_PORT:-8080} {
      		header_up CF-Connecting-IP {client_ip}
      		transport http {
      			max_conns_per_host 191900
      		}
      	}
      	header -Server
      	header -Via
      	handle_errors {
      		header -Server
      	}
      }
volumes:
  state:
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:

{"id": "AT001513", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/deploy/nfsu2", "originalBytes": 2701, "originalSha256": "bc6f06d3543e0482f0aaaaf306871f23006ff8010698eeef2598e345b7d93413", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 2701, "utf8TotalBytes": 2701}

#!/bin/sh
# The operator's commands to the game server of the Docker setup in this folder:
# copy it next to compose.yml (/srv/nfsu2), chmod +x, then
#   ./nfsu2 who [name]                     the players on the switch, and who left in the last hour (a name: theirs,
#                                          or the one over their car)
#   ./nfsu2 kick <player> [message]        off playing with others, with that message (a reload brings them back)
#   ./nfsu2 ban <player> <for> [message]   off until the ban ends: <for> is 30m, 12h, 3d, 2w or perm
#   ./nfsu2 raceban <player> <for> [msg]   off races with others until it ends (Online, LAN, free roam's lobby races
#                                          and outruns); free roam and chat stay
#   ./nfsu2 rename <player> [message]      its name taken away from everyone: its page asks for another
#   ./nfsu2 unban <name | #ban>            lift a ban
#   ./nfsu2 change #ban <races|full|for>   make a ban a race ban or a full one, or last <for> from now on
#   ./nfsu2 bans                           the bans in force
#   ./nfsu2 history <player | #ban>        a player's bans and renames, in force and ended in the last year
#   ./nfsu2 names | unname <name>          the names taken away; give one back
#   ./nfsu2 days [n]                       how many came each day (UTC), the last n days and today so far
#   ./nfsu2 settings [n] [setting]         the settings players changed, the last n days (7) and today so far,
#                                          most changed first; a setting's name: only it, with every value
#   ./nfsu2 logs [days] > logs.gz          the server's log of the last days (1: today so far), gzipped ("What the log
#                                          keeps"); from your computer: ssh root@<vps> /srv/nfsu2/nfsu2 logs 2 > logs.gz
# <player> is an address (10.77.x.y) or a name, as `who` shows them, or a [cheat] line's handle (c17); the message
# needs no quotes.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
if [ "$1" = logs ]; then
  days=${2:-1}
  case $days in
    '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "logs [days]: a number of days, 1 for today so far" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  if [ -t 1 ]; then
    echo "logs [days] > logs.gz: it is gzipped, send it to a file" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  # each day's file, the last $days of them: the days that ended as they are (gzipped), today's gzipped now
  exec docker compose exec -T server sh -c '
    cd /state/logs || exit 1
    for f in $(ls | grep -E "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}[.]log([.]gz)?$" | sort | tail -n "$1"); do
      case $f in
        *.gz) cat "$f" ;;
        *) gzip -c "$f" ;;
      esac
    done' sh "$days"
fi
exec docker compose exec -T server /app/nfsu2-server ctl "$@"

# Paths: the bundle in /opt/nfsu2-web, the game folder in /srv/nfsu2/game

ExecStart=/opt/nfsu2-web/nfsu2-server --data /srv/nfsu2/game --state /var/lib/nfsu2-web --behind-proxy --http-port 8080 --host game.example.com --max-peers 2000

#    CF-Connecting-IP header)
#ExecStart=/opt/nfsu2-web/nfsu2-server --data /srv/nfsu2/game --state /var/lib/nfsu2-web --behind-proxy --http-port 8080 --host game.example.com --real-ip-header cf-connecting-ip --max-peers 2000

#ExecStart=/opt/nfsu2-web/nfsu2-server --data /srv/nfsu2/game --state /var/lib/nfsu2-web --port 443 --http-port 0 --tls-cert %d/tls.crt --tls-key %d/tls.key --max-peers 2000

# The game's share of the VPS: the compose files put every container of theirs (the server, Caddy or the
# Cloudflare Tunnel's cloudflared and its namespace) into this slice (cgroup_parent), and the slice gets at most
# CPUQuota of the CPU between them, so the rest of the VPS always keeps the remainder whatever the players do.
# 2300 % is 23 of a 24-thread VPS, 1 left for the rest (1500 % on a 16-vCPU one: nfsu2.xyz, 11.8 of 12.8 taken at
# 4,300 players, 2026-10-23; the rest used about half a vCPU at 5,857, 2026-10-30).  For another VPS, its vCPUs less
# what the rest needs, x 100.  The server and cloudflared share it as their load goes; at the
# quota they are slowed down, never the rest of the VPS.  The server does not read the slice (compose.yml has no
# `cgroup: host`), so a full slice does not give players fewer friends.
#   cp web/deploy/nfsu2.slice /etc/systemd/system/ && systemctl daemon-reload
# then recreate the containers (docker compose up -d --force-recreate).  Without the file the containers still
# start, in a slice systemd makes for them with no limit.  Needs Docker's systemd cgroup driver (docker info:
# "Cgroup Driver: systemd", the default with cgroup v2).
[Unit]
Description=NFS Underground 2 in the browser: its containers' share of the CPU

[Slice]
CPUAccounting=yes
CPUQuota=2300%

#!/bin/bash
# Builds the bundle that runs the server on a VPS without Docker:
#
#   web/deploy/pack.sh [--out <dir>] [--no-build] [--data "<game folder>"] [--arch amd64|arm64] [--server <binary>]
#
# out/web/deploy/nfsu2-web-<rev>-<arch>.tar.gz holds nfsu2-web/ with
#   nfsu2-server      the server: one static binary for Linux on --arch (default amd64), built in Docker by
#                     web/server-rs/Dockerfile's binary stage (as the image's, cross-compiled: no emulation), or
#                     --server's (a Linux binary of your own, such as /app/nfsu2-server out of the image)
#   web/dist/         the page (the test pages and source maps are in web/dist-dev, never copied)
#   out/web/          the game module (nfsu2.wasm, nfsu2.json), built here with web/build.sh
#   deploy/           nfsu2-web.service (systemd), Caddyfile (an example), cloudflared.yml (an example),
#                     cloudflare-origin-pull-ca.pem (for Caddy behind Cloudflare's proxy)
#   README.md         how to set it up
# The server finds the page and the module in the folder NFSU2_REPO names (the unit sets /opt/nfsu2-web).
# The bundle NEVER holds the game folder or anything from it: the files are copied from a
# fixed list, and the bundle is refused if any file in it has the name and size
# of a file in the game folder (--data, else $NFSU2_DATA, when it is there),
# carries the game's file names, or names this machine (host name, home folder).
# The archive's owner is root, its modes 644/755, without macOS metadata.
# --no-build: use web/dist as it is (default: rebuild it with node build.mjs).
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
OUT="$ROOT/out/web/deploy" BUILD=1 DATA="${NFSU2_DATA:-}" ARCH=amd64 SERVER=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --out) OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --no-build) BUILD=0; shift ;;
    --data) DATA="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --arch) ARCH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --server) SERVER="$(cd "$(dirname "$2")" && pwd)/$(basename "$2")"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,25p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "pack.sh: unknown option $1"; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
case "$ARCH" in amd64|arm64) ;; *) echo "pack.sh: --arch amd64 or arm64, not $ARCH"; exit 2 ;; esac
[ -z "$DATA" ] && [ -d "$HOME/projects/nsfu2/Need for Speed - Underground 2" ] && DATA="$HOME/projects/nsfu2/Need for Speed - Underground 2"
cd "$ROOT"
REV="$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)$(git diff --quiet HEAD -- web/server-rs web/src web/index.html 2>/dev/null || echo +)"
[ -f out/web/nfsu2.wasm ] && [ -f out/web/nfsu2.json ] || { echo "no game module: build it first (web/build.sh)"; exit 1; }
if [ "$BUILD" = 1 ]; then (cd web && node build.mjs >/dev/null 2>&1) || { echo "the page did not build (cd web && node build.mjs)"; exit 1; }; fi

STAGE="$OUT/stage"
rm -rf "$STAGE"; mkdir -p "$STAGE/nfsu2-web"
B="$STAGE/nfsu2-web"
mkdir -p "$B/out/web" "$B/deploy"
# ---- the server ----
if [ -n "$SERVER" ]; then
  cp "$SERVER" "$B/nfsu2-server"
else
  command -v docker >/dev/null || { echo "no docker to build the server in: install it, or give one with --server"; exit 1; }
  echo "building the server for linux/$ARCH (docker build --target binary; the first build takes a few minutes)"
  docker build -q -f web/server-rs/Dockerfile --platform "linux/$ARCH" --target binary --output "type=local,dest=$STAGE/bin" . >/dev/null \
    || { echo "the server did not build (docker build -f web/server-rs/Dockerfile --target binary)"; exit 1; }
  mv "$STAGE/bin/nfsu2-server" "$B/nfsu2-server"; rm -rf "$STAGE/bin"
fi
[ "$(head -c 4 "$B/nfsu2-server" | od -An -c | tr -d ' ')" = '177ELF' ] || { echo "pack.sh: the server (${SERVER:-from docker build}) is no Linux binary"; exit 1; }
# ---- the fixed list ----
# the page: everything web/dist has (node build.mjs puts the test pages and source maps in web/dist-dev;
# they are left out here too, should an older build have left them in web/dist)
(cd web/dist && find . -type f ! -path './test/*' ! -name '*.map' -print) | while read -r f; do
  mkdir -p "$B/web/dist/$(dirname "$f")"; cp "web/dist/$f" "$B/web/dist/$f"
done
cp out/web/nfsu2.wasm out/web/nfsu2.json "$B/out/web/"
cp web/deploy/nfsu2-web.service web/deploy/Caddyfile web/deploy/cloudflared.yml "$B/deploy/"
cp web/server-rs/crates/headers/cloudflare-origin-pull-ca.pem "$B/deploy/"
cp web/deploy/README.md "$B/README.md"

# ---- refusals ----
fail() { echo "pack.sh: REFUSED: $*"; rm -rf "$STAGE"; exit 1; }
[ -z "$(find "$B" -type l -print -quit)" ] || fail "a symbolic link in the bundle"
GAME_NAMES='(^|/)SPEED2\.EXE$|\.(BUN|BIN|LZC|VIV|MUS|ASF|VP6|ABK|GIN|CSI|MPF|AUD|LZW|DLL|EXE)$'
bad="$(cd "$B" && find . -type f | grep -iE "$GAME_NAMES" || true)"
[ -z "$bad" ] || fail "game file names: $bad"
if [ -n "$DATA" ] && [ -d "$DATA" ]; then
  # name + size of every game file against every bundle file
  node -e '
    const fs = require("fs"), path = require("path");
    const walk = (d, out = []) => { for (const e of fs.readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true })) { const p = path.join(d, e.name);
      if (e.isDirectory()) walk(p, out); else if (e.isFile()) out.push(p); } return out; };
    const game = new Set(walk(process.argv[1]).map(p => path.basename(p).toLowerCase() + ":" + fs.statSync(p).size));
    const hit = walk(process.argv[2]).filter(p => game.has(path.basename(p).toLowerCase() + ":" + fs.statSync(p).size));
    if (hit.length) { console.log(hit.join("\n")); process.exit(1); }' "$DATA" "$B" || fail "files that match the game folder"
  echo "checked against the game folder: no file of it is in the bundle"
  # what the server leaves out of the game folder (GAME_ENTRIES, web/server-rs/src/app/manifest.rs): copy only the
  # rest to the VPS
  others="$(node -e '
    const fs = require("fs");
    const m = /const GAME_ENTRIES: \[&str; \d+\] = \[([^\]]*)\]/.exec(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[2], "utf8"));
    if (!m) process.exit(0);
    const keep = new Set([...m[1].matchAll(/"([^"]+)"/g)].map(x => x[1]));
    console.log(fs.readdirSync(process.argv[1]).filter(n => !n.startsWith(".") && !keep.has(n.toLowerCase())).join(", "));' "$DATA" web/server-rs/src/app/manifest.rs)"
  [ -z "$others" ] || echo "NOTE: the server serves only the game's own files; these of your game folder it never serves (leave them off the VPS): $others"
fi
HOSTNAME_SHORT="$(hostname | sed 's/\.local$//')"
for needle in "$HOME" "$HOSTNAME_SHORT"; do
  hit="$(grep -rlaF "$needle" "$B" || true)"
  [ -z "$hit" ] || fail "names this machine ($needle) in: $hit"
done
SIZE_MB=$(( $(du -sk "$B" | cut -f1) / 1024 ))
[ "$SIZE_MB" -lt 200 ] || fail "$SIZE_MB MB: more than the server, the page and the module"

# ---- the archive ----
find "$B" -type d -exec chmod 755 {} +; find "$B" -type f -exec chmod 644 {} +; chmod 755 "$B/nfsu2-server"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
TGZ="$OUT/nfsu2-web-$REV-$ARCH.tar.gz"
# owner root, no extended attributes: bsdtar (macOS) and GNU tar (Linux, WSL) spell it differently
if tar --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q bsdtar; then
  TAR_OWNER=(--no-mac-metadata --no-xattrs --uid 0 --gid 0 --uname root --gname root)
else
  TAR_OWNER=(--no-xattrs --owner=root:0 --group=root:0)
fi
COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar -C "$STAGE" "${TAR_OWNER[@]}" -czf "$TGZ" nfsu2-web
rm -rf "$STAGE"
echo "$TGZ"
echo "  $(du -h "$TGZ" | cut -f1), $(tar -tzf "$TGZ" | grep -vc '/$') files, sha256 $(shasum -a 256 "$TGZ" | cut -d' ' -f1)"

{"id": "AT001518", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/deploy/release.sh", "originalBytes": 8551, "originalSha256": "c7598bec2c67543076776777fcff3a7f0a010877f04706dc9a7a1e4caed22806", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 8551, "utf8TotalBytes": 8551}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# A new version on a Docker VPS (/srv/nfsu2) in one command, from your own machine: the game module
# of a commit, and the image of that commit (or a later one), then the server restarted and checked.
#
#   web/deploy/release.sh root@<vps> <folder>              the module in <folder> (nfsu2.wasm, nfsu2.json), and the
#                                                          image of its commit (sha-<rev> in nfsu2.json)
#   web/deploy/release.sh root@<vps> <folder> <commit>     the image of another commit, e.g. a later one that changed
#                                                          only the page or the server (the module stays the same)
#   web/deploy/release.sh root@<vps> --undo                back to the module and image before the last release
#   -n first: only say what it would do
#
# What it does: checks that the folder holds both files of one commit and that the registry has the image's tag;
# copies the files to <dir>/module.new; then on the VPS pulls the image first (the running server reads its module
# from disk at every request, so the new one goes in only once its image is there: a pull that fails leaves the site
# as it was, the files waiting in module.new), keeps the running module and .env (module.prev, .env.prev, for
# --undo; a try again of the same release keeps the ones before it), moves the new files into module/ (a rename
# each: no half-written file is ever served), makes them readable for the container (644), sets NFSU2_IMAGE in .env,
# restarts only the server at once (`docker compose up -d server`: cloudflared and the rest stay up), and waits
# until it is healthy with the new module.  Everyone in the game is cut off for a few seconds and reconnects; pages
# notice the new module by its ETag.  Last, module/release.json names the module's commit and the running image's,
# for the forum bot (discord-bot/repo.mjs): after a release of only the page or the server, the image's commit is
# what is live, though nfsu2.json still names the module's.  A try again of a release whose server is up already
# restarts nothing and only writes that file.
#
#   NFSU2_DIR    the folder on the VPS (default /srv/nfsu2)
#   NFSU2_REPO   the image without its tag (default ghcr.io/th0mk/nfsu2-web-rs)
set -euo pipefail

dry=0
[ "${1:-}" = -n ] && { dry=1; shift; }
vps="${1:-}"; arg="${2:-}"
dir="${NFSU2_DIR:-/srv/nfsu2}"
repo="${NFSU2_REPO:-ghcr.io/th0mk/nfsu2-web-rs}"
die(){ echo "release: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -n "$vps" ] && [ -n "$arg" ] || die "usage: release.sh [-n] user@vps <module folder> [commit] | release.sh [-n] user@vps --undo"

# the part that runs on the VPS: $1 what (release or undo), $2 the image, $3 the module's commit
remote=$(cat <<'REMOTE'
set -euo pipefail
what=$1 img=$2 rev=$3
cd "$NFSU2_DIR"
say(){ echo "  [vps] $*"; }
if [ "$what" = undo ]; then
  [ -f module.prev/nfsu2.wasm ] && [ -f module.prev/nfsu2.json ] && [ -f .env.prev ] || { echo "release: no earlier release kept here" >&2; exit 1; }
  mkdir -p module.new
  cp -p module.prev/nfsu2.wasm module.prev/nfsu2.json module.new/
  rev=$(grep -o '"rev":"[^"]*"' module.new/nfsu2.json | cut -d'"' -f4)
  img=$(grep '^NFSU2_IMAGE=' .env.prev | cut -d= -f2- || true)
fi
[ -f module.new/nfsu2.wasm ] && [ -f module.new/nfsu2.json ] || { echo "release: no module in $NFSU2_DIR/module.new" >&2; exit 1; }
say "image: ${img:-as compose.yml says}"
NFSU2_IMAGE="$img" docker compose pull -q server
if [ "$what" = release ]; then
  # the module and image of this release in place already (a try that stopped after the move): the ones kept stay
  if cmp -s module/nfsu2.json module.new/nfsu2.json && [ "$(grep '^NFSU2_IMAGE=' .env | cut -d= -f2- || true)" = "$img" ]; then
    say "this release again: the module and .env of before it stay kept"
  else
    rm -rf module.prev && mkdir module.prev
    cp -p module/nfsu2.wasm module/nfsu2.json module.prev/ 2>/dev/null || true
    cp -p .env .env.prev
  fi
fi
chmod 644 module.new/nfsu2.wasm module.new/nfsu2.json
mv -f module.new/nfsu2.wasm module/nfsu2.wasm
mv -f module.new/nfsu2.json module/nfsu2.json
rmdir module.new
say "module: $(grep -o '"rev":"[^"]*"' module/nfsu2.json)"
if [ -n "$img" ]; then
  if grep -q '^NFSU2_IMAGE=' .env; then sed -i "s#^NFSU2_IMAGE=.*#NFSU2_IMAGE=$img#" .env; else echo "NFSU2_IMAGE=$img" >> .env; fi
else
  sed -i '/^NFSU2_IMAGE=/d' .env
fi
docker compose up -d server
say "waiting for the server to be healthy..."
for i in $(seq 1 90); do
  st=$(docker inspect --format '{{.State.Health.Status}}' "$(docker compose ps -q server)" 2>/dev/null || echo starting)
  [ "$st" = healthy ] && break
  [ "$st" = unhealthy ] && { echo "release: the server is unhealthy: docker compose logs server" >&2; exit 1; }
  sleep 2
done
[ "$st" = healthy ] || { echo "release: not healthy after 3 minutes: docker compose logs server" >&2; exit 1; }
label=$(docker inspect --format '{{index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision"}}' "$(docker compose ps -q server)" 2>/dev/null || true)
say "healthy: module $rev, image ${label:0:7}"
# what is live, for the forum bot: the image's commit from its label, else from its sha- tag
image=${label:0:7}
[ -n "$image" ] || image=$(echo "$img" | sed -n 's/.*:sha-\([0-9a-f]*\)$/\1/p')
if [ -n "$image" ]; then
  printf '{"module":"%s","image":"%s"}\n' "$rev" "$image" > module/release.json.new
  chmod 644 module/release.json.new
  mv -f module/release.json.new module/release.json
else
  rm -f module/release.json
fi
REMOTE
)

if [ "$arg" = --undo ]; then
  echo "release: $vps:$dir back to the module and image of before the last release"
  [ $dry = 1 ] && exit 0
  ssh "$vps" "NFSU2_DIR='$dir' bash -s -- undo '' ''" <<<"$remote"
  exit 0
fi

# the module: both files, one commit, not from a checkout with changes
src="$arg"
[ -f "$src/nfsu2.wasm" ] && [ -f "$src/nfsu2.json" ] || die "$src needs nfsu2.wasm and nfsu2.json"
rev=$(grep -o '"rev":"[^"]*"' "$src/nfsu2.json" | cut -d'"' -f4)
size=$(grep -o '"size":[0-9]*' "$src/nfsu2.json" | cut -d: -f2)
[ -n "$rev" ] || die "$src/nfsu2.json has no rev"
case "$rev" in *+*) die "the module was built from a checkout with changes ($rev): build it from a commit";; esac
have=$(wc -c < "$src/nfsu2.wasm" | tr -d ' ')
[ "$size" = "$have" ] || die "nfsu2.json says $size bytes, nfsu2.wasm has $have: not one build"

# the image: its tag in the registry (a commit's image is missing when CI cancelled it for a newer push)
commit="${3:-$rev}"
# another commit's image: one after the module's, as the forum bot will take it (release.json)
if [ "${commit:0:7}" != "${rev:0:7}" ] && git cat-file -e "$commit^{commit}" 2>/dev/null && git cat-file -e "$rev^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
  git merge-base --is-ancestor "$rev" "$commit" || die "$commit does not come after the module's commit $rev"
fi
img="$repo:sha-${commit:0:7}"
reg="${repo%%/*}" path="${repo#*/}"
tok=$(curl -fsS "https://$reg/token?scope=repository:$path:pull" | sed -n 's/.*"token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p') || die "the registry $reg did not answer"
code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $tok" \
  -H 'Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json' \
  "https://$reg/v2/$path/manifests/sha-${commit:0:7}")
[ "$code" = 200 ] || die "no image $img (HTTP $code): CI may have cancelled it for a newer push; pass that newer commit if it changed only the page or the server"

# the start page's Changelog (CHANGELOG.md of the image's commit): its newest release should bring the module's commit,
# else this release's changes are missing from it.  A note, not a stop; nothing when this checkout lacks the commits
if git cat-file -e "$commit^{commit}" 2>/dev/null && git cat-file -e "$rev^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
  last=$(git show "$commit:CHANGELOG.md" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^## [0-9-]* (\([0-9a-f]*\))$/\1/p' | head -n 1)
  if [ -z "$last" ] || ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$rev" "$last" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "release: note: CHANGELOG.md's newest release${last:+ ($last)} comes before the module's commit $rev: the Changelog button will not list this release's changes" >&2
  fi
fi

echo "release: module $rev ($have bytes) and image $img to $vps:$dir"
[ $dry = 1 ] && exit 0
ssh "$vps" "mkdir -p '$dir/module.new'"
scp -q "$src/nfsu2.wasm" "$src/nfsu2.json" "$vps:$dir/module.new/"
ssh "$vps" "NFSU2_DIR='$dir' bash -s -- release '$img' '$rev'" <<<"$remote"
echo "release: done. Undo: web/deploy/release.sh $vps --undo"

END TEXT OBJECT AT001518

#!/bin/bash
# Generate the lifted C for the web build: ./gen.sh with the lifter's two
# code-size/speed options on:
#   FLAGABI  whole-program flag liveness across calls and returns
#            (tools/flagabi.py proves which functions return flags and which
#            take them at entry; every other call/ret has dead flags)
#   X87OPT   x87 stack slots as locals within a basic block
#   JTSWITCH MSVC switch jump tables as C switches inside the function, not
#            tail calls into a lifted copy of the rest of the body per target
#   LREGS    the guest registers and flags as locals of each lifted function,
#            stored to the CPU struct only around calls, returns and tail
#            jumps (tools/lregs.py)
#   FTOL2INL the CRT's _ftol2 in place at its call sites (cpu.h FTOL2_INL)
#   INLINE_LIST  the hot callees of tools/inline_hot.txt inlined at their
#            direct call sites (tools/inline_pick.py made the list from a
#            race's call counts; INLINE_LIST= turns it off)
# Measured in Chrome (race, NFSU2_FIXED_DT=120): -16 to -29 % instructions
# per frame and a 50 MB module instead of 65 MB (FLAGABI + X87OPT).  The Mac's
# gen.sh defaults are unchanged; this wrapper is the web build's generator.
#
#   web/gen.sh <path/to/SPEED2.EXE>      writes gen/all, gen/server (and out/flagabi.json)
#   WEB_LIFT=plain web/gen.sh <exe>      without the options (A/B)
#   JTSWITCH=0 web/gen.sh <exe>          the options without JTSWITCH (A/B); LREGS=0, FTOL2INL=0 and
#                                        INLINE_LIST= likewise
# gen.sh stamps the result (gen/all/stamp.txt, tools/genstamp.sh), which
# web/build.sh checks against the checkout.  In a worktree gen/all and
# gen/server are links to the main clone's, which every other worktree builds
# against: replace them with directories first (or GEN_SHARED=1 to regenerate
# the shared ones on purpose).  The default lift is made once per sources on a
# machine: web/tools/gencache.sh keeps it, this script copies a kept one in
# instead of lifting, and web/build.sh points a worktree's links at it.
set -e -o pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"; cd "$ROOT"
EXE="${1:-${NFSU2_DATA:+$NFSU2_DATA/SPEED2.EXE}}"
[ -f "$EXE" ] || { echo "usage: web/gen.sh path/to/SPEED2.EXE"; exit 1; }
for d in gen/all gen/server; do
  if [ -L "$d" ] && { [ "${GEN_SHARED:-}" != 1 ] || case "$(readlink "$d")" in "$(web/tools/gencache.sh dir)"/*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; }; then
    echo "web/gen.sh: $d is a link to $(readlink "$d"), which other worktrees build against;"
    echo "  rm $d && mkdir $d to lift into this worktree, or GEN_SHARED=1 web/gen.sh to regenerate the shared one (not a kept lift)"
    exit 1
  fi
done
# the default lift of these sources made before on this machine (web/tools/gencache.sh): copied, not made again
DEFAULTS=$( [ -z "${WEB_LIFT+x}${JTSWITCH+x}${LREGS+x}${FTOL2INL+x}${INLINE_LIST+x}" ] && echo 1 || true)
if [ "$DEFAULTS" = 1 ] && [ ! -L gen/all ] && [ ! -L gen/server ] && web/tools/gencache.sh get "$EXE"; then exit 0; fi
PY="$ROOT/.venv/bin/python"
mkdir -p out gen/all
# never label a new lift with an old run's options, never reuse an old flag table
rm -f gen/all/web-lift.txt out/flagabi.json
if [ "${WEB_LIFT:-opt}" = plain ]; then
  ./gen.sh "$EXE"
  LIFT=plain
else
  # flagabi.py needs the relocations, which gen.sh would only make later
  "$PY" tools/reloc2.py "$EXE"
  echo "FLAGABI: interprocedural flag liveness -> out/flagabi.json"
  # flagabi.py sees each function's control flow as the lift will, switches included
  export JTSWITCH="${JTSWITCH:-1}"
  "$PY" tools/flagabi.py "$EXE" out/flagabi.json > out/flagabi.log 2>&1 || { tail -20 out/flagabi.log; echo "web/gen.sh: flagabi.py failed"; exit 1; }
  grep -E "^summary|^  round" out/flagabi.log || true
  [ -s out/flagabi.json ] || { echo "web/gen.sh: flagabi.py wrote no out/flagabi.json"; exit 1; }
  export LREGS="${LREGS:-1}" FTOL2INL="${FTOL2INL:-1}" INLINE_LIST="${INLINE_LIST-$ROOT/tools/inline_hot.txt}"
  FLAGABI="$ROOT/out/flagabi.json" X87OPT=1 ./gen.sh "$EXE"
  LIFT="FLAGABI X87OPT$( [ "$JTSWITCH" = 1 ] && echo " JTSWITCH" || true)$( [ "$LREGS" = 1 ] && echo " LREGS" || true)$( [ "$FTOL2INL" = 1 ] && echo " FTOL2INL" || true)$( [ -n "$INLINE_LIST" ] && echo " INLINE_LIST" || true)"
fi
# a lift that failed function by function still says "gen OK": every function
# became an unsupported_insn(..., "lift-error") stub.  Refuse that.  A good
# lift of v1.2 NA has 8 such stubs (the same 8 on the Mac: addresses that are
# discovered as functions but never run); a broken one has thousands.
BAD=$(cat gen/all/shard_*.c | grep -c '"lift-error"' || true)
[ "$BAD" -le 64 ] || { echo "web/gen.sh: $BAD functions failed to lift (lift-error stubs in gen/all): not a usable lift"; rm -f gen/all/fntab.c
                       echo "incomplete: web/gen.sh found $BAD functions that failed to lift" > gen/all/stamp.txt; exit 1; }
echo "$LIFT" > gen/all/web-lift.txt
echo "web lift options: $LIFT"
[ "$DEFAULTS" != 1 ] || web/tools/gencache.sh put "$EXE"

END TEXT OBJECT AT001519

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# NFS Underground 2 in the browser: the server (web/server-rs) as a container image (web/deploy/compose.yml).
#
#   docker build -f web/server-rs/Dockerfile -t nfsu2-web-rs .
#
# The image holds the server (one static binary) and the page (web/dist, without the test pages and source maps).  It
# never holds the game or anything made from it (this Dockerfile's .dockerignore lets only the server's and the page's
# sources into the build); those are mounted:
#   /game     the NFS Underground 2 folder (the one with SPEED2.EXE), read-only, readable by everyone
#   /module   nfsu2.wasm and nfsu2.json, built with web/build.sh from the image's revision, read-only
#   /state    the server's keys (ETags, the switch's tokens), the Online mode's records and the bans: a volume, kept across
#             updates (a new ETag key would make every browser download the game data again)
# The server runs as uid 1000 (the user of the Node server's image before it, so a state volume that one wrote stays
# writable) and listens on 127.0.0.1:8080 of the network it is given: the VPS's own, with Caddy in front
# (web/deploy/compose.yml), or a tunnel's (compose.tunnel.yml).  Its command line is the server's options; by default
# --behind-proxy, which needs NFSU2_HOST, the name players open.
#
# Both stages that build run on the build machine's platform: the binary is cross-compiled (cargo-zigbuild, static
# musl) for the image's, so building it for arm64 on amd64 needs no emulation.
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM node:24-alpine AS page
ENV PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1
WORKDIR /src/web
COPY web/package.json web/package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
COPY app/registry-defaults.txt /src/app/
COPY CHANGELOG.md /src/
# the flags' pictures for Your flag (/flags.png)
COPY runtime/flags.dat /src/runtime/
COPY web/build.mjs web/index.html ./
# boot.js's texts in every language (bootTexts)
COPY web/tools/i18n-keys.mjs tools/
COPY web/src src
RUN node build.mjs && mkdir /state

# The CI (.github/workflows/image-rs.yml) builds the binaries on runners of their own and puts a folder with them
# (nfsu2-server-amd64, nfsu2-server-arm64) in place of this stage (--build-context server=<folder>): its zig,
# cargo-zigbuild, targets and CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG are this stage's, keep the two in step.
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM rust:1-bookworm AS server
ARG TARGETARCH
ARG ZIG=0.14.1
RUN case "$TARGETARCH" in \
      amd64) t=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl ;; \
      arm64) t=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl ;; \
      *) echo "no Rust target for $TARGETARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
    esac \
 && echo "$t" > /target && rustup target add "$t" \
 && curl -sSfL "https://ziglang.org/download/$ZIG/zig-$(uname -m)-linux-$ZIG.tar.xz" | tar -xJ -C /opt \
 && ln -s /opt/zig-*/zig /usr/local/bin/zig \
 && cargo install --locked cargo-zigbuild@0.23.4
WORKDIR /src
COPY web/server-rs web/server-rs
# no line tables in the image's binary (a third of its size); a panic still names its functions
ENV CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=0
# (the build folder goes once the binary is out: the layer, which the CI's cache keeps, holds 6 MB instead of 500)
RUN cd web/server-rs && cargo zigbuild --release --locked -p nfsu2-server --target "$(cat /target)" \
 && cp "target/$(cat /target)/release/nfsu2-server" "/nfsu2-server-$TARGETARCH" && rm -rf target

# the binary on its own, for a VPS without Docker (web/deploy/pack.sh):
#   docker build -f web/server-rs/Dockerfile --platform linux/amd64 --target binary --output <dir> .
FROM scratch AS binary
ARG TARGETARCH
COPY --from=server /nfsu2-server-$TARGETARCH /nfsu2-server

FROM alpine:3.22
ARG TARGETARCH
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="nfsu2-web-rs" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="NFS Underground 2 in the browser: the server, in Rust (bring your own game)" \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses="MIT"
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=page /src/web/dist web/dist
COPY --from=server /nfsu2-server-$TARGETARCH /app/nfsu2-server
COPY --from=page --chown=1000:1000 --chmod=700 /state /state
# NFSU2_REPO: where the server finds the page (web/dist); its own default is the checkout it was built in
ENV NFSU2_REPO=/app \
    NFSU2_DATA=/game \
    NFSU2_WASM=/module/nfsu2.wasm \
    NFSU2_STATE=/state \
    NFSU2_MAX_PEERS=24000
# (a uid without a name: this stage runs nothing, so building it for arm64 needs no emulation)
USER 1000:1000
VOLUME /state
# the module is there and the server answers (over the HTTP port, which stays on 127.0.0.1)
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=60s --start-interval=2s \
  CMD wget -q -O /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:${NFSU2_HTTP_PORT:-8080}/game.json" || exit 1
ENTRYPOINT ["/app/nfsu2-server"]
CMD ["--behind-proxy"]

# The server

The game's server, in Rust: it serves the page, the game module and the game's own files, and connects the players
(the virtual LAN switch, the free-roam hub and the game's Online mode).  Its options are in `src/options.rs`.

## Build and run

    web/server-rs/build.sh            # -> out/web/server-rs/nfsu2-server
    web/server-rs/build.sh --test     # and the workspace's own tests
    out/web/server-rs/nfsu2-server --data "<NFSU2 folder>" --http-port 8081 --state /tmp/state-rs

It needs Rust (https://rustup.rs) and a C compiler (zstd and mimalloc are C).

## The container image

`web/server-rs/Dockerfile` builds the image that `web/deploy/compose.yml` runs:

    docker build -f web/server-rs/Dockerfile -t nfsu2-web-rs .

{"id": "AT001529", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/server-rs/build.sh", "originalBytes": 2400, "originalSha256": "2d98afa526d2e25384028e775dfbc87db4a325793f2b8786b035cf0c21f1cc63", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 2400, "utf8TotalBytes": 2400}

#!/bin/bash
# The Rust server: web/server-rs/build.sh [--test]  ->  out/web/server-rs/nfsu2-server
# (and the free-roam load generator, out/web/server-rs/nfsu2-roamload: web/tools/server-compare.mjs --load crowd)
#   --test  also its own tests (every crate's, in Cargo.toml's profile.ci: release code without its slow link)
# Needs Rust (rustup: https://rustup.rs) and a C compiler (zstd and mimalloc are C).  The build folder is
# out/web/server-rs/target ($CARGO_TARGET_DIR to put it elsewhere).
# Sources built before are not built again: ~/.cache/nsfu2-web/server keeps the last 12 builds' binaries under a
# hash of every file in web/server-rs and the toolchain, and a checkout whose files hash the same gets copies of
# them (the server finds its checkout from where it sits, not from where it was built).
set -e -o pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
REPO="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
[ -f "$HOME/.cargo/env" ] && . "$HOME/.cargo/env"
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$REPO/out/web/server-rs/target}"
cd "$HERE"
BINS="nfsu2-server nfsu2-roamload"
CACHE="$HOME/.cache/nsfu2-web/server"
KEY="$( { find . -path ./target -prune -o -type f -print0 | LC_ALL=C sort -z | xargs -0 shasum -a 256
          rustc -vV; cargo -V; echo "${RUSTFLAGS:-}"; } | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-16)"
mkdir -p "$REPO/out/web/server-rs"
# a rename, so that a server starting meanwhile never runs a half-written binary
put(){ cp "$1" "$REPO/out/web/server-rs/$2.tmp"; mv -f "$REPO/out/web/server-rs/$2.tmp" "$REPO/out/web/server-rs/$2"; echo "out/web/server-rs/$2"; }
if [ -f "$CACHE/$KEY/done" ]; then
  for b in $BINS; do put "$CACHE/$KEY/$b" "$b"; done
  touch "$CACHE/$KEY"
  echo "(built before from the same sources: $CACHE/$KEY)"
else
  cargo build --release -p nfsu2-server -p nfsu2-roamload
  for b in $BINS; do put "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/$b" "$b"; done
  # into the cache: a folder of its own first, renamed when complete
  mkdir -p "$CACHE"; T="$(mktemp -d "$CACHE/.new-XXXXXX")"
  for b in $BINS; do cp "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/$b" "$T/$b"; done
  touch "$T/done"
  if [ -e "$CACHE/$KEY" ]; then rm -rf "$T"; else mv "$T" "$CACHE/$KEY"; fi
  ls -1dt "$CACHE"/*/ | tail -n +13 | while read -r d; do rm -rf "$d"; done
  find "$CACHE" -maxdepth 1 -name '.new-*' -mmin +60 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
fi
if [ "${1:-}" = --test ]; then cargo test --profile ci --workspace; fi

{"id": "AT001532", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/server-rs/crates/anticheat/src/lib.rs", "originalBytes": 4384, "originalSha256": "6960ac4304b4a5b7a44b9214177c738cb335e9ebc030f26b8bb59a34c1c1d68f", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 4384, "utf8TotalBytes": 4384}
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
//! What the race checks of the free-roam hub (nfsu2-roam: results.rs, hub.rs) and of the Online mode (nfsu2-online:
//! lobby.rs) share: the limits no honest race passes, the rule for a car's jump, and a track's quickest racers
//! ([`Quickest`]), which a win far quicker than theirs is measured against.  What differs stays with each check: what
//! makes a race clean, whose times it adds (the hub's: the winner's; the Online mode's: every finisher's), and the
//! hub's own quickest clean win.

/// no car of the game averages this over a race (m/s: 350 km/h; the fastest tuned cars make 350 at the most, a race's
/// average far less: a 2-lap circuit's was 112 km/h)
pub const RACE_MPS: f64 = 350.0 / 3.6;

/// a top speed no car of the game makes, however tuned (km/h)
pub const CAR_KMH: f64 = 420.0;

/// A winner in under THIRD_SHARE of the third quickest other racer's time of its track ([`Quickest::third`]), once the
/// track had QUICK_WINS clean races, is a `[cheat]` line: a car made faster than any tuning makes one.  Not when another
/// finisher came close (the winner over THIRD_SHARE of its time): that time can be driven.  TOP_KEPT: the quickest
/// racers kept of each track.
pub const THIRD_SHARE: f64 = 0.7;
pub const QUICK_WINS: u32 = 10;
pub const TOP_KEPT: usize = 4;

/// A car's jump at once (m) that no lag makes, and how many of the other racers' games must have had it so (or the only
/// other one: [`jump_seen`]).  Honest races' largest: 18-44 m (a reset to the road, a hit), 31 m after a 1.5 s stall
/// of a test's (runtime/racenet.c); a car a player said stood still for laps, then finished at once, jumped 279.9 m in
/// the reporter's game.
pub const JUMP_M: f64 = 150.0;
pub const JUMP_SEEN: usize = 2;

/// a drift race's mode (roam_core.h's race mode, the Online mode's race type): won by points, so left out of the time
/// rules
pub const MODE_DRIFT: u8 = 3;

/// whether the other racers' games had a car jump: `far` of them had it JUMP_M or more, JUMP_SEEN at least, or the
/// one when it is the only other one (`only_other`)
pub fn jump_seen(far: usize, only_other: bool) -> bool {
    far >= JUMP_SEEN || (only_other && far == 1)
}

/// A track's clean races: how many (`wins`, which the check counts as it sees fit), and its quickest racers, each once
/// by name with its best time, quickest first, TOP_KEPT at most
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Quickest {
    pub wins: u32,
    top: Vec<(String, f64)>,
}

impl Quickest {
    /// a racer's time (its best is kept); `wins` is left as it is
    pub fn add(&mut self, who: String, time: f64) {
        match self.top.iter_mut().find(|(w, _)| *w == who) {
            Some(x) => x.1 = x.1.min(time),
            None => self.top.push((who, time)),
        }
        self.top.sort_by(|a, b| a.1.total_cmp(&b.1));
        self.top.truncate(TOP_KEPT);
    }

    /// the racers kept, quickest first
    pub fn top(&self) -> &[(String, f64)] {
        &self.top
    }

    /// the third quickest racer's time but `who`'s, once the track had QUICK_WINS clean races
    pub fn third(&self, who: &str) -> Option<f64> {
        (self.wins >= QUICK_WINS).then(|| self.top.iter().filter(|(w, _)| w != who).nth(2).map(|x| x.1)).flatten()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn the_quickest_keep_each_racers_best_and_the_third_leaves_the_winner_out() {
        let mut q = Quickest::default();
        for (who, t) in [("a", 60.0), ("b", 62.0), ("c", 65.0), ("a", 58.0), ("d", 70.0), ("e", 71.0)] {
            q.add(who.into(), t);
        }
        let names: Vec<(&str, f64)> = q.top().iter().map(|(w, t)| (w.as_str(), *t)).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, [("a", 58.0), ("b", 62.0), ("c", 65.0), ("d", 70.0)], "each once, its best, TOP_KEPT");
        assert_eq!(q.third("x"), None, "not before QUICK_WINS");
        q.wins = QUICK_WINS;
        assert_eq!(q.third("x"), Some(65.0));
        assert_eq!(q.third("a"), Some(70.0), "the winner's own time is not one to beat");
        q.add("a".into(), 80.0);
        assert_eq!(q.top()[0], ("a".to_string(), 58.0), "a slower time leaves the best");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_jump_counts_by_two_games_or_the_only_other_one() {
        assert!(jump_seen(2, false) && jump_seen(3, true));
        assert!(!jump_seen(1, false) && jump_seen(1, true));
        assert!(!jump_seen(0, true));
    }
}
