//! A request's headers as Node's `IncomingMessage` builds `q.headers` (`_addHeaderLine`, `matchKnownFields`): names
//! in lower case; a second line of a header Node keeps once is dropped, `cookie` lines are joined with "; ", all
//! others with ", ".

use crate::Headers;
use crate::parse::latin1;

/// How Node joins a header's lines.
#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Join {
    /// the first line wins (Node's "no duplicates" fields)
    First,
    /// "; "
    Cookie,
    /// ", "
    List,
}

fn join_of(name: &str) -> Join {
    match name {
        "age"
        | "authorization"
        | "content-length"
        | "content-type"
        | "etag"
        | "expires"
        | "from"
        | "host"
        | "if-modified-since"
        | "if-unmodified-since"
        | "last-modified"
        | "location"
        | "max-forwards"
        | "proxy-authorization"
        | "referer"
        | "retry-after"
        | "server"
        | "user-agent" => Join::First,
        "cookie" => Join::Cookie,
        // (set-cookie, an array in Node, is a list here)
        _ => Join::List,
    }
}

/// Lines with more names than this are joined through an index (a request may carry up to 1000).
const LINEAR: usize = 32;

/// `q.headers` from the request's (name, value) lines in order; values are bytes as they came (latin1, as Node
/// reads them).
pub(crate) fn join<'a>(lines: impl Iterator<Item = (&'a [u8], &'a [u8])>) -> Headers {
    let mut list: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
    let mut index: Option<std::collections::HashMap<String, usize>> = None;
    for (name, value) in lines {
        let name = lower(name);
        let at = match &index {
            Some(ix) => ix.get(&name).copied(),
            None => list.iter().position(|(k, _)| *k == name),
        };
        match at {
            None => {
                if let Some(ix) = &mut index {
                    ix.insert(name.clone(), list.len());
                }
                list.push((name, latin1(value)));
                if index.is_none() && list.len() > LINEAR {
                    index = Some(list.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, (k, _))| (k.clone(), i)).collect());
                }
            }
            Some(i) => match join_of(&list[i].0) {
                Join::First => {}
                Join::Cookie => {
                    list[i].1.push_str("; ");
                    list[i].1.push_str(&latin1(value));
                }
                Join::List => {
                    list[i].1.push_str(", ");
                    list[i].1.push_str(&latin1(value));
                }
            },
        }
    }
    Headers { list }
}

/// a header name (a token: ASCII) in lower case
fn lower(name: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut s = String::with_capacity(name.len());
    for &b in name {
        s.push(b.to_ascii_lowercase() as char);
    }
    s
}

impl Headers {
    /// a header by its name (any case)
    pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.list.iter().find(|(k, _)| k.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name)).map(|(_, v)| v.as_str())
    }
    /// how many headers (after joining)
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.list.len()
    }
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.list.is_empty()
    }
}

                .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), v.to_string()))
                .collect();
        assert_eq!(got, want);
    }

    fn many_lines_join_the_same_through_the_index() {
        let names: Vec<String> = (0..100).map(|i| format!("x-{i}")).collect();
        let mut lines: Vec<(&str, &str)> = names.iter().map(|n| (n.as_str(), "a")).collect();
        lines.push(("X-7", "b"));
        lines.push(("host", "h"));
        lines.push(("Host", "i"));
        let got = h(&lines);
        assert_eq!(got.len(), 101);
        assert_eq!(got[7].1, "a, b");
        assert_eq!(got[100], ("host".to_string(), "h".to_string()));
    }

    /// repeats): q.headers must come out the same

        let names = [

            "User-Agent",

            "Upgrade",
            "Connection",
            "Content-Length",

            "Cache-Control",
            "Accept-Encoding",
            "Accept-Language",
            "X-Forwarded-Host",
            "X-Forwarded-Proto",
            "Content-Encoding",
            "Transfer-Encoding",
            "If-Match",
            "Location",
            "Server",
            "From",
            "Expires",
            "Last-Modified",
            "Retry-After",
            "Max-Forwards",
            "Proxy-Authorization",
            "If-Modified-Since",
            "If-Unmodified-Since",
            "X-A",
            "x-a",
            "Sec-WebSocket-Key",
            "CF-Connecting-IP",
            "cf-connecting-ip",
            "Range",
            "TE",
        ];
        let values = ["a", "b", "1, 2", "x=y", "", "c; d", "\u{e9}"];
        let mut rng = crate::node::Rng(42);
        let mut cases = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..2000 {
            let n = 1 + rng.below(8);
            let lines: Vec<(String, String)> = (0..n).map(|_| (rng.pick(&names).to_string(), rng.pick(&values).to_string())).collect();
            cases.push(lines);

                return Object.entries(m.headers).map(([k, v]) => [k, Array.isArray(v) ? v.join(', ') : v]);
              });
              process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(out));
            });"#;
        let Some(out) = crate::node::run(script, &input) else {
            eprintln!("skipped: no node to compare with");
            return;
        };
        let want: Vec<Vec<(String, String)>> = serde_json::from_str(&out).unwrap_or_default();
        assert_eq!(want.len(), cases.len());
        for (lines, want) in cases.iter().zip(want) {
            // the bytes on the wire are latin1 (é is one byte), as Node reads them
            let raw: Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)> =
                lines.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_bytes().to_vec(), v.chars().map(|c| c as u32 as u8).collect())).collect();
            let got = join(raw.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_slice(), v.as_slice()))).list;
            assert_eq!(got, want, "{lines:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn values_are_latin1() {
        let got = join([(&b"x"[..], &b"a\xffb"[..])].into_iter()).list;
        assert_eq!(got[0].1, "a\u{ff}b");
    }

//! The server's own HTTP/1.1, on tokio, on every core: what Node's `http.createServer` / `https.createServer` did
//! for the Node server it replaced, with the rules that server set on them ([`Limits`]), and the answers to what it
//! cannot read ([`Service::client_error`], [`raw_refusal`]).  Not hyper: the audits' rules need answers of the
//! server's own to requests a library refuses by itself (with the security headers), the pipelining cut, a
//! keep-alive time per connection, and the connection budget before any TLS.
//!
//! - [`serve`]: the accept loop of one listening socket (plain, or TLS with [`tls::TlsState`])
//! - [`Service`]: what the server does with a connection, a request, an upgrade, a request it cannot read
//! - [`Request`], [`Response`]: one exchange, as Node's `IncomingMessage` / `ServerResponse` were to the Node server
//! - [`Stream`]: a connection, plain or TLS, that an upgrade hands over (the /lan WebSocket), split into halves
//!
//! Inside: `parse` reads requests as llhttp 9 (Node 24's parser) does, `conn` runs a connection as Node's http server
//! did (its timers, the pipelining cut, the refusals), `response` writes answers as Node's `ServerResponse`.  What
//! differs from Node on purpose is said where it is (a request Node would have dropped unanswered when a later one
//! broke the connection is answered first; a TLS handshake has `handshake_timeout` in all, not between its bytes).

mod conn;
mod head;
mod headers;
mod parse;
mod response;
pub mod tls;

/// The unit tests' cross-checks run node itself.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod node {
    use std::io::Write;
    use std::process::{Command, Stdio};

    /// `node --input-type=module -e <script>` with `input` on its stdin: its stdout, or None without node (the
    /// caller skips, with a message)
    pub fn run(script: &str, input: &str) -> Option<String> {
        let mut child = Command::new("node")
            .args(["--input-type=module", "-e", script])
            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
            .stderr(Stdio::inherit())
            .spawn()
            .ok()?;
        child.stdin.take()?.write_all(input.as_bytes()).ok()?;
        let out = child.wait_with_output().ok()?;
        assert!(out.status.success(), "node failed");
        String::from_utf8(out.stdout).ok()
    }

    /// a seeded generator (xorshift64*)
    pub struct Rng(pub u64);
    impl Rng {
        pub fn next(&mut self) -> u64 {
            self.0 ^= self.0 >> 12;
            self.0 ^= self.0 << 25;
            self.0 ^= self.0 >> 27;
            self.0.wrapping_mul(0x2545_f491_4f6c_dd1d)
        }
        pub fn below(&mut self, n: usize) -> usize {
            (self.next() % n as u64) as usize
        }
        pub fn pick<'a>(&mut self, list: &[&'a str]) -> &'a str {
            list[self.below(list.len())]
        }
    }
}

/// The limits of one connection and of a listening socket (the ones the Node server set on Node's http server).
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Limits {
    /// request line + headers (Node's maxHeaderSize; above: 431)
    pub max_header_size: usize,
    /// the whole header must arrive within this (from the request's first byte; slow-loris): 408
    pub headers_timeout: Duration,
    /// and the whole request (nothing takes a body but the test PUTs): 408
    pub request_timeout: Duration,
    /// a TLS handshake (Node's default is 120 s)
    pub handshake_timeout: Duration,
    /// a connection with nothing to do for this long goes (Node's server.setTimeout: reads and writes reset it); an
    /// answer the client stopped reading is ended sooner, by the progress rule
    pub socket_idle: Duration,
    /// requests queued on one connection without a finished answer (browsers and proxies send one at a time); one
    /// more and the connection goes
    pub pipelined: usize,
    /// connections at once on one listening socket (Node's maxConnections: more are closed at once)
    pub max_connections: usize,
    /// how often the header and request timeouts are checked (Node's connectionsCheckingInterval)
    pub check_interval: Duration,
    /// a response must move: at least `progress_bytes` in every `progress`... (a 1 MiB block or the 7 MB module takes
    /// seconds; a client that stops reading, or reads a trickle, is let go)
    pub progress_bytes: u64,
    pub progress: Duration,
    /// ...and may take this long at most (the progress rule: conn.rs `progress`)
    pub response_max: Duration,
}

impl Default for Limits {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Limits {
            max_header_size: 16 << 10,
            headers_timeout: Duration::from_secs(15),
            request_timeout: Duration::from_secs(30),
            handshake_timeout: Duration::from_secs(15),
            socket_idle: Duration::from_secs(120),
            pipelined: 4,
            max_connections: 1024,
            check_interval: Duration::from_secs(5),
            progress_bytes: 64 << 10,
            progress: Duration::from_secs(20),
            response_max: Duration::from_secs(15 * 60),
        }
    }
}

/// The HTTP version of a request (Node's `q.httpVersion`).
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Version {
    Http10,
    /// HTTP/1.1, and the other versions Node takes (0.9, 2.0), which the server's "HTTP/1.1 needs a Host" counts as
    /// HTTP/1.1: only HTTP/1.0 may come without one ([`Request::http_version`] has the exact version)
    Http11,
}

/// A request's headers as Node's `q.headers` has them: names in lower case, duplicates joined as Node joins them
/// (most with ", "; `cookie` with "; "; the ones Node keeps only once, such as `host`, `content-length`,
/// `content-type`, `user-agent`, `authorization`, `referer`: the first).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Headers {
    list: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

impl Headers {
    pub fn has(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.get(name).is_some()
    }
    /// every (name, value) after joining, in the order the names first came
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&str, &str)> {
        self.list.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v.as_str()))
    }
}

/// What a request's connection is, for the server's rules.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ConnInfo {
    /// the TCP peer
    pub peer_addr: SocketAddr,
    /// `socket.remoteAddress` as Node gives it: "127.0.0.1", "::1", "::ffff:1.2.3.4" on a dual-stack listener
    pub peer: String,
    /// TLS (`socket.encrypted`)
    pub encrypted: bool,
}

/// One request (Node's `IncomingMessage`).
pub struct Request {
    pub method: String,
    /// the request target as sent (Node's `q.url`): "/path?query", or an absolute URL
    pub url: String,
    pub version: Version,
    pub headers: Headers,
    pub conn: ConnInfo,
    /// the body, for the few requests that take one (PUT /artifacts/): read with `read_body`
    body: Body,
    major: u8,
    minor: u8,
}

/// The body of a request (Content-Length or chunked).
pub struct Body {
    rx: Option<mpsc::Receiver<conn::BodyMsg>>,
    /// its Content-Length (None: chunked, or no body)
    length: Option<u64>,
}

/// Why a body could not be read.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum BodyError {
    /// more than the limit
    TooLarge,
    /// the client went, sent a broken body, or took too long
    Broken,
}

impl Request {
    /// the whole body, at most `limit` bytes
    pub async fn read_body(&mut self, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, BodyError> {
        let Some(rx) = self.body.rx.as_mut() else { return Ok(Vec::new()) };
        if self.body.length.is_some_and(|n| n > limit as u64) {
            return Err(BodyError::TooLarge);
        }
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(self.body.length.map_or(0, |n| n as usize).min(limit).min(1 << 20));
        loop {
            match rx.recv().await {
                Some(conn::BodyMsg::Data(b)) => {
                    if out.len() + b.len() > limit {
                        return Err(BodyError::TooLarge);
                    }
                    out.extend_from_slice(&b);
                }
                Some(conn::BodyMsg::End) => {
                    self.body.rx = None;
                    return Ok(out);
                }
                None => return Err(BodyError::Broken),
            }
        }
    }
    /// Node's `q.httpVersion`: "1.1", "1.0", "0.9" or "2.0"
    pub fn http_version(&self) -> &'static str {
        match (self.major, self.minor) {
            (1, 0) => "1.0",
            (0, 9) => "0.9",
            (2, 0) => "2.0",
            _ => "1.1",
        }
    }
}

impl nfsu2_headers::Req for Request {
    fn peer(&self) -> &str {
        &self.conn.peer
    }
    fn header(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.headers.get(name)
    }
    fn encrypted(&self) -> bool {
        self.conn.encrypted
    }
}

/// One answer (Node's `ServerResponse`), written to its connection.  Headers are given in order with lower-case
/// names, as the server gives them to `head`; the engine adds what Node added (`Date`, `Connection`,
/// `Keep-Alive: timeout=<the connection's>` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` when there is no Content-Length on
/// HTTP/1.1).  A HEAD request's answer has no body, whatever is written.  Bytes written count towards the
/// response's progress (`Limits::progress_bytes`): an answer the client does not take fast enough is cut, and the
/// connection with it.
pub struct Response {
    io: Option<WriteHalf>,
    out: Vec<u8>,
    flow: Arc<response::Flow>,
    meta: response::Meta,
    status: u16,
    /// what set_header gave (Node's kOutHeaders)
    pre: Vec<(String, String)>,
    /// what head gave
    given: Vec<(String, String)>,
    phase: response::Phase,
    has_body: bool,
    chunked: bool,
    /// the connection goes after this answer (Node's `_last`)
    last: bool,
    /// Node's `shouldKeepAlive`
    keep: bool,
    /// end() without a head: Content-Length 0 (Node's `_contentLength`)
    implicit_len: Option<u64>,
}

/// A request the engine could not read (what it is answered with: [`Service::client_error`]).
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ClientError {
    /// a request Node's parser refuses (an HPE_ error): 400
    Parse,
    /// request line + headers over `max_header_size`: 431
    HeaderOverflow,
    /// the header or the request took too long: 408
    Timeout,
}

/// What the server does with a connection, a request, an upgrade, a request it cannot read.
pub trait Service: Send + Sync + 'static {
    /// A new TCP connection, before any TLS or byte: None closes it at once.  What it returns is dropped when the
    /// connection goes (the per-client connection budget gives its share back).
    fn admit(&self, peer: &SocketAddr) -> Option<Box<dyn Send + Sync>>;
    /// This peer's TLS handshake must show a client certificate that the TLS state's client CA signed, or it fails
    /// (tls.rs; a proxy whose forwarding headers are believed, at addresses others connect from too).  Nobody by
    /// default.
    fn client_certificate(&self, _peer: &SocketAddr) -> bool {
        false
    }
    /// How long an idle keep-alive connection from this peer is kept, and what its answers' `Keep-Alive: timeout=`
    /// says (Cloudflare's own connections: 905 s; others 65 s).
    fn keep_alive(&self, peer: &SocketAddr) -> Duration;
    /// One request.  The engine has counted it against `pipelined` already.
    fn request<'a>(&'a self, req: Request, res: &'a mut Response) -> impl Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'a;
    /// A request with an Expect other than 100-continue on HTTP/1.1 (Node's 'checkExpectation'; for 100-continue the
    /// engine writes "100 Continue" itself and calls `request`).
    fn expectation<'a>(&'a self, req: Request, res: &'a mut Response) -> impl Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'a;
    /// A request that asks for an upgrade (Connection: upgrade and an Upgrade header; Node's 'upgrade' event): the
    /// service takes the connection over, and the 101 or a refusal (`raw_refusal`) is its to write.
    fn upgrade(&self, req: Request, up: Upgraded) -> impl Future<Output = ()> + Send;
    /// A request the engine cannot read: the raw answer to write before the connection goes, or None to close it at
    /// once.
    fn client_error(&self, e: ClientError) -> Option<Vec<u8>>;
}

/// A connection an upgrade hands over, and what was read past the request's head (Node's `head`).
pub struct Upgraded {
    pub stream: Stream,
    pub pre: Bytes,
    /// the connection's shares: keep it for as long as the stream is kept
    pub hold: Hold,
}

/// What a connection holds while it is open: its share of the per-client connection budget (`Service::admit`'s) and
/// its place on the listener's count (`Limits::max_connections`).  An upgrade hands it over with the stream, and
/// whoever takes the stream keeps it until the connection closes: Node counted an upgraded socket (the /lan WebSocket,
/// open for hours) in both until its 'close', and a crowd of WebSockets must not leave the per-client limits and
/// maxConnections free for more connections than the port was sized for.
pub struct Hold(#[allow(dead_code)] Vec<Box<dyn Send + Sync>>);

impl Hold {
    /// holds nothing (a connection made by hand, in a test)
    pub fn none() -> Hold {
        Hold(Vec::new())
    }
}

/// A connection, plain or TLS, or plain on a Unix socket (`serve_unix`).
pub enum Stream {
    Plain(TcpStream),
    Tls(Box<tokio_rustls::server::TlsStream<TcpStream>>),
    Unix(UnixStream),
}

impl Stream {
    /// SO_SNDBUF (the kernel's send buffer for this connection; Linux grows it to megabytes by itself.  On a Unix
    /// socket it holds what waits in the reader's queue: there is no receive buffer of the reader's own)
    pub fn set_send_buffer(&self, bytes: usize) -> io::Result<()> {
        match self {
            Stream::Plain(s) => socket2::SockRef::from(s).set_send_buffer_size(bytes),
            Stream::Tls(s) => socket2::SockRef::from(s.get_ref().0).set_send_buffer_size(bytes),
            Stream::Unix(s) => socket2::SockRef::from(s).set_send_buffer_size(bytes),
        }
    }
    /// a read half and a write half that tasks on different threads can own (plain TCP: lock-free)
    pub fn split(self) -> (ReadHalf, WriteHalf) {
        match self {
            Stream::Plain(s) => {
                let (r, w) = s.into_split();
                (ReadHalf::Plain(r), WriteHalf::Plain(w))
            }
            Stream::Tls(s) => {
                let (r, w) = tokio::io::split(*s);
                (ReadHalf::Tls(r), WriteHalf::Tls(w))
            }
            Stream::Unix(s) => {
                let (r, w) = s.into_split();
                (ReadHalf::Unix(r), WriteHalf::Unix(w))
            }
        }
    }
}

pub enum ReadHalf {
    Plain(tokio::net::tcp::OwnedReadHalf),
    Tls(tokio::io::ReadHalf<tokio_rustls::server::TlsStream<TcpStream>>),
    Unix(tokio::net::unix::OwnedReadHalf),
}
pub enum WriteHalf {
    Plain(tokio::net::tcp::OwnedWriteHalf),
    Tls(tokio::io::WriteHalf<tokio_rustls::server::TlsStream<TcpStream>>),
    Unix(tokio::net::unix::OwnedWriteHalf),
}

impl AsyncRead for ReadHalf {
    fn poll_read(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>, buf: &mut ReadBuf<'_>) -> Poll<io::Result<()>> {
        match self.get_mut() {
            ReadHalf::Plain(r) => Pin::new(r).poll_read(cx, buf),
            ReadHalf::Tls(r) => Pin::new(r).poll_read(cx, buf),
            ReadHalf::Unix(r) => Pin::new(r).poll_read(cx, buf),
        }
    }
}

            WriteHalf::Tls(w) => Pin::new(w).poll_write(cx, buf),
            WriteHalf::Unix(w) => Pin::new(w).poll_write(cx, buf),
        }
    }
    fn poll_write_vectored(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>, bufs: &[io::IoSlice<'_>]) -> Poll<io::Result<usize>> {
        match self.get_mut() {
            WriteHalf::Plain(w) => Pin::new(w).poll_write_vectored(cx, bufs),
            WriteHalf::Tls(w) => Pin::new(w).poll_write_vectored(cx, bufs),
            WriteHalf::Unix(w) => Pin::new(w).poll_write_vectored(cx, bufs),
        }
    }
    fn is_write_vectored(&self) -> bool {
        match self {
            WriteHalf::Plain(w) => w.is_write_vectored(),
            WriteHalf::Tls(w) => w.is_write_vectored(),

        }

    fn poll_flush(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<io::Result<()>> {

            WriteHalf::Tls(w) => Pin::new(w).poll_flush(cx),

        }

    fn poll_shutdown(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<io::Result<()>> {
        match self.get_mut() {
            WriteHalf::Plain(w) => Pin::new(w).poll_shutdown(cx),
            WriteHalf::Tls(w) => Pin::new(w).poll_shutdown(cx),
            WriteHalf::Unix(w) => Pin::new(w).poll_shutdown(cx),
        }
    }
}

/// Listen on `port` at `host`; a `fallback` host (the server's "::" falls back to "0.0.0.0" on a machine without
/// IPv6, for EAFNOSUPPORT, EADDRNOTAVAIL, EINVAL) is tried when that fails.  Ok: the listener and the host it is on.
/// Err: the message the server dies with after "cannot listen: " ("port N is in use", or the error's as Node wrote
/// it).
pub async fn bind(host: &str, port: u16, fallback: Option<&str>) -> Result<(TcpListener, String), String> {
    let mut host = host.to_string();
    let mut fallback = fallback.map(str::to_string);
    loop {
        match listen_on(&host, port).await {
            Ok(l) => return Ok((l, host)),
            Err(e) => {
                let code = e.raw_os_error().unwrap_or(0);
                if code == libc::EADDRINUSE {
                    return Err(format!("port {port} is in use"));
                }
                let retry = if matches!(code, libc::EAFNOSUPPORT | libc::EADDRNOTAVAIL | libc::EINVAL) { fallback.take() } else { None };
                match retry {
                    Some(f) => host = f,
                    None => return Err(listen_message(&e, &host, port)),
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

async fn listen_on(host: &str, port: u16) -> io::Result<TcpListener> {
    let ip: IpAddr = match host.trim_start_matches('[').trim_end_matches(']').parse() {
        Ok(ip) => ip,
        // a name, as Node's listen() looks it up
        Err(_) => match tokio::net::lookup_host((host, port)).await?.next() {
            Some(a) => a.ip(),
            None => return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, format!("getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND {host}"))),
        },
    };
    let addr = SocketAddr::new(ip, port);
    let sock = socket2::Socket::new(socket2::Domain::for_address(addr), socket2::Type::STREAM, Some(socket2::Protocol::TCP))?;
    if addr.is_ipv6() {
        // "::" takes IPv4 too (Node's default dual stack)
        sock.set_only_v6(false)?;
    }
    // as libuv: a restarted server may bind while old connections linger in TIME_WAIT
    sock.set_reuse_address(true)?;
    sock.set_nonblocking(true)?;
    sock.bind(&addr.into())?;
    // more than Node's 511: when a Cloudflare Tunnel connection goes, the players on it (a thousand and more) come back
    // within a second, each a new connection from cloudflared; past the backlog the kernel drops the handshake and the
    // client tries again a second or more later.  The kernel takes at most its somaxconn (Linux: 4096 since 5.4)
    sock.listen(4096)?;
    TcpListener::from_std(sock.into())
}

/// Node's message for a listen error: "listen EACCES: permission denied 0.0.0.0:80" (":::80" for "::")
fn listen_message(e: &io::Error, host: &str, port: u16) -> String {
    let (code, text) = match e.raw_os_error() {
        Some(libc::EACCES) => ("EACCES", "permission denied"),
        Some(libc::EPERM) => ("EPERM", "operation not permitted"),
        Some(libc::EADDRNOTAVAIL) => ("EADDRNOTAVAIL", "address not available"),
        Some(libc::EAFNOSUPPORT) => ("EAFNOSUPPORT", "address family not supported"),
        Some(libc::EINVAL) => ("EINVAL", "invalid argument"),
        _ => return e.to_string(),
    };
    format!("listen {code}: {text} {host}:{port}")
}

/// The accept loop of one listening socket, until the process ends: each connection on a task of its own (on every
/// core), TLS first when `tls` is given (within `handshake_timeout`; a handshake that fails or times out closes the
/// connection without a byte of HTTP; a refused one looks as Node's did, `tls::TlsState::handshake`), then requests
/// in turn.
pub fn serve<S: Service>(
    listener: TcpListener,
    tls: Option<Arc<tls::TlsState>>,
    limits: Arc<Limits>,
    service: Arc<S>,
) -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<()> {
    tokio::spawn(accept_loop(Listener::Tcp(listener), tls, limits, service))
}

/// The same for a Unix socket, plain HTTP: a proxy on this machine reaches the server there without TCP (cloudflared's
/// `unix:` origin), and each of its connections counts as one from `peer` (the address the proxy would have on TCP,
/// 127.0.0.1, so it is the trusted proxy it is there).
pub fn serve_unix<S: Service>(
    listener: UnixListener,
    peer: SocketAddr,
    limits: Arc<Limits>,
    service: Arc<S>,
) -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<()> {
    tokio::spawn(accept_loop(Listener::Unix(listener, peer), None, limits, service))
}

enum Listener {
    Tcp(TcpListener),
    Unix(UnixListener, SocketAddr),
}

enum Accepted {
    Tcp(TcpStream),
    Unix(UnixStream),
}

impl Listener {
    async fn accept(&self) -> io::Result<(Accepted, SocketAddr)> {
        match self {
            Listener::Tcp(l) => l.accept().await.map(|(s, peer)| (Accepted::Tcp(s), peer)),
            Listener::Unix(l, peer) => l.accept().await.map(|(s, _)| (Accepted::Unix(s), *peer)),
        }
    }
}

/// a connection on the listener's count (Node's server._connections) while it lives
struct Open(Arc<AtomicUsize>);
impl Drop for Open {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.0.fetch_sub(1, Relaxed);
    }
}

async fn accept_loop<S: Service>(listener: Listener, tls: Option<Arc<tls::TlsState>>, limits: Arc<Limits>, service: Arc<S>) {
    // Node checks the header and request times of a server's connections on one interval from its start
    let epoch = Instant::now();
    let open = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
    loop {
        let (sock, peer) = match listener.accept().await {
            Ok(c) => c,
            Err(e) => {
                // out of file descriptors (or memory): wait a little, the connections that end give them back
                if matches!(e.raw_os_error(), Some(libc::EMFILE | libc::ENFILE | libc::ENOBUFS | libc::ENOMEM)) {
                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
                }
                continue;
            }
        };
        // Node's maxConnections: more are closed at once, before anything else sees them
        if open.load(Relaxed) >= limits.max_connections {
            drop(sock);
            continue;
        }
        open.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
        let count = Open(open.clone());
        // Service::admit: the per-client connection budget, before any TLS or byte.  (It runs on this loop: a panic
        // in it costs this connection only, not the loop and with it the port.)
        let Ok(Some(admitted)) = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| service.admit(&peer))) else { continue };
        // Node's http server: noDelay
        if let Accepted::Tcp(tcp) = &sock {
            let _ = tcp.set_nodelay(true);
        }
        let (tls, limits, service) = (tls.clone(), limits.clone(), service.clone());
        // (given back when the connection's task ends, or, for an upgrade, when whoever took the stream lets it go)
        let hold = Hold(vec![admitted, Box::new(count)]);
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            connection(sock, peer, tls, limits, &*service, epoch, hold).await;
        });
    }
}

async fn connection<S: Service>(
    sock: Accepted,
    peer: SocketAddr,
    tls: Option<Arc<tls::TlsState>>,
    limits: Arc<Limits>,
    service: &S,
    epoch: Instant,
    hold: Hold,
) {
    let encrypted = tls.is_some();
    let stream = match (sock, tls) {
        (Accepted::Tcp(tcp), Some(tls)) => {
            // (on the heap for the handshake only: its state, a rustls connection being made, would otherwise be part
            // of the connection's future for as long as the connection lives)
            let accept = Box::pin(tls.handshake(tcp, service.client_certificate(&peer)));
            let done = if limits.handshake_timeout.is_zero() {
                Ok(accept.await)
            } else {
                tokio::time::timeout(limits.handshake_timeout, accept).await
            };
            match done {
                Ok(Some(s)) => Stream::Tls(Box::new(s)),
                // failed or too slow: the connection goes, without a byte of HTTP (an answer queued into a TLS socket
                // whose handshake never finished held the socket for good, and 1024 such sockets locked the port: the
                // phase-2 deploy review's finding 2)
                _ => return,
            }
        }
        (Accepted::Tcp(tcp), None) => Stream::Plain(tcp),
        // (never TLS: serve_unix gives none)
        (Accepted::Unix(s), _) => Stream::Unix(s),
    };
    let info = ConnInfo { peer_addr: peer, peer: remote_address(&peer), encrypted };
    let keep_alive = service.keep_alive(&peer);
    conn::serve(stream, info, limits, keep_alive, epoch, service, hold).await;
}

/// Node's `socket.remoteAddress`: an IPv4 client of a dual-stack listener is "::ffff:a.b.c.d"
fn remote_address(peer: &SocketAddr) -> String {
    match peer.ip() {
        IpAddr::V4(a) => a.to_string(),
        IpAddr::V6(a) => a.to_string(),
    }
}

/// A refusal on a connection taken over by an upgrade: the raw answer, then the connection goes (at once once
/// written, or after 1 s at most).
pub async fn raw_refusal(stream: Stream, answer: Vec<u8>) {
    let (mut r, mut w) = stream.split();
    conn::refuse_io(&mut r, &mut w, &answer).await;
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// a service with no state of its own
    struct Nil;
    impl Service for Nil {
        fn admit(&self, _: &SocketAddr) -> Option<Box<dyn Send + Sync>> {
            None
        }
        fn keep_alive(&self, _: &SocketAddr) -> Duration {
            Duration::ZERO
        }
        async fn request<'a>(&'a self, _req: Request, _res: &'a mut Response) {}
        async fn expectation<'a>(&'a self, _req: Request, _res: &'a mut Response) {}
        async fn upgrade(&self, _req: Request, _up: Upgraded) {}
        fn client_error(&self, _: ClientError) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
            None
        }
    }

    /// What every connection's task holds for as long as it lives, besides the service's own futures: an array kept
    /// across an await, or a handshake's rustls state, would be part of it on every connection, the idle ones' too
    /// (the refusal's 4 KiB read buffer and the handshake made it 6 KiB; idle keep-alive connections come by the
    /// thousand)
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_connections_future_holds_no_buffer() {
        let l = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.expect("bind");
        let c = TcpStream::connect(l.local_addr().expect("addr")).await.expect("connect");
        let (s, peer) = l.accept().await.expect("accept");
        let f = connection(Accepted::Tcp(s), peer, None, Arc::new(Limits::default()), &Nil, Instant::now(), Hold::none());
        let size = std::mem::size_of_val(&f);
        assert!(size < 4096, "{size} bytes");
        drop((f, c));
    }
}

//! The request parser: what llhttp 9.3 (Node 24's parser, strict: no lenient flags, the Node server set none) accepts
//! and refuses, so that a request Node answered 400 is answered 400 here and one it served is read the same way.
//! It reads the bytes as they come (a state per byte, nothing read twice), keeps what Node keeps (the URL, the header
//! names and values) and counts toward `max_header_size` what Node counts: the URL, the names, and the values with
//! their trailing whitespace, but not the method, the version, separators or a value's leading whitespace.
//!
//! The rules, as Node 24 applies them (each was checked against it, tests/cross_node.rs):
//! - a method llhttp knows (RTSP ones only with RTSP/x.y), one or more spaces, a URL of llhttp's strict characters
//!   (origin form, `*`, or `scheme://authority...`), spaces, `HTTP/`, `RTSP/` or `ICE/`, a version of 0.9, 1.0, 1.1
//!   or 2.0, CRLF; a URL followed by the line end is an HTTP/0.9 request (headers still follow)
//! - `PRI` is only ever the HTTP/2 preface: a 400 either way
//! - header lines end in CRLF (a bare LF or CR is a 400), names are tokens followed at once by `:`, values are
//!   tab, space, visible ASCII or obs-text; a line that starts with whitespace (obsolete folding) is a 400
//! - Content-Length: digits and trailing spaces, once, never with Transfer-Encoding; Transfer-Encoding: chunked only
//!   as the last coding, once (a request whose last coding is not chunked is read, then answered 400)
//! - chunk sizes in hex, extensions as tokens or quoted strings, CRLF everywhere, trailers as header lines

const M_GET: u8 = 1;
const M_POST: u8 = 3;
const M_CONNECT: u8 = 5;
const M_OPTIONS: u8 = 6;
const M_SOURCE: u8 = 33;
const M_PRI: u8 = 34;
const M_QUERY: u8 = 46;
/// the longest method name ("GET_PARAMETER")
const METHOD_MAX: usize = 13;

/// methods llhttp takes with HTTP/x.y
fn http_method(m: u8) -> bool {
    m <= M_PRI || m == M_QUERY
}
/// with RTSP/x.y (the RTSP ones, and GET and POST for AirPlay)
fn rtsp_method(m: u8) -> bool {
    (35..=45).contains(&m) || m == M_OPTIONS || m == M_GET || m == M_POST
}

/// Node keeps the first 1000 header lines of a request (MAX_HEADER_PAIRS: 2000 names and values); the others are
/// read and checked, and dropped.
pub(crate) const HEADER_LINES_KEPT: usize = 1000;
/// Node's limit on one chunk's extensions (kMaxChunkExtensionsSize): more is a 400
const CHUNK_EXTENSIONS_MAX: usize = 16 << 10;

// ---- character classes (llhttp's) ----
fn tchar(b: u8) -> bool {
    b.is_ascii_alphanumeric()
        || matches!(b, b'!' | b'#' | b'$' | b'%' | b'&' | b'\'' | b'*' | b'+' | b'-' | b'.' | b'^' | b'_' | b'`' | b'|' | b'~')
}
/// STRICT_URL_CHAR: visible ASCII but `#` and `?` (which start a fragment or a query)
fn url_char(b: u8) -> bool {
    (0x21..=0x7e).contains(&b) && b != b'#' && b != b'?'
}
/// USERINFO_CHARS, and the brackets and `@` an authority may hold
fn server_char(b: u8) -> bool {
    b.is_ascii_alphanumeric()
        || matches!(
            b,
            b'-' | b'_'
                | b'.'
                | b'!'
                | b'~'
                | b'*'
                | b'\''
                | b'('
                | b')'
                | b'%'
                | b';'
                | b':'
                | b'&'
                | b'='
                | b'+'
                | b'$'
                | b','
                | b'['
                | b']'
                | b'@'
        )
}
/// a header value's characters: tab, space, visible ASCII, obs-text
fn value_char(b: u8) -> bool {
    b == b'\t' || (0x20..=0x7e).contains(&b) || b >= 0x80
}
/// inside a quoted chunk extension (qdtext)
fn qdtext(b: u8) -> bool {
    b == b'\t' || b == b' ' || b == 0x21 || (0x23..=0x5b).contains(&b) || (0x5d..=0x7e).contains(&b) || b >= 0x80
}
fn hex(b: u8) -> Option<u64> {
    (b as char).to_digit(16).map(u64::from)
}

// llhttp's flags

/// The headers llhttp reads itself.
#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
enum Special {
    None,
    Connection,
    ContentLength,
    TransferEncoding,
    Upgrade,
}

fn special(name: &[u8]) -> Special {
    let is = |s: &str| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(s.as_bytes());
    match name.len() {
        7 if is("upgrade") => Special::Upgrade,
        10 if is("connection") => Special::Connection,
        14 if is("content-length") => Special::ContentLength,
        16 if is("proxy-connection") => Special::Connection,
        17 if is("transfer-encoding") => Special::TransferEncoding,
        _ => Special::None,
    }
}

/// A request's head, as Node's parser hands it to the server.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Head {
    pub method: u8,
    pub url: String,
    pub major: u8,
    pub minor: u8,
    pub headers: Headers,
    /// llhttp's `should_keep_alive` at the end of the head (the answer's Connection header)
    pub keep_alive: bool,
    /// Connection: upgrade with an Upgrade header: the rest of the connection is not HTTP
    pub upgrade: bool,
    /// CONNECT (Node has no listener for it: the connection goes at once)

}

impl Head {

    }
}

/// What the parser found in the bytes it was given.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub(crate) enum Event {
    /// all of it read: more is needed
    More,
    /// a request begins (its first byte; Node's header and request times count from here)
    Begin,
    Head(Box<Head>),
    /// body bytes: the last `len` of the bytes consumed
    Body(usize),
    /// the request (and its body) is complete
    End,
    Error(ClientError),
}

pub(crate) struct Parser {
    max_header: usize,
    st: St,
    trailers: bool,
    method: u8,
    mlen: usize,
    mbuf: [u8; METHOD_MAX],
    proto: u8,

    major: u8,
    minor: u8,

    hbuf: Vec<u8>,

    fields: Vec<[u32; 4]>,
    /// the line being read is one Node keeps
    keep_line: bool,
    lines: usize,
    name_start: usize,

    /// for the trailers)
    counted: usize,
    flags: u16,
    special: Special,

    te: Te,
    /// the value of the line has started (it is not empty)
    value_seen: bool,

    chunk_digits: bool,

}

/// a head's URL, names and values (a browser's: a few hundred bytes), and its lines, to start with
const HEAD_BUFFER: usize = 512;
const FIELDS: usize = 16;
/// what an idle connection's parser keeps of what a larger head grew (Cloudflare's heads, with its own headers,
/// are 1-2 KiB)
const IDLE_HEAD_BUFFER: usize = 4096;
const IDLE_FIELDS: usize = 64;

const PRI_PREFACE: &[u8] = b"\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n";
const PROTOS: [&[u8]; 3] = [b"HTTP/", b"RTSP/", b"ICE/"];

impl Parser {
    pub fn new(max_header: usize) -> Self {
        Parser {
            max_header,
            st: St::Start,
            trailers: false,
            method: 0,
            mlen: 0,
            mbuf: [0; METHOD_MAX],
            proto: 0,
            k: 0,
            major: 0,
            minor: 0,
            hbuf: Vec::with_capacity(HEAD_BUFFER),
            url_end: 0,
            fields: Vec::with_capacity(FIELDS),
            keep_line: false,
            lines: 0,
            name_start: 0,
            value_start: 0,
            counted: 0,
            flags: 0,
            special: Special::None,
            cl: Cl::First,
            te: Te::Start(0),
            value_seen: false,
            content_length: 0,
            remaining: 0,
            chunk_digits: false,
            ext_bytes: 0,
        }
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    fn held(&self) -> (usize, usize) {
        (self.hbuf.capacity(), self.fields.capacity())
    }

    /// the parser stopped for good (an upgrade, CONNECT, an error): what follows is not its to read
    pub fn stopped(&self) -> bool {
        self.st == St::Stopped
    }

    /// an event is due without another byte (the end of a request without a body, or its refusal)
    pub fn pending(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.st, St::EndNext | St::FailNext)
    }

    /// between requests: the last one was read to its end, the next has not begun
    pub fn between(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self.st, St::Start | St::Closed)
    }

    /// The client ended its side: an error if a request was under way (llhttp's "Invalid EOF state").
    pub fn eof_error(&self) -> Option<ClientError> {
        match self.st {
            St::Start | St::Closed | St::Stopped => None,
            _ => Some(ClientError::Parse),
        }
    }

    /// The parser stops: nothing more is read (an upgrade's head, a timeout).
    pub fn stop(&mut self) {
        self.st = St::Stopped;
    }

    /// Between requests (the connection waits for the next): the buffers a large head grew are let go, so that an
    /// idle keep-alive connection holds what a usual head needs, not the 16 KiB of the largest it ever read.
    pub fn idle(&mut self) {
        if !self.between() {
            return;
        }
        if self.hbuf.capacity() > IDLE_HEAD_BUFFER {
            self.hbuf = Vec::with_capacity(HEAD_BUFFER);
        }
        if self.fields.capacity() > IDLE_FIELDS {
            self.fields = Vec::with_capacity(FIELDS);
        }
    }

    fn fail(&mut self, e: ClientError) -> Event {
        self.st = St::Stopped;
        Event::Error(e)
    }

    /// one more byte toward max_header_size: Node refuses a head at max_header_size counted bytes
    #[inline]
    fn count(&mut self) -> bool {
        self.counted += 1;
        self.counted >= self.max_header
    }

    /// Reads from `input`: (bytes consumed, what was found).  Call again with what is left until it says `More`.
    pub fn parse(&mut self, input: &[u8]) -> (usize, Event) {
        let mut i = 0;
        // states that hand out an event without a byte
        match self.st {
            St::EndNext => {
                self.st = self.after_message();
                return (0, Event::End);
            }
            St::FailNext => return (0, self.fail(ClientError::Parse)),
            // (never called then: what follows is not the parser's)
            St::Stopped => return (0, Event::More),
            St::Body => return self.body(input),
            St::ChunkData => return self.chunk_data(input),
            _ => {}
        }
        while i < input.len() {
            // the common runs at once: a header value, a path or query, a header name (each byte as the state's
            // own rule would take it, nothing else)
            let run = match self.st {
                St::Value if self.special == Special::None => run_of(&input[i..], value_char),
                St::Url(Url::Path) => run_of(&input[i..], url_char),
                St::Url(Url::Query) => run_of(&input[i..], |b| url_char(b) || b == b'?'),
                St::Name => run_of(&input[i..], tchar),
                _ => 0,
            };
            if run > 0 {
                self.hbuf.extend_from_slice(&input[i..i + run]);
                self.counted += run;
                i += run;
                if self.counted >= self.max_header {
                    return (i, self.fail(ClientError::HeaderOverflow));
                }
                continue;
            }
            let b = input[i];
            i += 1;
            match self.st {
                St::Start => {
                    if b == b'\r' || b == b'\n' {
                        continue;
                    }
                    self.begin();
                    self.st = St::Method;
                    i -= 1;
                    return (i, Event::Begin);
                }
                St::Closed => {
                    if b == b'\r' || b == b'\n' {
                        continue;
                    }
                    // llhttp: "Data after `Connection: close`"
                    return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                }
                St::Method => {
                    if b == b' ' && self.mlen > 0 {
                        match METHODS.iter().position(|m| m.as_bytes() == &self.mbuf[..self.mlen]) {
                            Some(m) => {
                                self.method = m as u8;
                                self.st = St::SpacesBeforeUrl;
                            }
                            None => return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse)),
                        }
                        continue;
                    }
                    if self.mlen == METHOD_MAX {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    self.mbuf[self.mlen] = b;
                    self.mlen += 1;
                    let prefix = &self.mbuf[..self.mlen];
                    if !METHODS.iter().any(|m| m.as_bytes().starts_with(prefix)) {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                }
                St::SpacesBeforeUrl => {
                    if b == b' ' {
                        continue;
                    }
                    // CONNECT's target is an authority (host:port)
                    self.st = St::Url(if self.method == M_CONNECT { Url::Server } else { Url::Start });
                    i -= 1;
                }
                St::Url(u) => {
                    let next = match (u, b) {
                        (_, b' ') if !matches!(u, Url::Start | Url::Schema | Url::Slash1 | Url::Slash2) => {
                            self.url_end = self.hbuf.len();
                            self.st = St::SpacesAfterUrl;
                            continue;
                        }
                        (_, b'\r' | b'\n') if !matches!(u, Url::Start | Url::Schema | Url::Slash1 | Url::Slash2) => {
                            // HTTP/0.9: the line ends after the URL; headers still follow
                            self.url_end = self.hbuf.len();
                            self.major = 0;
                            self.minor = 9;
                            self.st = if b == b'\r' { St::Url09Lf } else { St::LineStart };
                            continue;
                        }
                        (Url::Start, b'/' | b'*') => Url::Path,
                        (Url::Start, b) if b.is_ascii_alphabetic() => Url::Schema,
                        (Url::Schema, b) if b.is_ascii_alphabetic() => Url::Schema,
                        (Url::Schema, b':') => Url::Slash1,
                        (Url::Slash1, b'/') => Url::Slash2,
                        (Url::Slash2, b'/') => Url::Server,
                        (Url::Server, b'/') => Url::Path,
                        (Url::Server, b'?') => Url::Query,
                        (Url::Server, b) if server_char(b) => Url::Server,
                        (Url::Path, b'?') => Url::Query,
                        (Url::Path, b'#') => Url::Fragment,
                        (Url::Path, b) if url_char(b) => Url::Path,
                        (Url::Query, b'#') => Url::Fragment,
                        (Url::Query, b) if url_char(b) || b == b'?' => Url::Query,
                        (Url::Fragment, b) if url_char(b) || b == b'?' || b == b'#' => Url::Fragment,
                        _ => return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse)),
                    };
                    self.hbuf.push(b);
                    self.st = St::Url(next);
                    if self.count() {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::HeaderOverflow));
                    }
                }
                St::Url09Lf => {
                    if b != b'\n' {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    self.st = St::LineStart;
                }
                St::SpacesAfterUrl => {
                    if b == b' ' {
                        continue;
                    }
                    match PROTOS.iter().position(|p| p[0] == b) {
                        Some(p) => {
                            self.proto = p as u8;
                            self.k = 1;
                            self.st = St::Proto;
                        }
                        None => return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse)),
                    }
                }
                St::Proto => {
                    let p = PROTOS[self.proto as usize];
                    if b != p[self.k as usize] {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    self.k += 1;
                    if self.k as usize == p.len() {
                        let ok = match self.proto {
                            0 => http_method(self.method),
                            1 => rtsp_method(self.method),
                            _ => self.method == M_SOURCE,
                        };
                        if !ok {
                            return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                        }
                        self.st = St::Major;
                    }
                }
                St::Major => match b {
                    b'0'..=b'9' => {
                        self.major = b - b'0';
                        self.st = St::Dot;
                    }
                    _ => return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse)),
                },
                St::Dot => {
                    if b != b'.' {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    self.st = St::Minor;
                }
                St::Minor => {
                    if !b.is_ascii_digit() {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    self.minor = b - b'0';
                    if !matches!((self.major, self.minor), (0, 9) | (1, 0) | (1, 1) | (2, 0)) {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    if self.method == M_PRI {
                        self.k = 0;
                        self.st = St::Pri;
                    } else {
                        self.st = St::LineCr;
                    }
                }
                St::Pri => {
                    // the HTTP/2 preface, or not: Node answers 400 to both (HPE_PAUSED_H2_UPGRADE, HPE_INVALID_VERSION)
                    if b != PRI_PREFACE[self.k as usize] {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    self.k += 1;
                    if self.k as usize == PRI_PREFACE.len() {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                }
                St::LineCr => {
                    if b != b'\r' {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    self.st = St::LineLf;
                }
                St::LineLf => {
                    if b != b'\n' {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    self.st = St::LineStart;
                }
                St::LineStart => {
                    if b == b'\r' {
                        self.st = St::HeadLf;
                    } else if tchar(b) {
                        // every line is kept for llhttp's own reading of it (what is kept is counted, so it stays
                        // under max_header_size); Node hands the server only the first ones
                        self.keep_line = !self.trailers && self.lines < HEADER_LINES_KEPT;
                        self.lines += 1;
                        self.name_start = self.hbuf.len();
                        self.hbuf.push(b);
                        self.st = St::Name;
                        if self.count() {
                            return (i, self.fail(ClientError::HeaderOverflow));
                        }
                    } else {
                        // a bare LF, obsolete line folding (a line that starts with whitespace), anything else
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                }
                St::Name => {
                    if tchar(b) {
                        self.hbuf.push(b);
                        if self.count() {
                            return (i, self.fail(ClientError::HeaderOverflow));
                        }
                    } else if b == b':' {
                        if let Some(e) = self.name_done() {
                            return (i, self.fail(e));
                        }
                        self.st = St::ValueOws;
                    } else {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                }
                St::ValueOws => {
                    if b == b' ' || b == b'\t' {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if b == b'\r' {
                        if self.special == Special::ContentLength {
                            // llhttp: "Empty Content-Length"
                            return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                        }
                        self.st = St::ValueLf;
                        continue;
                    }
                    if !value_char(b) {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    if let Some(e) = self.value_starts() {
                        return (i, self.fail(e));
                    }
                    self.st = St::Value;
                    i -= 1;
                }
                St::Value => {
                    if b == b'\r' {
                        if let Some(e) = self.value_ends() {
                            return (i, self.fail(e));
                        }
                        self.st = St::ValueLf;
                        continue;
                    }
                    if !value_char(b) {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    if let Some(e) = self.special_byte(b) {
                        return (i, self.fail(e));
                    }
                    self.hbuf.push(b);
                    if self.count() {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::HeaderOverflow));
                    }
                }
                St::ValueLf => {
                    if b != b'\n' {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    self.line_done();
                    self.st = St::LineStart;
                }
                St::HeadLf => {
                    if b != b'\n' {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    if self.trailers {
                        self.st = self.after_message();
                        return (i, Event::End);
                    }
                    return (i, self.head_done());
                }
                St::ChunkSize => {
                    if let Some(d) = hex(b) {
                        if self.remaining > u64::MAX >> 4 {
                            return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                        }
                        self.remaining = self.remaining << 4 | d;
                        self.chunk_digits = true;
                    } else if self.chunk_digits && b == b';' {
                        self.st = St::ChunkExt(Ext::Name(true));
                    } else if self.chunk_digits && b == b'\r' {
                        self.st = St::ChunkSizeLf;
                    } else {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                }
                St::ChunkSizeLf => {
                    if b != b'\n' {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    // Node resets its header count at each chunk size (the trailers count from here)
                    self.counted = 0;
                    if self.remaining == 0 {
                        self.trailers = true;
                        self.st = St::LineStart;
                    } else {
                        // the data is handed out in runs, not bytes
                        self.st = St::ChunkData;
                        let (n, e) = self.chunk_data(&input[i..]);
                        return (i + n, e);
                    }
                }
                St::ChunkExt(x) => {
                    let next = match (x, b) {
                        (Ext::Name(true), b'\r') => return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse)),
                        (Ext::Name(_), b) if tchar(b) => Ext::Name(false),
                        (Ext::Name(_), b'=') => Ext::ValueStart,
                        (Ext::Name(_), b';') => Ext::Name(true),
                        (Ext::ValueStart, b'"') => Ext::Quoted,
                        (Ext::ValueStart | Ext::Value, b) if tchar(b) => Ext::Value,
                        (Ext::ValueStart | Ext::Value | Ext::QuotedEnd, b';') => Ext::Name(true),
                        (Ext::Quoted, b'"') => Ext::QuotedEnd,
                        (Ext::Quoted, b'\\') => Ext::QuotedPair,
                        (Ext::Quoted, b) if qdtext(b) => Ext::Quoted,
                        (Ext::QuotedPair, b) if b == b'\t' || b == b' ' || (0x21..=0x7e).contains(&b) || b >= 0x80 => Ext::Quoted,
                        (Ext::Name(false) | Ext::ValueStart | Ext::Value | Ext::QuotedEnd, b'\r') => {
                            self.st = St::ChunkSizeLf;
                            continue;
                        }
                        _ => return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse)),
                    };
                    if b != b'=' && b != b';' {
                        self.ext_bytes += 1;
                        if self.ext_bytes > CHUNK_EXTENSIONS_MAX {
                            return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                        }
                    }
                    self.st = St::ChunkExt(next);
                }
                St::ChunkDataCr => {
                    if b != b'\r' {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    self.st = St::ChunkDataLf;
                }
                St::ChunkDataLf => {
                    if b != b'\n' {
                        return (i, self.fail(ClientError::Parse));
                    }
                    self.chunk_start();
                }
                St::EndNext | St::FailNext | St::Stopped | St::Body | St::ChunkData => unreachable!(),
            }
        }
        (i, Event::More)
    }

    /// a request starts: what the last one left is cleared
    fn begin(&mut self) {
        self.trailers = false;
        self.counted = 0;
        self.mlen = 0;
        self.hbuf.clear();
        self.fields.clear();
        self.url_end = 0;
        self.lines = 0;
        self.flags = 0;
        self.content_length = 0;
        self.major = 1;
        self.minor = 1;
    }

    fn chunk_start(&mut self) {
        self.remaining = 0;
        self.chunk_digits = false;
        self.ext_bytes = 0;
        self.st = St::ChunkSize;
    }

    /// llhttp's should_keep_alive: HTTP/1.1 unless Connection: close; earlier ones only with Connection: keep-alive
    fn keep_alive(&self) -> bool {
        if self.major > 0 && self.minor > 0 { self.flags & F_CONNECTION_CLOSE == 0 } else { self.flags & F_CONNECTION_KEEP_ALIVE != 0 }
    }

    /// where the parser goes once a request is complete (by the flags then, trailers included)
    fn after_message(&self) -> St {
        if self.keep_alive() { St::Start } else { St::Closed }
    }

    /// A header name ended (at its colon): what llhttp checks there.
    fn name_done(&mut self) -> Option<ClientError> {
        self.special = special(&self.hbuf[self.name_start..]);
        self.value_seen = false;
        self.value_start = self.hbuf.len();
        match self.special {
            Special::TransferEncoding if self.flags & F_CONTENT_LENGTH != 0 => return Some(ClientError::Parse),
            // a second Content-Length (even the same), or one after Transfer-Encoding
            Special::ContentLength if self.flags & (F_CONTENT_LENGTH | F_TRANSFER_ENCODING) != 0 => return Some(ClientError::Parse),
            _ => {}
        }
        self.cl = Cl::First;
        self.te = Te::Start(0);
        None
    }

    /// The first byte of a value (after the whitespace llhttp drops).
    fn value_starts(&mut self) -> Option<ClientError> {
        self.value_seen = true;
        match self.special {
            Special::TransferEncoding => {
                // after chunked, no other coding (llhttp strict)
                if self.flags & F_CHUNKED != 0 {
                    return Some(ClientError::Parse);
                }
                self.flags |= F_TRANSFER_ENCODING;
            }
            Special::Upgrade => self.flags |= F_UPGRADE,
            _ => {}
        }
        None
    }

    /// A byte of a value, for the headers llhttp reads itself.
    fn special_byte(&mut self, b: u8) -> Option<ClientError> {
        match self.special {
            Special::ContentLength => match (self.cl, b) {
                (Cl::First | Cl::Digits, b'0'..=b'9') => {
                    let d = u64::from(b - b'0');
                    match self.content_length.checked_mul(10).and_then(|v| v.checked_add(d)) {
                        Some(v) => self.content_length = v,
                        None => return Some(ClientError::Parse),
                    }
                    self.cl = Cl::Digits;
                }
                (Cl::Digits | Cl::Spaces, b' ') => self.cl = Cl::Spaces,
                _ => return Some(ClientError::Parse),
            },
            Special::TransferEncoding => loop {
                match self.te {
                    Te::Start(k) => {
                        if b.to_ascii_lowercase() == b"chunked"[k as usize] {
                            self.te = if k == 6 { Te::ChunkedLast } else { Te::Start(k + 1) };
                            break;
                        }
                        self.te = Te::Token;
                    }
                    Te::ChunkedLast => {
                        if b == b' ' {
                            break;
                        }
                        if b == b',' {
                            // chunked followed by another coding
                            return Some(ClientError::Parse);
                        }
                        self.te = Te::Token;
                    }
                    Te::Token => {
                        if b == b',' {
                            self.te = Te::Ows;
                        }
                        break;
                    }
                    Te::Ows => {
                        if b == b' ' || b == b'\t' {
                            break;
                        }
                        self.te = Te::Start(0);
                    }
                }
            },
            _ => {}
        }
        None
    }

    /// The value ended (CR).
    fn value_ends(&mut self) -> Option<ClientError> {
        match self.special {
            Special::ContentLength => {
                if self.cl == Cl::First {
                    return Some(ClientError::Parse);
                }
                self.flags |= F_CONTENT_LENGTH;
            }
            Special::TransferEncoding => {
                if self.te == Te::ChunkedLast {
                    self.flags |= F_CHUNKED;
                }
            }
            Special::Connection => {
                let v = &self.hbuf[self.value_start..];
                self.flags |= connection_flags(v);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        None
    }

    /// A header line ended (CRLF).
    fn line_done(&mut self) {
        if self.keep_line {
            self.fields.push([self.name_start as u32, self.value_start as u32, self.value_start as u32, self.hbuf.len() as u32]);
        }
        self.special = Special::None;
    }

    /// The empty line: the head is complete.
    fn head_done(&mut self) -> Event {
        // Node resets its count at the end of each head
        self.counted = 0;
        let upgrade = (self.flags & F_UPGRADE != 0 && self.flags & F_CONNECTION_UPGRADE != 0) || self.method == M_CONNECT;
        let close = self.method == M_CONNECT;
        let body = if upgrade || close {
            BodyKind::None
        } else if self.flags & F_CHUNKED != 0 {
            BodyKind::Chunked
        } else if self.flags & F_CONTENT_LENGTH != 0 && self.content_length > 0 {
            BodyKind::Length(self.content_length)
        } else {
            BodyKind::None
        };
        let head = Box::new(Head {
            method: self.method,
            url: latin1(&self.hbuf[..self.url_end]),
            major: self.major,
            minor: self.minor,
            headers: crate::headers::join(self.fields.iter().map(|f| {
                let name = &self.hbuf[f[0] as usize..f[1] as usize];
                let mut value = &self.hbuf[f[2] as usize..f[3] as usize];
                // Node trims the value's trailing whitespace (llhttp already dropped the leading)
                while let [rest @ .., b' ' | b'\t'] = value {
                    value = rest;
                }
                (name, value)
            })),
            keep_alive: self.keep_alive(),
            upgrade: upgrade && !close,
            close,
            pri: self.method == M_PRI,
            body,
        });
        self.st = if upgrade || close {
            // what follows is another protocol (or nothing)
            St::Stopped
        } else {
            match body {
                BodyKind::Chunked => {
                    self.chunk_start();
                    St::ChunkSize
                }
                BodyKind::Length(n) => {
                    self.remaining = n;
                    St::Body
                }
                // a request with a Transfer-Encoding whose last coding is not chunked: llhttp hands the head to the
                // server, then refuses (RFC 9112 6.3: the length cannot be known)
                BodyKind::None if self.flags & F_TRANSFER_ENCODING != 0 => St::FailNext,
                BodyKind::None => St::EndNext,
            }
        };
        // the trailers (if any) are read for llhttp's flags, not kept
        self.hbuf.clear();
        self.fields.clear();
        Event::Head(head)
    }

    /// Content-Length body bytes.
    fn body(&mut self, input: &[u8]) -> (usize, Event) {
        if input.is_empty() {
            return (0, Event::More);
        }
        if self.remaining == 0 {
            self.st = self.after_message();
            return (0, Event::End);
        }
        let n = (self.remaining.min(input.len() as u64)) as usize;
        self.remaining -= n as u64;
        if self.remaining == 0 {
            self.st = St::EndNext;
        }
        (n, Event::Body(n))
    }

    /// Chunk data bytes.
    fn chunk_data(&mut self, input: &[u8]) -> (usize, Event) {
        if input.is_empty() {
            return (0, Event::More);
        }
        let n = (self.remaining.min(input.len() as u64)) as usize;
        self.remaining -= n as u64;
        if self.remaining == 0 {
            self.st = St::ChunkDataCr;
        }
        (n, Event::Body(n))
    }
}

/// how many bytes from the start `ok` takes
#[inline]
fn run_of(s: &[u8], ok: impl Fn(u8) -> bool) -> usize {
    s.iter().position(|&b| !ok(b)).unwrap_or(s.len())
}

/// The tokens of a Connection header as llhttp reads them: close, keep-alive or upgrade, each between commas, with
/// leading whitespace and trailing spaces (not tabs: llhttp's rule), case-insensitive.
pub(crate) fn connection_flags(v: &[u8]) -> u16 {
    let mut flags = 0;
    for token in v.split(|&b| b == b',') {
        let mut t = token;
        while let [b' ' | b'\t', rest @ ..] = t {
            t = rest;
        }
        while let [rest @ .., b' '] = t {
            t = rest;
        }
        if t.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"close") {
            flags |= F_CONNECTION_CLOSE;
        } else if t.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"keep-alive") {
            flags |= F_CONNECTION_KEEP_ALIVE;
        } else if t.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"upgrade") {
            flags |= F_CONNECTION_UPGRADE;
        }
    }
    flags
}

/// bytes as Node turns them into a string (latin1: one character per byte)
pub(crate) fn latin1(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    if b.is_ascii() {
        // ASCII: the bytes are the string
        return String::from_utf8(b.to_vec()).unwrap_or_default();
    }
    b.iter().map(|&c| c as char).collect()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// every event of a parse of `input` given in pieces of `step` bytes (body runs joined; what is left after the
    /// parser stopped as "rest")
    fn events(input: &[u8], step: usize, max: usize) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut p = Parser::new(max);
        let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        let mut buf: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
        for piece in input.chunks(step) {
            buf.extend_from_slice(piece);
            while !p.stopped() {
                let (n, e) = p.parse(&buf);
                let done = matches!(e, Event::More);
                match e {
                    Event::More => {}
                    Event::Begin => out.push("begin".into()),
                    Event::Head(h) => out.push(format!(
                        "head {} {} {}.{} {:?} ka={} up={} close={} {:?}",
                        h.method_str(),
                        h.url,
                        h.major,
                        h.minor,
                        h.headers.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
                        h.keep_alive,
                        h.upgrade,
                        h.close,
                        h.body
                    )),
                    Event::Body(len) => {
                        let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[n - len..n]).to_string();
                        match out.last_mut() {
                            Some(last) if last.starts_with("body ") => last.push_str(&s),
                            _ => out.push(format!("body {s}")),
                        }
                    }
                    Event::End => out.push("end".into()),
                    Event::Error(e) => out.push(format!("error {e:?}")),
                }
                buf.drain(..n);
                if done {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        if p.stopped() && !buf.is_empty() {
            out.push(format!("rest {}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf)));
        }
        out
    }

    fn all_steps(input: &[u8]) -> Vec<String> {
        let whole = events(input, input.len().max(1), 16 << 10);
        for step in [1, 2, 3, 7] {
            assert_eq!(events(input, step, 16 << 10), whole, "in pieces of {step}: {:?}", String::from_utf8_lossy(input));
        }
        whole
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_simple_request() {
        let e = all_steps(b"GET /a?b HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nX-A:  1 \r\n\r\n");
        assert_eq!(e, vec!["begin", "head GET /a?b 1.1 [(\"host\", \"x\"), (\"x-a\", \"1\")] ka=true up=false close=false None", "end"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn bodies_with_a_length_and_chunked() {
        let e = all_steps(b"POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 3\r\n\r\nabcGET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n");
        assert_eq!(e[1], "head POST / 1.1 [(\"content-length\", \"3\")] ka=true up=false close=false Length(3)");
        assert_eq!(e[2], "body abc");
        assert!(e.contains(&"head GET / 1.0 [] ka=false up=false close=false None".to_string()));
        let e = all_steps(b"POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nTransfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked\r\n\r\n3;a=\"b;c\"\r\nabc\r\n2\r\nde\r\n0\r\nT: 1\r\n\r\n");
        assert_eq!(e[2], "body abcde");
        assert_eq!(e.last().map(String::as_str), Some("end"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn what_node_refuses() {
        for bad in [
            &b"get / HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n"[..],
            b"FOO / HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n",
            b"DESCRIBE / HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n",
            b"GET / HTTP/1.1\n\n",
            b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: a\n\r\n",
            b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost : a\r\n\r\n",
            b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nX: a\r\n b\r\n\r\n",
            b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\n",
            b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n",
            b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked, gzip\r\n\r\n",
            b"GET /\x7f HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n",
            b"GET / HTTP/1.2\r\n\r\n",
            b"PRI * HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n",
            b"POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n3 \r\nabc\r\n0\r\n\r\n",
        ] {
            let e = all_steps(bad);
            assert!(e.iter().any(|x| x == "error Parse"), "{:?}: {e:?}", String::from_utf8_lossy(bad));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_coding_other_than_chunked_last_is_refused_after_the_head() {
        let e = all_steps(b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nTransfer-Encoding: gzip\r\n\r\n");
        assert!(e[1].starts_with("head GET"));
        assert_eq!(e[2], "error Parse");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_header_limit_counts_what_node_counts() {
        // URL 1 + name 1 + value 197 = 199 < 200; one more (even a trailing space) is 200
        let ok = format!("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nX:   {}\r\n\r\n", "a".repeat(197));
        assert!(events(ok.as_bytes(), 5, 200).iter().any(|x| x.starts_with("head")));
        let over = format!("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nX: {} \r\n\r\n", "a".repeat(197));
        assert!(events(over.as_bytes(), 5, 200).contains(&"error HeaderOverflow".to_string()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_idle_parser_lets_go_of_what_a_large_head_grew() {
        let pad: String = (0..400).map(|i| format!("X-{i}: {}\r\n", "v".repeat(30))).collect();
        let big = format!("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n{pad}\r\n");
        let mut p = Parser::new(16 << 10);
        // half of it: in the middle of a head nothing is let go
        let half = big.len() / 2;
        assert!(matches!(p.parse(&big.as_bytes()[..half]), (0, Event::Begin)));
        assert!(matches!(p.parse(&big.as_bytes()[..half]), (n, Event::More) if n == half));
        let mid = p.held();
        p.idle();
        assert_eq!(p.held(), mid);
        let (_, e) = p.parse(&big.as_bytes()[half..]);
        assert!(matches!(e, Event::Head(_)), "{e:?}");
        assert!(matches!(p.parse(&[]), (0, Event::End)));
        assert!(p.held().0 > IDLE_HEAD_BUFFER && p.held().1 > IDLE_FIELDS, "{:?}", p.held());
        p.idle();
        assert!(p.held().0 <= IDLE_HEAD_BUFFER && p.held().1 <= IDLE_FIELDS, "{:?}", p.held());
        // and it reads the next one as ever
        let (_, e) = p.parse(b"GET /b HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n");
        assert!(matches!(e, Event::Begin));
    }

    #[test]
    fn upgrade_stops_and_leaves_the_rest() {
        let e = all_steps(b"GET /lan HTTP/1.1\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nContent-Length: 2\r\n\r\nxyz");
        assert!(e[1].contains("up=true"));
        assert_eq!(e.last().map(String::as_str), Some("rest xyz"));
    }

    /// the methods Node lists (http.METHODS) are exactly those llhttp takes with HTTP/x.y, PRI aside
    #[test]
    fn methods_as_node_lists_them() {
        let Some(out) = crate::node::run("import http from 'node:http'; process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(http.METHODS));", "") else {
            eprintln!("skipped: no node to compare with");
            return;
        };
        let want: Vec<String> = serde_json::from_str(&out).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut got: Vec<String> =
            (0..METHODS.len() as u8).filter(|&m| http_method(m) && m != M_PRI).map(|m| METHODS[m as usize].to_string()).collect();
        got.sort();
        assert_eq!(got, want);
    }

    #[test]
    fn connection_tokens() {
        assert_eq!(connection_flags(b"close"), F_CONNECTION_CLOSE);
        assert_eq!(connection_flags(b"x, Keep-Alive "), F_CONNECTION_KEEP_ALIVE);
        assert_eq!(connection_flags(b"close\t"), 0);
        assert_eq!(connection_flags(b"closed"), 0);
        assert_eq!(connection_flags(b"x,, close"), F_CONNECTION_CLOSE);
        assert_eq!(connection_flags(b"Upgrade, HTTP2-Settings"), F_CONNECTION_UPGRADE);
    }
}
