#[tokio::test]
async fn bodies_up_to_a_limit() {
    let (addr, _) = engine(short(), Duration::from_secs(65)).await;
    let ok = exchange(addr, &Case::new("POST /small HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 4\r\n\r\nabcd")).await;
    assert!(ok.text.ends_with("\r\n\r\nabcd\n"), "{ok:?}");
    let big = exchange(addr, &Case::new("POST /small HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nabcde")).await;
    assert!(big.text.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large\r\n") && big.closed, "{big:?}");
    let chunked =
        exchange(addr, &Case::new("POST /small HTTP/1.1\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n3\r\nabc\r\n3\r\ndef\r\n0\r\n\r\n")).await;
    assert!(chunked.text.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 413 ") && chunked.closed, "{chunked:?}");
    let in_bits = exchange(
        addr,
        &Case {
            parts: vec![b"POST /small HTTP/1.1\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n2\r\nab\r\n".to_vec(), b"1\r\nc\r\n0\r\n\r\n".to_vec()],
            gap: Duration::from_millis(100),
            end: false,
            wait: Duration::from_millis(600),
        },
    )
    .await;
    assert!(in_bits.text.ends_with("\r\n\r\nabc\n"), "{in_bits:?}");
}

//! What an idle keep-alive connection holds (thousands of them sit idle between a page's requests, for 65 s, or
//! 905 s for Cloudflare's): the bytes allocated, counted by a global allocator of this test's own, after one exchange
//! of a few bytes each way and after one with a head and an answer just under 16 KiB.  (A connection kept the buffers
//! its largest exchange had grown, its parser's for the head and its answer's for the head and a body written with
//! it, for as long as it lived: about 32 KiB each, for whoever sends one large head on each of its connections.)

mod common;

use std::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout, System};
use std::net::SocketAddr;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicIsize, Ordering::Relaxed};
use std::time::Duration;

use common::TestService;
use nfsu2_http::Limits;
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};
use tokio::net::TcpStream;

/// bytes allocated now, in this test binary
static LIVE: AtomicIsize = AtomicIsize::new(0);

struct Counting;

// SAFETY: every call goes to the system allocator as it came; only the count is added
unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for Counting {
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, l: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        let p = unsafe { System.alloc(l) };
        if !p.is_null() {
            LIVE.fetch_add(l.size() as isize, Relaxed);
        }
        p
    }
    unsafe fn alloc_zeroed(&self, l: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        let p = unsafe { System.alloc_zeroed(l) };
        if !p.is_null() {
            LIVE.fetch_add(l.size() as isize, Relaxed);
        }
        p
    }
    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, p: *mut u8, l: Layout) {
        unsafe { System.dealloc(p, l) };
        LIVE.fetch_sub(l.size() as isize, Relaxed);
    }
    unsafe fn realloc(&self, p: *mut u8, l: Layout, new: usize) -> *mut u8 {
        let q = unsafe { System.realloc(p, l, new) };
        if !q.is_null() {
            LIVE.fetch_add(new as isize - l.size() as isize, Relaxed);
        }
        q
    }
}

#[global_allocator]
static ALLOC: Counting = Counting;

/// an answer's whole length once its head is in: the head and its Content-Length
fn answer_len(b: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    let end = b.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n")?;
    let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..end]).to_ascii_lowercase();
    let len: usize = head.split("content-length: ").nth(1).and_then(|r| r.split("\r\n").next()).and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
    Some(end + 4 + len)
}

/// `n` connections, each one request (a head of about `head` bytes) and its answer (`body` bytes in one write, so
/// that the head and the body go out together), then all of them idle: the bytes allocated per connection
async fn held(addr: SocketAddr, n: usize, head: usize, body: usize) -> f64 {
    let pad: String = (0..head / 1000).map(|i| format!("X-Pad-{i:02}: {}\r\n", "p".repeat(990))).collect();
    let req = format!("GET /huge?{body} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n{pad}\r\n");
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; 64 << 10];
    let mut conns = Vec::with_capacity(n);
    let before = LIVE.load(Relaxed);
    for _ in 0..n {
        let mut s = TcpStream::connect(addr).await.expect("connect");
        s.write_all(req.as_bytes()).await.expect("write");
        let (mut got, mut want) = (0usize, usize::MAX);
        while got < want {
            let k = s.read(&mut buf[got..]).await.expect("read");
            assert!(k > 0, "closed");
            got += k;
            if want == usize::MAX {
                want = answer_len(&buf[..got]).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
            }
        }
        conns.push(s);
    }
    // (the connections' tasks reach their wait for the next request)
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
    let per = (LIVE.load(Relaxed) - before) as f64 / n as f64;
    drop(conns);
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
    per
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn an_idle_connection_keeps_no_buffer_its_last_exchange_grew() {
    let n = 300;
    let addr = common::start(Limits { max_connections: 4 * n, ..Limits::default() }, TestService::new(Duration::from_secs(65))).await;
    let small = held(addr, n, 0, 100).await;
    let large = held(addr, n, 15_000, 15_000).await;
    eprintln!("an idle connection holds {small:.0} bytes after a small exchange, {large:.0} after a large one");
    assert!(large - small < 4096.0, "{:.0} bytes more after a large exchange", large - small);
}

// Node's http server with the rules the Node server set on it (LIMITS: its sizes, timeouts and keep-alive;
// onClientError, refuseSocket, onReq's pipelining count), and a test service: the reference the Rust engine is
// compared with (tests/cross_node.rs).  Every route answers the same bytes as the Rust tests' service
// (tests/common/mod.rs).
//   node ref_server.mjs '<json options>'     prints "listening <port>" once it is up (on 127.0.0.1, port 0)
import http from 'node:http';

const o = JSON.parse(process.argv[2] || '{}');
const LIMITS = {
  maxHeaderSize: o.maxHeaderSize ?? 16 << 10,
  headersTimeout: o.headersTimeout ?? 15_000,
  requestTimeout: o.requestTimeout ?? 30_000,
  keepAliveTimeout: o.keepAliveTimeout ?? 65_000,
  socketIdle: o.socketIdle ?? 120_000,
  maxConnections: o.maxConnections ?? 1024,
  pipelined: o.pipelined ?? 4,
  check: o.check ?? 5_000,
};
const STATUS = { 400: 'Bad Request', 408: 'Request Timeout', 431: 'Request Header Fields Too Large' };
const rawResponse = code => `HTTP/1.1 ${code} ${STATUS[code]}\r\ncontent-length: 0\r\nconnection: close\r\n\r\n`;
function refuseSocket(sock, code) {
  try { if (sock.writable) sock.end(rawResponse(code)); } catch { /* gone */ }
  setTimeout(() => sock.destroy(), 1000).unref();
}
const echo = q => JSON.stringify({ m: q.method, u: q.url, v: q.httpVersion, h: Object.entries(q.headers) });
function plain(q, s, code, text, extra = {}) {
  const body = text + '\n';
  s.writeHead(code, { 'content-type': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8', 'content-length': Buffer.byteLength(body), ...extra });
  s.end(q.method === 'HEAD' ? undefined : body);
}
const sleep = ms => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms));

async function handler(q, s) {
  const p = q.url.split('?')[0];
  if (p === '/chunked') { s.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'text/plain' }); s.write('hello'); await sleep(20); s.write(' world'); s.end(); return; }
  if (p === '/empty') { s.writeHead(200, { 'x-a': '1' }); s.end(); return; }
  if (p === '/204') { s.writeHead(204, { 'x-a': '1' }); s.end(); return; }
  if (p === '/304') { s.writeHead(304, { etag: '"e"' }); s.end(); return; }
  if (p === '/204te') { s.writeHead(204, { 'transfer-encoding': 'chunked' }); s.end(); return; }
  if (p === '/te') { s.writeHead(200, { 'transfer-encoding': 'chunked' }); s.write('ab'); s.end(); return; }
  if (p === '/close') { s.writeHead(200, { 'content-length': 2, connection: 'close' }); s.end('ok'); return; }
  if (p === '/keep') { s.writeHead(200, { 'content-length': 2, connection: 'keep-alive' }); s.end('ok'); return; }
  if (p === '/ka') { s.setHeader('Keep-Alive', 'timeout=7'); s.writeHead(200, { 'content-length': 2, 'x-b': '2', 'keep-alive': 'timeout=8' }); s.end('ok'); return; }
  if (p === '/ka2') { s.setHeader('Keep-Alive', 'timeout=7'); s.writeHead(200, { 'content-length': 2 }); s.end('ok'); return; }
  if (p === '/date') { s.writeHead(200, { date: 'yesterday', 'content-length': 2 }); s.end('ok'); return; }
  if (p === '/big') { const b = Buffer.alloc(200_000, 0x61); s.writeHead(200, { 'content-length': b.length }); s.end(b); return; }
  if (p === '/bigchunked') { s.writeHead(200, {}); s.write(Buffer.alloc(70_000, 0x62)); s.end(Buffer.alloc(10, 0x63)); return; }
  if (p === '/slow') { await sleep(150); plain(q, s, 200, 'slow'); return; }
  if (p.startsWith('/status/')) { s.writeHead(+p.slice(8), { 'content-length': 0 }); s.end(); return; }
  if (p === '/body') {
    const parts = [];
    for await (const c of q) parts.push(c);
    const b = Buffer.concat(parts);
    const body = JSON.stringify({ n: b.length, hex: b.toString('hex') });
    s.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'content-length': Buffer.byteLength(body) });
    s.end(body);
    return;
  }
  const body = echo(q);
  s.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'content-length': Buffer.byteLength(body) });
  s.end(q.method === 'HEAD' ? undefined : body);
}

const kQueued = Symbol('queued');
const onReq = (q, s) => {
  const conn = q.socket;
  conn[kQueued] = (conn[kQueued] ?? 0) + 1;
  if (conn[kQueued] > LIMITS.pipelined) return conn.destroy();
  let done = false;
  const finished = () => { if (!done) { done = true; conn[kQueued]--; } };
  s.once('finish', finished); s.once('close', finished);
  handler(q, s).catch(() => { try { if (!s.headersSent) plain(q, s, 500, 'Server error'); else s.destroy(); } catch { /* gone */ } });
};
function onClientError(e, sock) {
  const code = e?.code === 'HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW' ? 431 : e?.code === 'ERR_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT' ? 408
    : String(e?.code ?? '').startsWith('HPE_') ? 400 : 0;
  if (o.logErrors) console.log(`clientError ${e?.code} writable=${sock.writable}`);
  if (!code || !sock.writable) return sock.destroy();
  refuseSocket(sock, code);
}
function onUpgrade(q, sock, head) {
  sock.on('error', () => {});
  sock.end(`HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nx-up: ${echo(q)}\r\nx-pre: ${head.toString('hex')}\r\n\r\n`);
  setTimeout(() => sock.destroy(), 1000).unref();
}
const srv = http.createServer({ maxHeaderSize: LIMITS.maxHeaderSize, headersTimeout: LIMITS.headersTimeout, requestTimeout: LIMITS.requestTimeout,
  connectionsCheckingInterval: LIMITS.check, requireHostHeader: false }, onReq);
srv.keepAliveTimeout = LIMITS.keepAliveTimeout;
srv.maxConnections = LIMITS.maxConnections;
srv.setTimeout(LIMITS.socketIdle);
srv.on('clientError', onClientError);
srv.on('upgrade', onUpgrade);
srv.on('checkExpectation', (q, s) => plain(q, s, 417, 'Expectation failed', { connection: 'close' }));
srv.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => console.log(`listening ${srv.address().port}`));
process.on('SIGTERM', () => process.exit(0));

// Node's https server with the Node server's TLS rules (certNames, sniCallback, a default context only for a
// certificate that names an address, minVersion, handshakeTimeout, onClientError): the reference for how a handshake
// the server refuses looks on the wire (tests/tls.rs).
//   node tls_server.mjs <cert> <key>     prints "listening <port>" once it is up (on 127.0.0.1, port 0)
import https from 'node:https';
import tls from 'node:tls';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import crypto from 'node:crypto';

const [certFile, keyFile] = process.argv.slice(2);
const key = fs.readFileSync(keyFile), cert = fs.readFileSync(certFile);
const x = new crypto.X509Certificate(cert);
const dns = [], ips = [];
for (const part of String(x.subjectAltName ?? '').split(/,\s*/)) {
  if (part.startsWith('DNS:')) dns.push(part.slice(4).toLowerCase());
  else if (part.startsWith('IP Address:')) ips.push(part.slice(11));
}
const certCtx = tls.createSecureContext({ key, cert, minVersion: 'TLSv1.2' });
const sniMatch = (name, list) => list.some(d => d === name || (d.startsWith('*.') && name.endsWith(d.slice(1)) && !name.slice(0, -(d.length - 1)).includes('.')));
function sniCallback(servername, cb) {
  const n = String(servername ?? '').toLowerCase().replace(/\.$/, '');
  if (sniMatch(n, dns)) return cb(null, certCtx);
  cb(new Error('not a name of this server'));
}
const tlsFiles = { SNICallback: sniCallback, ...(ips.length ? { key, cert } : {}) };
const srv = https.createServer({ ...tlsFiles, minVersion: 'TLSv1.2', handshakeTimeout: 15_000 }, (q, s) => s.end('ok'));
// onClientError: no HTTP to answer a handshake with, the connection goes at once
srv.on('clientError', (e, sock) => sock.destroy());
srv.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => console.log(`listening ${srv.address().port}`));
process.on('SIGTERM', () => process.exit(0));

//! TLS: the certificate only for the names it covers (the audit's F4), for handshakes without a name only when it
//! names an address; its names (DNS names in lower case, addresses in their plain form); refused handshakes as
//! Node's https server refuses them; the key formats; a renewed certificate taken without a restart; a handshake that

mod common;

fn ssl(dir: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> bool {
    Command::new("openssl").args(args).current_dir(dir).output().map(|o| o.status.success()).unwrap_or(false)
}

struct Certs {
    _dir: tempfile::TempDir,
    dir: PathBuf,

impl Certs {
    /// cf-sim.mjs makeTestCerts (a CA, and a server certificate for localhost, nfsu2.test and 127.0.0.1), and
    /// audit.test.mjs's F4 certificate (game.test and *.wild.test, no address), and a few more
    fn make() -> Option<Certs> {

        let d = tmp.path().to_path_buf();

            && std::fs::write(d.join("server.ext"), "subjectAltName=DNS:localhost,DNS:nfsu2.test,IP:127.0.0.1\nbasicConstraints=CA:FALSE\nkeyUsage=critical,digitalSignature\nextendedKeyUsage=serverAuth\n").is_ok()

            && ssl(&d, &["x509", "-req", "-in", "server.csr", "-CA", "ca.crt", "-CAkey", "ca.key", "-CAcreateserial", "-out", "server.crt", "-days", "30", "-extfile", "server.ext"])

            && ssl(&d, &[&["req", "-x509"][..], &ec, &["-keyout", "k2.pem", "-out", "c2.pem", "-days", "5", "-subj", "/CN=game.test", "-addext", "subjectAltName=DNS:game.test"]].concat())

            && ssl(&d, &["rsa", "-in", "rsa8.key", "-traditional", "-out", "rsa1.key"])

/// a client that takes any certificate (the tests look at which one it was)
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Any(Arc<rustls::crypto::CryptoProvider>);
impl ServerCertVerifier for Any {
    fn verify_server_cert(
        &self,
        _: &CertificateDer<'_>,
        _: &[CertificateDer<'_>],
        _: &ServerName<'_>,
        _: &[u8],
        _: UnixTime,
    ) -> Result<ServerCertVerified, rustls::Error> {
        Ok(ServerCertVerified::assertion())
    }
    fn verify_tls12_signature(
        &self,
        m: &[u8],
        c: &CertificateDer<'_>,
        d: &DigitallySignedStruct,
    ) -> Result<HandshakeSignatureValid, rustls::Error> {
        rustls::crypto::verify_tls12_signature(m, c, d, &self.0.signature_verification_algorithms)
    }
    fn verify_tls13_signature(
        &self,
        m: &[u8],
        c: &CertificateDer<'_>,
        d: &DigitallySignedStruct,
    ) -> Result<HandshakeSignatureValid, rustls::Error> {
        rustls::crypto::verify_tls13_signature(m, c, d, &self.0.signature_verification_algorithms)
    }
    fn supported_verify_schemes(&self) -> Vec<SignatureScheme> {
        self.0.signature_verification_algorithms.supported_schemes()
    }
}

fn connector(alpn: &[&[u8]], versions: &[&'static rustls::SupportedProtocolVersion]) -> tokio_rustls::TlsConnector {
    let provider = Arc::new(rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider());
    let mut config = rustls::ClientConfig::builder_with_provider(provider.clone())
        .with_protocol_versions(versions)
        .expect("versions")
        .dangerous()
        .with_custom_certificate_verifier(Arc::new(Any(provider)))
        .with_no_client_auth();
    config.alpn_protocols = alpn.iter().map(|a| a.to_vec()).collect();
    tokio_rustls::TlsConnector::from(Arc::new(config))
}

/// A handshake with this server name (None: none, as for an address): the certificate the server showed.
async fn hello(addr: std::net::SocketAddr, name: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let tcp = TcpStream::connect(addr).await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let sn = match name {
        Some(n) => ServerName::try_from(n.to_string()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?,
        None => ServerName::IpAddress(std::net::IpAddr::from([127, 0, 0, 1]).into()),
    };
    let tls =
        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), connector(&[], &[&rustls::version::TLS13, &rustls::version::TLS12]).connect(sn, tcp))
            .await
            .map_err(|_| "timeout".to_string())?
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let (_, conn) = tls.get_ref();
    Ok(conn.peer_certificates().and_then(|c| c.first()).map(|c| c.as_ref().to_vec()).unwrap_or_default())
}

fn der(pem: &Path) -> Vec<u8> {
    let data = std::fs::read(pem).expect("pem");
    rustls_pemfile::certs(&mut &data[..]).next().expect("a certificate").expect("pem").as_ref().to_vec()
}

async fn tls_engine(state: Arc<TlsState>, limits: Limits) -> std::net::SocketAddr {
    let (l, _) = nfsu2_http::bind("127.0.0.1", 0, None).await.expect("bind");
    let addr = l.local_addr().expect("addr");
    nfsu2_http::serve(l, Some(state), Arc::new(limits), TestService::new(Duration::from_secs(65)));
    addr
}

macro_rules! certs_or_skip {
    () => {
        match Certs::make() {
            Some(c) => c,
            None => {
                eprintln!("skipped: no openssl to make test certificates");
                return;
            }
        }
    };
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn f4_no_certificate_without_the_servers_name_or_for_another() {
    let c = certs_or_skip!();
    let (state, names) = TlsState::load(&c.p("c.pem"), &c.p("k.pem")).expect("load");
    assert_eq!(names.dns, vec!["game.test", "*.wild.test"]);
    assert!(names.ips.is_empty());
    let addr = tls_engine(state, Limits::default()).await;
    let own = der(&c.p("c.pem"));
    assert!(hello(addr, None).await.is_err(), "no SNI: no certificate");
    assert!(hello(addr, Some("scan.invalid")).await.is_err(), "another name: no certificate");
    assert!(hello(addr, Some("a.b.wild.test")).await.is_err(), "two labels under the wildcard");
    assert!(hello(addr, Some("wild.test")).await.is_err(), "the wildcard's zone itself");
    assert_eq!(hello(addr, Some("game.test")).await.as_deref(), Ok(own.as_slice()));
    assert_eq!(hello(addr, Some("a.wild.test")).await.as_deref(), Ok(own.as_slice()), "a wildcard name of the certificate");
    assert_eq!(hello(addr, Some("GAME.TEST")).await.as_deref(), Ok(own.as_slice()), "case does not matter");
}

/// A ClientHello with this server name (None: none), as rustls's client writes it.
fn client_hello(name: Option<&str>, versions: &[&'static rustls::SupportedProtocolVersion]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let provider = Arc::new(rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider());
    let config = rustls::ClientConfig::builder_with_provider(provider.clone())
        .with_protocol_versions(versions)
        .expect("versions")
        .dangerous()
        .with_custom_certificate_verifier(Arc::new(Any(provider)))
        .with_no_client_auth();
    let sn = match name {
        Some(n) => ServerName::try_from(n.to_string()).expect("name"),
        None => ServerName::IpAddress(std::net::IpAddr::from([127, 0, 0, 1]).into()),
    };
    let mut c = rustls::ClientConnection::new(Arc::new(config), sn).expect("client");
    let mut hello = Vec::new();
    while c.wants_write() {
        c.write_tls(&mut hello).expect("hello");
    }
    hello
}

/// A ClientHello sent on its own: what came back, and whether the connection ended in a reset.  (Only for handshakes
/// the server refuses: it ends the connection.)
async fn refusal(addr: std::net::SocketAddr, hello: &[u8]) -> (Vec<u8>, bool) {
    let mut s = TcpStream::connect(addr).await.expect("connect");
    s.write_all(hello).await.expect("send");
    let mut got = Vec::new();
    let mut buf = [0u8; 4096];
    loop {
        match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), s.read(&mut buf)).await {
            Ok(Ok(0)) => return (got, false),
            Ok(Ok(n)) => got.extend_from_slice(&buf[..n]),
            Ok(Err(e)) => return (got, e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionReset),
            Err(_) => panic!("the server neither refused nor went on: {got:?}"),
        }
    }
}

/// a fatal handshake_failure alert in a TLS 1.2 record, as OpenSSL sends it for a handshake it has no certificate for
const HANDSHAKE_FAILURE: [u8; 7] = [0x15, 0x03, 0x03, 0x00, 0x02, 0x02, 0x28];

#[tokio::test]
async fn refused_handshakes_look_as_nodes_do() {
    // Node (OpenSSL) has no certificate for a handshake without a name (tls_server.mjs gives it none): a fatal
    // handshake_failure alert; for a name its SNI callback refuses, the socket is destroyed: closed without a byte.
    // (rustls sent access_denied for both.)  No certificate either way.
    let c = certs_or_skip!();
    let both = [&rustls::version::TLS13, &rustls::version::TLS12];
    let twelve = [&rustls::version::TLS12];
    // a name rustls refuses as none at all (illegal_parameter); OpenSSL takes any bytes but NUL, and the SNI callback
    // refused it as another name
    let mut odd = client_hello(Some("x.test"), &both);
    if let Some(i) = odd.windows(6).position(|w| w == b"x.test") {
        odd[i] = b' ';
    }
    let cases: [(&str, &str, Vec<u8>, bool); 7] = [
        ("c.pem", "k.pem", client_hello(None, &both), true),
        ("c.pem", "k.pem", client_hello(None, &twelve), true),
        ("c.pem", "k.pem", client_hello(Some("scan.invalid"), &both), false),
        ("c.pem", "k.pem", client_hello(Some("a.b.wild.test"), &twelve), false),
        ("c.pem", "k.pem", odd, false),
        // a certificate that names an address: shown without a name, but not for another name
        ("chain.crt", "server.key", client_hello(Some("other.test"), &both), false),
        ("chain.crt", "server.key", client_hello(Some("other.test"), &twelve), false),
    ];
    for (i, (cert, key, hello, alert)) in cases.iter().enumerate() {
        let (state, _) = TlsState::load(&c.p(cert), &c.p(key)).expect("load");
        let addr = tls_engine(state, Limits::default()).await;
        let got = refusal(addr, hello).await;
        let want = if *alert { (HANDSHAKE_FAILURE.to_vec(), false) } else { (Vec::new(), false) };
        assert_eq!(got, want, "case {i}: {cert}");
        // Node's own server on the same certificate, the same ClientHello
        let node = common::NodeRef::script("tls_server.mjs", &[c.p(cert).display().to_string(), c.p(key).display().to_string()]).await;
        match node {
            Some(n) => assert_eq!(refusal(n.addr, hello).await, got, "node, case {i}: {cert}"),
            None => eprintln!("skipped: no node to compare with"),
        }
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_certificate_that_names_an_address_is_shown_without_a_name_too() {
    let c = certs_or_skip!();
    let (state, names) = TlsState::load(&c.p("chain.crt"), &c.p("server.key")).expect("load");
    assert_eq!(names.dns, vec!["localhost", "nfsu2.test"]);
    assert_eq!(names.ips, vec!["127.0.0.1"]);
    let addr = tls_engine(state, Limits::default()).await;
    let leaf = der(&c.p("server.crt"));
    assert_eq!(hello(addr, None).await.as_deref(), Ok(leaf.as_slice()));
    assert_eq!(hello(addr, Some("nfsu2.test")).await.as_deref(), Ok(leaf.as_slice()));
    assert!(hello(addr, Some("other.test")).await.is_err(), "a name it does not cover still fails");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn names_as_node_prints_them() {
    let c = certs_or_skip!();
    let (_, names) = TlsState::load(&c.p("v6.crt"), &c.p("v6.key")).expect("load");
    // Node: "IP Address:0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1" (bareIp: lower case), DNS names in lower case
    assert_eq!(names.ips, vec!["0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1"]);
    assert_eq!(names.dns, vec!["upper.test"]);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_key_formats_a_certificate_comes_with() {
    let c = certs_or_skip!();
    for (cert, key) in [("c.pem", "k.pem"), ("c.pem", "sec1.key"), ("rsa.crt", "rsa8.key"), ("rsa.crt", "rsa1.key")] {
        let (state, names) = TlsState::load(&c.p(cert), &c.p(key)).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{key}: {e}"));
        let addr = tls_engine(state, Limits::default()).await;
        let name = names.dns[0].clone();
        assert_eq!(hello(addr, Some(&name)).await.as_deref(), Ok(der(&c.p(cert)).as_slice()), "{key}");
    }
    // the first line of the PEM says which: PKCS#8, SEC1, PKCS#1
    let first = |f: &str| std::fs::read_to_string(c.p(f)).unwrap_or_default().lines().next().unwrap_or_default().to_string();
    assert_eq!(first("k.pem"), "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----");
    assert_eq!(first("sec1.key"), "-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----");
    assert_eq!(first("rsa1.key"), "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn files_that_cannot_be_used() {
    let c = certs_or_skip!();
    let missing = c.p("missing.key");
    let e = TlsState::load(&c.p("c.pem"), &missing).err().unwrap_or_default();
    assert_eq!(e, format!("ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '{}'", missing.display()));
    let e = TlsState::load(&c.p("nosan.crt"), &c.p("nosan.key")).err().unwrap_or_default();
    assert_eq!(e, format!("{} names no host (no subjectAltName)", c.p("nosan.crt").display()));
    let e = TlsState::load(&c.p("c.pem"), &c.p("server.key")).err().unwrap_or_default();
    assert!(e.contains("does not belong"), "{e}");
    std::fs::write(c.p("junk.pem"), "not a certificate\n").unwrap();
    assert!(TlsState::load(&c.p("junk.pem"), &c.p("k.pem")).is_err());
    assert!(TlsState::load(&c.p("c.pem"), &c.p("junk.pem")).is_err());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_renewed_certificate_without_a_restart() {
    let c = certs_or_skip!();
    let (crt, key) = (c.p("live.crt"), c.p("live.key"));
    std::fs::copy(c.p("c.pem"), &crt).unwrap();
    std::fs::copy(c.p("k.pem"), &key).unwrap();
    let (state, _) = TlsState::load(&crt, &key).expect("load");
    let addr = tls_engine(state.clone(), Limits::default()).await;
    assert_eq!(hello(addr, Some("game.test")).await.as_deref(), Ok(der(&c.p("c.pem")).as_slice()));
    std::fs::copy(c.p("c2.pem"), &crt).unwrap();
    std::fs::copy(c.p("k2.pem"), &key).unwrap();
    let names = state.reload().expect("reload");
    assert_eq!(names.dns, vec!["game.test"]);
    assert_eq!(hello(addr, Some("game.test")).await.as_deref(), Ok(der(&c.p("c2.pem")).as_slice()), "the new one");
    assert!(hello(addr, Some("a.wild.test")).await.is_err(), "the old one's names are gone");
    // a broken renewal: the certificate in use stays
    std::fs::write(&crt, "broken").unwrap();
    assert!(state.reload().is_err());
    assert_eq!(hello(addr, Some("game.test")).await.as_deref(), Ok(der(&c.p("c2.pem")).as_slice()));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_handshake_that_never_finishes_is_closed_after_the_handshake_time() {
    let c = certs_or_skip!();
    let (state, _) = TlsState::load(&c.p("chain.crt"), &c.p("server.key")).expect("load");
    let limits = Limits { handshake_timeout: Duration::from_millis(300), ..Limits::default() };
    let addr = tls_engine(state, limits).await;
    let mut socks = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..50 {
        socks.push(TcpStream::connect(addr).await.unwrap());
    }
    let t0 = tokio::time::Instant::now();
    for s in &mut socks {
        let (got, closed) = common::read_all(s, 2000).await;
        assert!(closed && got.is_empty(), "closed without a byte");
    }
    let dt = t0.elapsed();
    assert!(dt >= Duration::from_millis(250) && dt < Duration::from_millis(1200), "{dt:?}");
    // meanwhile and after, a real client gets in
    assert!(hello(addr, Some("nfsu2.test")).await.is_ok());
}

/// A GET over TLS (these versions, this client certificate and key, or none): whether an answer came.  (TLS 1.3's
/// client finishes its handshake before the server checks its certificate: a refusal shows when it reads.)
async fn get_with(
    addr: std::net::SocketAddr,
    versions: &[&'static rustls::SupportedProtocolVersion],
    cert: Option<(&Path, &Path)>,
) -> bool {
    let provider = Arc::new(rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider());
    let b = rustls::ClientConfig::builder_with_provider(provider.clone())
        .with_protocol_versions(versions)
        .expect("versions")
        .dangerous()
        .with_custom_certificate_verifier(Arc::new(Any(provider)));
    let config = match cert {
        Some((c, k)) => {
            let chain = rustls_pemfile::certs(&mut &std::fs::read(c).unwrap()[..]).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>().unwrap();
            let key = rustls_pemfile::private_key(&mut &std::fs::read(k).unwrap()[..]).unwrap().unwrap();
            b.with_client_auth_cert(chain, key).expect("client certificate")
        }
        None => b.with_no_client_auth(),
    };
    let tcp = TcpStream::connect(addr).await.unwrap();
    let go = async {
        let mut s =
            tokio_rustls::TlsConnector::from(Arc::new(config)).connect(ServerName::try_from("nfsu2.test").unwrap(), tcp).await.ok()?;
        s.write_all(b"GET /x HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: nfsu2.test\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n").await.ok()?;
        let mut all = Vec::new();
        s.read_to_end(&mut all).await.ok()?;
        Some(all.starts_with(b"HTTP/1.1 200"))
    };
    tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), go).await.ok().flatten().unwrap_or(false)
}

/// A peer the service names must show a client certificate that the client CA signed (with --trusted-proxies
/// cloudflare, Cloudflare's origin-pull certificate: any of its customers connects from its addresses too, the second
/// security audit): without one, or with one another CA signed, nothing gets through; the other peers are asked for
/// none; without a client CA, a peer that must show one is refused.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_peer_that_must_prove_itself_shows_a_certificate_of_the_client_ca() {
    let c = certs_or_skip!();
    let d = &c.dir;
    let ec = ["-newkey", "ec", "-pkeyopt", "ec_paramgen_curve:prime256v1", "-nodes"];
    assert!(
        ssl(
            d,
            &[
                &["req", "-x509"][..],
                &ec,
                &[
                    "-keyout",
                    "cca.key",
                    "-out",
                    "cca.crt",
                    "-days",
                    "30",
                    "-subj",
                    "/CN=test origin-pull CA",
                    "-addext",
                    "basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE",
                    "-addext",
                    "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign"
                ]
            ]
            .concat()
        ) && std::fs::write(
            d.join("client.ext"),
            "basicConstraints=CA:FALSE\nkeyUsage=critical,digitalSignature\nextendedKeyUsage=clientAuth\n"
        )
        .is_ok()
            && ssl(d, &[&["req"][..], &ec, &["-keyout", "client.key", "-out", "client.csr", "-subj", "/CN=origin-pull"]].concat())
            && ssl(
                d,
                &[
                    "x509",
                    "-req",
                    "-in",
                    "client.csr",
                    "-CA",
                    "cca.crt",
                    "-CAkey",
                    "cca.key",
                    "-CAcreateserial",
                    "-out",
                    "client.crt",
                    "-days",
                    "30",
                    "-extfile",
                    "client.ext"
                ]
            )
            && ssl(
                d,
                &[
                    &["req", "-x509"][..],
                    &ec,
                    &[
                        "-keyout",
                        "rogue.key",
                        "-out",
                        "rogue.crt",
                        "-days",
                        "5",
                        "-subj",
                        "/CN=origin-pull",
                        "-addext",
                        "extendedKeyUsage=clientAuth"
                    ]
                ]
                .concat()
            ),
        "client certificates"
    );
    let ca = std::fs::read(c.p("cca.crt")).unwrap();
    let (state, _) = TlsState::load_with_client_ca(&c.p("chain.crt"), &c.p("server.key"), &ca).expect("load");
    let (l, _) = nfsu2_http::bind("127.0.0.1", 0, None).await.expect("bind");
    let proving = l.local_addr().unwrap();
    let svc = TestService::new(Duration::from_secs(65));
    svc.prove.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
    nfsu2_http::serve(l, Some(state.clone()), Arc::new(Limits::default()), svc);
    let (client, rogue) = ((c.p("client.crt"), c.p("client.key")), (c.p("rogue.crt"), c.p("rogue.key")));
    for v in [&[&rustls::version::TLS13][..], &[&rustls::version::TLS12][..]] {
        assert!(!get_with(proving, v, None).await, "{v:?}: no client certificate");
        assert!(!get_with(proving, v, Some((&rogue.0, &rogue.1))).await, "{v:?}: one another CA signed");
        assert!(get_with(proving, v, Some((&client.0, &client.1))).await, "{v:?}: the client CA's");
    }
    // the same certificate state for peers the service does not name: no client certificate asked
    let others = tls_engine(state, Limits::default()).await;
    assert!(get_with(others, &[&rustls::version::TLS13], None).await);
    // no client CA: nothing to prove with
    let (plain, _) = TlsState::load(&c.p("chain.crt"), &c.p("server.key")).expect("load");
    let (l, _) = nfsu2_http::bind("127.0.0.1", 0, None).await.expect("bind");
    let refused = l.local_addr().unwrap();
    let svc = TestService::new(Duration::from_secs(65));
    svc.prove.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
    nfsu2_http::serve(l, Some(plain), Arc::new(Limits::default()), svc);
    assert!(!get_with(refused, &[&rustls::version::TLS13], Some((&client.0, &client.1))).await);
    // Cloudflare's own CA (built in) is one the server takes; a file without a certificate is not
    assert!(TlsState::load_with_client_ca(&c.p("chain.crt"), &c.p("server.key"), nfsu2_headers::CLOUDFLARE_ORIGIN_PULL_CA).is_ok());
    assert!(TlsState::load_with_client_ca(&c.p("chain.crt"), &c.p("server.key"), b"junk").is_err());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn http_over_tls() {
    let c = certs_or_skip!();
    let (state, _) = TlsState::load(&c.p("chain.crt"), &c.p("server.key")).expect("load");
    let addr = tls_engine(state, Limits::default()).await;
    for versions in [&[&rustls::version::TLS13][..], &[&rustls::version::TLS12][..]] {
        let tcp = TcpStream::connect(addr).await.unwrap();
        let mut s =
            connector(&[b"h2", b"http/1.1"], versions).connect(ServerName::try_from("nfsu2.test").unwrap(), tcp).await.expect("handshake");
        assert_eq!(s.get_ref().1.alpn_protocol(), Some(&b"http/1.1"[..]), "Node's ALPN");
        // keep-alive, then a pipelined pair, then a large answer
        let mut all = Vec::new();
        s.write_all(b"GET /conninfo HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: nfsu2.test\r\n\r\n").await.unwrap();
        let mut buf = vec![0u8; 1 << 16];
        let n = s.read(&mut buf).await.unwrap();
        let first = common::mask_dates(&buf[..n]);
        assert!(first.contains("\r\n\r\n127.0.0.1 true 127.0.0.1:"), "{first}");
        s.write_all(b"GET /x HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\nGET /big HTTP/1.1\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n").await.unwrap();
        s.read_to_end(&mut all).await.unwrap_or_default();
        let t = common::mask_dates(&all);
        assert!(t.contains("\"u\":\"/x\""), "{}", &t[..t.len().min(300)]);
        assert!(t.ends_with(&"a".repeat(200_000)), "the whole large answer");
    }
    // an upgrade over TLS: the halves whole again, and what came after the head
    let tcp = TcpStream::connect(addr).await.unwrap();
    let mut s =
        connector(&[], &[&rustls::version::TLS13]).connect(ServerName::try_from("nfsu2.test").unwrap(), tcp).await.expect("handshake");
    s.write_all(b"GET /lan HTTP/1.1\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\n\r\nPRE").await.unwrap();
    let mut all = Vec::new();
    let _ = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(3), s.read_to_end(&mut all)).await;
    let t = common::mask_dates(&all);
    assert!(t.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\n") && t.contains("x-pre: 505245\r\n"), "{t}");
}

//! A Unix socket's connections (serve_unix: cloudflared's `unix:` origin): answered as a TCP connection's are, each as
//! one from the peer the listener was given (the trusted proxy's 127.0.0.1), and an upgrade (the /lan WebSocket) hands
//! the stream on whole, its send buffer settable as a TCP one's.

use std::net::SocketAddr;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

use nfsu2_http::{ClientError, Limits, Request, Response, Service, Upgraded};
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};
use tokio::net::{UnixListener, UnixStream};

/// answers "ok" with the peer it was given, and echoes on an upgraded connection
#[derive(Default)]
struct Echo {
    peers: Mutex<Vec<SocketAddr>>,
    sndbuf: Mutex<Option<bool>>,
}

impl Service for Echo {
    fn admit(&self, peer: &SocketAddr) -> Option<Box<dyn Send + Sync>> {
        self.peers.lock().unwrap().push(*peer);
        Some(Box::new(()))
    }
    fn keep_alive(&self, _: &SocketAddr) -> Duration {
        Duration::from_secs(5)
    }
    async fn request<'a>(&'a self, req: Request, res: &'a mut Response) {
        let body = format!("ok {}", req.conn.peer);
        res.head(200, vec![("content-length".into(), body.len().to_string())]);
        let _ = res.write(body.as_bytes()).await;
        let _ = res.end().await;
    }
    async fn expectation<'a>(&'a self, _req: Request, _res: &'a mut Response) {}
    async fn upgrade(&self, _req: Request, mut up: Upgraded) {
        *self.sndbuf.lock().unwrap() = Some(up.stream.set_send_buffer(32 << 10).is_ok());
        let _ = up.stream.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\n\r\n").await;
        let mut b = [0u8; 64];
        while let Ok(n) = up.stream.read(&mut b).await {
            if n == 0 || up.stream.write_all(&b[..n]).await.is_err() {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    fn client_error(&self, _: ClientError) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        None
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_unix_sockets_connections_are_answered_and_upgraded() {
    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("nfsu2-unix-{}", std::process::id()));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
    let path = dir.join("http.sock");
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);
    let svc = Arc::new(Echo::default());
    let peer: SocketAddr = ([127, 0, 0, 1], 0).into();
    nfsu2_http::serve_unix(UnixListener::bind(&path).unwrap(), peer, Arc::new(Limits::default()), svc.clone());

    // a request, and a second one on the same connection
    let mut c = UnixStream::connect(&path).await.unwrap();
    for _ in 0..2 {
        c.write_all(b"GET /game.json HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n").await.unwrap();
        let mut b = [0u8; 256];
        let n = c.read(&mut b).await.unwrap();
        let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..n]);
        assert!(s.starts_with("HTTP/1.1 200") && s.ends_with("ok 127.0.0.1"), "{s:?}");
    }

    // an upgrade: the stream itself, both ways
    let mut u = UnixStream::connect(&path).await.unwrap();
    u.write_all(b"GET /lan HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\n\r\n").await.unwrap();
    let mut b = [0u8; 64];
    let n = u.read(&mut b).await.unwrap();
    assert!(b[..n].starts_with(b"HTTP/1.1 101"), "{:?}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..n]));
    u.write_all(b"ping").await.unwrap();
    let n = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), u.read(&mut b)).await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(&b[..n], b"ping");

    assert_eq!(*svc.peers.lock().unwrap(), vec![peer, peer], "each connection as from the given peer");
    assert_eq!(*svc.sndbuf.lock().unwrap(), Some(true), "the send buffer is set on a Unix socket too");
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
}

{"id": "AT001563", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/server-rs/crates/http/tests/upgrade_hold.rs", "originalBytes": 6546, "originalSha256": "e6ba9fbcae519cb4c6deaccf20cc52b9bb79ae415dc635c0ede541a2eb2b8bfd", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 6546, "utf8TotalBytes": 6546}

//! An upgraded connection (the /lan WebSocket) still counts while whoever took it keeps it: in the listener's count
//! (max_connections) and in the per-client connection budget (Service::admit's share), as Node counted an upgraded
//! socket until its 'close'.  (Before, both were given back as soon as the engine handed the stream on, so a crowd of
//! WebSockets left the port's limits free for as many more connections.)

use std::net::SocketAddr;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::time::Duration;

use nfsu2_http::{ClientError, Limits, Request, Response, Service, Upgraded};
use std::sync::Mutex;
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};
use tokio::net::TcpStream;

/// a service that keeps every upgraded connection, and counts its admit shares
#[derive(Default)]
struct Keeper {
    kept: Mutex<Vec<Upgraded>>,
    shares: Arc<AtomicUsize>,
}

struct Share(Arc<AtomicUsize>);
impl Drop for Share {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.0.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
    }
}

impl Service for Keeper {
    fn admit(&self, _: &SocketAddr) -> Option<Box<dyn Send + Sync>> {
        self.shares.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        Some(Box::new(Share(self.shares.clone())))
    }
    fn keep_alive(&self, _: &SocketAddr) -> Duration {
        Duration::from_secs(5)
    }
    async fn request<'a>(&'a self, _req: Request, res: &'a mut Response) {
        res.head(200, vec![("content-length".into(), "2".into())]);
        let _ = res.write(b"ok").await;
        let _ = res.end().await;
    }
    async fn expectation<'a>(&'a self, _req: Request, _res: &'a mut Response) {}
    async fn upgrade(&self, _req: Request, mut up: Upgraded) {
        let _ = up.stream.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\n\r\n").await;
        self.kept.lock().unwrap().push(up);
    }
    fn client_error(&self, _: ClientError) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        None
    }
}

async fn upgrade(addr: SocketAddr) -> TcpStream {
    let mut c = TcpStream::connect(addr).await.expect("connect");
    c.write_all(b"GET /lan HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\n\r\n").await.expect("write");
    let mut b = [0u8; 64];
    let n = c.read(&mut b).await.expect("the 101");
    assert!(b[..n].starts_with(b"HTTP/1.1 101"), "{:?}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..n]));
    c
}

/// whether a new connection is let in: an answer to a request, or closed without a byte
async fn let_in(addr: SocketAddr) -> bool {
    let mut c = TcpStream::connect(addr).await.expect("connect");
    let _ = c.write_all(b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n").await;
    let mut b = [0u8; 256];
    matches!(tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), c.read(&mut b)).await, Ok(Ok(n)) if n > 0)
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_upgraded_connection_counts_while_it_is_kept() {
    let (listener, _) = nfsu2_http::bind("127.0.0.1", 0, None).await.expect("bind");
    let addr = listener.local_addr().expect("addr");
    let svc = Arc::new(Keeper::default());
    let limits = Limits { max_connections: 2, ..Limits::default() };
    nfsu2_http::serve(listener, None, Arc::new(limits), svc.clone());
    let a = upgrade(addr).await;
    let b = upgrade(addr).await;
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
    assert_eq!(svc.kept.lock().unwrap().len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(svc.shares.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 2, "both upgraded connections keep their admit share");
    assert!(!let_in(addr).await, "two upgraded connections fill a port of max_connections 2");
    // the service lets them go: the port has room again, the shares are back
    svc.kept.lock().unwrap().clear();
    drop((a, b));
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
    assert!(let_in(addr).await, "room again once they are gone");
}

/// a service that lets every upgraded connection go at once (a refusal), and panics on an upgrade to /panic
#[derive(Default)]
struct Dropper {
    shares: Arc<AtomicUsize>,
}

impl Service for Dropper {
    fn admit(&self, _: &SocketAddr) -> Option<Box<dyn Send + Sync>> {
        self.shares.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        Some(Box::new(Share(self.shares.clone())))
    }
    fn keep_alive(&self, _: &SocketAddr) -> Duration {
        Duration::from_secs(5)
    }
    async fn request<'a>(&'a self, _req: Request, res: &'a mut Response) {
        res.head(200, vec![("content-length".into(), "2".into())]);
        let _ = res.write(b"ok").await;
        let _ = res.end().await;
    }
    async fn expectation<'a>(&'a self, _req: Request, _res: &'a mut Response) {}
    async fn upgrade(&self, req: Request, up: Upgraded) {
        if req.url == "/panic" {
            panic!("an upgrade that fails");
        }
        drop(up);
    }
    fn client_error(&self, _: ClientError) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        None
    }
}

async fn shares_back(shares: &AtomicUsize, what: &str) {
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    while shares.load(Ordering::SeqCst) != 0 {
        assert!(t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(2), "{what}: shares still held");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5)).await;
    }
}

// Every connection that no upgrade keeps gives its shares back as it goes: one that was answered, an upgrade the
// service let go (its refusals), an upgrade whose service panicked.  (A port of max_connections 1: each in turn.)
#[tokio::test]
async fn any_other_connection_gives_its_shares_back_as_it_goes() {
    let (listener, _) = nfsu2_http::bind("127.0.0.1", 0, None).await.expect("bind");
    let addr = listener.local_addr().expect("addr");
    let svc = Arc::new(Dropper::default());
    nfsu2_http::serve(listener, None, Arc::new(Limits { max_connections: 1, ..Limits::default() }), svc.clone());
    assert!(let_in(addr).await, "a request answered");
    shares_back(&svc.shares, "an answered connection that the client closed").await;
    for path in ["/lan", "/panic"] {
        let mut c = TcpStream::connect(addr).await.expect("connect");
        let req = format!("GET {path} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\n\r\n");
        c.write_all(req.as_bytes()).await.expect("write");
        let mut b = [0u8; 64];
        let n = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), c.read(&mut b)).await.expect("closed in time").unwrap_or(0);
        assert_eq!(n, 0, "{path}: closed without an answer");
        shares_back(&svc.shares, path).await;
        assert!(let_in(addr).await, "{path}: the port has room again");
        shares_back(&svc.shares, path).await;
    }
}

//! Players in free roam who are not driving: in a race, a shop, the menus or loading (runtime/roam_core.h RC_ST_*, as
//! their own HELLOs and SNAPs say).  Their game draws no other car then, and no one draws theirs, but the hub keeps
//! their links (up to 32 friends, so that the cars are there as soon as they drive again): pings, pongs and HELLOs both
//! ways, and their friends' car states 20 times a second.  On nfsu2.xyz (2026-10-30, 5,800 players) about 2,900 of the
//! 5,060 in free roam were such players, and the bots measured what they cost: a player in a race got 70 % of the
//! messages of one driving (web/tools/roam-crowd.mjs --race), each a message the server and cloudflared pay for (the
//! kernel's work for each message, not its bytes, was most of the CPU).
//!
//! So what their friends send them waits for the slow clock (`LanOptions::away_ms`, half a second: a ping's and a
//! pong's times are moved on by their waits, compact.rs `waited`), and of the car states sent to them they get one in
//! 16 (`SHARE`); the hub's own messages (its lists, the world map) and LAN play's go as they go to anyone, and take
//! what waits along.  The first HELLO or SNAP of theirs that says they drive (or are paused there) ends it: the next
//! tick brings them every friend's car.  Players driving near each other get what they always got.

use crate::lag::SHARE_FULL;

/// of the car states sent to a player who is not driving, the share it gets (as a path far behind gets, lag.rs)
pub(crate) const SHARE: u32 = SHARE_FULL / 16;

/// runtime/roam_core.h RC_DEFAULT_PORT
const ROAM_PORT: u16 = 47210;

/// The free-roam status a frame of a player's own says, when it is a HELLO or a SNAP of free roam (to anyone: its
/// friends, the hub): RC_ST_*.  The CRC is not checked: a player who says the wrong thing gets its own traffic slower
/// or as it is now, no one else's.
pub(crate) fn status(frame: &[u8]) -> Option<u8> {
    if frame.len() < 16 + 20 || frame[0] != crate::KIND_UDP || &frame[16..20] != b"N2FR" || frame[20] != 1 {
        return None;
    }
    if u16::from_be_bytes([frame[14], frame[15]]) != ROAM_PORT {
        return None;
    }
    // after the datagram's 16-byte header: a HELLO's core version (2) and platform (1), then its status; a SNAP's
    // status first
    match frame[21] {
        1 => Some(frame[16 + 19]),
        3 => Some(frame[16 + 16]),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// a status of a player who is not driving: the menus (0), loading (1), a race (3), a shop (4); not in free roam (2)
/// or paused there (5), and not a number the core does not send (as for anyone)
pub(crate) fn away(status: u8) -> bool {
    matches!(status, 0 | 1 | 3 | 4)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn frame(kind: u8, port: u16, body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut f = vec![0u8; 16];
        f[0] = crate::KIND_UDP;
        f[12..14].copy_from_slice(&ROAM_PORT.to_be_bytes());
        f[14..16].copy_from_slice(&port.to_be_bytes());
        f.extend_from_slice(b"N2FR");
        f.extend_from_slice(&[1, kind, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 0, 1, 0, 0]);
        f.extend_from_slice(body);
        f.extend_from_slice(&[0; 4]);
        f
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_hellos_and_a_snaps_status() {
        // HELLO: core version 8, platform 3, status 4 (a shop)
        assert_eq!(status(&frame(1, ROAM_PORT, &[8, 0, 3, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0])), Some(4));
        // SNAP: status 2 (driving) first
        assert_eq!(status(&frame(3, ROAM_PORT, &[2, 7, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0])), Some(2));
        // a ping, another port, another kind of frame: none
        assert_eq!(status(&frame(6, ROAM_PORT, &[0; 8])), None);
        assert_eq!(status(&frame(1, 9999, &[8, 0, 3, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0])), None);
        let mut lan = frame(1, ROAM_PORT, &[8, 0, 3, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
        lan[0] = crate::KIND_LAN_UDP;
        assert_eq!(status(&lan), None);
        assert_eq!(status(&frame(1, ROAM_PORT, &[])[..30]), None);
        assert!(away(0) && away(1) && away(3) && away(4) && !away(2) && !away(5) && !away(6) && !away(202));
    }
}
