//! A connection: its queue (what the switch sends it, taken by its writer all at once), its writer, the bundle clock,
//! and the ws library's states and close rules (the WebSocket library of the Node server: the crate doc's last part).

use std::sync::atomic::{
    AtomicBool, AtomicU8, AtomicU32, AtomicU64, AtomicUsize,
    Ordering::{AcqRel, Acquire, Relaxed, Release, SeqCst},
};
use std::sync::{Arc, Weak};
use std::time::Duration;

use bytes::Bytes;
use nfsu2_ws::frame;
use parking_lot::Mutex;
use tokio::io::{AsyncRead, AsyncWrite, AsyncWriteExt};
use tokio::sync::Notify;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use crate::{AttachCtx, BUNDLE_OUT, CLOSE_TIMEOUT, KIND_BUNDLE, LanSwitch, Peer, Stats, compact, mix};

/// how a page takes its datagrams (`Conn::compact`): as bundles of before, compact bundles, compact bundles with deltas,
/// and with friends' car states by their fields (fpred.rs)
pub(crate) const PLAIN: u8 = 0;
pub(crate) const COMPACT: u8 = 1;
pub(crate) const DELTAS: u8 = 2;
pub(crate) const FPRED: u8 = 3;
/// with DELTAS or FPRED: every other datagram as what changed too (its hello said "ldelta":1: compact.rs `Refs::other`)
pub(crate) const OTHERS: u8 = 0x10;

/// ws's readyState
const OPEN: u8 = 1;
const CLOSING: u8 = 2;
const CLOSED: u8 = 3;

/// Something for a connection's writer.
pub(crate) enum Out {
    /// a text message (a control message of the switch's)
    Text(Bytes),
    /// a binary message as it is (a host's frame)
    Raw(Bytes),
    /// a frame from a browser, alone: its source and destination written in as it goes out
    Frame {
        data: Bytes,
        src: u32,
        dst: u32,
    },
    /// a datagram to a peer that takes bundles: into the writer's next bundle (one alone goes as a `Frame`); `at`: when
    /// it was queued (`now_us`), for a free-roam ping or pong only (compact.rs `timed`), else 0
    Dgram {
        data: Bytes,
        src: u32,
        dst: u32,
        at: u32,
    },
    Ping([u8; 8]),
    Pong(Bytes),
    /// a close frame's payload; nothing goes after it
    Close(Bytes),
    /// both close frames went: the writer ends its half of the connection (ws `socket.end()`)
    End,
}

/// a frame's header for a payload of `len` (RFC 6455 5.2: 2, 4 or 10 bytes from a server)
fn header_len(len: usize) -> usize {
    if len < 126 {
        2
    } else if len < 65536 {
        4
    } else {
        10
    }
}

impl Out {
    /// the bytes it puts on the wire, as `buffered` counts them (ws's bufferedAmount counts the frame's header too);
    /// a datagram for a bundle counts in `dgram` instead (4 + its length, its entry in the bundle)
    fn wire_len(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Out::Text(b) | Out::Raw(b) | Out::Pong(b) | Out::Close(b) => header_len(b.len()) + b.len(),
            Out::Frame { data, .. } => header_len(data.len()) + data.len(),
            Out::Ping(p) => header_len(p.len()) + p.len(),
            Out::Dgram { .. } | Out::End => 0,
        }
    }
}

/// What the switch has queued for one connection.
pub(crate) struct OutQueue {
    pub(crate) q: Mutex<Vec<Out>>,
    /// bytes handed to the writer and not yet taken by the kernel (the ws library's `bufferedAmount`)
    buffered: AtomicUsize,
    /// datagrams waiting for the bundle clock (their bytes as bundle entries)
    dgram: AtomicUsize,
    wake: Notify,
    /// on the bundle clock's list for its next tick, on the slow clock's, and on LAN play's (`Clock::lane`)
    armed: [AtomicBool; 3],
}

impl OutQueue {
    pub(crate) fn buffered(&self) -> usize {
        self.buffered.load(Relaxed)
    }
    pub(crate) fn dgram(&self) -> usize {
        self.dgram.load(Relaxed)
    }
    /// `buffered` for the stream pump.  A sender that leaves segments waiting at the switch sets `streaming` and then
    /// reads `buffered`; the writer lowers `buffered` and then reads `streaming` (and pumps when it is set).  With
    /// both sides SeqCst one of them sees the other's write, so the segments go after the writer's next write; with
    /// Relaxed both could miss (x86 lets a load pass an earlier store) and they waited for whatever woke the writer
    /// next, up to the keepalive's ping.  (On x86 the writer's side costs nothing more: its decrements are locked
    /// instructions either way, its load a plain one.)
    pub(crate) fn buffered_synced(&self) -> usize {
        self.buffered.load(SeqCst)
    }
}

/// The close handshake as ws kept it: whether its close frame went, the client's (code and reason), a protocol error.
#[derive(Default)]
struct CloseState {
    sent: bool,
    received: Option<(u16, Bytes)>,
    errored: bool,
}

/// A connection's own state, before and after it holds an address.
pub(crate) struct Conn {
    pub(crate) id: u64,
    state: AtomicU8,
    /// ends both tasks at once (ws `terminate()`, the close timer, a write that failed)
    pub(crate) kill: CancellationToken,
    killed: AtomicBool,
    pub(crate) out: OutQueue,
    close: Mutex<CloseState>,
    /// the peer it holds an address as, from its admission until its close logic took it
    pub(crate) peer: Mutex<Option<Arc<Peer>>>,
    /// stream segments wait at the switch for this connection (a hint for its writer: pump after each write)
    pub(crate) streaming: AtomicBool,
    /// how its datagrams go (its hello said "compact":1, "delta":1 and "fpred":1: compact.rs): `PLAIN`, `COMPACT`,
    /// `DELTAS` or `FPRED`, with `OTHERS` when it said "ldelta":1 too;
    /// compact ones leave out the address it holds.  One word, so that its writer never sees compact without the
    /// deltas its page takes (the page keeps the last bodies of every compact bundle it was sent)
    pub(crate) compact: AtomicU8,
    pub(crate) vip: AtomicU32,
    /// while it waits in line for a place (queue.rs): its place, and what it sent meanwhile
    pub(crate) wait: Mutex<crate::queue::Wait>,
    /// the operator removed it (a kick or a ban: `LanSwitch::expel_conn`)
    pub(crate) expelled: AtomicBool,
    /// the id its page keeps (its hello's "id"), for `who`
    pub(crate) browser: std::sync::OnceLock<Arc<str>>,
    /// the keyphrase its page plays with, as the server knows it (its hello's "claim": `AttachOpts::on_claim`)
    pub(crate) owner: std::sync::OnceLock<Arc<str>>,
    /// it races nobody (a race ban: its hello's `HelloAnswer::no_races`, or `LanSwitch::set_races`): no frame that
    /// races another player goes from it or to it (`crate::races`)
    pub(crate) no_races: AtomicBool,
    /// its WebSocket messages each way and LAN play's datagrams it sent, since the [players] line last took them
    /// (`LanSwitch::messages_by_kind`): what each kind of player costs the kernel and cloudflared
    pub(crate) msgs_in: AtomicU64,
    pub(crate) msgs_out: AtomicU64,
    pub(crate) lan_sent: AtomicU64,
    /// its page echoes a compact bundle's stamp (its hello's "echo":1: `LanSwitch::probe`), and one is wanted: the next
    /// compact bundle its writer makes carries it
    pub(crate) echo: AtomicBool,
    pub(crate) stamp: AtomicBool,
}

impl Conn {
    pub(crate) fn new(id: u64) -> Self {
        Conn {
            id,
            state: AtomicU8::new(OPEN),
            kill: CancellationToken::new(),
            killed: AtomicBool::new(false),
            out: OutQueue {
                q: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
                buffered: AtomicUsize::new(0),
                dgram: AtomicUsize::new(0),
                wake: Notify::new(),
                armed: [AtomicBool::new(false), AtomicBool::new(false), AtomicBool::new(false)],
            },
            close: Mutex::new(CloseState::default()),
            peer: Mutex::new(None),
            streaming: AtomicBool::new(false),
            compact: AtomicU8::new(PLAIN),
            vip: AtomicU32::new(0),
            wait: Mutex::new(Default::default()),
            expelled: AtomicBool::new(false),
            browser: Default::default(),
            owner: Default::default(),
            no_races: AtomicBool::new(false),
            msgs_in: AtomicU64::new(0),
            msgs_out: AtomicU64::new(0),
            lan_sent: AtomicU64::new(0),
            echo: AtomicBool::new(false),
            stamp: AtomicBool::new(false),
        }
    }

    /// ws `readyState === OPEN`
    pub(crate) fn open(&self) -> bool {
        self.state.load(Acquire) == OPEN
    }

    /// ws `terminate()`: the connection goes at once (its close logic follows on its own task).  True for the call
    /// that ended it (so that a cut is counted once).
    pub(crate) fn terminate(&self) -> bool {
        if self.killed.swap(true, AcqRel) {
            return false;
        }
        let _ = self.state.compare_exchange(OPEN, CLOSING, AcqRel, Acquire);
        self.kill.cancel();
        true
    }

    /// the connection is over (its reader ended): nothing is sent to it any more
    fn end(&self) {
        self.killed.store(true, Release);
        self.state.store(CLOSED, Release);
        self.kill.cancel();
    }

    /// queued to the writer, which wakes at once (while the connection is open: ws sends nothing after a close)
    pub(crate) fn push(&self, item: Out) {
        if !self.open() {
            return;
        }
        self.push_any(item);
    }

    fn push_any(&self, item: Out) {
        let n = item.wire_len();
        {
            let mut q = self.out.q.lock();
            q.push(item);
            // counted under the lock: the writer subtracts only what it took
            self.out.buffered.fetch_add(n, Relaxed);
        }
        self.out.wake.notify_one();
    }

    /// a datagram for a peer that takes bundles: it waits for the bundle clock (or goes at once without one: no clock,
    /// or LAN play's, route.rs `post`); a
    /// bundle's worth (BUNDLE_OUT) wakes the writer at once: a full bundle does not wait for the tick
    pub(crate) fn push_dgram(self: &Arc<Self>, data: Bytes, src: u32, dst: u32, clock: Option<&Clock>) {
        if !self.open() {
            return;
        }
        let n = 4 + data.len();
        let total = {
            let mut q = self.out.q.lock();
            let at = if compact::timed(&data) { now_us() | 1 } else { 0 };
            q.push(Out::Dgram { data, src, dst, at });
            self.out.dgram.fetch_add(n, Relaxed) + n
        };
        match clock {
            Some(c) if total <= BUNDLE_OUT => {
                let armed = &self.out.armed[c.lane];
                if !armed.load(Relaxed) && !armed.swap(true, AcqRel) {
                    c.arm(self);
                }
            }
            _ => self.out.wake.notify_one(),
        }
    }

    /// ws `close(code, reason)` with the close frame's payload: the frame, then up to 30 s for the client's
    pub(crate) fn close(self: &Arc<Self>, payload: Bytes) {
        let _cs = self.close.lock();
        if self.state.compare_exchange(OPEN, CLOSING, AcqRel, Acquire).is_ok() {
            self.push_any(Out::Close(payload));
            self.close_timer();
        }
    }

    /// the client's close frame (ws `receiverOnConclude`): answered with its code (none for 1005), and once both
    /// went the connection ends
    pub(crate) fn close_received(self: &Arc<Self>, code: u16, reason: Bytes) {
        let mut cs = self.close.lock();
        let answer = close_payload(code, &reason);
        cs.received = Some((code, reason));
        if self.state.compare_exchange(OPEN, CLOSING, AcqRel, Acquire).is_ok() {
            self.push_any(Out::Close(answer));
            self.close_timer();
        } else if cs.sent {
            self.push_any(Out::End);
        }
    }

    /// a protocol error (ws `receiverOnError`): a close frame with the error's code only
    pub(crate) fn protocol_error(self: &Arc<Self>, code: u16) {
        let mut cs = self.close.lock();
        cs.errored = true;
        if self.state.compare_exchange(OPEN, CLOSING, AcqRel, Acquire).is_ok() {
            self.push_any(Out::Close(Bytes::copy_from_slice(&code.to_be_bytes())));
            self.close_timer();
        } else if cs.sent {
            self.push_any(Out::End);
        }
    }

    /// the writer sent the close frame: true when the connection may end now (the client's came, or it broke the
    /// protocol)
    fn close_sent(&self) -> bool {
        let mut cs = self.close.lock();
        cs.sent = true;
        cs.received.is_some() || cs.errored
    }

    /// what the switch's 'close' sees: the client's close frame, or 1006 without one
    pub(crate) fn close_code(&self) -> (u16, Bytes) {
        self.close.lock().received.clone().unwrap_or((1006, Bytes::new()))
    }

    /// its page let go of its place itself (1000 "idle" or "closed": no network feature in use, or the game ended),
    /// or the operator removed it: nothing is kept for it (its address, its place in line)
    pub(crate) fn let_go(&self) -> bool {
        let (code, reason) = self.close_code();
        (code == 1000 && (&reason[..] == b"idle" || &reason[..] == b"closed")) || self.expelled.load(Relaxed)
    }

    /// ws's closeTimeout: a client that never answers the close frame is cut after 30 s
    fn close_timer(self: &Arc<Self>) {
        let me = self.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            tokio::select! {
                _ = me.kill.cancelled() => {}
                _ = tokio::time::sleep(CLOSE_TIMEOUT) => { me.terminate(); }
            }
        });
    }
}

/// a close frame's payload for a code and its reason (1005: none, ws's `close()`)
pub(crate) fn close_payload(code: u16, reason: &[u8]) -> Bytes {
    if code == 1005 {
        return Bytes::new();
    }
    let mut p = Vec::with_capacity(2 + reason.len());
    p.extend_from_slice(&code.to_be_bytes());
    p.extend_from_slice(reason);
    Bytes::from(p)
}

/// A connection's tasks: its reader (which routes what it reads) and its writer; when the reader ends (the client
/// went, or the kill token: `terminate()`, the close timer, a failed write), the connection is over: the writer is
/// stopped and the close logic runs once (also when a task panicked: the rest of the switch goes on).
pub(crate) async fn run<R, W>(sw: Arc<LanSwitch>, conn: Arc<Conn>, r: R, w: W, pre: bytes::Bytes, ctx: Arc<AttachCtx>)
where
    R: AsyncRead + Unpin + Send + 'static,
    W: AsyncWrite + Unpin + Send + 'static,
{
    let writer = tokio::spawn(write_loop(sw.clone(), conn.clone(), w));
    let reader = tokio::spawn(crate::reader::read_loop(sw.clone(), conn.clone(), r, pre, ctx.clone()));
    let _ = reader.await;
    conn.end();
    // (the writer waits on nothing but its queue and its socket: stopping it here spares it a wait on the kill token
    // for each wake-up and each write, the switch's hottest path)
    writer.abort();
    let _ = writer.await;
    sw.closed(&conn, &ctx);
}

/// a panic in the writer ends its connection too
struct KillOnPanic(Arc<Conn>);

impl Drop for KillOnPanic {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if std::thread::panicking() {
            self.0.terminate();
        }
    }
}

/// The largest write buffer (bytes) and list of items a writer keeps for its next wake-up (two bundles' worth)
const KEEP_BUF: usize = 2 * BUNDLE_OUT;
const KEEP_ITEMS: usize = 1024;

/// The writer: everything queued at once into one write.  It runs until its connection's supervisor stops it.
async fn write_loop<W: AsyncWrite + Unpin>(sw: Arc<LanSwitch>, conn: Arc<Conn>, mut w: W) {
    let _guard = KillOnPanic(conn.clone());
    let mut items: Vec<Out> = Vec::new();
    let mut buf: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    let mut close_sent = false;
    // a compact bundle as it is made, and the last bodies its page was sent (compact.rs `Refs`)
    let mut body: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    let mut refs = compact::Refs::default();
    let mut fp = crate::fpred::Fpred::default();
    loop {
        conn.out.wake.notified().await;
        loop {
            {
                let mut q = conn.out.q.lock();
                if q.is_empty() {
                    // (the queue's list is the writer's of the turn before: it may be the burst's)
                    if q.capacity() > KEEP_ITEMS {
                        *q = Vec::new();
                    }
                    break;
                }
                std::mem::swap(&mut *q, &mut items);
                conn.out.dgram.store(0, Relaxed);
            }
            let m = conn.compact.load(Relaxed);
            let (mode, others) = (m & !OTHERS, m & OTHERS != 0);
            // a round trip timed by this batch's first compact bundle (LanSwitch::probe): its probe's ping now, as
            // the bundle goes out behind what was queued before it
            let stamp = (mode != PLAIN
                && conn.stamp.load(Relaxed)
                && items.iter().any(|it| matches!(it, Out::Dgram { .. }))
                && conn.stamp.swap(false, Relaxed))
            .then(|| conn.peer.lock().clone())
            .flatten()
            .map(|p| p.probe.lock().ping(nfsu2_util::mono_ms()));
            let c = (mode != PLAIN).then(|| Compact {
                own: conn.vip.load(Relaxed),
                refs: (mode >= DELTAS).then_some(&mut refs),
                fp: (mode == FPRED).then_some(&mut fp),
                others: others && mode >= DELTAS,
                body: &mut body,
                stamp,
            });
            let e = encode(&sw.stats, &items, &mut buf, &mut close_sent, c);
            if !buf.is_empty() {
                sw.stats.msg(mix::OUT_WRITES);
            }
            conn.msgs_out.fetch_add(e.msgs, Relaxed);
            conn.out.buffered.fetch_add(e.extra, Relaxed);
            // what the kernel takes leaves `buffered` as it goes (what was skipped after a close frame at the end)
            let mut at = 0;
            while at < buf.len() {
                match w.write(&buf[at..]).await {
                    Ok(n) if n > 0 => {
                        at += n;
                        conn.out.buffered.fetch_sub(n, SeqCst);
                    }
                    _ => {
                        // the socket failed (ws: destroyed, 'close' with 1006)
                        conn.terminate();
                        return;
                    }
                }
            }
            conn.out.buffered.fetch_sub(e.counted + e.extra - buf.len(), SeqCst);
            // (a TLS stream holds what it took until it is flushed)
            if !buf.is_empty() && w.flush().await.is_err() {
                conn.terminate();
                return;
            }
            buf.clear();
            items.clear();
            if e.end || (e.close && conn.close_sent()) {
                let _ = w.shutdown().await;
                return;
            }
            // (SeqCst: see OutQueue::buffered_synced)
            if conn.streaming.load(SeqCst) {
                sw.pump(&conn);
            }
        }
        // a burst's buffers are not kept for good: every connection would keep its largest write (a stalled link's
        // queue, the hello's peer list: about 100 KB at 2000 players, 256 MB in all); what free roam writes a tick
        // stays far under these
        if buf.capacity() > KEEP_BUF {
            buf = Vec::new();
        }
        if body.capacity() > KEEP_BUF {
            body = Vec::new();
        }
        if items.capacity() > KEEP_ITEMS {
            items = Vec::new();
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct Encoded {
    /// what the items taken had added to `buffered`
    counted: usize,
    /// the datagrams' bytes on the wire (they were counted in `dgram`)
    extra: usize,
    close: bool,
    end: bool,
    /// the WebSocket messages it made (a close frame not among them, as in `Stats::msg`)
    msgs: u64,
}

/// A page that takes compact bundles: the address it holds, the last bodies it was sent when it takes deltas (and the
/// last car states, when it takes them by their fields), and the writer's buffer for the bundle being made.
pub(crate) struct Compact<'a> {
    own: u32,
    refs: Option<&'a mut compact::Refs>,
    fp: Option<&'a mut crate::fpred::Fpred>,
    /// every other datagram as what changed too (`OTHERS`)
    others: bool,
    body: &'a mut Vec<u8>,
    /// a probe's ping for the first bundle's header (compact.rs `F_STAMPED`)
    stamp: Option<[u8; 8]>,
}

/// the items into `buf` in order, the datagrams as bundles (compact ones for a page that takes them) where the first
/// of them stands: what was queued before it goes first (a newcomer's welcome before its first datagrams: a page in
/// line said hello before its welcome, so its datagrams are bundles from the start, and a page that takes deltas keeps
/// the last bodies of every bundle it is sent; the datagrams were all written ahead of the batch's other items once);
/// nothing after a close frame
fn encode(stats: &Stats, items: &[Out], buf: &mut Vec<u8>, close_sent: &mut bool, compact: Option<Compact<'_>>) -> Encoded {
    let mut e = Encoded::default();
    let mut compact = Some(compact);
    for it in items {
        e.counted += it.wire_len();
        if matches!(it, Out::End) {
            e.end = true;
            continue;
        }
        if *close_sent {
            continue;
        }
        match it {
            Out::Dgram { .. } => {
                // (every datagram of the batch, once)
                if let Some(c) = compact.take() {
                    let start = buf.len();
                    e.msgs += match c {
                        Some(c) => bundle_compact(stats, items, buf, c),
                        None => bundle(stats, items, buf),
                    };
                    e.extra = buf.len() - start;
                }
            }
            Out::Text(b) => {
                stats.msg(mix::OUT_TEXT);
                e.msgs += 1;
                frame::encode(frame::TEXT, b, buf)
            }
            Out::Raw(b) => {
                stats.msg(mix::OUT_HOST);
                e.msgs += 1;
                frame::encode(frame::BINARY, b, buf)
            }
            Out::Frame { data, src, dst } => {
                stats.msg(mix::OUT_FRAME);
                e.msgs += 1;
                one_frame(buf, data, *src, *dst)
            }
            Out::Ping(p) => {
                stats.msg(mix::OUT_PING);
                e.msgs += 1;
                frame::encode(frame::PING, p, buf)
            }
            Out::Pong(b) => {
                stats.msg(mix::OUT_PONG);
                e.msgs += 1;
                frame::encode(frame::PONG, b, buf)
            }
            Out::Close(p) => {
                frame::encode(frame::CLOSE, p, buf);
                *close_sent = true;
                e.close = true;
            }
            Out::End => {}
        }
    }
    e
}

/// a frame with its source and destination written in (the one copy a datagram gets); bytes 1-3 are reserved: 0 on
/// the wire, whatever the switch's copy holds there (compact.rs `mark`)
pub(crate) fn with_addrs(buf: &mut Vec<u8>, data: &[u8], src: u32, dst: u32) {
    buf.extend_from_slice(&[data[0], 0, 0, 0]);
    buf.extend_from_slice(&src.to_be_bytes());
    buf.extend_from_slice(&dst.to_be_bytes());
    buf.extend_from_slice(&data[12..]);
}

fn one_frame(buf: &mut Vec<u8>, data: &[u8], src: u32, dst: u32) {
    frame::header(frame::BINARY, data.len(), buf);
    with_addrs(buf, data, src, dst);
}

/// the datagrams as bundles of at most BUNDLE_OUT (entries of n = 0: each with its destination in it); one alone
/// goes as it is
fn bundle(stats: &Stats, items: &[Out], buf: &mut Vec<u8>) -> u64 {
    let mut dgrams = items.iter().filter_map(|it| match it {
        Out::Dgram { data, src, dst, .. } => Some((data, *src, *dst)),
        _ => None,
    });
    let Some(mut next) = dgrams.next() else { return 0 };
    let mut msgs = 0;
    let mut chunk: smallvec::SmallVec<[(&Bytes, u32, u32); 32]> = smallvec::SmallVec::new();
    loop {
        // a bundle takes datagrams while it stays within BUNDLE_OUT (the one that would not fit begins the next)
        chunk.clear();
        let mut sum = 0;
        let mut rest = None;
        loop {
            let l = 4 + next.0.len();
            if !chunk.is_empty() && sum + l > BUNDLE_OUT {
                rest = Some(next);
                break;
            }
            sum += l;
            chunk.push(next);
            match dgrams.next() {
                Some(d) => next = d,
                None => break,
            }
        }
        msgs += 1;
        if chunk.len() == 1 {
            let (d, src, dst) = chunk[0];
            stats.msg(mix::OUT_FRAME);
            one_frame(buf, d, src, dst);
        } else {
            stats.msg(mix::OUT_BUNDLE);
            frame::header(frame::BINARY, 4 + sum, buf);
            buf.extend_from_slice(&[KIND_BUNDLE, 0, 0, 0]);
            for (d, src, dst) in &chunk {
                let len = d.len() as u16;
                buf.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0]);
                buf.extend_from_slice(&len.to_be_bytes());
                with_addrs(buf, d, *src, *dst);
            }
            stats.bundles_out.inc();
        }
        match rest {
            Some(d) => next = d,
            None => return msgs,
        }
    }
}

/// the datagrams as compact bundles (compact.rs) of BUNDLE_OUT at most, a datagram alone in one too (its 16-byte
/// header costs more than a bundle's 4 and an entry's 5)
fn bundle_compact(stats: &Stats, items: &[Out], buf: &mut Vec<u8>, c: Compact<'_>) -> u64 {
    let Compact { own, mut refs, mut fp, others, body, stamp } = c;
    body.clear();
    body.extend_from_slice(&[compact::KIND_COMPACT, 0, 0, 0]);
    if let Some(s) = stamp {
        body[1] = compact::F_STAMPED;
        body.extend_from_slice(&s);
    }
    let (mut n, mut msgs) = (0, 0);
    let (now, mut moved) = (now_us(), [0u8; compact::TIMED_MAX]);
    for it in items {
        let Out::Dgram { data, src, dst, at: queued } = it else { continue };
        let data = compact::waited(data, if *queued != 0 { now.wrapping_sub(*queued) } else { 0 }, &mut moved);
        let at = body.len();
        compact::entry_fp(body, data, *src, *dst, own, refs.as_deref_mut(), fp.as_deref_mut(), others);
        stats.entry_out(data, *src, *dst, &body[at..]);
        // a bundle takes datagrams while it stays within BUNDLE_OUT (the one that would not fit begins the next; it
        // was written as the next one, in order, so the page reads the same entries the writer made)
        if n > 0 && body.len() > BUNDLE_OUT {
            compact_out(stats, buf, &body[..at]);
            msgs += 1;
            // (a stamp went with the first: what follows the header now is the next entry)
            body[1] = 0;
            body.drain(4..at);
            n = 0;
        }
        n += 1;
    }
    if n > 0 {
        compact_out(stats, buf, body);
        msgs += 1;
    }
    msgs
}

/// the switch's clock for a datagram's wait for the bundle clock: µs since its first reading, wrapping
pub(crate) fn now_us() -> u32 {
    static START: std::sync::OnceLock<std::time::Instant> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    START.get_or_init(std::time::Instant::now).elapsed().as_micros() as u32
}

fn compact_out(stats: &Stats, buf: &mut Vec<u8>, bundle: &[u8]) {
    stats.msg(mix::OUT_BUNDLE);
    frame::header(frame::BINARY, bundle.len(), buf);
    buf.extend_from_slice(bundle);
    stats.bundles_out.inc();
}

const SHARDS: usize = 16;

/// one of the clock's lists, on a cache line of its own
#[repr(align(128))]
struct Shard(Mutex<Vec<Arc<Conn>>>);

/// The bundle clock: the writers of the peers with datagrams waiting, woken every tick.  Its lists are sharded by
/// connection, so that senders to different receivers rarely meet on one lock, and each shard ticks on a task of its
/// own, at a phase of its own: the wake-ups of a crowd's writers are spread over the tick and over the runtime's
/// workers (one task waking them all put them all on its own worker, for the others to steal).  Its tick can change
/// while it runs (the switch's `bundle_tick`).  Each tick is the period give or take `jitter` of it, at random: the game
/// takes the smallest delay of a friend's snapshots in 2 s for the path's (roam_core.c off_estimate) and draws a solid
/// car where its driver is now from it, and a tick as long as the time between those snapshots (50 ms, roam_rate 20)
/// made each wait about as long as the one before, so the car came out behind by that wait (roam-pair, 2026-10-24: up
/// to 14 ms, 0.22 m off on average).  A tick that wanders gives each snapshot another wait, and the smallest of 2 s
/// is about none.
pub(crate) struct Clock {
    shards: Box<[Shard]>,
    period_us: AtomicU64,
    jitter: f64,
    /// which of a connection's flags says it is on this clock's list: 0 the bundle clock, 1 the slow one (away.rs), 2
    /// LAN play's (`LanOptions::lan_ms`).  Each one's tick wakes the writer, which takes all that waits.
    lane: usize,
}

impl Clock {
    pub(crate) fn new(period: Duration, jitter: f64, lane: usize) -> Self {
        let shards = (0..SHARDS).map(|_| Shard(Mutex::new(Vec::new()))).collect();
        let jitter = if jitter.is_finite() { jitter.clamp(0.0, 0.9) } else { 0.0 };
        Clock { shards, period_us: AtomicU64::new(period.as_micros() as u64), jitter, lane: lane.min(2) }
    }

    /// the next tick's length: the period, give or take `jitter` of it (`rng` a shard's own xorshift state)
    fn next_period(&self, rng: &mut u64) -> Duration {
        let p = self.period();
        if self.jitter <= 0.0 {
            return p;
        }
        *rng ^= *rng << 13;
        *rng ^= *rng >> 7;
        *rng ^= *rng << 17;
        let u = (*rng >> 11) as f64 / (1u64 << 53) as f64;
        p.mul_f64(1.0 + self.jitter * (2.0 * u - 1.0))
    }

    pub(crate) fn period(&self) -> Duration {
        Duration::from_micros(self.period_us.load(Relaxed).max(1))
    }

    pub(crate) fn set_period(&self, d: Duration) {
        self.period_us.store(d.as_micros() as u64, Relaxed);
    }

    fn arm(&self, conn: &Arc<Conn>) {
        self.shards[conn.id as usize % SHARDS].0.lock().push(conn.clone());
    }

    /// every armed writer of one shard woken (its flag cleared first: a datagram queued after it took its queue arms
    /// it again)
    fn tick(&self, shard: usize, spare: &mut Vec<Arc<Conn>>) {
        std::mem::swap(&mut *self.shards[shard].0.lock(), spare);
        for c in spare.drain(..) {
            c.out.armed[self.lane].store(false, Release);
            c.out.wake.notify_one();
        }
    }

    /// its tasks, until the switch is gone
    pub(crate) fn start(me: Weak<Clock>) {
        let Some(period) = me.upgrade().map(|c| c.period()) else { return };
        for shard in 0..SHARDS {
            let me = me.clone();
            let phase = period * shard as u32 / SHARDS as u32;
            let seed = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).map_or(0, |d| d.as_nanos() as u64);
            let mut rng = (seed ^ (shard as u64 + 1).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)) | 1;
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                let mut next = tokio::time::Instant::now() + phase;
                let mut spare = Vec::new();
                loop {
                    tokio::time::sleep_until(next).await;
                    let Some(c) = me.upgrade() else { return };
                    c.tick(shard, &mut spare);
                    // a tick that came late does not make the next ones come sooner
                    next = (next + c.next_period(&mut rng)).max(tokio::time::Instant::now());
                }
            });
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn dg(len: usize, dst: u32) -> Out {
        let mut d = vec![1u8; len];
        d[8..12].copy_from_slice(&0xFFFF_FFFFu32.to_be_bytes());
        Out::Dgram { data: Bytes::from(d), src: 0x0A4D_0002, dst, at: 0 }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_tick_wanders_within_its_jitter_and_keeps_its_mean() {
        let c = Clock::new(Duration::from_millis(50), 0.4, 0);
        let mut rng = 0x1234_5678_9ABC_DEF1u64;
        let ticks: Vec<Duration> = (0..10_000).map(|_| c.next_period(&mut rng)).collect();
        assert!(ticks.iter().all(|t| (Duration::from_millis(30)..=Duration::from_millis(70)).contains(t)));
        let mean = ticks.iter().sum::<Duration>() / ticks.len() as u32;
        assert!((Duration::from_micros(49_500)..=Duration::from_micros(50_500)).contains(&mean), "{mean:?}");
        assert!(ticks.iter().any(|t| *t < Duration::from_millis(32)) && ticks.iter().any(|t| *t > Duration::from_millis(68)));
        assert_eq!(Clock::new(Duration::from_millis(50), 0.0, 0).next_period(&mut rng), Duration::from_millis(50));
        assert_eq!(Clock::new(Duration::from_millis(50), f64::NAN, 0).next_period(&mut rng), Duration::from_millis(50));
    }

    #[test]
    fn header_lengths_match_rfc6455() {
        for len in [0, 1, 125, 126, 1000, 65535, 65536, 100_000] {
            let mut b = Vec::new();
            frame::header(frame::BINARY, len, &mut b);
            assert_eq!(b.len(), header_len(len), "{len}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn datagrams_become_bundles_of_at_most_bundle_out_one_alone_as_it_is() {
        let stats = Stats::default();
        // one alone: as it is, its addresses written in
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        let mut cs = false;
        let e = encode(&stats, &[dg(20, 0x0A4D_0103)], &mut buf, &mut cs, None);
        assert_eq!(e.extra, buf.len());
        assert_eq!(buf[0], 0x82);
        assert_eq!(buf[1] as usize, 20);
        assert_eq!(&buf[2 + 4..2 + 8], &0x0A4D_0002u32.to_be_bytes());
        assert_eq!(&buf[2 + 8..2 + 12], &0x0A4D_0103u32.to_be_bytes());
        assert_eq!(stats.bundles_out.get(), 0);
        // 8 KB datagrams: four to a bundle (4 x 8004 bytes fit in 32 KB), then the fifth alone
        let items: Vec<Out> = (0..5).map(|i| dg(8000, i)).collect();
        buf.clear();
        encode(&stats, &items, &mut buf, &mut cs, None);
        assert_eq!(stats.bundles_out.get(), 1);
        assert_eq!(buf[0], 0x82);
        assert_eq!(buf[1], 126);
        let len = u16::from_be_bytes([buf[2], buf[3]]) as usize;
        assert_eq!(len, 4 + 4 * 8004);
        assert_eq!(buf[4], KIND_BUNDLE);
        let second = 4 + len;
        assert_eq!(u16::from_be_bytes([buf[second + 2], buf[second + 3]]), 8000);
        assert_eq!(&buf[second + 4 + 8..second + 4 + 12], &4u32.to_be_bytes());
        assert_eq!(buf.len(), second + 4 + 8000);
        // 4 x 8192 + 4 x 4 is over 32 KB: three, then one alone
        let items: Vec<Out> = (0..4).map(|i| dg(8192, i)).collect();
        buf.clear();
        encode(&stats, &items, &mut buf, &mut cs, None);
        assert_eq!(stats.bundles_out.get(), 2);
        assert_eq!(u16::from_be_bytes([buf[2], buf[3]]) as usize, 4 + 3 * 8196);
    }

    // a newcomer's welcome, queued before its first datagrams, goes before their bundle (a page in line takes bundles
    // from its first moment); what came after the first datagram goes after the bundle; after a close frame nothing
    #[test]
    fn the_welcome_goes_before_the_first_bundle() {
        let stats = Stats::default();
        let (mut buf, mut cs) = (Vec::new(), false);
        let items = vec![Out::Text(Bytes::from_static(b"w")), dg(20, 1), Out::Text(Bytes::from_static(b"p")), dg(20, 2)];
        encode(&stats, &items, &mut buf, &mut cs, None);
        assert_eq!(&buf[..3], &[0x81, 1, b'w']);
        assert_eq!(&buf[3..5], &[0x82, 4 + 2 * 24]);
        assert_eq!(buf[5], KIND_BUNDLE);
        assert_eq!(&buf[5 + 4 + 2 * 24..], &[0x81, 1, b'p']);
        buf.clear();
        let items = vec![Out::Close(Bytes::from_static(&[3, 0xE8])), dg(20, 1)];
        encode(&stats, &items, &mut buf, &mut false, None);
        assert_eq!(buf, [0x88, 2, 3, 0xE8], "nothing after the close frame");
    }

    #[test]
    fn nothing_goes_after_a_close_frame() {
        let stats = Stats::default();
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        let mut cs = false;
        let items =
            vec![Out::Text(Bytes::from_static(b"a")), Out::Close(Bytes::from_static(&[3, 0xF5])), Out::Text(Bytes::from_static(b"b"))];
        let e = encode(&stats, &items, &mut buf, &mut cs, None);
        assert!(e.close && cs);
        assert_eq!(buf, [0x81, 1, b'a', 0x88, 2, 3, 0xF5]);
        assert_eq!(e.counted, 3 + 4 + 3);
    }
}

//! Free roam's car states by their fields (a page whose hello said "fpred":1 besides "delta":1): a friend's SNAP of one
//! state (runtime/roam_core.c rc_encode, put_state, put_statex) goes to it as the fields that differ from what the page
//! can work out itself, each as a small number.  A byte-level delta (compact.rs `Refs`) sends every byte a float's
//! last bits touched; here
//! - the position goes in millimetres, the velocity in centimetres a second and the time in steps of 256 µs: the page
//!   writes back the floats and microseconds those make, so the game gets the state rounded that far (at most 0.5 mm,
//!   0.5 cm/s and 128 µs off, about 4 mm along the road at 30 m/s), with a CRC that checks out;
//! - the time is taken to go on as it went (the last interval again), the sequence number too, and the position by the
//!   last one's velocity over the time between: what is left of them is mostly nothing or a few millimetres;
//! - every other field is taken to be what it was, and goes as its difference when it is not.
//!
//! On real drives (roam-pair, 4 games, 2026-10-24) a car state took 36 bytes an entry as a byte delta, about 20 so.
//!
//! An entry: [0] `F_FPRED`, [1..2] the source's low 16 bits, [3] the length of what follows (at most 255: a longer one
//! goes as the byte delta instead); then a bitmap of the fields that differ (LEB128, 7 a byte, field 0 in bit 0, the
//! groups of zeros at the end left out), then each of those as a zigzag LEB128 varint of the difference (`diff`).  The
//! fields are in `NF` order, the often-changing first.  Both ends keep each source's last state (as the page restores
//! it: the rounded one), and the one before for the time and the sequence; a source with none goes against zeros.  Past
//! `REFS_MAX` sources, a new one clears them all first, on both ends.  Anything else of the datagram that a state of
//! this layout cannot carry (more states than one, a field of a newer core) goes as before, and leaves this state alone.
//!
//! The arithmetic is integers only, the same on the page (web/src/net/proto.ts `FpredState`): the rounding of the
//! position, the velocity and the time is done here, once; the page and this end only turn integers into floats (one
//! IEEE division and a conversion to f32, the same everywhere).

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::hash::BuildHasherDefault;

use crate::compact::{KeyHash, REFS_MAX};

/// the entry's flags byte: the kind 1 with F_ROAM and F_WHOLE, which together go with nothing else (compact.rs)
pub const F_FPRED: u8 = 0x61;
/// the fields: the time and sequence number first (a standing car's only changes, mostly), then what a moving one
/// changes
pub const NF: usize = 53;
const T: usize = 0; // steps of 256 µs, 24 bits
const SEQ: usize = 1;
const P: usize = 2; // x, y, z: millimetres
const V: usize = 5; // centimetres a second
const Q: usize = 8; // 4, i16
const W: usize = 12; // 3, i16
const SPEED: usize = 15;
const RPM: usize = 16;
const STEER: usize = 17;
const WZ: usize = 18; // 4, i16
const ENG: usize = 22;
const EACC: usize = 23;
const EDCL: usize = 24;
const THR: usize = 25;
const BRK: usize = 26;
const GEAR: usize = 27;
const BITS: usize = 28;
const NOS: usize = 29;
const HYD: usize = 30;
const THUMPS: usize = 31;
const EBASE: usize = 32;
const SLIP: usize = 33; // 12 bytes: each wheel's two slips and its surface
const XLEN: usize = 45;
const CLOCK: usize = 46;
const STATUS: usize = 47;
const EPOCH: usize = 48;
const CFG_REV: usize = 49;
const N: usize = 50;
const FLAGS: usize = 51;
const SENDER: usize = 52;
/// runtime/roam_core.h RC_HF_STATEX: the header's flag for a state's extension
const HF_STATEX: i64 = 0x0040;

/// a field's width when its difference wraps (bits), 0 for a signed one that does not
const fn width(i: usize) -> u32 {
    match i {
        RPM | ENG | SEQ | CFG_REV | FLAGS => 16,
        T => 24,
        SENDER => 32,
        EACC | EDCL | THR | BRK | GEAR | BITS | NOS | HYD | THUMPS | EBASE | XLEN | CLOCK | STATUS | EPOCH | N => 8,
        i if i >= SLIP && i < SLIP + 12 => 8,
        _ => 0,
    }
}

/// each field's `width` as the shift there and back that wraps a difference to it (`signed`); 0 for one that does not
const SHIFT: [u32; NF] = {
    let mut s = [0; NF];
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < NF {
        s[i] = if width(i) == 0 { 0 } else { 64 - width(i) };
        i += 1;
    }
    s
};

/// a car state's fields (`NF`), as integers
pub type Fields = [i64; NF];

/// what an extension of `x` bytes holds past the wheels' heights and the nitrous, as roam_core.c get_statex reads it:
/// the hydraulics, the wheels' slips, the engine; None when a newer core's fields follow those (or it is too short)
fn layout(x: usize) -> Option<(bool, bool, bool)> {
    let (hyd, slip) = (x >= 11, x >= 23);
    let base = 9 + if hyd { 2 } else { 0 } + if slip { 12 } else { 0 };
    let eng = x >= base + 5;
    (x >= 9 && base + if eng { 5 } else { 0 } == x).then_some((hyd, slip, eng))
}

fn rd16(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> i64 {
    u16::from_le_bytes([b[o], b[o + 1]]) as i64
}
fn rds16(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> i64 {
    i16::from_le_bytes([b[o], b[o + 1]]) as i64
}
fn rd32(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_le_bytes([b[o], b[o + 1], b[o + 2], b[o + 3]])
}
fn rdf(b: &[u8], o: usize) -> f32 {
    f32::from_le_bytes([b[o], b[o + 1], b[o + 2], b[o + 3]])
}

/// x to the nearest whole number, halves away from zero (`f64::round`), for the x `fields` rounds: an f32 times 1000 or
/// 100, within 1e9.  Such an x has at most 31 significant bits, so x ± 0.5 is exact and the cast's truncation is the
/// rounding.  `f64::round` is a call into the C library on the x86-64 the image is built for (no SSE4.1): six for every
/// car state to every friend took 1.7 % of the switch's own work on nfsu2.xyz (2026-11-05).
fn round(x: f64) -> i64 {
    (x + 0.5f64.copysign(x)) as i64
}

/// The fields of a SNAP's body (the datagram from its sender's id on, without its CRC: what a compact entry carries),
/// rounded as they go; None when it is not a SNAP of one state of this layout, or a float is not a finite one this
/// can carry.
pub fn fields(body: &[u8]) -> Option<Fields> {
    if body.len() < 66 || body[12] != 1 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut v = [0i64; NF];
    v[SENDER] = rd32(body, 0) as i64;
    v[SEQ] = rd16(body, 4);
    v[FLAGS] = rd16(body, 6);
    v[STATUS] = body[8] as i64;
    v[EPOCH] = body[9] as i64;
    v[CFG_REV] = rd16(body, 10);
    v[N] = 1;
    v[CLOCK] = body[13] as i64;
    v[T] = ((rd32(body, 14) as i64 + 128) >> 8) & 0xFF_FFFF;
    for i in 0..3 {
        let (p, s) = (rdf(body, 18 + 4 * i), rdf(body, 30 + 4 * i));
        if !p.is_finite() || p.abs() > 1e6 || !s.is_finite() || s.abs() > 1e6 {
            return None;
        }
        v[P + i] = round(p as f64 * 1000.0);
        v[V + i] = round(s as f64 * 100.0);
    }
    for i in 0..4 {
        v[Q + i] = rds16(body, 42 + 2 * i);
    }
    for i in 0..3 {
        v[W + i] = rds16(body, 50 + 2 * i);
    }
    v[STEER] = rds16(body, 56);
    v[THR] = body[58] as i64;
    v[BRK] = body[59] as i64;
    v[RPM] = rd16(body, 60);
    v[SPEED] = rds16(body, 62);
    v[GEAR] = body[64] as i64;
    v[BITS] = body[65] as i64;
    let mut end = 66;
    if v[FLAGS] & HF_STATEX != 0 {
        if body.len() < 67 {
            return None;
        }
        let x = body[66] as usize;
        v[XLEN] = x as i64;
        end = 67 + x;
        if x > 0 {
            let (hyd, slip, eng) = layout(x)?;
            if body.len() < end {
                return None;
            }
            for i in 0..4 {
                v[WZ + i] = rds16(body, 67 + 2 * i);
            }
            v[NOS] = body[75] as i64;
            let mut k = 76;
            if hyd {
                v[HYD] = body[76] as i64;
                v[THUMPS] = body[77] as i64;
                k = 78;
            }
            if slip {
                for i in 0..12 {
                    v[SLIP + i] = body[78 + i] as i64;
                }
                k = 90;
            }
            if eng {
                v[ENG] = rd16(body, k);
                v[EACC] = body[k + 2] as i64;
                v[EDCL] = body[k + 3] as i64;
                v[EBASE] = body[k + 4] as i64;
            }
        }
    }
    (body.len() == end).then_some(v)
}

/// The body a state's fields make (the page does the same, proto.ts): its floats and time as the page writes them back.
/// False when the fields make no state of this layout (nothing is written then).
pub fn write(v: &Fields, out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> bool {
    let x = v[XLEN] as usize;
    let groups = if v[FLAGS] & HF_STATEX != 0 && x > 0 {
        match layout(x) {
            Some(g) => Some(g),
            None => return false,
        }
    } else {
        None
    };
    if v[N] != 1 || !(0..256).contains(&v[XLEN]) {
        return false;
    }
    out.extend_from_slice(&(v[SENDER] as u32).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(v[SEQ] as u16).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(v[FLAGS] as u16).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&[v[STATUS] as u8, v[EPOCH] as u8]);
    out.extend_from_slice(&(v[CFG_REV] as u16).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&[1, v[CLOCK] as u8]);
    out.extend_from_slice(&((v[T] as u32) << 8).to_le_bytes());
    for i in 0..3 {
        out.extend_from_slice(&((v[P + i] as f64 / 1000.0) as f32).to_le_bytes());
    }
    for i in 0..3 {
        out.extend_from_slice(&((v[V + i] as f64 / 100.0) as f32).to_le_bytes());
    }
    for i in Q..Q + 4 {
        out.extend_from_slice(&(v[i] as i16).to_le_bytes());
    }
    for i in W..W + 3 {
        out.extend_from_slice(&(v[i] as i16).to_le_bytes());
    }
    out.extend_from_slice(&(v[STEER] as i16).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&[v[THR] as u8, v[BRK] as u8]);
    out.extend_from_slice(&(v[RPM] as u16).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&(v[SPEED] as i16).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&[v[GEAR] as u8, v[BITS] as u8]);
    if v[FLAGS] & HF_STATEX != 0 {
        out.push(x as u8);
        if let Some((hyd, slip, eng)) = groups {
            for i in WZ..WZ + 4 {
                out.extend_from_slice(&(v[i] as i16).to_le_bytes());
            }
            out.push(v[NOS] as u8);
            if hyd {
                out.extend_from_slice(&[v[HYD] as u8, v[THUMPS] as u8]);
            }
            if slip {
                out.extend((SLIP..SLIP + 12).map(|i| v[i] as u8));
            }
            if eng {
                out.extend_from_slice(&(v[ENG] as u16).to_le_bytes());
                out.extend_from_slice(&[v[EACC] as u8, v[EDCL] as u8, v[EBASE] as u8]);
            }
        }
    }
    true
}

/// a SNAP's body as the game gets it through this (rounded; None: it would go as before, as it is)
pub fn rounded(body: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let v = fields(body)?;
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(body.len());
    write(&v, &mut out).then_some(out)
}

/// what both ends keep of a source: its last state, and the one before's time and sequence number (`two`: there was one)
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Last {
    v: Fields,
    t2: i64,
    seq2: i64,
    two: bool,
}

/// the value field i is taken to have: its last, the time and sequence number as they went, the position carried on by
/// the last velocity for the time since (`t`: this state's time, when known)
fn predict(last: Option<&Last>, t: Option<i64>) -> Fields {
    let Some(l) = last else { return [0; NF] };
    let mut w = l.v;
    if l.two {
        w[T] = (2 * l.v[T] - l.t2) & 0xFF_FFFF;
        w[SEQ] = (2 * l.v[SEQ] - l.seq2) & 0xFFFF;
    }
    if let Some(t) = t {
        let dt = signed(t - l.v[T], 24);
        // at most about a second: anything longer is a new start, not a drive
        if (0..=4096).contains(&dt) {
            for i in 0..3 {
                // mm = cm/s x 10 x dt x 256 µs, rounded: the velocity times dt x 16 / 6250
                w[P + i] = l.v[P + i] + (l.v[V + i] * dt * 16 + 3125).div_euclid(6250);
            }
        }
    }
    w
}

/// a difference of `bits` bits, signed (0: as it is): its low bits, the top one the sign
fn signed(d: i64, bits: u32) -> i64 {
    if bits == 0 {
        return d;
    }
    (d << (64 - bits)) >> (64 - bits)
}

fn diff(i: usize, cur: i64, want: i64) -> i64 {
    signed(cur - want, width(i))
}

fn apply(i: usize, want: i64, d: i64) -> i64 {
    match width(i) {
        0 => want + d,
        b => (want + d) & ((1 << b) - 1),
    }
}

/// u as a LEB128 varint into e at n: where it ends (e holds the 10 bytes of the longest)
fn put_varint_at(e: &mut [u8], mut n: usize, mut u: u64) -> usize {
    while u >= 0x80 {
        e[n] = u as u8 | 0x80;
        u >>= 7;
        n += 1;
    }
    e[n] = u as u8;
    n + 1
}

fn get_varint(b: &[u8], at: &mut usize) -> Option<u64> {
    let mut u = 0u64;
    for k in 0..10 {
        let x = *b.get(*at)?;
        *at += 1;
        u |= ((x & 0x7F) as u64) << (7 * k);
        if x & 0x80 == 0 {
            return Some(u);
        }
    }
    None
}

/// One end's last states by source (the switch's writer for its page, or a decoder of the page's: `Decoder`).
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Fpred {
    last: HashMap<u16, Last, BuildHasherDefault<KeyHash>>,
}

impl Fpred {
    fn keep(&mut self, src: u16, v: &Fields) {
        if let Some(l) = self.last.get_mut(&src) {
            (l.t2, l.seq2, l.two) = (l.v[T], l.v[SEQ], true);
            l.v = *v;
            return;
        }
        if self.last.len() >= REFS_MAX {
            self.last.clear();
        }
        self.last.insert(src, Last { v: *v, t2: 0, seq2: 0, two: false });
    }

    /// The entry of a state from `src` into `buf`; false when it would be longer than 255 (nothing written, nothing
    /// kept: it goes as before).
    ///
    /// What `predict` makes, without making it: each field against its last value, and then the time, the sequence
    /// number and the position against theirs; the source looked up once and its last state brought up to date where it
    /// is.  The switch's writers do this for every car state to every friend, and the whole prediction's copies (three
    /// of 424 bytes and a second lookup) were most of it (nfsu2.xyz, 2026-11-05: a fifth of the switch's own work).
    /// The same bytes as `predict`'s way (the tests' `encode_by_predict`).
    pub fn encode(&mut self, buf: &mut Vec<u8>, src: u16, cur: &Fields) -> bool {
        let last = self.last.get_mut(&src);
        let mut d = [0i64; NF];
        let mut mask = 0u64;
        match last.as_deref() {
            None => {
                for i in 0..NF {
                    d[i] = (cur[i] << SHIFT[i]) >> SHIFT[i];
                }
            }
            Some(l) => {
                for i in 0..NF {
                    d[i] = ((cur[i] - l.v[i]) << SHIFT[i]) >> SHIFT[i];
                }
                if l.two {
                    d[T] = diff(T, cur[T], (2 * l.v[T] - l.t2) & 0xFF_FFFF);
                    d[SEQ] = diff(SEQ, cur[SEQ], (2 * l.v[SEQ] - l.seq2) & 0xFFFF);
                }
                let dt = signed(cur[T] - l.v[T], 24);
                if (0..=4096).contains(&dt) {
                    for i in P..P + 3 {
                        d[i] = diff(i, cur[i], l.v[i] + (l.v[i + V - P] * dt * 16 + 3125).div_euclid(6250));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        for (i, &x) in d.iter().enumerate() {
            mask |= ((x != 0) as u64) << i;
        }
        // the entry made on the stack (its head, the bitmap and up to NF varints of 10 bytes at most), then added at once
        let mut e = [0u8; 4 + 10 * (NF + 1)];
        let [s0, s1] = src.to_be_bytes();
        (e[0], e[1], e[2]) = (F_FPRED, s0, s1);
        let mut n = put_varint_at(&mut e, 4, mask);
        let mut m = mask;
        while m != 0 {
            let x = d[m.trailing_zeros() as usize];
            m &= m - 1;
            n = put_varint_at(&mut e, n, ((x << 1) ^ (x >> 63)) as u64);
        }
        if n - 4 > 255 {
            return false;
        }
        e[3] = (n - 4) as u8;
        buf.extend_from_slice(&e[..n]);
        match last {
            Some(l) => {
                (l.t2, l.seq2, l.two) = (l.v[T], l.v[SEQ], true);
                l.v = *cur;
            }
            None => self.keep(src, cur),
        }
        true
    }

    /// An entry's state from `src` (`e`: what follows its 4-byte head) as its body (the datagram from its sender's id on,
    /// without the CRC); None when it is broken.  What the page does (proto.ts `FpredState.take`).
    pub fn decode(&mut self, src: u16, e: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        let mut at = 0;
        let mask = get_varint(e, &mut at)?;
        if mask >> NF != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        let mut d = [0i64; NF];
        for (i, x) in d.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            if mask >> i & 1 == 1 {
                let u = get_varint(e, &mut at)?;
                *x = (u >> 1) as i64 ^ -((u & 1) as i64);
            }
        }
        if at != e.len() {
            return None;
        }
        let last = self.last.get(&src);
        let t = apply(T, predict(last, None)[T], d[T]);
        let want = predict(last, Some(t));
        let mut cur = [0i64; NF];
        for i in 0..NF {
            cur[i] = apply(i, want[i], d[i]);
        }
        let mut body = Vec::with_capacity(96);
        if !write(&cur, &mut body) {
            return None;
        }
        self.keep(src, &cur);
        Some(body)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// a SNAP's body (the datagram from its sender's id on, without the CRC) as roam_core.c rc_encode makes it: one
    /// state, with an extension of `x` bytes when `x` is Some (its fields from `k`, so that each state differs)
    pub(crate) fn body(sender: u32, seq: u16, t: u32, p: [f32; 3], v: [f32; 3], k: i32, x: Option<u8>) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut b = Vec::new();
        b.extend_from_slice(&sender.to_le_bytes());
        b.extend_from_slice(&seq.to_le_bytes());
        b.extend_from_slice(&(if x.is_some() { 0x0040u16 } else { 0 } | 0x0020).to_le_bytes());
        b.extend_from_slice(&[2, 7]);
        b.extend_from_slice(&0x0102u16.to_le_bytes());
        b.extend_from_slice(&[1, 3]);
        b.extend_from_slice(&t.to_le_bytes());
        for f in p.iter().chain(v.iter()) {
            b.extend_from_slice(&f.to_le_bytes());
        }
        for q in [100 + k, -200, 30000 - k, 5] {
            b.extend_from_slice(&(q as i16).to_le_bytes());
        }
        for w in [k * 3, -k, 7] {
            b.extend_from_slice(&(w as i16).to_le_bytes());
        }
        b.extend_from_slice(&((k * 101) as i16).to_le_bytes());
        b.extend_from_slice(&[200, (k % 3) as u8]);
        b.extend_from_slice(&(3000 + 7 * k as u16).to_le_bytes());
        b.extend_from_slice(&((1500 + k) as i16).to_le_bytes());
        b.extend_from_slice(&[4, 0x10]);
        if let Some(x) = x {
            b.push(x);
            if x > 0 {
                for i in 0..4 {
                    b.extend_from_slice(&((-300 + k + i) as i16).to_le_bytes());
                }
                b.push(0);
                let (hyd, slip, eng) = layout(x as usize).expect("a layout");
                if hyd {
                    b.extend_from_slice(&[1, 2]);
                }
                if slip {
                    b.extend((0..12).map(|i| (i * 9 + k) as u8));
                }
                if eng {
                    b.extend_from_slice(&(4000 + k as u16).to_le_bytes());
                    b.extend_from_slice(&[10, 20, 30]);
                }
            }
        }
        b
    }

    /// through an encoder and a decoder (the switch's writer and the page): what the page writes is the rounded body
    fn through(enc: &mut Fpred, dec: &mut Fpred, src: u16, b: &[u8]) -> usize {
        let v = fields(b).expect("a state this carries");
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        assert!(enc.encode(&mut buf, src, &v));
        assert_eq!(buf[0], F_FPRED);
        assert_eq!(u16::from_be_bytes([buf[1], buf[2]]), src);
        assert_eq!(buf[3] as usize, buf.len() - 4);
        let got = dec.decode(src, &buf[4..]).expect("it decodes");
        assert_eq!(got, rounded(b).unwrap(), "the rounded body");
        buf.len()
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_extension_comes_back_rounded() {
        for x in [None, Some(0), Some(9), Some(11), Some(16), Some(23), Some(28)] {
            let (mut enc, mut dec) = (Fpred::default(), Fpred::default());
            for k in 0..5 {
                let b =
                    body(0xABCD_0001, 10 + k as u16, 1_000_000 + 50_000 * k as u32, [1695.123, -884.5, 24.25], [12.5, -3.25, 0.01], k, x);
                through(&mut enc, &mut dec, 0x0102, &b);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_rounding_is_that_far_and_no_farther() {
        let b = body(1, 1, 123_456_789, [1695.1234, -884.5006, 24.2496], [12.345, -3.2549, 0.004], 0, Some(16));
        let r = rounded(&b).unwrap();
        for i in 0..3 {
            let (a, c) = (rdf(&b, 18 + 4 * i) as f64, rdf(&r, 18 + 4 * i) as f64);
            assert!((a - c).abs() <= 0.0005 + 1e-4, "position {i}: {a} {c}");
            let (a, c) = (rdf(&b, 30 + 4 * i) as f64, rdf(&r, 30 + 4 * i) as f64);
            assert!((a - c).abs() <= 0.005 + 1e-6, "velocity {i}: {a} {c}");
        }
        assert!((rd32(&b, 14) as i64 - rd32(&r, 14) as i64).abs() <= 128);
        assert_eq!(b[42..], r[42..], "the rest as it was");
        assert_eq!(b[..14], r[..14]);
    }

    // a car driving a circle at 20 a second, its frames a little late now and then: each comes back rounded, a moving
    // one in a few bytes, a standing one in fewer
    #[test]
    fn a_drive_is_a_few_bytes_a_state() {
        let (mut enc, mut dec) = (Fpred::default(), Fpred::default());
        let (mut moving, mut standing) = (0, 0);
        let mut t = 4_000_000_000u32; // wraps on the way
        for k in 0..400i32 {
            t = t.wrapping_add(50_000 + if k % 7 == 0 { 16_667 } else { 0 });
            let a = k as f64 * 0.05;
            let (p, v) = if k < 300 {
                (
                    [(1000.0 + 40.0 * a.cos()) as f32, (-500.0 + 40.0 * a.sin()) as f32, 24.0],
                    [(-40.0 * a.sin()) as f32, (40.0 * a.cos()) as f32, 0.0],
                )
            } else {
                ([1040.0, -500.0, 24.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
            };
            let b = body(7, k as u16, t, p, v, if k < 300 { k } else { 300 }, Some(16));
            let n = through(&mut enc, &mut dec, 0x0305, &b);
            if k > 2 && k < 300 {
                moving += n;
            } else if k > 302 {
                standing += n;
            }
        }
        let (m, s) = (moving as f64 / 297.0, standing as f64 / 97.0);
        assert!(m < 30.0 && s < 8.0, "{m:.1} bytes a moving state, {s:.1} a standing one");
    }

    #[test]
    fn what_this_cannot_carry_goes_as_before() {
        let ok = body(1, 1, 1, [1.0; 3], [0.0; 3], 0, Some(16));
        assert!(fields(&ok).is_some());
        let mut three = ok.clone();
        three[12] = 3;
        assert!(fields(&three).is_none(), "more states than one");
        for x in [10u8, 12, 14, 24, 30] {
            let mut b = body(1, 1, 1, [1.0; 3], [0.0; 3], 0, Some(0));
            b[66] = x;
            b.extend(std::iter::repeat_n(0, x as usize));
            assert!(fields(&b).is_none(), "an extension of {x}: a newer core's fields");
        }
        for f in [f32::NAN, f32::INFINITY, 2e6] {
            assert!(fields(&body(1, 1, 1, [f, 0.0, 0.0], [0.0; 3], 0, None)).is_none());
            assert!(fields(&body(1, 1, 1, [0.0; 3], [0.0, f, 0.0], 0, None)).is_none());
        }
        let mut long = ok.clone();
        long.push(0);
        assert!(fields(&long).is_none() && fields(&ok[..ok.len() - 1]).is_none(), "a length that is not the layout's");
        // fields that would take more than 255 bytes: not written, not kept
        let mut enc = Fpred::default();
        let mut big = [0i64; NF];
        for (i, x) in big.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            *x = if width(i) == 0 { 1 << 60 } else { (1 << width(i)) / 2 - 1 };
        }
        big[N] = 1;
        let mut buf = vec![9];
        assert!(!enc.encode(&mut buf, 5, &big) && buf == [9] && enc.last.is_empty());
    }

    // the time and the sequence number wrap, a frame is late (no prediction past a second), the epoch and the clock
    // change, a far friend gets every fourth: each still comes back rounded
    #[test]
    fn the_edges_of_the_predictions() {
        let (mut enc, mut dec) = (Fpred::default(), Fpred::default());
        let mut seq = 65_530u16;
        let mut t = u32::MAX - 120_000;
        for k in 0..30i32 {
            seq = seq.wrapping_add(if k > 20 { 4 } else { 1 });
            t = t.wrapping_add(match k {
                10 => 3_000_000,
                11 => 0,
                _ => 50_000,
            });
            let mut b = body(9, seq, t, [-12000.5, 300.25, -2.0], [-60.0, 1.5, -0.25], k, if k % 2 == 0 { Some(16) } else { Some(28) });
            if k == 15 {
                b[9] = 8; // a teleport
                b[13] = 4; // a re-anchored clock
            }
            if k > 20 {
                b[6] |= 4; // every fourth
            }
            through(&mut enc, &mut dec, 0x0909, &b);
        }
    }

    // past REFS_MAX sources both ends forget them all at once, and still agree
    #[test]
    fn many_sources_both_ends_forget_together() {
        let (mut enc, mut dec) = (Fpred::default(), Fpred::default());
        for round in 0..3u32 {
            for s in 0..(REFS_MAX as u16 + 40) {
                let b =
                    body(s as u32, round as u16, 1_000_000 * round + s as u32, [s as f32, 2.0, 3.0], [1.0, 0.0, 0.0], s as i32, Some(11));
                through(&mut enc, &mut dec, s, &b);
            }
            assert!(enc.last.len() <= REFS_MAX && enc.last.len() == dec.last.len());
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_broken_entry_decodes_to_nothing() {
        let mut enc = Fpred::default();
        let b = body(1, 1, 1, [1.0; 3], [0.0; 3], 0, Some(16));
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        assert!(enc.encode(&mut buf, 3, &fields(&b).unwrap()));
        let e = &buf[4..];
        assert!(Fpred::default().decode(3, &e[..e.len() - 1]).is_none(), "cut short");
        let mut more = e.to_vec();
        more.push(0);
        assert!(Fpred::default().decode(3, &more).is_none(), "one too many");
        assert!(Fpred::default().decode(3, &[0xFF; 9]).is_none(), "a bitmap past the fields");
    }

    fn put_varint(buf: &mut Vec<u8>, mut u: u64) {
        while u >= 0x80 {
            buf.push(u as u8 | 0x80);
            u >>= 7;
        }
        buf.push(u as u8);
    }

    /// `encode` as it was until 2026-11-05: the whole prediction (`predict`), then the differences, then `keep`
    fn encode_by_predict(f: &mut Fpred, buf: &mut Vec<u8>, src: u16, cur: &Fields) -> bool {
        let want = predict(f.last.get(&src), Some(cur[T]));
        let start = buf.len();
        buf.push(F_FPRED);
        buf.extend_from_slice(&src.to_be_bytes());
        buf.push(0);
        let mut d = [0i64; NF];
        let mut mask = 0u64;
        for i in 0..NF {
            d[i] = diff(i, cur[i], want[i]);
            if d[i] != 0 {
                mask |= 1 << i;
            }
        }
        put_varint(buf, mask);
        for &x in d.iter().filter(|&&x| x != 0) {
            put_varint(buf, ((x << 1) ^ (x >> 63)) as u64);
        }
        let len = buf.len() - start - 4;
        if len > 255 {
            buf.truncate(start);
            return false;
        }
        buf[start + 3] = len as u8;
        f.keep(src, cur);
        true
    }

    /// xorshift64*, for the tests' made-up states
    struct Rng(u64);
    impl Rng {
        fn next(&mut self) -> u64 {
            self.0 ^= self.0 >> 12;
            self.0 ^= self.0 << 25;
            self.0 ^= self.0 >> 27;
            self.0.wrapping_mul(0x2545_F491_4F6C_DD1D)
        }
        fn below(&mut self, n: u64) -> u64 {
            self.next() % n
        }
    }

    // the encoder and `predict`'s way give the same bytes, the same answer and keep the same: over states that drive,
    // stand, jump in time (back, past a second), wrap their time and sequence, change any field, come from more
    // sources than REFS_MAX, and now and then cannot go in 255 bytes
    #[test]
    fn the_encoder_is_predicts_way_byte_for_byte() {
        let mut rng = Rng(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
        let (mut a, mut b) = (Fpred::default(), Fpred::default());
        let mut state: HashMap<u16, Fields> = HashMap::new();
        let (mut said, mut long) = (0, 0);
        for k in 0..400_000u32 {
            // most from a few sources; some from many (forgetting them all past REFS_MAX)
            let src = if rng.below(10) < 8 { rng.below(24) as u16 } else { rng.below(600) as u16 };
            let mut v = *state.entry(src).or_insert_with(|| {
                let mut v = [0i64; NF];
                v[N] = 1;
                v
            });
            let step = match rng.below(20) {
                0 => rng.below(1 << 24) as i64,
                1 => -(rng.below(300) as i64),
                2 => 4096 + rng.below(3) as i64,
                _ => 190 + rng.below(30) as i64,
            };
            v[T] = (v[T] + step) & 0xFF_FFFF;
            v[SEQ] = (v[SEQ] + 1 + (rng.below(8) == 0) as i64 * rng.below(5) as i64) & 0xFFFF;
            if rng.below(4) != 0 {
                for i in 0..3 {
                    v[V + i] = (v[V + i] + rng.below(201) as i64 - 100).clamp(-100_000_000, 100_000_000);
                    v[P + i] = (v[P + i] + v[V + i] / 20 + rng.below(9) as i64 - 4).clamp(-1_000_000_000, 1_000_000_000);
                }
            }
            // any field, within what `fields` makes of it (a position within 1e9 mm, a velocity 1e8 cm/s, an i16)
            for _ in 0..rng.below(6) {
                let i = rng.below(NF as u64) as usize;
                let within = |r: &mut Rng, m: i64| r.below(2 * m as u64 + 1) as i64 - m;
                v[i] = match (width(i), i) {
                    (0, P..=7) if i < V => within(&mut rng, 1_000_000_000),
                    (0, V..=7) => within(&mut rng, 100_000_000),
                    (0, _) => within(&mut rng, 32768),
                    (w, _) => rng.below(1 << w) as i64,
                };
            }
            // now and then one with every field at its widest, mostly too long for an entry (then nothing is kept: the
            // next goes against the last as before)
            if rng.below(5000) == 0 {
                for (i, x) in v.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                    *x = match (width(i), i) {
                        (0, V..=7) => 100_000_000,
                        (0, _) => 1 << 62,
                        (w, _) => (1 << w) / 2 - 1,
                    };
                }
            } else {
                state.insert(src, v);
            }
            let (mut x, mut y) = (vec![k as u8], vec![k as u8]);
            let (ok_a, ok_b) = (a.encode(&mut x, src, &v), encode_by_predict(&mut b, &mut y, src, &v));
            assert_eq!((ok_a, &x), (ok_b, &y), "state {k} from {src}");
            said += ok_a as u32;
            long += !ok_a as u32;
            if k % 997 == 0 {
                assert_eq!(a.last.len(), b.last.len());
                for (s, l) in &a.last {
                    let m = &b.last[s];
                    assert!(l.v == m.v && (l.t2, l.seq2, l.two) == (m.t2, m.seq2, m.two), "source {s} kept the same");
                }
            }
        }
        assert!(said > 390_000 && long > 0, "{said} written, {long} too long");
    }

    // `round` is `f64::round` for what `fields` rounds: positions and velocities of every 61st f32 within 1e6 (of every
    // one with `cargo test -- --ignored`), and the halves (n ± 0.5) within 1e9
    fn rounds_like_f64(step: usize) {
        for bits in (0..=u32::MAX).step_by(step) {
            let p = f32::from_bits(bits);
            if p.is_finite() && p.abs() <= 1e6 {
                for x in [p as f64 * 1000.0, p as f64 * 100.0] {
                    assert_eq!(round(x), x.round() as i64, "{p}: {x}");
                }
            }
        }
        for n in (-1_000_000_000i64..=1_000_000_000).step_by(step * 7919).chain(-3..=3) {
            for x in [n as f64 - 0.5, n as f64 + 0.5] {
                assert_eq!(round(x), x.round() as i64, "{x}");
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn round_is_f64_round() {
        rounds_like_f64(61);
    }

    #[test]
    #[ignore]
    fn round_is_f64_round_for_every_f32() {
        rounds_like_f64(1);
    }
}
