//! Who is on the switch (admission, a connection's close, the free addresses, "LAN full", the reservations, the peer
//! list's changes, the store): all of it under the one `members` lock, which routing never takes.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
use std::time::Duration;

use bytes::Bytes;
use indexmap::{IndexMap, IndexSet};
use nfsu2_util::json::write_str;
use nfsu2_util::{Bucket, now_ms, vip_str};
use serde_json::{Map, Value};

use crate::conn::{Conn, Out};
use crate::queue::Line;
use crate::text::{js_string, new_token, token_fits, token_hash};
use crate::{ADDRS, AttachCtx, CtlBuckets, LanSwitch, MASK, Pair, Peer, slot, vip_at};

/// A departed holder's address, kept for its token only.
pub(crate) struct Reservation {
    pub(crate) hash: [u8; 32],
    pub(crate) until: i64,
    /// the client (group) and site it was reserved for (none for one from the store)
    pub(crate) group: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub(crate) site: Option<Arc<str>>,
}

pub(crate) struct Members {
    /// in the order they came (a replaced holder keeps its place): the peer lists, info and the store show it
    pub(crate) peers: IndexMap<u32, Arc<Peer>>,
    /// the ones of `peers` whose LAN play is not off (in no order: LAN play's broadcasts, `LanSwitch::lan_all`)
    lan: IndexMap<u32, Arc<Peer>>,
    pub(crate) reserved: IndexMap<u32, Reservation>,
    next: usize,
    /// the peer list: addresses that joined, got their name or left since the last change went out, and the ones
    /// that left
    changed: IndexSet<u32>,
    left: IndexSet<u32>,
    delta_armed: bool,
    /// the store: a save waits (`era` tells a stale timer), the order of what was saved
    save_armed: bool,
    save_gen: u64,
    save_seq: u64,
    /// the pages waiting for a place (queue.rs)
    pub(crate) line: Line,
}

impl Members {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self {
        Members {
            peers: IndexMap::new(),
            lan: IndexMap::new(),
            reserved: IndexMap::new(),
            next: 0,
            changed: IndexSet::new(),
            left: IndexSet::new(),
            delta_armed: false,
            save_armed: false,
            save_gen: 0,
            save_seq: 0,
            line: Line::default(),
        }
    }

    /// a free address that is nobody's reservation, or 0: a reservation is never given to anyone but its token (the
    /// review of the audit's F1, in the crate doc).  (The expired ones went just before: `LanSwitch::expire`.)
    pub(crate) fn allocate(&mut self) -> u32 {
        for i in 0..ADDRS {
            let k = (self.next + i) % ADDRS;
            let c = vip_at(k);
            if !self.peers.contains_key(&c) && !self.reserved.contains_key(&c) {
                self.next = (k + 1) % ADDRS;
                return c;
            }
        }
        0
    }

    /// a newcomer has no place now: every place is taken, by a player or kept for one who dropped (a reservation holds
    /// its place as it holds its address, also where there are more addresses than places), so also every address
    /// (no address is both held and kept)
    pub(crate) fn full(&self, max_peers: usize) -> bool {
        let now = now_ms();
        self.peers.len() + self.reserved.values().filter(|r| r.until > now).count() >= max_peers.min(ADDRS)
    }
}

impl LanSwitch {
    /// A connection admitted: the address (given back only to the token that held it), the welcome, the peer list.
    /// None: not admitted now (closed already; "LAN full"; or, for a page that can wait, in line: queue.rs, the reader
    /// finds its peer once the line admits it).
    pub(crate) fn admit(&self, conn: &Arc<Conn>, ctx: &Arc<AttachCtx>, hello: Option<Map<String, Value>>) -> Option<Arc<Peer>> {
        if !conn.open() {
            return None;
        }
        let mut m = self.members.lock();
        let mut held = held_address(&m, hello.as_ref());
        // a page back with its ticket: its place in line again (it never had an address), or the place the line gave
        // it as its link went (its welcome lost with it: queue.rs `seated`)
        if held.0 == 0
            && ctx.queue
            && let Some(Value::String(t)) = hello.as_ref().and_then(|h| h.get("ticket"))
        {
            let t = t.clone();
            if self.rejoin(&mut m, conn, ctx, hello.clone(), &t) {
                drop(m);
                self.let_in();
                return conn.peer.lock().clone();
            }
            held = m.line.seated_for(&m.peers, &m.reserved, &t);
        }
        // a newcomer waits while anyone does
        let place = self.place(&mut m, held, false);
        match place {
            Some((vip, old, resumed)) => {
                let (peer, count) = self.seat(&mut m, conn, ctx, hello, vip, old);
                drop(m);
                if let Some(f) = &ctx.on_join {
                    f(peer.vip, resumed, count);
                }
                Some(peer)
            }
            None => {
                if !(ctx.queue && self.enqueue(&mut m, conn, ctx, hello)) {
                    self.stats.refused.inc();
                    drop(m);
                    conn.close(lan_full());
                }
                None
            }
        }
    }

    /// A place for one who asks: the address its token held (`held`: it, and the connection of the same client it
    /// replaces, which takes no new place; a reservation's place was never free), or a free one; None when there is
    /// none for it now: the switch full, or (unless `first`, the line's first) others waiting before it.  A resumed
    /// address leaves its reservation here.
    pub(crate) fn place(&self, m: &mut Members, held: (u32, Option<Arc<Peer>>), first: bool) -> Option<(u32, Option<Arc<Peer>>, bool)> {
        self.expire(m);
        let (vip, old) = held;
        if vip != 0 {
            // (more players than places only after a restart with fewer: the store's reservations)
            if old.is_none() && m.peers.len() >= self.o.max_peers {
                return None;
            }
            m.reserved.shift_remove(&vip);
            self.stats.resumed.inc();
            return Some((vip, old, true));
        }
        if (!first && m.line.before_newcomers()) || m.full(self.o.max_peers) {
            return None;
        }
        match m.allocate() {
            0 => None,
            v => Some((v, None, false)),
        }
    }

    /// The connection takes its place: its peer, the welcome, the peer list, the table; the holder it replaces goes.
    /// The players on the switch now come back with it (for `on_join`, which the caller runs once the lock is gone).
    pub(crate) fn seat(
        &self,
        m: &mut Members,
        conn: &Arc<Conn>,
        ctx: &AttachCtx,
        hello: Option<Map<String, Value>>,
        vip: u32,
        old: Option<Arc<Peer>>,
    ) -> (Arc<Peer>, usize) {
        let o = &self.o;
        let token = new_token();
        let now = nfsu2_util::mono_ms();
        // (for its writer: a compact bundle leaves out the address a datagram was sent to, its own)
        conn.vip.store(vip, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        let peer = Arc::new(Peer {
            vip,
            conn: conn.clone(),
            group: ctx.group.clone(),
            site: ctx.site.clone(),
            token_hash: token_hash(&token),
            name: Default::default(),
            hello: false.into(),
            bundle: false.into(),
            lan: false.into(),
            udp: 0.into(),
            frames_in: 0.into(),
            frames_out: 0.into(),
            fed_online: false.into(),
            buckets: parking_lot::Mutex::new(Pair::new(o.frame_rate, o.byte_rate)),
            ctl: parking_lot::Mutex::new(CtlBuckets { texts: Bucket::new_at(o.text_rate, now), ctl: Bucket::new_at(o.ctl_rate, now) }),
            alive: true.into(),
            last_in: now_ms().into(),
            probe: parking_lot::Mutex::new(crate::lag::Probe::new(now)),
            share: crate::lag::SHARE_FULL.into(),
            away: false.into(),
            roam_at: 0.into(),
            listed: false.into(),
            ident: ctx.ident.clone(),
            since: now_ms(),
            country: ctx.country,
            lan_to: Default::default(),
            plates: Default::default(),
        });
        if let Some(h) = &hello {
            peer.ctl.lock().texts.take_at(now, 1.0);
            greet(&peer, h, self.o.fpred, self.o.probe_echo);
            self.hand_hub(&peer, h);
        }
        m.peers.insert(vip, peer.clone());
        // (a replaced holder's place on it goes with it)
        m.lan.swap_remove(&vip);
        if peer.lan() {
            m.lan.insert(vip, peer.clone());
        }
        *conn.peer.lock() = Some(peer.clone());
        // the welcome (and a resume's whole list, which has the newcomer on it) are queued before the other players'
        // readers can find the newcomer: nothing they route to it comes first (Node sent both before it went back to
        // its event loop)
        // "bundle":1 for pages of before 2026-10-31 (ebe65786): they bundle what they send only when the welcome says
        // so, and sent every friend its own copy of each car state without it (nfsu2.xyz 2026-10-31: 8x the bytes in)
        let welcome = format!(r#"{{"t":"welcome","vip":{vip},"vipStr":"{}","mask":"{MASK}","token":"{token}","bundle":1}}"#, vip_str(vip));
        conn.push(Out::Text(Bytes::from(welcome)));
        if peer.hello.load(Relaxed) {
            let list = self.list_for(m, &peer);
            self.send(&peer, Out::Text(list));
        }
        if let Some(i) = slot(vip) {
            self.table[i].store(Some(peer.clone()));
        }
        self.publish(m);
        // the same client's older connection (it died without a close): it goes, and its late close changes nothing
        if let Some(old) = old {
            old.conn.terminate();
        }
        self.peers_changed(m, vip, false);
        self.persist(m);
        (peer, m.peers.len())
    }

    /// the 'close' of a connection: its client's limits let go, and for the holder of an address, the address
    /// reserved for its token (not when the page closed the connection itself, 1000 "idle" or "closed": no network
    /// feature in use, or the game ended; such a page comes back without a token, so its address is free at once; nor
    /// when the operator removed it).  It is kept a while for the operator's `who`.
    /// An old connection's late close must not take the address from a new holder.
    pub(crate) fn closed(&self, conn: &Arc<Conn>, ctx: &AttachCtx) {
        self.leave_group(false, &ctx.group);
        if let Some(s) = &ctx.site {
            self.leave_group(true, s);
        }
        let Some(peer) = conn.peer.lock().take() else {
            self.left_line(conn);
            return;
        };
        self.streams.lock().remove(conn.id);
        conn.streaming.store(false, Relaxed);
        let vip = peer.vip;
        let mut m = self.members.lock();
        if !m.peers.get(&vip).is_some_and(|p| Arc::ptr_eq(p, &peer)) {
            return;
        }
        m.peers.shift_remove(&vip);
        m.lan.swap_remove(&vip);
        if let Some(i) = slot(vip) {
            self.table[i].store(None);
        }
        self.publish(&m);
        if conn.let_go() {
            self.stats.released.inc();
        } else {
            self.reserve(&mut m, vip, &peer);
        }
        self.persist(&mut m);
        self.peers_changed(&mut m, vip, true);
        let count = m.peers.len();
        // the hosts hear of it before the lock goes: a page that resumes this address can only be admitted after, so
        // its first frames never reach a host before the old connection's departure (which would take the new
        // connection's streams with it); posting only queues
        if let Some(h) = &self.online {
            h.peer_gone(vip);
        }
        if let Some(h) = &self.roam {
            h.peer_gone(vip);
        }
        drop(m);
        {
            let mut g = self.gone.lock();
            if g.len() >= crate::GONE_MAX {
                g.pop_front();
            }
            g.push_back(peer.who("", Some(now_ms())));
        }
        if let Some(im) = &self.impair {
            im.forget(vip);
        }
        if let Some(f) = &ctx.on_leave {
            f(vip, peer.name(), count);
        }
        // (its place to the line's first, when it went back at once)
        self.let_in();
    }

    /// the copy-on-write lists of every peer (in the order of `peers`) and of those with LAN play open, after a change
    fn publish(&self, m: &Members) {
        self.all.store(Arc::new(m.peers.values().cloned().collect()));
        self.publish_lan(m);
    }

    fn publish_lan(&self, m: &Members) {
        self.lan_all.store(Arc::new(m.lan.values().cloned().collect()));
    }

    /// peer's LAN play, from its hello or its {"t":"lan"} (only its own reader sets it, as its connection's close
    /// logic runs after that reader ended): on the list of those with LAN play open or not, while it holds its address
    pub(crate) fn set_lan(&self, peer: &Arc<Peer>, on: bool) {
        let mut m = self.members.lock();
        peer.lan.store(on, Relaxed);
        self.lan_changed(&mut m, peer);
        // the peer list follows LAN play (`list_for`): the whole list as it opens, no changes while it is shut
        if !m.peers.get(&peer.vip).is_some_and(|p| Arc::ptr_eq(p, peer)) || !peer.hello.load(Relaxed) {
            return;
        }
        if !on {
            peer.listed.store(false, Relaxed);
        } else if !peer.listed.swap(true, Relaxed) {
            let list = self.peer_list(&m);
            self.send(peer, Out::Text(list));
        }
    }

    /// the list a peer gets with its hello: the whole list, and the changes after it (`listed`), unless its LAN play is
    /// shut: then only the server's own hosts (the Online host, which the game connects to as it opens the Online
    /// screens, before the whole list could come).  Only LAN play needs the other players' addresses (the module's
    /// peer bits answer a connect to an address nobody holds at once; runtime/web/net_lan.c); free roam's come from
    /// its hub.
    fn list_for(&self, m: &Members, peer: &Peer) -> Bytes {
        let all = peer.lan();
        peer.listed.store(all, Relaxed);
        if all { self.peer_list(m) } else { self.hosts_list() }
    }

    fn lan_changed(&self, m: &mut Members, peer: &Arc<Peer>) {
        let vip = peer.vip;
        if !m.peers.get(&vip).is_some_and(|p| Arc::ptr_eq(p, peer)) {
            return;
        }
        let want = peer.lan();
        if want == m.lan.contains_key(&vip) {
            return;
        }
        if want {
            m.lan.insert(vip, peer.clone());
        } else {
            m.lan.swap_remove(&vip);
        }
        self.publish_lan(m);
    }

    /// The reservations past their time go.  The hosts hear of each one from the store that goes so (`Host::peer_gone`):
    /// a player of before a restart who did not come back for its address, whose leaving they never saw (the Online
    /// host keeps the races going on over a restart, and their players' names, until it hears they left).  The ones
    /// a departure made, they heard of at the departure.  Whether any went.
    pub(crate) fn expire(&self, m: &mut Members) -> bool {
        let now = now_ms();
        let before = m.reserved.len();
        let mut lapsed = Vec::new();
        m.reserved.retain(|v, r| {
            if r.until > now {
                return true;
            }
            if r.group.is_none() {
                lapsed.push(*v);
            }
            false
        });
        // (under the lock: a page that takes the address later can only be admitted after, so its frames never reach
        // a host before this; posting only queues)
        for vip in lapsed {
            if let Some(h) = &self.online {
                h.peer_gone(vip);
            }
            if let Some(h) = &self.roam {
                h.peer_gone(vip);
            }
        }
        m.reserved.len() != before
    }

    /// vip is kept for its token for `reserve_ms`; past its client's (and site's) share of reservations
    /// (`group_reserve`, `site_reserve`: so that one client cannot reserve them all), that client's own oldest go
    fn reserve(&self, m: &mut Members, vip: u32, peer: &Peer) {
        let now = now_ms();
        let group = peer.group.id.clone();
        let site = peer.site.as_ref().map(|s| s.id.clone());
        m.reserved.insert(
            vip,
            Reservation { hash: peer.token_hash, until: now + self.o.reserve_ms, group: Some(group.clone()), site: site.clone() },
        );
        let trim = |m: &mut Members, by_site: bool, id: &Arc<str>, max: usize| {
            let mut mine: Vec<(u32, i64)> = m
                .reserved
                .iter()
                .filter(|(_, r)| r.until > now && if by_site { r.site.as_ref() == Some(id) } else { r.group.as_ref() == Some(id) })
                .map(|(v, r)| (*v, r.until))
                .collect();
            // the oldest first (a stable sort: equal times stay in the order of `reserved`)
            mine.sort_by_key(|e| e.1);
            for (v, _) in &mine[..mine.len().saturating_sub(max)] {
                m.reserved.shift_remove(v);
                self.stats.evicted.inc();
            }
        };
        trim(m, false, &group, self.o.group_reserve);
        if let Some(site) = &site {
            trim(m, true, site, self.o.site_reserve);
        }
    }

    /// the whole peer list, as a message (the Online host on it as `server: true`)
    pub(crate) fn peer_list(&self, m: &Members) -> Bytes {
        self.list_of(m.peers.values())
    }

    /// the list of the server's own hosts alone
    fn hosts_list(&self) -> Bytes {
        self.list_of(std::iter::empty())
    }

    fn list_of<'a>(&self, peers: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &'a Arc<Peer>>) -> Bytes {
        let mut s = String::with_capacity(32 + 48 * peers.len());
        s.push_str(r#"{"t":"peers","peers":["#);
        let mut first = true;
        for p in peers {
            if !first {
                s.push(',');
            }
            first = false;
            entry(&mut s, p.vip, p.name());
        }
        for h in [&self.online, &self.roam].into_iter().flatten() {
            if h.listed() {
                if !first {
                    s.push(',');
                }
                first = false;
                entry(&mut s, h.vip(), h.name());
                s.pop();
                s.push_str(r#","server":true}"#);
            }
        }
        s.push_str("]}");
        Bytes::from(s)
    }

    /// vip joined, got its name or left; everyone hears of it `peers_ms` later, with whatever else changed by then
    pub(crate) fn peers_changed(&self, m: &mut Members, vip: u32, left: bool) {
        m.changed.insert(vip);
        if left {
            m.left.insert(vip);
        }
        if !m.delta_armed {
            m.delta_armed = true;
            self.after(Duration::from_millis(self.o.peers_ms), |sw| sw.send_delta());
        }
    }

    /// a timer of the switch's (ended by `stop()`)
    fn after(&self, d: Duration, f: impl FnOnce(&LanSwitch) + Send + 'static) {
        let me = self.me.clone();
        let stopped = self.stopped.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            tokio::select! {
                _ = stopped.cancelled() => {}
                _ = tokio::time::sleep(d) => {
                    if let Some(sw) = me.upgrade() {
                        f(&sw);
                    }
                }
            }
        });
    }

    /// the changes, to the clients that take them (sent under the lock, so that a client's
    /// whole list and the changes after it reach it in the order they were made)
    fn send_delta(&self) {
        let mut m = self.members.lock();
        m.delta_armed = false;
        let mut s = String::from(r#"{"t":"delta","peers":["#);
        let mut first = true;
        for v in &m.changed {
            if let Some(p) = m.peers.get(v) {
                if !first {
                    s.push(',');
                }
                first = false;
                entry(&mut s, p.vip, p.name());
            }
        }
        s.push_str(r#"],"gone":["#);
        for (i, v) in m.left.iter().enumerate() {
            if i > 0 {
                s.push(',');
            }
            s.push_str(&v.to_string());
        }
        s.push_str("]}");
        m.changed.clear();
        m.left.clear();
        let msg = Bytes::from(s);
        for p in m.peers.values() {
            if p.listed.load(Relaxed) && p.open() {
                self.send(p, Out::Text(msg.clone()));
            }
        }
    }

    /// a hello, the connection's first (later ones change nothing): its name and what it takes, the whole list
    pub(crate) fn hello(&self, peer: &Arc<Peer>, msg: &Map<String, Value>) {
        let mut m = self.members.lock();
        if peer.hello.load(Relaxed) {
            return;
        }
        let was = peer.name().to_string();
        greet(peer, msg, self.o.fpred, self.o.probe_echo);
        self.hand_hub(peer, msg);
        self.lan_changed(&mut m, peer);
        let list = self.list_for(&m, peer);
        self.send(peer, Out::Text(list));
        if peer.name() != was {
            self.peers_changed(&mut m, peer.vip, false);
        }
    }

    /// A hello's name (as the peer took it) and "block" to the free-roam hub, with the page's address: every
    /// connection's hello, a new one's (`hello`), a resumed one's or one let in from the line (`seat`), as the hub
    /// forgets a page's when its connection goes (`Host::peer_gone`, posted before a resume can take the address).
    fn hand_hub(&self, peer: &Peer, hello: &Map<String, Value>) {
        if let Some(h) = &self.roam {
            h.page_name(peer.vip, peer.name());
            let names = block_names(hello);
            if !names.is_empty() {
                h.blocks(peer.vip, names);
            }
        }
    }

    /// the store gets the addresses held and reserved, shortly after a change
    pub(crate) fn persist(&self, m: &mut Members) {
        if self.store.is_none() || m.save_armed {
            return;
        }
        m.save_armed = true;
        let era = m.save_gen;
        self.after_always(Duration::from_millis(500), move |sw| {
            if sw.members.lock().save_gen == era {
                sw.flush(false);
            }
        });
    }

    /// a timer that `stop()` does not end (a change after the stop is still saved)
    fn after_always(&self, d: Duration, f: impl FnOnce(&LanSwitch) + Send + 'static) {
        let me = self.me.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            tokio::time::sleep(d).await;
            if let Some(sw) = me.upgrade() {
                f(&sw);
            }
        });
    }

    /// the store's list, taken under the lock, written on a blocking thread (or here, as the switch stops)
    fn flush(&self, now: bool) {
        let Some(store) = self.store.clone() else { return };
        let (seq, json) = {
            let mut m = self.members.lock();
            m.save_armed = false;
            m.save_gen += 1;
            m.save_seq += 1;
            (m.save_seq, store_list(&m))
        };
        if now {
            store.save(seq, &json);
        } else {
            tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || store.save(seq, &json));
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn flush_now(&self) {
        self.flush(true);
    }
}

/// what the store keeps: the addresses held, then the ones reserved, each with its token's hash
fn store_list(m: &Members) -> String {
    let now = now_ms();
    let mut s = String::from("[");
    let mut first = true;
    let mut one = |s: &mut String, v: u32, h: &[u8; 32]| {
        if !first {
            s.push(',');
        }
        first = false;
        s.push_str(r#"{"v":""#);
        s.push_str(&vip_str(v));
        s.push_str(r#"","h":""#);
        s.push_str(&nfsu2_util::js::base64url(h));
        s.push_str(r#""}"#);
    };
    for p in m.peers.values() {
        one(&mut s, p.vip, &p.token_hash);
    }
    for (v, r) in &m.reserved {
        if r.until > now && !m.peers.contains_key(v) {
            one(&mut s, *v, &r.hash);
        }
    }
    s.push(']');
    s
}

/// the address a hello's token held: one reserved for it, or one a connection of the same client holds (which this one
/// replaces); 0 for none
pub(crate) fn held_address(m: &Members, hello: Option<&Map<String, Value>>) -> (u32, Option<Arc<Peer>>) {
    let Some(Value::String(tok)) = hello.and_then(|h| h.get("token")) else { return (0, None) };
    let w = crate::vip_num(&js_string(hello.and_then(|h| h.get("vip"))));
    match m.peers.get(&w) {
        None if m.reserved.get(&w).is_some_and(|r| r.until > now_ms() && token_fits(tok, &r.hash)) => (w, None),
        Some(h) if token_fits(tok, &h.token_hash) => (w, Some(h.clone())),
        _ => (0, None),
    }
}

/// `{"vip":N,"name":"..."}`
fn entry(s: &mut String, vip: u32, name: &str) {
    s.push_str(r#"{"vip":"#);
    s.push_str(&vip.to_string());
    s.push_str(r#","name":"#);
    write_str(s, name);
    s.push('}');
}

/// a full switch's answer (a fixed reason)
pub(crate) fn lan_full() -> Bytes {
    let mut p = 1013u16.to_be_bytes().to_vec();
    p.extend_from_slice(b"LAN full");
    Bytes::from(p)
}

/// a hello's "block": the names (as the game shows them over cars: printable ASCII, at most 24) of the players the page
/// blocks, at most BLOCK_MAX of them, each trimmed; what is not a string, an empty one and those past the cap are left
/// out, a longer one is cut
const BLOCK_MAX: usize = 32;
fn block_names(m: &Map<String, Value>) -> Vec<String> {
    let Some(Value::Array(a)) = m.get("block") else { return Vec::new() };
    a.iter()
        .filter_map(|v| v.as_str())
        .map(|s| s.chars().filter(|c| (' '..='~').contains(c)).take(24).collect::<String>().trim().to_string())
        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
        .take(BLOCK_MAX)
        .collect()
}

/// a connection's first hello: its player's name, whether it takes bundles (and which), whether it echoes their
/// stamps, and whether it has LAN play open
fn greet(peer: &Peer, m: &Map<String, Value>, fpred: bool, echo: bool) {
    use nfsu2_util::json::is_num;
    peer.hello.store(true, Relaxed);
    peer.bundle.store(is_num(m.get("bundle"), 1.0), Relaxed);
    use crate::conn::{COMPACT, DELTAS, FPRED, OTHERS, PLAIN};
    let compact = match (is_num(m.get("compact"), 1.0), is_num(m.get("delta"), 1.0), is_num(m.get("fpred"), 1.0)) {
        (false, ..) => PLAIN,
        (true, false, _) => COMPACT,
        (true, true, false) => DELTAS,
        (true, true, true) => FPRED,
    };
    let compact = if compact == FPRED && !fpred { DELTAS } else { compact };
    let compact = if compact >= DELTAS && is_num(m.get("ldelta"), 1.0) { compact | OTHERS } else { compact };
    peer.conn.compact.store(compact, Relaxed);
    peer.conn.echo.store(echo && compact != PLAIN && is_num(m.get("echo"), 1.0), Relaxed);
    peer.lan.store(is_num(m.get("lan"), 1.0), Relaxed);
    peer.udp.store(crate::udp_of(m.get("udp")), Relaxed);
    if let Some(Value::String(name)) = m.get("name") {
        let _ = peer.name.set(crate::clean_name(name).into_boxed_str());
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::LanOptions;

    // a hello's "block": strings only, trimmed, printable ASCII, at most 24 characters each and BLOCK_MAX names
    #[test]
    fn a_hellos_block_is_names_as_the_game_shows_them() {
        let m = |v: Value| block_names(v.as_object().unwrap());
        assert_eq!(m(serde_json::json!({ "t": "hello" })), Vec::<String>::new());
        assert_eq!(m(serde_json::json!({ "block": "bob" })), Vec::<String>::new());
        let long = "x".repeat(40);
        assert_eq!(
            m(serde_json::json!({ "block": ["  Bob ", 7, "", "   ", "Zoë\u{0}!", long] })),
            vec!["Bob".to_string(), "Zo!".to_string(), "x".repeat(24)]
        );
        let many: Vec<String> = (0..40).map(|i| format!("p{i}")).collect();
        assert_eq!(m(serde_json::json!({ "block": many })).len(), BLOCK_MAX);
    }

    /// Node sent the welcome (and a resume's whole list) before it went back to its event loop: no frame from another
    /// player could come first.  Here the other players' readers route on other cores: a newcomer they can find (the
    /// table, the list of all) must have its welcome queued already.
    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
    async fn the_welcome_is_queued_before_anyone_can_send_to_the_newcomer() {
        const N: usize = 300;
        let sw = LanSwitch::new(LanOptions { max_peers: 24000, ..LanOptions::default() }, "", None, None, None, None);
        // a sender on another core: it looks at each address the switch hands out next, as soon as it is taken
        let watcher = {
            let sw = sw.clone();
            std::thread::spawn(move || {
                let mut early = 0;
                for i in 0..N {
                    let p = loop {
                        if let Some(p) = sw.table[slot(vip_at(i)).unwrap()].load_full() {
                            break p;
                        }
                        std::hint::spin_loop();
                    };
                    let q = p.conn.out.q.lock();
                    if !matches!(q.first(), Some(Out::Text(t)) if t.starts_with(br#"{"t":"welcome""#)) {
                        early += 1;
                    }
                }
                early
            })
        };
        let peers: Vec<_> = (0..N).map(|i| crate::route::tests::peer(&sw, &format!("g{i}"))).collect();
        let early = watcher.join().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(early, 0, "{early} of {N} newcomers could be sent to before their welcome was queued");
        drop(peers);
        sw.stop();
    }

    /// what `full()` costs (under the members lock) at 1000 players: the start page asks for it with /players
    #[tokio::test]
    #[ignore]
    async fn what_full_costs() {
        let sw = LanSwitch::new(LanOptions { max_peers: 24000, ..LanOptions::default() }, "", None, None, None, None);
        let peers: Vec<_> = (0..1000).map(|i| crate::route::tests::peer(&sw, &format!("g{i}"))).collect();
        let t = std::time::Instant::now();
        let mut n = 0;
        for _ in 0..10_000 {
            n += sw.full() as usize;
        }
        println!("full() at 1000 players: {:.2} us a call ({n} full)", t.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 1e6 / 10_000.0);
        drop(peers);
        sw.stop();
    }

//! What the pages were sent, by kind: the [players] count of where the bytes go.  Each entry of a compact bundle
//! (compact.rs) counts its bytes as it went, under its datagram's kind: free roam's by their type (runtime/roam_core.h
//! RC_MSG_*), LAN play's UDP (the game's own races, Online's and free roam's lobby races) and the rest; each message
//! of a host (the free-roam hub's lists and map, the Online server's segments: `send_to`, a WebSocket message each,
//! never in a bundle) counts as its whole frame.  On nfsu2.xyz (2026-10-30, 5,800 players) the entries other than car
//! states carried more bytes than the car states, 104 bytes each on average: this says which they were.
//!
//! The same kinds count what the pages send (`of_page`): each entry of a page's bundle under its datagram's kind (those
//! to the hub as the hub's), the destinations an entry lists past the first, the bundles' and entries' headers and the
//! control messages (JSON) as kinds of their own.  After the 2026-10-31 release the server took in 865 Mbit/s, and
//! nothing counted what (`MSGS`: and how many messages each way, which cloudflared pays for one by one).

use crate::compact::ROAM_OK;
use crate::{BROADCAST, KIND_UDP};

/// runtime/roam_core.h RC_MSG_*: a free-roam datagram's type (0: one this does not know)
const ROAM_TYPES: [&str; 21] = [
    "?",
    "hello",
    "peers",
    "car state",
    "car look",
    "car look ask",
    "ping",
    "pong",
    "bye",
    "duel",
    "map ask",
    "map",
    "lobby",
    "lobbies",
    "race report",
    "say",
    "race results",
    "map delta",
    "near ask",
    "near",
    "crash damage",
];
const R: usize = ROAM_TYPES.len();
/// a free-roam datagram whose magic, length or CRC did not check out (or another kind 1 on free roam's ports)
const ROAM_BAD: usize = R;
const UDP_OTHER: usize = R + 1;
/// LAN play's UDP (KIND_LAN_UDP), to the page's own address, to all
const LAN_UDP: usize = R + 2;
const LAN_BCAST: usize = R + 3;
const OTHER_KIND: usize = R + 4;
/// the hub's messages, by free roam's types (R of them)
const HUB: usize = R + 5;
const ONLINE: usize = HUB + R;
const OTHER_HOST: usize = ONLINE + 1;
/// from the pages: the destinations a bundle entry lists (4 bytes each; one alone is in its frame), the bundles' and
/// their entries' headers, the control messages (JSON), LAN play's TCP segments (the Online server's and a LAN race
/// host's streams)
pub(crate) const ADDRS: usize = OTHER_HOST + 1;
pub(crate) const FRAMING: usize = OTHER_HOST + 2;
pub(crate) const TEXT: usize = OTHER_HOST + 3;
const LAN_TCP: usize = OTHER_HOST + 4;
/// the kinds
pub const KINDS: usize = LAN_TCP + 1;
/// runtime/web/net_proto.h: LAN play's UDP and TCP
const KIND_LAN_UDP: u8 = 3;
const KIND_LAN_TCP: u8 = 4;
/// runtime/roam_core.h RC_DEFAULT_PORT
const ROAM_PORT: u16 = 47210;

/// a kind's name in the count
pub fn name(i: usize) -> String {
    match i {
        i if i < R => ROAM_TYPES[i].to_string(),
        ROAM_BAD => "free roam's port, unchecked".into(),
        UDP_OTHER => "UDP, other ports".into(),
        LAN_UDP => "LAN UDP".into(),
        LAN_BCAST => "LAN UDP broadcast".into(),
        OTHER_KIND => "other frames".into(),
        i if i < ONLINE => format!("hub {}", ROAM_TYPES[i - HUB]),
        ONLINE => "Online server".into(),
        OTHER_HOST => "other host".into(),
        ADDRS => "destinations".into(),
        FRAMING => "bundle headers".into(),
        TEXT => "control messages".into(),
        _ => "LAN TCP".into(),
    }
}

/// a free-roam datagram's type at [16 + 5] of its frame, as a kind (0 for one past those known)
fn roam_type(data: &[u8]) -> usize {
    let t = data[16 + 5] as usize;
    if t < R { t } else { 0 }
}

/// nfsu2-roam's ROAM_HUB_VIP: the free-roam hub's address, whose lists, map and lobbies go in bundles too
const HUB_VIP: u32 = crate::BASE | 0xFD;

/// the kind of a datagram (the switch's copy: byte 1 says whether free roam's checked out) that went from `src` to
/// `dst` in a compact bundle (the hub's by their type, as its messages of their own were: `of_host`)
pub(crate) fn of_entry(data: &[u8], src: u32, dst: u32) -> usize {
    if data.len() < 16 {
        return OTHER_KIND;
    }
    match data[0] {
        KIND_UDP if src == HUB_VIP && data[1] == ROAM_OK && data.len() > 16 + 5 => HUB + roam_type(data),
        KIND_UDP if data[1] == ROAM_OK && data.len() > 16 + 5 => roam_type(data),
        KIND_UDP if u16::from_be_bytes([data[14], data[15]]) == ROAM_PORT => ROAM_BAD,
        KIND_UDP => UDP_OTHER,
        KIND_LAN_UDP if dst == BROADCAST => LAN_BCAST,
        KIND_LAN_UDP => LAN_UDP,
        _ => OTHER_KIND,
    }
}

/// the kind of a frame a page sent to `dst`: free roam's by their type (those to the hub as the hub's)
pub(crate) fn of_page(data: &[u8], dst: u32) -> usize {
    if data.len() < 16 {
        return OTHER_KIND;
    }
    let roam = data.len() > 16 + 5 && &data[16..20] == b"N2FR";
    match data[0] {
        KIND_UDP if roam && dst == HUB_VIP => HUB + roam_type(data),
        KIND_UDP if roam => roam_type(data),
        KIND_UDP if u16::from_be_bytes([data[14], data[15]]) == ROAM_PORT => ROAM_BAD,
        KIND_UDP => UDP_OTHER,
        KIND_LAN_UDP if dst == BROADCAST => LAN_BCAST,
        KIND_LAN_UDP => LAN_UDP,
        KIND_LAN_TCP => LAN_TCP,
        _ => OTHER_KIND,
    }
}

/// WebSocket messages each way by type (`Stats::msg`), and the writes the server made (each batch a page's writer
/// took): every one is work for the kernel and for cloudflared, whatever its size
pub(crate) const IN_BUNDLE: usize = 0;
pub(crate) const IN_FRAME: usize = 1;
pub(crate) const IN_TEXT: usize = 2;
pub(crate) const IN_PONG: usize = 3;
pub(crate) const IN_PING: usize = 4;
pub(crate) const OUT_BUNDLE: usize = 5;
pub(crate) const OUT_FRAME: usize = 6;
pub(crate) const OUT_TEXT: usize = 7;
pub(crate) const OUT_HOST: usize = 8;
pub(crate) const OUT_PING: usize = 9;
pub(crate) const OUT_PONG: usize = 10;
pub(crate) const OUT_WRITES: usize = 11;
pub const MSGS: usize = 12;

/// The count's line of messages by kind of player (`LanSwitch::messages_by_kind`): for each kind with players, how many,
/// their messages each way a second, and each one's
pub fn kinds_line(kinds: &[crate::KindMsgs], secs: f64) -> Option<String> {
    let parts: Vec<String> = kinds
        .iter()
        .filter(|k| k.players > 0 && secs > 0.0)
        .map(|k| {
            let (i, o, n) = (k.msgs_in as f64 / secs, k.msgs_out as f64 / secs, k.players as f64);
            format!("{} {}: {i:.0} in, {o:.0} out a second ({:.1} and {:.1} each)", k.kind, k.players, i / n, o / n)
        })
        .collect();
    (!parts.is_empty()).then(|| parts.join("; "))
}

/// The count's line of messages: each way a second, by type, and the writes
pub fn msg_line(now: &[u64], was: &[u64], secs: f64) -> Option<String> {
    let d = |i: usize| now[i].saturating_sub(was.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0)) as f64 / secs.max(1.0);
    let (inn, out) = ((IN_BUNDLE..=IN_PING).map(d).sum::<f64>(), (OUT_BUNDLE..=OUT_PONG).map(d).sum::<f64>());
    if inn + out == 0.0 {
        return None;
    }
    Some(format!(
        "in {inn:.0}/s (bundles {:.0}, frames {:.0}, control {:.0}, pongs {:.0}, pings {:.0}), out {out:.0}/s (bundles {:.0}, \
         frames {:.0}, control {:.0}, hosts {:.0}, pings {:.0}, pongs {:.0}) in {:.0} writes/s",
        d(IN_BUNDLE),
        d(IN_FRAME),
        d(IN_TEXT),
        d(IN_PONG),
        d(IN_PING),
        d(OUT_BUNDLE),
        d(OUT_FRAME),
        d(OUT_TEXT),
        d(OUT_HOST),
        d(OUT_PING),
        d(OUT_PONG),
        d(OUT_WRITES)
    ))
}

/// the kind of a host's message (its source at [4..8])
pub(crate) fn of_host(data: &[u8], roam: Option<u32>, online: Option<u32>) -> usize {
    let src = (data.len() >= 8).then(|| u32::from_be_bytes([data[4], data[5], data[6], data[7]]));
    if src.is_some() && src == roam {
        if data.len() > 16 + 5 && data[0] == KIND_UDP && &data[16..20] == b"N2FR" { HUB + roam_type(data) } else { HUB }
    } else if src.is_some() && src == online {
        ONLINE
    } else {
        OTHER_HOST
    }
}

/// The count's line: the kinds by their bytes since `was`, the largest first, those of at least 0.5 % of all (and
/// how many fell under that).  `now` and `was`: bytes of each kind, then entries of each.
pub fn line(now: &[u64], was: &[u64], secs: f64) -> Option<String> {
    let d = |i: usize| now[i].saturating_sub(was.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0));
    let total: u64 = (0..KINDS).map(d).sum();
    if total == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut ks: Vec<usize> = (0..KINDS).filter(|&i| d(i) > 0).collect();
    ks.sort_by_key(|&i| std::cmp::Reverse(d(i)));
    let secs = secs.max(1.0);
    let shown: Vec<String> = ks
        .iter()
        .filter(|&&i| d(i) * 200 >= total)
        .map(|&i| {
            let (b, n) = (d(i), d(KINDS + i).max(1));
            format!(
                "{} {:.0} % ({:.1} Mbit/s, {:.0}/s, {:.1} B each)",
                name(i),
                b as f64 * 100.0 / total as f64,
                b as f64 * 8.0 / secs / 1e6,
                n as f64 / secs,
                b as f64 / n as f64
            )
        })
        .collect();
    let rest = ks.len() - shown.len();
    Some(format!(
        "{:.1} Mbit/s: {}{}",
        total as f64 * 8.0 / secs / 1e6,
        shown.join(", "),
        if rest > 0 { format!(", {rest} smaller kinds") } else { String::new() }
    ))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::BASE;

    #[test]
    fn kinds_line_says_each_kind_with_players_a_second_and_each_ones() {
        let k = |kind, players, msgs_in, msgs_out| crate::KindMsgs { kind, players, msgs_in, msgs_out };
        let kinds = [
            k("racing or in a race lobby", 10, 30_000, 45_000),
            k("in Online mode", 0, 0, 0),
            k("driving in free roam", 4, 24_000, 24_600),
        ];
        assert_eq!(
            kinds_line(&kinds, 300.0).unwrap(),
            "racing or in a race lobby 10: 100 in, 150 out a second (10.0 and 15.0 each); driving in free roam 4: 80 in, 82 out a second (20.0 and 20.5 each)"
        );
        assert_eq!(kinds_line(&[k("in Online mode", 0, 5, 5)], 300.0), None);
    }

    fn frame(kind: u8, b1: u8, src: u32, dport: u16, data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut f = vec![kind, b1, 0, 0];
        f.extend_from_slice(&src.to_be_bytes());
        f.extend_from_slice(&(BASE | 9).to_be_bytes());
        f.extend_from_slice(&ROAM_PORT.to_be_bytes());
        f.extend_from_slice(&dport.to_be_bytes());
        f.extend_from_slice(data);
        f
    }

    // every kind has a name, the entries and the hosts' messages land where they are
    #[test]
    fn kinds() {
        let mut roam = b"N2FR\x01\x06".to_vec();
        roam.resize(24, 0);
        assert_eq!(name(of_entry(&frame(1, ROAM_OK, BASE | 2, ROAM_PORT, &roam), BASE | 2, BASE | 9)), "ping");
        let mut dents = roam.clone();
        dents[5] = 20;
        assert_eq!(name(of_entry(&frame(1, ROAM_OK, BASE | 2, ROAM_PORT, &dents), BASE | 2, BASE | 9)), "crash damage");
        dents[5] = 18;
        assert_eq!(name(of_page(&frame(1, 0, BASE | 2, ROAM_PORT, &dents), HUB_VIP)), "hub near ask");
        assert_eq!(name(of_entry(&frame(1, 0, BASE | 2, ROAM_PORT, &roam), BASE | 2, BASE | 9)), "free roam's port, unchecked");
        assert_eq!(name(of_entry(&frame(1, 0, BASE | 2, 3659, &roam), BASE | 2, BASE | 9)), "UDP, other ports");
        assert_eq!(name(of_entry(&frame(3, 0, BASE | 2, 9999, &roam), BASE | 2, BASE | 9)), "LAN UDP");
        assert_eq!(name(of_entry(&frame(3, 0, BASE | 2, 9999, &roam), BASE | 2, BROADCAST)), "LAN UDP broadcast");
        assert_eq!(name(of_entry(&[3, 0, 0], BASE | 2, BASE | 9)), "other frames");
        let mut peers = roam.clone();
        peers[5] = 2;
        let (hub, online) = (Some(BASE | 0xFD), Some(BASE | 1));
        assert_eq!(name(of_host(&frame(1, 0, BASE | 0xFD, ROAM_PORT, &peers), hub, online)), "hub peers");
        // the hub's list in a bundle: the same kind
        assert_eq!(name(of_entry(&frame(1, ROAM_OK, BASE | 0xFD, ROAM_PORT, &peers), BASE | 0xFD, BASE | 9)), "hub peers");
        assert_eq!(name(of_entry(&frame(1, ROAM_OK, BASE | 2, ROAM_PORT, &peers), BASE | 2, BASE | 9)), "peers");
        peers[5] = 200;
        assert_eq!(name(of_host(&frame(1, 0, BASE | 0xFD, ROAM_PORT, &peers), hub, online)), "hub ?");
        assert_eq!(name(of_host(&frame(4, 0, BASE | 1, 0, &[1; 30]), hub, online)), "Online server");
        assert_eq!(name(of_host(&frame(4, 0, BASE | 7, 0, &[1; 30]), hub, online)), "other host");
        // what pages send
        assert_eq!(name(of_page(&frame(1, 0, BASE | 2, ROAM_PORT, &roam), BASE | 9)), "ping");
        assert_eq!(name(of_page(&frame(1, 0, BASE | 2, ROAM_PORT, &peers), HUB_VIP)), "hub ?");
        assert_eq!(name(of_page(&frame(4, 0, BASE | 2, 0, &[1; 30]), BASE | 1)), "LAN TCP");
        assert_eq!(name(of_page(&frame(3, 0, BASE | 2, 9999, &roam), BROADCAST)), "LAN UDP broadcast");
        for k in [ADDRS, FRAMING, TEXT] {
            assert!(!name(k).is_empty());
        }
        let names: std::collections::HashSet<String> = (0..KINDS).map(name).collect();
        assert_eq!(names.len(), KINDS, "each its own");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_line() {
        let mut now = vec![0u64; 2 * KINDS];
        now[3] = 30_000_000;
        now[KINDS + 3] = 1_000_000;
        now[LAN_UDP] = 60_000_000;
        now[KINDS + LAN_UDP] = 500_000;
        now[6] = 100;
        now[KINDS + 6] = 5;
        let l = line(&now, &[], 300.0).unwrap();
        assert!(l.starts_with("2.4 Mbit/s: LAN UDP 67 % (1.6 Mbit/s, 1667/s, 120.0 B each), car state 33 %"), "{l}");
        assert!(l.ends_with(", 1 smaller kinds"), "{l}");
        assert_eq!(line(&now, &now, 300.0), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_message_line() {
        let mut now = vec![0u64; MSGS];
        now[IN_BUNDLE] = 6000;
        now[OUT_BUNDLE] = 3000;
        now[OUT_PING] = 300;
        now[OUT_WRITES] = 3000;
        let l = msg_line(&now, &[], 300.0).unwrap();
        assert!(l.starts_with("in 20/s (bundles 20, frames 0, control 0, pongs 0, pings 0), out 11/s (bundles 10,"), "{l}");
        assert!(l.ends_with("pings 1, pongs 0) in 10 writes/s"), "{l}");
        assert_eq!(msg_line(&now, &now, 300.0), None);
    }
}

//! Where the players are and how long their paths are, for the server's 5-minute counts (its `[players]` lines): each
//! player's round trip to the server by its country (Cloudflare's CF-IPCountry: `AttachOpts::country`) and by region,
//! and of the pairs that play together, free roam's links (the hub's: `Host::link_pairs`) and LAN play's (a race, its
//! lobby: UDP from one player to another), how many are of one country and of one region, and how long the way from one
//! player to the other through the server is (the two players' round trips together).  What it would bring to connect
//! players near each other some other way (a direct link, a server in their region) is in those numbers.
//!
//! A round trip is the player's lowest of the last 30-60 s (lag.rs `Probe::base`): its path without the queues on it.
//! Nothing here costs a datagram more than `race_with` (a load or two on the sender's own peer, a store when the pair
//! is new); the rest is made when the counts are, every 5 minutes.  Counts only: never a player's own.

    u16::from_be_bytes(c)

        b"BR" | b"AR" | b"CL" | b"CO" | b"PE" | b"VE" | b"EC" | b"BO" | b"PY" | b"UY" | b"GY" | b"SR" | b"GF" | b"FK" | b"GS" => 12,
        b"EG" | b"LY" | b"TN" | b"DZ" | b"MA" | b"SD" | b"EH" => 13,
        b"NG" | b"GH" | b"CI" | b"SN" | b"ML" | b"BF" | b"NE" | b"TD" | b"CM" | b"CF" | b"GA" | b"CG" | b"CD" | b"AO" | b"ZM" | b"ZW"
        | b"MZ" | b"MW" | b"TZ" | b"KE" | b"UG" | b"RW" | b"BI" | b"ET" | b"ER" | b"DJ" | b"SO" | b"SS" | b"ZA" | b"NA" | b"BW" | b"LS"
        | b"SZ" | b"MG" | b"MU" | b"SC" | b"KM" | b"RE" | b"YT" | b"CV" | b"GM" | b"GN" | b"GW" | b"SL" | b"LR" | b"TG" | b"BJ" | b"MR"
        | b"ST" | b"GQ" | b"SH" => 14,
        _ => REGIONS.len() - 1,
    }
}

/// the players a peer's LAN play sent UDP to since the last count, at most this many (a race has six players)
pub(crate) const LAN_TO: usize = 8;

/// LAN play's UDP from a player to `dst`: noted in its `lan_to` (only its own reader calls this).  Two places a
/// destination may be at; a third that hashes there takes one of them (a count is not worse for it).
pub(crate) fn race_with(to: &[AtomicU32; LAN_TO], dst: u32) {
    let h = (dst.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B1) >> 29) as usize;
    let (a, b) = (&to[h], &to[h ^ 1]);
    let (x, y) = (a.load(Relaxed), b.load(Relaxed));
    if x == dst || y == dst {
        return;
    }
    if x == 0 { a.store(dst, Relaxed) } else { b.store(dst, Relaxed) }
}

/// what `race_with` noted since the last time, into `out`, and none kept
pub(crate) fn take(to: &[AtomicU32; LAN_TO], out: &mut Vec<u32>) {
    out.extend(to.iter().map(|s| s.swap(0, Relaxed)).filter(|&d| d != 0));
}

/// One player as the counts see it: its address, country (`code`; 0 not known) and round trip (lag.rs `Probe::base`:
/// none before its first pong).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Seen {
    pub vip: u32,
    pub country: u16,
    pub base: Option<f64>,
}

/// the median and the 90th percentile (nearest rank) of `v`, sorted here; None for none
fn p50_90(v: &mut [f64]) -> Option<(f64, f64)> {
    if v.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    v.sort_unstable_by(f64::total_cmp);
    let at = |p: f64| v[((p * v.len() as f64).ceil() as usize).clamp(1, v.len()) - 1];
    Some((at(0.5), at(0.9)))
}

/// "n p50/p90" of round trips (ms, whole)
fn spread(v: &mut [f64]) -> String {
    match p50_90(v) {
        Some((a, b)) => format!("{} {:.0}/{:.0}", v.len(), a, b),
        None => "0".into(),
    }
}

/// the countries most players are in, the most first, then one entry for the rest
const TOP_COUNTRIES: usize = 12;

/// The counts' lines (without "[players] "): the round trips by country and by region, and the pairs' of free roam
/// (`roam`, the hub's links now) and of LAN play (`lan`, since the last count), each pair once.  None while no player
/// has a round trip yet.
pub fn lines(players: &[Seen], roam: &[(u32, u32)], lan: &[(u32, u32)]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let timed: Vec<&Seen> = players.iter().filter(|p| p.base.is_some()).collect();
    if timed.is_empty() {
        return out;
    }
    let untimed = players.len() - timed.len();
    let mut all: Vec<f64> = timed.iter().filter_map(|p| p.base).collect();
    // by country, the unknown ones last
    let mut by: HashMap<u16, Vec<f64>> = HashMap::new();
    for p in &timed {
        by.entry(p.country).or_default().extend(p.base);
    }
    let mut unknown = by.remove(&0).unwrap_or_default();
    let mut countries: Vec<(u16, Vec<f64>)> = by.into_iter().collect();
    countries.sort_unstable_by(|a, b| b.1.len().cmp(&a.1.len()).then(a.0.cmp(&b.0)));
    let mut l = format!(
        "round trips to the server by country (each player's lowest of the last 30-60 s, players and ms p50/p90): all {}",
        spread(&mut all)
    );
    for (c, v) in countries.iter_mut().take(TOP_COUNTRIES) {
        let _ = write!(l, "; {} {}", letters(*c), spread(v));
    }
    if countries.len() > TOP_COUNTRIES {
        let mut rest: Vec<f64> = countries[TOP_COUNTRIES..].iter().flat_map(|(_, v)| v.iter().copied()).collect();
        let _ = write!(l, "; {} more countries {}", countries.len() - TOP_COUNTRIES, spread(&mut rest));
    }
    if !unknown.is_empty() {
        let _ = write!(l, "; unknown {}", spread(&mut unknown));
    }
    if untimed > 0 {
        let _ = write!(l, "; {untimed} not timed yet");
    }
    out.push(l);
    // by region, the most first
    let mut regions: Vec<Vec<f64>> = vec![Vec::new(); REGIONS.len()];
    for p in &timed {
        regions[region(p.country)].extend(p.base);
    }
    let mut order: Vec<usize> = (1..REGIONS.len()).filter(|&r| !regions[r].is_empty()).collect();
    order.sort_by_key(|&r| std::cmp::Reverse(regions[r].len()));
    if !regions[0].is_empty() {
        order.push(0);
    }
    let mut l = String::from("round trips to the server by region:");
    for (i, r) in order.into_iter().enumerate() {
        let _ = write!(l, "{} {} {}", if i == 0 { "" } else { ";" }, REGIONS[r], spread(&mut regions[r]));
    }
    out.push(l);
    // the pairs
    let at: HashMap<u32, &Seen> = players.iter().map(|p| (p.vip, p)).collect();
    if let Some(l) = pairs(&at, roam) {
        out.push(format!("free-roam links now: {l}"));
    }
    if let Some(l) = pairs(&at, lan) {
        out.push(format!("LAN play's pairs since the last count (races, their lobbies): {l}"));
    }
    out
}

/// One kind of pairs: how many, the shares of one country and one region (of those whose two countries are known),
/// and the way from one player to the other through the server (both round trips together): all, within one region,
/// across regions.  None for no pair of two players on the switch.
fn pairs(at: &HashMap<u32, &Seen>, list: &[(u32, u32)]) -> Option<String> {
    let (mut n, mut known, mut country, mut region_) = (0usize, 0usize, 0usize, 0usize);
    let (mut all, mut same, mut across) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    for (a, b) in list {
        let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (at.get(a), at.get(b)) else { continue };
        n += 1;
        let both = a.country != 0 && b.country != 0;
        let one = both && region(a.country) == region(b.country);
        if both {
            known += 1;
            country += (a.country == b.country) as usize;
            region_ += one as usize;
        }
        if let (Some(x), Some(y)) = (a.base, b.base) {
            all.push(x + y);
            if both {
                if one { same.push(x + y) } else { across.push(x + y) }
            }
        }
    }
    if n == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let pct = |k: usize| if known == 0 { 0.0 } else { 100.0 * k as f64 / known as f64 };
    let mut l = format!("{n} {} of players", if n == 1 { "pair" } else { "pairs" });
    if known > 0 {
        let _ = write!(
            l,
            ", {:.0} % in one country and {:.0} % in one region (of the {known} whose countries are known)",
            pct(country),
            pct(region_)
        );
    }
    let _ = write!(
        l,
        "; from one player to the other through the server (their round trips together, pairs and ms p50/p90): all {}, \
         within one region {}, across regions {}",
        spread(&mut all),
        spread(&mut same),
        spread(&mut across)
    );
    Some(l)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn seen(vip: u32, c: &[u8; 2], base: Option<f64>) -> Seen {
        Seen { vip, country: if c == b"--" { 0 } else { code(*c) }, base }
    }

    #[test]
    fn percentiles_by_nearest_rank() {
        assert_eq!(p50_90(&mut []), None);
        assert_eq!(p50_90(&mut [7.0]), Some((7.0, 7.0)));
        assert_eq!(p50_90(&mut [4.0, 1.0, 3.0, 2.0]), Some((2.0, 4.0)));
        let mut v: Vec<f64> = (1..=10).rev().map(f64::from).collect();
        assert_eq!(p50_90(&mut v), Some((5.0, 9.0)));
        let mut v: Vec<f64> = (1..=100).map(f64::from).collect();
        assert_eq!(p50_90(&mut v), Some((50.0, 90.0)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn countries_and_regions() {
        assert_eq!(REGIONS[region(code(*b"DE"))], "Western Europe");
        assert_eq!(REGIONS[region(code(*b"RU"))], "Eastern Europe");
        assert_eq!(REGIONS[region(code(*b"TR"))], "Western Asia");
        assert_eq!(REGIONS[region(code(*b"BR"))], "South America");
        assert_eq!(REGIONS[region(code(*b"MX"))], "Central America and the Caribbean");
        assert_eq!(REGIONS[region(code(*b"ZA"))], "Sub-Saharan Africa");
        assert_eq!(REGIONS[region(code(*b"AQ"))], "elsewhere");
        assert_eq!(region(0), 0);
        assert_eq!(letters(code(*b"NL")), "NL");
    }

    // a destination noted once, at most LAN_TO of them, all taken at once
    #[test]
    fn lan_pairs_noted_and_taken() {
        let to: [AtomicU32; LAN_TO] = Default::default();
        for d in [5, 6, 5, 7, 6, 5] {
            race_with(&to, d);
        }
        let mut got = Vec::new();
        take(&to, &mut got);
        got.sort_unstable();
        assert_eq!(got, [5, 6, 7]);
        take(&to, &mut got);
        assert_eq!(got.len(), 3, "taken: none left");
        // a race's five others, each noted (they may share a place: then each is there or its neighbour)
        let to: [AtomicU32; LAN_TO] = Default::default();
        let others = [0x0A4D_0003u32, 0x0A4D_0104, 0x0A4D_0205, 0x0A4D_0306, 0x0A4D_0407];
        for _ in 0..3 {
            others.iter().for_each(|&d| race_with(&to, d));
        }
        let mut got = Vec::new();
        take(&to, &mut got);
        assert!(got.len() >= 3 && got.iter().all(|d| others.contains(d)), "{got:x?}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_lines() {
        let p = [
            seen(1, b"DE", Some(20.0)),
            seen(2, b"DE", Some(30.0)),
            seen(3, b"NL", Some(15.0)),
            seen(4, b"BR", Some(200.0)),
            seen(5, b"BR", Some(220.0)),
            seen(6, b"--", Some(90.0)),
            seen(7, b"RU", None),
        ];
        let l = lines(&p, &[(1, 2), (1, 3), (4, 5), (1, 4), (3, 6), (2, 99)], &[(4, 5)]);
        assert_eq!(l.len(), 4, "{l:#?}");
        assert_eq!(
            l[0],
            "round trips to the server by country (each player's lowest of the last 30-60 s, players and ms p50/p90): \
             all 6 30/220; BR 2 200/220; DE 2 20/30; NL 1 15/15; unknown 1 90/90; 1 not timed yet"
        );
        assert_eq!(l[1], "round trips to the server by region: Western Europe 3 20/30; South America 2 200/220; unknown 1 90/90");
        // (2, 99): a player gone; (3, 6): a country not known, in the ways only
        assert_eq!(
            l[2],
            "free-roam links now: 5 pairs of players, 50 % in one country and 75 % in one region (of the 4 whose countries \
             are known); from one player to the other through the server (their round trips together, pairs and ms \
             p50/p90): all 5 105/420, within one region 3 50/420, across regions 1 220/220"
        );
        assert!(l[3].starts_with("LAN play's pairs since the last count (races, their lobbies): 1 pair of players, 100 % in one country"));
        // nobody timed: nothing
        assert!(lines(&[seen(1, b"DE", None)], &[], &[]).is_empty());
        // the rest past the top countries in one entry
        let many: Vec<Seen> = (0..20u8).map(|i| seen(u32::from(i) + 1, &[b'A' + i, b'A'], Some(f64::from(i)))).collect();
        let l = lines(&many, &[], &[]);
        assert!(l[0].ends_with("; 8 more countries 8 15/19"), "{}", l[0]);
    }
}

//! Players' license plates in free roam (runtime/plates.c): a HELLO to a peer carries the player's plate after its
//! flag, with the header flag RC_HF_PLATE (runtime/roam_core.h): up to 8 capitals and digits that every other player
//! near it sees on its car.  The switch is where all of them pass, so here (route.rs, every frame a page sends,
//! bundled or not) a plate HELLO goes on, but
//!  - one whose plate is not capitals and digits, or is cut short, goes on without it (as a game's own decoder would
//!    show none);
//!  - one whose plate reads as a slur (nfsu2_names `blocked_plate`: as a player's name, and the words that read as one
//!    only on a plate, "BIGFAG", "HH88") goes on without it, and a `[plate]` line says
//!    so (once for each plate of the player): the operator's tools take the player by the name the line gives (`ctl
//!    who`, `kick`, `ban`, as for a name).  The player is heard as before: a game whose word list is older than the
//!    server's (a page or module of before a new round of the name filter) passes its own plate, and only the plate
//!    goes;
//!  - one whose plate is another than the player's last one within `EVERY_MS` of it goes on with the last one until
//!    then, so a player who changes plates again and again costs the others a texture's pixels every 10 s at most;
//!    each plate that goes is a `[plate]` line.
//!
//! The HELLO is rewritten for that (`rewrite`: the plate's bytes, the header's flag, the length, the CRC), and only
//! one whose length and CRC are right: one that is not goes as it came, and every game drops it.  A HELLO without the
//! flag (an older game's, a player without a plate) is not looked at.

use parking_lot::Mutex;

/// a player's plate changes for the others at most this often (runtime/roam_game.c PLATE_EVERY_US)
pub(crate) const EVERY_MS: i64 = 10_000;
/// runtime/roam_core.h RC_PLATE_MAX
pub(crate) const MAX: usize = 8;

const HF_CREW: u16 = 0x0200;
const HF_PLATE: u16 = 0x8000;
/// the switch frame's header before the datagram: kind, addresses, ports
const FRAME_HDR: usize = 16;

/// A plate HELLO's plate, as `hello_plate` found it
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) enum Found<'a> {
    /// its plate: at `at` in the datagram (its length byte), with the name over the player's car
    Plate { at: usize, plate: &'a [u8], name: &'a [u8] },
    /// one whose plate is cut short or not capitals and digits (or not where the flag says)
    Broken,
}

/// A free-roam frame's HELLO plate: None for any other frame (`frame`: a switch frame, the datagram after its header)
pub(crate) fn hello_plate(frame: &[u8]) -> Option<Found<'_>> {
    let d = frame.get(FRAME_HDR..)?;
    if frame[0] != crate::KIND_UDP || d.len() < 29 + 4 || &d[..4] != b"N2FR" || d[4] != 1 || d[5] != 1 {
        return None;
    }
    let flags = u16::from_le_bytes([d[14], d[15]]);
    if flags & HF_PLATE == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    Some(parse(&d[..d.len() - 4], flags).unwrap_or(Found::Broken))
}

/// After the 16-byte header: core 2, platform, status, port 2, cfg 2, room 4, the name (its length, then it), the ids
/// it hears (their count, then 4 each), then with RC_HF_CREW the crews (their count, 4 each), the links (1), the outrun's
/// player (4), the flag (its length, then it) and the plate (its length, then it): roam_core.c rc_encode
fn parse(d: &[u8], flags: u16) -> Option<Found<'_>> {
    if flags & HF_CREW == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let nl = *d.get(28)? as usize;
    let name = d.get(29..29 + nl)?;
    let mut at = 29 + nl;
    let seen = *d.get(at)? as usize;
    at += 1 + 4 * seen;
    let crews = *d.get(at)? as usize;
    at += 1 + 4 * crews + 1 + 4;
    let flag = *d.get(at)? as usize;
    at += 1 + flag;
    let n = *d.get(at)? as usize;
    let plate = d.get(at + 1..at + 1 + n)?;
    (seen <= 64 && crews <= 4 && flag <= 6 && (1..=MAX).contains(&n) && ok(plate)).then_some(Found::Plate { at, plate, name })
}

/// capitals and digits only (runtime/roam_core.c rc_plate_ok)
pub(crate) fn ok(plate: &[u8]) -> bool {
    plate.len() <= MAX && plate.iter().all(|b| b.is_ascii_uppercase() || b.is_ascii_digit())
}

/// A plate HELLO's frame with `plate` in place of its own (the plate's bytes at `at`), or without one (`plate` None:
/// the header's flag off, the plate's bytes gone; `at` None: a plate not found, only the flag off); the datagram's
/// length and CRC made right.  None: the frame's length or CRC was not right to begin with (it goes as it came, and no
/// game takes it)
pub(crate) fn rewrite(frame: &[u8], at: Option<usize>, plate: Option<&[u8]>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    if !intact(frame) {
        return None;
    }
    let d = &frame[FRAME_HDR..];
    let n = d.len();
    let mut out = frame[..FRAME_HDR].to_vec();
    match at {
        Some(at) => {
            let end = at + 1 + *d.get(at)? as usize;
            if end > n - 4 {
                return None;
            }
            out.extend_from_slice(&d[..at]);
            if let Some(p) = plate {
                out.push(p.len() as u8);
                out.extend_from_slice(p);
            }
            out.extend_from_slice(&d[end..n - 4]);
        }
        None => out.extend_from_slice(&d[..n - 4]),
    }
    let flags = u16::from_le_bytes([out[FRAME_HDR + 14], out[FRAME_HDR + 15]]);
    let flags = if plate.is_some_and(|p| !p.is_empty()) { flags } else { flags & !HF_PLATE };
    out[FRAME_HDR + 14..FRAME_HDR + 16].copy_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
    let len = (out.len() - FRAME_HDR + 4) as u16;
    out[FRAME_HDR + 6..FRAME_HDR + 8].copy_from_slice(&len.to_le_bytes());
    let crc = crc32fast::hash(&out[FRAME_HDR..]);
    out.extend_from_slice(&crc.to_le_bytes());
    Some(out)
}

/// a frame's datagram has the length and CRC it says: a game takes it (one that has not is not judged either)
pub(crate) fn intact(frame: &[u8]) -> bool {
    let Some(d) = frame.get(FRAME_HDR..) else { return false };
    let n = d.len();
    n >= 29 + 4
        && u16::from_le_bytes([d[6], d[7]]) as usize == n
        && u32::from_le_bytes([d[n - 4], d[n - 3], d[n - 2], d[n - 1]]) == crc32fast::hash(&d[..n - 4])
}

/// What the switch keeps of a player's plates (lib.rs Peer)
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Seen {
    /// the plate that last went to the others, and when (mono ms)
    last: Option<(Box<[u8]>, i64)>,
    /// the last plate taken out as a slur (its line is written once)
    refused: Option<Box<[u8]>>,
}

/// What to do with a plate HELLO
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub(crate) enum Verdict {
    /// on as it is
    Go,
    /// on, a new plate: a `[plate]` line
    New,
    /// on with the player's last plate instead (a change too soon)
    Last(Box<[u8]>),
    /// on without its plate: it reads as a slur, a `[plate]` line (the first time)
    Slur { tell: bool },
}

/// The verdict on `plate` (checked by `hello_plate`) from the player whose plates `seen` keeps, at `now` (mono ms)
pub(crate) fn judge(seen: &Mutex<Seen>, plate: &[u8], now: i64) -> Verdict {
    let mut s = seen.lock();
    if nfsu2_names::blocked_plate(std::str::from_utf8(plate).unwrap_or("")) {
        let tell = s.refused.as_deref() != Some(plate);
        s.refused = Some(plate.into());
        return Verdict::Slur { tell };
    }
    match &s.last {
        Some((p, _)) if **p == *plate => Verdict::Go,
        Some((p, at)) if now - at < EVERY_MS => Verdict::Last(p.clone()),
        _ => {
            s.last = Some((plate.into(), now));
            Verdict::New
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// a switch frame with a HELLO of core 17 from "Ann", its plate `plate` (none: no plate field at all), the header's
    /// `flags`, length and CRC right
    pub(crate) fn frame(plate: &[u8], flags: u16) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut f = vec![0u8; 16];
        f[0] = crate::KIND_UDP;
        let mut d = vec![0u8; 29];
        d[..4].copy_from_slice(b"N2FR");
        d[4] = 1;
        d[5] = 1;
        d[14..16].copy_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
        d[16] = 17;
        d[28] = 3;
        d.extend_from_slice(b"Ann");
        d.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
        if flags & HF_PLATE != 0 || !plate.is_empty() {
            d.push(plate.len() as u8);
            d.extend_from_slice(plate);
        }
        let n = (d.len() + 4) as u16;
        d[6..8].copy_from_slice(&n.to_le_bytes());
        let crc = crc32fast::hash(&d);
        d.extend_from_slice(&crc.to_le_bytes());
        f.extend_from_slice(&d);
        f
    }

    #[test]
    fn capitals_and_digits_are_a_plate_anything_else_is_broken() {
        for p in [&b"A"[..], b"AB123456", b"0", b"ZZZZZZZZ"] {
            assert!(
                matches!(hello_plate(&frame(p, HF_CREW | HF_PLATE)), Some(Found::Plate { plate, name: b"Ann", .. }) if plate == p),
                "{p:?}"
            );
        }
        for p in [&b""[..], b"123456789", b"lower", b"A B", b"A\0B", b"A-B", "\u{c9}".as_bytes()] {
            assert_eq!(hello_plate(&frame(p, HF_CREW | HF_PLATE)), Some(Found::Broken), "{p:?}");
        }
        // without the flags: not a plate HELLO, or a broken one
        assert_eq!(hello_plate(&frame(b"", HF_CREW)), None);
        assert_eq!(hello_plate(&frame(b"AB12", HF_PLATE)), Some(Found::Broken));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_hello_cut_short_is_broken() {
        let f = frame(b"ABCDEFGH", HF_CREW | HF_PLATE);
        for n in 16 + 29 + 4..f.len() {
            assert!(!matches!(hello_plate(&f[..n]), Some(Found::Plate { plate: b"ABCDEFGH", .. })), "{n}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_rewritten_hello_is_the_one_a_game_would_send_with_that_plate_or_none() {
        let f = frame(b"N1GGER", HF_CREW | HF_PLATE);
        let Some(Found::Plate { at, .. }) = hello_plate(&f) else { panic!("a plate HELLO") };
        // another plate in its place, or none: the HELLO the game makes with it, byte for byte
        assert_eq!(rewrite(&f, Some(at), Some(b"OLD1")).unwrap(), frame(b"OLD1", HF_CREW | HF_PLATE));
        let none = rewrite(&f, Some(at), None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(none, frame(b"", HF_CREW));
        assert_eq!(hello_plate(&none), None, "no plate HELLO any more");
        // a broken one: the flag off, its bytes left after the rest (a game reads past them: none)
        let b = frame(b"A B", HF_CREW | HF_PLATE);
        let r = rewrite(&b, None, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(u16::from_le_bytes([r[16 + 14], r[16 + 15]]), HF_CREW);
        assert_eq!(r.len(), b.len());
        assert_eq!(hello_plate(&r), None);
        // a frame whose CRC or length is not right goes as it came
        let mut bad = f.clone();
        *bad.last_mut().unwrap() ^= 1;
        assert_eq!(rewrite(&bad, Some(at), None), None);
        let mut short = f.clone();
        short.truncate(f.len() - 1);
        assert_eq!(rewrite(&short, Some(at), None), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn slurs_are_taken_out_and_told_once_changes_wait_ten_seconds() {
        let seen = Mutex::new(Seen::default());
        assert_eq!(judge(&seen, b"N1GGER", 0), Verdict::Slur { tell: true });
        assert_eq!(judge(&seen, b"N1GGER", 100), Verdict::Slur { tell: false });
        assert_eq!(judge(&seen, b"1488", 200), Verdict::Slur { tell: true });
        // and what reads as one only on a plate (nfsu2_names blocked_plate)
        assert_eq!(judge(&seen, b"BIGFAG", 200), Verdict::Slur { tell: true });
        assert_eq!(judge(&seen, b"HH88", 200), Verdict::Slur { tell: true });
        assert_eq!(judge(&seen, b"ABC123", 300), Verdict::New);
        assert_eq!(judge(&seen, b"ABC123", 400), Verdict::Go);
        assert_eq!(judge(&seen, b"XYZ9", 300 + EVERY_MS - 1), Verdict::Last(b"ABC123"[..].into()));
        assert_eq!(judge(&seen, b"ABC123", 300 + EVERY_MS - 1), Verdict::Go);
        assert_eq!(judge(&seen, b"XYZ9", 300 + EVERY_MS), Verdict::New);
    }
}

{"id": "AT001576", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/server-rs/crates/lan/src/queue.rs", "originalBytes": 15447, "originalSha256": "bfdde88382fdb37c7bf62654c2a9dadb3ce715ffa3e6cea1909fbdf03d2d6f81", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 15447, "utf8TotalBytes": 15447}
