//! The line: when every place is taken, a page that can wait (/lan?queue, `AttachOpts::queue`) is not closed with "LAN
//! full" but waits in line, first come first served, and takes the first place that frees up once everyone before it
//! has one.  While anyone waits every newcomer waits too, so asking again and again never passes the line (a page of
//! before, which cannot wait, gets "LAN full" as it did, until the line is empty); only a page with its token back for
//! the address it held (a dropped player, `reserve_ms`) goes in at once: that place was never free.
//!
//! What a waiting page hears: {"t":"queue","pos":p,"of":n,"eta":s,"ticket":"..."} at once (the ticket only then), the
//! same without the ticket every `line_tell_ms` when its place changed, and its welcome when its turn comes (from then
//! on it is a player like any other).  pos: its place, 1 the next in; of: everyone in line; eta: about how many seconds
//! until its turn, at the pace the line moved up over the last `PACE_MS` (those who went in and those who left it; left
//! out until it moved a few times).
//!
//! A waiting page's connection that ends without the page letting it go (a dropped link: not 1000 "idle" or
//! "closed") keeps its place for `reserve_ms`, as a dropped player's address is kept: the page comes back with
//! ?resume and the ticket in its hello and takes its place again.  Meanwhile the ones after it go in as places free up,
//! and it is the first of them once it is back.  What a page sends while it waits: its hello (kept for its welcome),
//! {"t":"lan"} (kept the same way), {"t":"ping"} (answered); its frames go nowhere.  One that sends nothing for
//! `SILENT_MS` is gone (the page pings every 2 s), and so is its place.

use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};
use std::sync::Arc;

use bytes::Bytes;
use indexmap::IndexMap;
use nfsu2_util::{Bucket, mono_ms, now_ms};
use serde_json::{Map, Value};

use crate::conn::{Conn, Out};
use crate::members::{Members, held_address};
use crate::text::{new_token, parse_json, token_fits, token_hash};
use crate::{AttachCtx, LanSwitch};

/// the pace of the line is what went in this long ago or since (ms)
const PACE_MS: f64 = 5.0 * 60_000.0;
/// the line moved at least this many times before a page is told how long it may wait
const PACE_MIN: usize = 3;
/// a waiting page that sends nothing for this long has gone (ms)
const SILENT_MS: f64 = 60_000.0;

/// One in line.
pub(crate) struct Waiter {
    /// its connection; none while it is away (its place kept for its ticket until `until`)
    conn: Option<(Arc<Conn>, Arc<AttachCtx>)>,
    ticket: [u8; 32],
    until: i64,
    /// the place it was last told (0: none yet)
    told: usize,
    /// when it came into line (mono ms)
    came: f64,
}

/// The pages waiting for a place, in their order (under the `members` lock).
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Line {
    /// by a number of their own: a page back with its ticket takes its entry again
    waiters: IndexMap<u64, Waiter>,
    next: u64,
    /// when the line last moved up (mono ms, `PACE_MS`): one went in, or left it (let go, or away too long)
    moved: VecDeque<f64>,
    /// since when anyone has waited (mono ms), and the longest wait of those that went in since (ms)
    since: Option<f64>,
    longest: f64,
    /// when the waiting pages were last told their places (mono ms)
    told_at: f64,
    /// the pages the line let in lately, by their tickets: the address it gave each and the hash of its token, until
    /// when (now_ms).  A page whose link went as it was let in never had its welcome (nor its token): back with its
    /// ticket it takes that place, held or kept for it, as its token would (`seated_for`)
    seated: HashMap<[u8; 32], (u32, [u8; 32], i64)>,
}

impl Line {
    /// the place a ticket's page was given lately (as `held_address` gives a token's): its address, and the
    /// connection of the same page that the switch still holds there; (0, None) for none
    pub(crate) fn seated_for(
        &self,
        peers: &IndexMap<u32, Arc<crate::Peer>>,
        reserved: &IndexMap<u32, crate::members::Reservation>,
        ticket: &str,
    ) -> (u32, Option<Arc<crate::Peer>>) {
        let now = now_ms();
        let Some(&(vip, token, _)) = self.seated.iter().find(|(h, s)| s.2 > now && token_fits(ticket, h)).map(|(_, s)| s) else {
            return (0, None);
        };
        match peers.get(&vip) {
            Some(p) if p.token_hash == token => (vip, Some(p.clone())),
            None if reserved.get(&vip).is_some_and(|r| r.hash == token && r.until > now) => (vip, None),
            _ => (0, None),
        }
    }
    /// anyone waits (or is away and keeps a place)
    pub(crate) fn waiting(&self) -> bool {
        !self.waiters.is_empty()
    }
    /// anyone waits who is there (not away): a newcomer would come after them (the ones away it passes, as the
    /// line's places that free up do, until they are back)
    pub(crate) fn before_newcomers(&self) -> bool {
        self.waiters.values().any(|w| w.conn.is_some())
    }
    pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.waiters.len()
    }
    /// the line's pace: places a second it moves up by (None until it moved `PACE_MIN` times)
    fn pace(&mut self, now: f64) -> Option<f64> {
        while self.moved.front().is_some_and(|&t| t < now - PACE_MS) {
            self.moved.pop_front();
        }
        let n = self.moved.len();
        if n < PACE_MIN {
            return None;
        }
        // from the first of them until now (a stall since the last one counts), 10 s at least
        let span = (now - self.moved[0]).max(10_000.0);
        Some(n as f64 / (span / 1000.0))
    }
}

/// What a waiting connection sent (its `Conn::wait`, its own lock: never taken before the `members` lock).
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Wait {
    /// its entry in line (0: not in line)
    pub(crate) id: u64,
    /// its hello and LAN play, for its welcome
    hello: Option<Map<String, Value>>,
    texts: Option<Bucket>,
    /// when it last sent anything (mono ms)
    last_in: f64,
}

/// {"t":"queue",...}
fn told(pos: usize, of: usize, eta: Option<f64>, ticket: Option<&str>) -> Bytes {
    let mut s = format!(r#"{{"t":"queue","pos":{pos},"of":{of}"#);
    if let Some(e) = eta {
        s.push_str(&format!(r#","eta":{}"#, e.round() as u64));
    }
    if let Some(t) = ticket {
        s.push_str(&format!(r#","ticket":"{t}""#));
    }
    s.push('}');
    Bytes::from(s)
}

impl LanSwitch {
    /// conn waits in line (false: the line is full, or the connection is gone)
    pub(crate) fn enqueue(&self, m: &mut Members, conn: &Arc<Conn>, ctx: &Arc<AttachCtx>, hello: Option<Map<String, Value>>) -> bool {
        if m.line.waiters.len() >= self.o.max_waiting || !conn.open() {
            return false;
        }
        let now = mono_ms();
        m.line.next += 1;
        let id = m.line.next;
        let ticket = new_token();
        *conn.wait.lock() = Wait { id, hello, texts: Some(Bucket::new_at(self.o.text_rate, now)), last_in: now };
        let of = m.line.waiters.len() + 1;
        m.line
            .waiters
            .insert(id, Waiter { conn: Some((conn.clone(), ctx.clone())), ticket: token_hash(&ticket), until: 0, told: of, came: now });
        if m.line.since.is_none() {
            m.line.since = Some(now);
            m.line.longest = 0.0;
        }
        self.stats.queued.inc();
        let eta = m.line.pace(now).map(|p| of as f64 / p);
        conn.push(Out::Text(told(of, of, eta, Some(&ticket))));
        true
    }

    /// a page back with its ticket takes its place in line again (its connection of before, if the switch still holds
    /// it, goes); false: no place in line has that ticket
    pub(crate) fn rejoin(
        &self,
        m: &mut Members,
        conn: &Arc<Conn>,
        ctx: &Arc<AttachCtx>,
        hello: Option<Map<String, Value>>,
        ticket: &str,
    ) -> bool {
        // (compared in constant time, as a token is)
        let Some(pos) = m.line.waiters.values().position(|w| token_fits(ticket, &w.ticket)) else { return false };
        let now = mono_ms();
        let of = m.line.waiters.len();
        let (&id, w) = m.line.waiters.get_index_mut(pos).expect("its place");
        if let Some((old, _)) = w.conn.replace((conn.clone(), ctx.clone())) {
            old.terminate();
        }
        w.until = 0;
        w.told = pos + 1;
        *conn.wait.lock() = Wait { id, hello, texts: Some(Bucket::new_at(self.o.text_rate, now)), last_in: now };
        self.stats.rejoined.inc();
        let eta = m.line.pace(now).map(|p| (pos + 1) as f64 / p);
        conn.push(Out::Text(told(pos + 1, of, eta, None)));
        true
    }

    /// a connection that ended while it waited: its place goes when the page let go (1000 "idle" or "closed", or the
    /// operator removed it), else
    /// it is kept for its ticket for `reserve_ms` (a newer connection of the same page that took it changes nothing)
    pub(crate) fn left_line(&self, conn: &Arc<Conn>) {
        let id = conn.wait.lock().id;
        if id == 0 {
            return;
        }
        let done = conn.let_go();
        let mut m = self.members.lock();
        let Some(w) = m.line.waiters.get_mut(&id) else { return };
        if !w.conn.as_ref().is_some_and(|(c, _)| Arc::ptr_eq(c, conn)) {
            return;
        }
        if done {
            m.line.waiters.shift_remove(&id);
            m.line.moved.push_back(mono_ms());
            self.stats.line_left.inc();
            if !m.line.waiting() {
                m.line.since = None;
            }
        } else {
            w.conn = None;
            w.until = now_ms() + self.o.reserve_ms;
        }
    }

    /// The line's first ones take the places that are free, as many as there are.
    pub(crate) fn let_in(&self) {
        loop {
            let mut m = self.members.lock();
            // (one whose connection is closing is passed over: its close comes next)
            let Some((&id, (conn, ctx))) =
                m.line.waiters.iter().find_map(|(id, w)| w.conn.as_ref().filter(|(c, _)| c.open()).map(|c| (id, c.clone())))
            else {
                return;
            };
            // (its wait held until it is seated: a message its reader takes meanwhile, its hello say, goes to the player
            // it is then, `waiting_text`, not to a wait that was just let go)
            let mut wait = conn.wait.lock();
            let held = held_address(&m, wait.hello.as_ref());
            let Some((vip, old, resumed)) = self.place(&mut m, held, true) else { return };
            let hello = wait.hello.take();
            let (came, ticket) = m.line.waiters.shift_remove(&id).map_or((f64::NAN, None), |w| (w.came, Some(w.ticket)));
            let now = mono_ms();
            m.line.moved.push_back(now);
            if m.line.since.is_some() {
                m.line.longest = m.line.longest.max(now - came);
            }
            if !m.line.waiting() {
                m.line.since = None;
            }
            self.stats.line_in.inc();
            let (peer, count) = self.seat(&mut m, &conn, &ctx, hello, vip, old);
            if let Some(t) = ticket {
                m.line.seated.insert(t, (peer.vip, peer.token_hash, now_ms() + self.o.reserve_ms));
            }
            *wait = Wait::default();
            drop(wait);
            drop(m);
            if let Some(f) = &ctx.on_join {
                f(peer.vip, resumed, count);
            }
        }
    }

    /// Every second while anyone waits: the places kept for those away run out, the silent ones go, the free places
    /// are taken, and every `line_tell_ms` the waiting pages whose place changed hear it.
    pub(crate) fn line_tick(&self) {
        let now = mono_ms();
        let silent: Vec<Arc<Conn>> = {
            let mut m = self.members.lock();
            let wall = now_ms();
            if !m.line.seated.is_empty() {
                m.line.seated.retain(|_, s| s.2 > wall);
            }
            if !m.line.waiting() {
                return;
            }
            let before = m.line.waiters.len();
            m.line.waiters.retain(|_, w| w.conn.is_some() || w.until > wall);
            for _ in m.line.waiters.len()..before {
                self.stats.line_left.inc();
                m.line.moved.push_back(now);
            }
            if !m.line.waiting() {
                m.line.since = None;
            }
            m.line
                .waiters
                .values()
                .filter_map(|w| w.conn.as_ref().map(|(c, _)| c))
                .filter(|c| c.wait.lock().last_in < now - SILENT_MS)
                .cloned()
                .collect()
        };
        for c in silent {
            c.terminate();
        }
        self.let_in();
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        {
            let mut m = self.members.lock();
            if !m.line.waiting() || now - m.line.told_at < self.o.line_tell_ms as f64 {
                return;
            }
            m.line.told_at = now;
            let pace = m.line.pace(now);
            let of = m.line.waiters.len();
            for (i, w) in m.line.waiters.values_mut().enumerate() {
                if let Some((c, _)) = w.conn.as_ref().filter(|_| w.told != i + 1) {
                    w.told = i + 1;
                    out.push((c.clone(), told(i + 1, of, pace.map(|p| (i + 1) as f64 / p), None)));
                }
            }
        }
        for (c, msg) in out {
            c.push(Out::Text(msg));
        }
    }

    /// a control message from a page in line: its hello and LAN play are kept for its welcome, a ping is answered
    /// (`text_rate`, `max_text` as for a player)
    /// (false: it is not waiting, it was let in just now: the message is the player's)
    pub(crate) fn waiting_text(&self, conn: &Conn, b: &Bytes) -> bool {
        let now = mono_ms();
        let mut w = conn.wait.lock();
        if w.id == 0 {
            return false;
        }
        w.last_in = now;
        if b.len() > self.o.max_text || !w.texts.as_mut().is_some_and(|t| t.take_at(now, 1.0)) {
            self.stats.limited.inc();
            return true;
        }
        let Some(Value::Object(m)) = parse_json(b) else { return true };
        match m.get("t").and_then(Value::as_str) {
            Some("hello") => {
                if w.hello.is_none() {
                    w.hello = Some(m);
                }
            }
            Some("lan") => {
                if let (Some(h), Some(on)) = (w.hello.as_mut(), m.get("on")) {
                    h.insert("lan".into(), on.clone());
                    match m.get("udp") {
                        Some(u) => h.insert("udp".into(), u.clone()),
                        None => h.remove("udp"),
                    };
                }
            }
            Some("ping") => {
                if let Some(id) = m.get("id").and_then(nfsu2_util::json::safe_integer) {
                    conn.push(Out::Text(Bytes::from(format!(r#"{{"t":"pong","id":{id}}}"#))));
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        true
    }

    /// pages in line now, and of those that went in since the line last began, the longest wait (s)
    pub(crate) fn line_view(&self) -> (usize, u64) {
        let m = self.members.lock();
        (m.line.len(), (m.line.longest / 1000.0) as u64)
    }
}

//! A connection's reader: a resume's wait for its hello, then its messages (text, binary, ping, pong, close), each
//! frame routed here, on the reader's own core.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
use std::time::Duration;

use bytes::Bytes;
use nfsu2_util::{mono_ms, now_ms};
use nfsu2_ws::{Message, ReadError, WsReader};
use serde_json::{Map, Value};
use tokio::io::{AsyncRead, AsyncReadExt};
use tokio::time::Instant;

use crate::compact::{F_STAMPED, KIND_COMPACT};
use crate::conn::{Conn, Out};
use crate::text::parse_json;
use crate::{AttachCtx, Cut, KIND_BUNDLE, LanSwitch, Peer, mix};

pub(crate) async fn read_loop<R>(sw: Arc<LanSwitch>, conn: Arc<Conn>, mut r: R, pre: Bytes, ctx: Arc<AttachCtx>)
where
    R: AsyncRead + Unpin + Send,
{
    let mut peer = conn.peer.lock().clone();
    // a resume: the hello first (the welcome follows it), within `resume_wait_ms`
    let mut wait = (ctx.resume && peer.is_none()).then(|| Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(sw.o.resume_wait_ms));
    let mut ws = WsReader::new(&mut r, pre, sw.o.max_payload);
    // one wait for the kill token for the connection's life (a new one each message registered with the token and
    // left it again: two locks a message)
    let killed = conn.kill.cancelled();
    tokio::pin!(killed);
    // its first control message, the hello, names its page's id: a banned one goes (the crate doc's Kicks and bans)
    let mut first_text = true;
    loop {
        // (a page that waited in line has its peer once the line let it in: queue.rs)
        if peer.is_none() && wait.is_none() {
            peer = conn.peer.lock().clone();
        }
        let m = {
            let next = ws.next();
            tokio::pin!(next);
            loop {
                tokio::select! {
                    biased;
                    _ = &mut killed => return,
                    m = &mut next => break m,
                    _ = tokio::time::sleep_until(wait.unwrap_or_else(Instant::now)), if wait.is_some() => {
                        // no hello in time: a fresh address (and the message being read is an ordinary one)
                        wait = None;
                        peer = sw.admit(&conn, &ctx, None);
                    }
                }
            }
        };
        // (a connection that was cut is no longer open: what it sent last goes nowhere)
        match m {
            Ok(Message::Text(b)) => {
                if std::mem::take(&mut first_text) && sw.hello_refused(&conn, &ctx, &b) {
                    continue;
                }
                if wait.take().is_some() {
                    peer = sw.admit(&conn, &ctx, first_hello(&sw, &b));
                } else if let Some(p) = peer.as_ref().filter(|_| conn.open()) {
                    sw.on_message(p, true, b);
                } else if peer.is_none() && conn.open() && !sw.waiting_text(&conn, &b) {
                    // let in just now: the player's message
                    peer = conn.peer.lock().clone();
                    if let Some(p) = &peer {
                        sw.on_message(p, true, b);
                    }
                }
            }
            Ok(Message::Binary(b)) => {
                if wait.take().is_some() {
                    peer = sw.admit(&conn, &ctx, None);
                } else if let Some(p) = peer.as_ref().filter(|_| conn.open()) {
                    sw.on_message(p, false, b);
                    // the Online host behind (nfsu2_util::Backlog): what this client sends it waits in its socket.  (A
                    // load first, not a swap: free roam's messages never feed the host, and a swap is a locked write
                    // on each of them; only this reader sets and clears the flag.)
                    if p.fed_online.load(Relaxed) {
                        p.fed_online.store(false, Relaxed);
                        if sw.online_backlog.over() {
                            tokio::select! {
                                biased;
                                _ = &mut killed => return,
                                _ = sw.online_backlog.room() => {}
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            Ok(Message::Ping(d)) => {
                sw.stats.msg(mix::IN_PING);
                conn.msgs_in.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
                // answered here, under the rate and while the queue has room (nfsu2-ws answers none itself): an answer
                // to every ping queues pongs without a limit for a client that never reads (the phase-2 deploy
                // review's finding 1, of the ws library's own answer: gigabytes in seconds); a copy, not the block the
                // ping was read into (the crate doc's one copy)
                if peer.as_ref().filter(|_| conn.open()).is_some_and(|p| !sw.flood(p) && sw.room(p, Cut::Slow)) {
                    conn.push(Out::Pong(Bytes::copy_from_slice(&d)));
                }
            }
            Ok(Message::Pong(d)) => {
                sw.stats.msg(mix::IN_PONG);
                conn.msgs_in.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
                // only a pong carrying the payload of one of the switch's pings counts: its round trip is timed, and
                // for a ping queued since the keepalive's last tick it says the client is there (lag.rs)
                if let Some(p) = &peer {
                    let ours = p.probe.lock().pong(&d, nfsu2_util::mono_ms(), &p.share);
                    match ours {
                        Some(true) => p.alive.store(true, Relaxed),
                        Some(false) => {}
                        None => {
                            sw.flood(p);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            Ok(Message::Close(code, reason)) => {
                conn.close_received(code, reason);
                break;
            }
            Err(ReadError::Protocol { code, .. }) => {
                conn.protocol_error(code);
                break;
            }
            Err(ReadError::Closed) => return,
        }
    }
    // after a close frame (or a broken one) nothing more is read as messages: what comes is drained until the client
    // ends the connection, or the close timer does
    drop(ws);
    let mut scratch = vec![0u8; 4096];
    loop {
        tokio::select! {
            biased;
            _ = &mut killed => return,
            n = r.read(&mut scratch) => match n {
                Ok(0) | Err(_) => return,
                Ok(_) => {}
            },
        }
    }
}

/// a resume's first message: a hello, when it is one
fn first_hello(sw: &LanSwitch, b: &Bytes) -> Option<Map<String, Value>> {
    if b.len() > sw.o.max_text {
        return None;
    }
    match parse_json(b) {
        Some(Value::Object(m)) if m.get("t").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("hello") => Some(m),
        _ => None,
    }
}

impl LanSwitch {
    /// a control frame over `ctl_rate` cuts the connection (no browser sends any)
    pub(crate) fn flood(&self, p: &Peer) -> bool {
        if p.ctl.lock().ctl.take_at(mono_ms(), 1.0) {
            return false;
        }
        self.cut(p, Cut::Flood);
        true
    }

    /// a message of an admitted connection: a control message (`text_rate`, `max_text`), a bundle (`max_bundle`) or
    /// a frame (`max_frame`)
    fn on_message(&self, peer: &Arc<Peer>, text: bool, data: Bytes) {
        peer.alive.store(true, Relaxed);
        peer.conn.msgs_in.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
        peer.last_in.store(now_ms(), Relaxed);
        let n = data.len();
        let o = &self.o;
        if text {
            self.stats.msg(mix::IN_TEXT);
            self.stats.entry_in(mix::TEXT, n);
            if n > o.max_text || !peer.ctl.lock().texts.take_at(mono_ms(), 1.0) {
                self.stats.limited.inc();
                return;
            }
            let Some(Value::Object(m)) = parse_json(&data) else { return };
            match m.get("t").and_then(Value::as_str) {
                Some("hello") => self.hello(peer, &m),
                Some("lan") => {
                    // its sockets' ports first: a broadcast routed after the list changed sees them
                    peer.udp.store(crate::udp_of(m.get("udp")), Relaxed);
                    self.set_lan(peer, nfsu2_util::json::is_num(m.get("on"), 1.0))
                }
                Some("ping") => {
                    if let Some(id) = m.get("id").and_then(nfsu2_util::json::safe_integer) {
                        self.send(peer, Out::Text(Bytes::from(format!(r#"{{"t":"pong","id":{id}}}"#))));
                    }
                }
                Some("friend" | "room" | "flying") => self.page_text(peer, m.clone()),
                _ => {}
            }
            return;
        }
        if n < 12 {
            return;
        }
        if data[0] == KIND_BUNDLE {
            if n > o.max_bundle {
                self.stats.limited.inc();
                return;
            }
            self.stats.bundles_in.inc();
            self.stats.msg(mix::IN_BUNDLE);
            self.stats.entry_in(mix::FRAMING, 4);
            let mut at = 4;
            // a stamp of the switch's echoed (LanSwitch::probe): its 8 bytes, then how long the page held it (µs, at
            // most 10 s); its round trip timed as a pong's, less that wait
            if data[1] & F_STAMPED != 0 {
                if n < 16 {
                    self.stats.limited.inc();
                    return;
                }
                self.stats.entry_in(mix::FRAMING, 12);
                let held = (be32(&data, 12) as f64 / 1000.0).min(10_000.0);
                match peer.probe.lock().pong(&data[4..12], mono_ms() - held, &peer.share) {
                    Some(true) => peer.alive.store(true, Relaxed),
                    Some(false) => {}
                    None => {
                        self.flood(peer);
                    }
                }
                self.stats.echoes.inc();
                at = 16;
            }
            // each entry as a frame of its own; a broken entry, or one over the budgets, ends the bundle
            while at + 4 <= n {
                let k = data[at] as usize;
                let len = u16::from_be_bytes([data[at + 2], data[at + 3]]) as usize;
                let f = at + 4 + 4 * k;
                let end = f + len;
                if len < 12 || len > o.max_frame || end > n || data[f] == KIND_BUNDLE || data[f] == KIND_COMPACT {
                    self.stats.limited.inc();
                    return;
                }
                let frame = data.slice(f..end);
                self.stats.entry_in(mix::FRAMING, 4);
                if k > 0 {
                    self.stats.entry_in(mix::ADDRS, 4 * k);
                }
                self.stats.entry_in(mix::of_page(&frame, if k == 0 { be32(&frame, 8) } else { be32(&data, at + 4) }), len);
                let routed = if k == 0 {
                    self.route(peer, &frame, std::iter::once(be32(&frame, 8)))
                } else {
                    self.route(peer, &frame, (0..k).map(|j| be32(&data, at + 4 + 4 * j)))
                };
                if !routed {
                    return;
                }
                at = end;
            }
            return;
        }
        // (a compact bundle is the switch's own: the page takes its sources as they are)
        self.stats.msg(mix::IN_FRAME);
        if n > o.max_frame || data[0] == KIND_COMPACT {
            self.stats.limited.inc();
            return;
        }
        self.stats.entry_in(mix::of_page(&data, be32(&data, 8)), n);
        self.route(peer, &data, std::iter::once(be32(&data, 8)));
    }
}

fn be32(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_be_bytes([b[at], b[at + 1], b[at + 2], b[at + 3]])
}

//! A frame from a browser to the browsers it reaches, the free-roam hub or the Online host (the sender's budgets, the
//! receivers' queue rules, the stream rules).  It runs on the sender's reader, on whatever core that is.

use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{
    AtomicBool,
    Ordering::{Relaxed, SeqCst},
};

use bytes::{BufMut, Bytes, BytesMut};
use nfsu2_util::{FrameCtx, mono_ms};

use crate::away;
use crate::compact;
use crate::conn::{Conn, Out};
use crate::lag::{self, SHARE_FULL};
use crate::{BROADCAST, Cause, Cut, KIND_LAN_ICMP, KIND_LAN_UDP, KIND_STREAM, KIND_UDP, LanSwitch, Peer, STREAM_LOW, plates, slot};

/// What a stream segment waiting at the switch costs it besides its bytes (its entry here, its copy's allocation),
/// counted with them against `stream_share` and `stream_queue`, so that those bound the memory for segments of a few
/// bytes too (the second security audit: 12-byte segments, 87,000 of them under one client's share).  A LAN race's
/// segments are far larger and far fewer.
const SEGMENT_COST: usize = 128;

/// what a stream segment counts for in the switch's queue
fn cost(data: &Bytes) -> usize {
    data.len() + SEGMENT_COST
}

/// The stream segments (kind 4) waiting at each receiver (by connection), behind the switch's one lock for them.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Streams {
    by_conn: HashMap<u64, StreamQueue>,
    /// tells one sending client's queued segments from those of the same client after it was cut
    era: u64,
}

impl Streams {
    pub(crate) fn remove(&mut self, conn: u64) {
        self.by_conn.remove(&conn);
    }
}

/// The stream segments waiting at one receiver, behind the switch's own queue (`stream_queue`, `stream_share`).
#[derive(Default)]
struct StreamQueue {
    sq: VecDeque<Segment>,
    /// bytes queued by sending client (each segment's `cost`), in the order they first queued (the first of equals
    /// is cut)
    queued: Vec<Queued>,
    total: usize,
    /// since when the queue is not empty, and when a segment last went out
    since: f64,
    out: f64,
}

struct Queued {
    group: Arc<str>,
    era: u64,
    n: usize,
}

struct Segment {
    data: Bytes,
    src: u32,
    dst: u32,
    group: Arc<str>,
    era: u64,
}

impl StreamQueue {
    fn mine(&self, g: &str) -> Option<usize> {
        self.queued.iter().position(|q| &*q.group == g)
    }
}

impl LanSwitch {
    /// One frame, to each of `dsts` in turn (the frame's own destination, or a bundle entry's list): from peer to the
    /// browsers each reaches, the free-roam hub or the Online host, within peer's budgets.  False: over them (what
    /// follows in a bundle goes too).
    ///
    /// Each destination costs k frames of n bytes (k the others on a broadcast's list, 1 for any other), and the first
    /// one the buckets cannot pay for ends it.  The buckets are locked once for all of them (32 friends were 32 times
    /// three locks and a clock read): the destinations go up to the first whose running total one of the buckets
    /// cannot pay for, which is where checking them one destination after the other stops.
    pub(crate) fn route(&self, peer: &Arc<Peer>, data: &Bytes, dsts: impl Iterator<Item = u32> + Clone) -> bool {
        // free roam's license plates (plates.rs): a HELLO goes on without a broken plate or a slur, and with the last
        // plate for a change too soon
        let fixed;
        let data = match plates::hello_plate(data).and_then(|p| self.plate_fix(peer, data, p)) {
            Some(f) => {
                fixed = f;
                &fixed
            }
            None => data,
        };
        let n = data.len();
        let lan_only = (KIND_LAN_UDP..=KIND_LAN_ICMP).contains(&data[0]);
        if lan_only {
            peer.conn.lan_sent.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
        }
        let reaches = |p: &Arc<Peer>| !Arc::ptr_eq(p, peer) && p.open() && (!lan_only || p.lan());
        // what the switch sends for each: a broadcast costs its size for every player on its list but the sender (all
        // of them, or for LAN play's kinds those with LAN play open), so the switch never sends more for a client
        // than its budgets allow (the audit's F2: one 4 MB/s sender made it send 15 x that), and never walks the
        // list for a broadcast that was not paid for (the crate doc's How the work is shared out)
        let list = dsts.clone().any(|d| d == BROADCAST).then(|| if lan_only { self.lan_all.load() } else { self.all.load() });
        let on_list = !lan_only || peer.lan();
        let reached = list.as_ref().map_or(0, |l| l.len().saturating_sub(usize::from(on_list)));
        let costs = dsts.clone().map(|d| if d == BROADCAST { reached.max(1) } else { 1 });
        let (paid, all_paid) = self.charge(peer, mono_ms(), n as f64, costs);
        // free roam: whether the sender drives, from its own HELLO or SNAP (away.rs)
        if let Some(st) = away::status(data) {
            peer.away.store(away::away(st), Relaxed);
            peer.roam_at.store((mono_ms() as u64).max(1), Relaxed);
        }
        if paid > 0 {
            self.stats.frames.add(paid as u64);
            self.stats.bytes.add((n * paid) as u64);
            peer.frames_in.fetch_add(paid as u64, Relaxed);
        }
        // the frame's own copy for the browsers' queues, not the sender's read block (the crate doc's one copy)
        let own_copy;
        let data = if dsts.clone().take(paid).any(|d| Some(d) != self.roam_vip && Some(d) != self.online_vip) {
            own_copy = compact::mark(data);
            &own_copy
        } else {
            data
        };
        for dst in dsts.take(paid) {
            let count = if dst == BROADCAST { reached } else { 0 };
            self.route_one(peer, data, dst, list.as_deref().map(|a| &a[..]), count, &reaches);
        }
        if !all_paid {
            self.stats.limited.inc();
        }
        all_paid
    }

    /// A HELLO with a license plate from `peer` (plates.rs): the frame to send in its place (without its plate, or with
    /// the player's last one), None to send it as it is; the `[plate]` line of a new one or of a slur
    fn plate_fix(&self, peer: &Peer, data: &Bytes, p: plates::Found<'_>) -> Option<Bytes> {
        if !plates::intact(data) {
            return None; // (no game takes it)
        }
        let plates::Found::Plate { at, plate, name } = p else {
            return plates::rewrite(data, None, None).map(Bytes::from);
        };
        let name: String = String::from_utf8_lossy(name).chars().map(|c| if c.is_control() { '?' } else { c }).collect();
        let plate_s = std::str::from_utf8(plate).unwrap_or("");
        match plates::judge(&peer.plates, plate, mono_ms() as i64) {
            plates::Verdict::Go => None,
            plates::Verdict::New => {
                self.line(&format!("[plate] {} \"{name}\" {plate_s}", nfsu2_util::vip_str(peer.vip)));
                None
            }
            plates::Verdict::Last(last) => plates::rewrite(data, Some(at), Some(&last)).map(Bytes::from),
            plates::Verdict::Slur { tell } => {
                if tell {
                    self.line(&format!(
                        "[plate] {} \"{name}\" {plate_s}: reads as a slur, dropped (its HELLOs go on without it)",
                        nfsu2_util::vip_str(peer.vip)
                    ));
                }
                plates::rewrite(data, Some(at), None).map(Bytes::from)
            }
        }
    }

    /// one destination that was paid for: the trace, a host, or the browsers
    fn route_one(
        &self,
        peer: &Arc<Peer>,
        data: &Bytes,
        dst: u32,
        all: Option<&[Arc<Peer>]>,
        count: usize,
        reaches: &impl Fn(&Arc<Peer>) -> bool,
    ) {
        let vip = peer.vip;
        // the hub, the online host and the trace see the frame as sent to them
        if let Some(tap) = &self.tap {
            tap(&own(data, vip, dst));
        }
        if self.roam_vip == Some(dst) {
            // a player under a race ban advertises no lobby race to the hub, and asks to join none (crate::races)
            if peer.conn.no_races.load(Relaxed) && crate::races(data) {
                self.stats.dropped.inc();
                return;
            }
            if let Some(roam) = &self.roam {
                roam.frame(vip, own(data, vip, dst), self.frame_ctx(peer, None));
            }
            return;
        }
        if self.online_vip == Some(dst) {
            if let Some(online) = &self.online {
                // what the host sends while it handles the frame is charged to the sender's budgets
                let cause = Arc::new(Cause {
                    peer: peer.clone(),
                    stats: self.stats.clone(),
                    over: AtomicBool::new(false),
                    counted: AtomicBool::new(false),
                });
                let mut ctx = self.frame_ctx(peer, Some(cause));
                ctx.slot = Some(self.online_backlog.enter());
                peer.fed_online.store(true, Relaxed);
                online.frame(vip, own(data, vip, dst), ctx);
            }
            return;
        }
        if dst == BROADCAST {
            match all {
                Some(all) if count > 0 => {
                    // LAN play's UDP: only to the pages with a socket on its port (the others drop it on arrival:
                    // runtime/web/net_lan.c udp_ports).  Its sender paid for them all (`route`), as before.
                    let port = (data[0] == KIND_LAN_UDP && data.len() >= 16).then(|| u16::from_be_bytes([data[14], data[15]]));
                    for p in all.iter().filter(|p| reaches(p)) {
                        if port.is_some_and(|d| !p.takes_udp(d)) {
                            self.stats.bcast_skipped.inc();
                            self.stats.bcast_skipped_bytes.add(data.len() as u64);
                            continue;
                        }
                        self.deliver(peer, p, data, dst);
                    }
                }
                _ => self.stats.dropped.inc(),
            }
            return;
        }
        let one = slot(dst).map(|i| self.table[i].load());
        match one.as_deref().and_then(|p| p.as_ref()).filter(|p| p.open()) {
            Some(p) => {
                // LAN play's UDP from one player to another (a race, its lobby): the pair, for the 5-minute counts
                // (paths.rs; a load or two, rarely a store)
                if data[0] == KIND_LAN_UDP {
                    crate::paths::race_with(&peer.lan_to, dst);
                }
                self.deliver(peer, p, data, dst)
            }
            None => self.stats.dropped.inc(),
        }
    }

    /// the sender's buckets (connection, client, site, locked in that order everywhere) refilled to `now`: how many
    /// of the destinations (each `costs` frames of n bytes, in order) they pay for, and whether that was all of them;
    /// what those cost is taken
    fn charge(&self, peer: &Peer, now: f64, n: f64, costs: impl Iterator<Item = usize>) -> (usize, bool) {
        let mut a = peer.buckets.lock();
        let mut b = peer.group.buckets.lock();
        let mut c = peer.site.as_ref().map(|s| s.buckets.lock());
        // what the poorest bucket has (checks one destination after the other subtract whole frames and bytes from
        // what each has, exactly: a running total compared with what each had is the same check)
        let (mut frames, mut bytes) = a.refill(now);
        for (f, b) in [Some(b.refill(now)), c.as_mut().map(|c| c.refill(now))].into_iter().flatten() {
            frames = frames.min(f);
            bytes = bytes.min(b);
        }
        let (mut total, mut paid, mut all) = (0.0, 0, true);
        for k in costs {
            let t = total + k as f64;
            if t > frames || t * n > bytes {
                all = false;
                break;
            }
            total = t;
            paid += 1;
        }
        if paid > 0 {
            a.spend_paid(total, total * n);
            b.spend_paid(total, total * n);
            if let Some(c) = c.as_mut() {
                c.spend_paid(total, total * n);
            }
        }
        (paid, all)
    }

    fn frame_ctx(&self, peer: &Peer, cause: Option<Arc<Cause>>) -> FrameCtx {
        FrameCtx {
            group: peer.group.id.clone(),
            site: peer.site.as_ref().map(|s| s.id.clone()),
            cause: cause.map(|c| c as Arc<dyn nfsu2_util::Charge>),
            slot: None,
            owner: peer.conn.owner.get().cloned(),
            no_races: peer.conn.no_races.load(Relaxed),
        }
    }

    /// one frame to one peer, through the impairment when it is on (LAN play's kinds only), always through
    /// `send_frame` (the queue rules).  A frame that races (crate::races) neither leaves a player under a race ban nor
    /// reaches one: its honest friends' games never hear its outrun offers and lobby races, nor it theirs, and no LAN
    /// play (a race once it starts) goes either way.
    pub(crate) fn deliver(&self, from: &Arc<Peer>, p: &Arc<Peer>, data: &Bytes, dst: u32) {
        if (from.conn.no_races.load(Relaxed) || p.conn.no_races.load(Relaxed)) && crate::races(data) {
            self.stats.dropped.inc();
            return;
        }
        match &self.impair {
            Some(im) if (KIND_LAN_UDP..=KIND_LAN_ICMP).contains(&data[0]) => im.deliver(&self.stats, from, p, data, dst),
            _ => self.deliver_now(from, p, data, dst),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn deliver_now(&self, from: &Arc<Peer>, p: &Arc<Peer>, data: &Bytes, dst: u32) {
        if p.open() && self.send_frame(from, p, data, dst) {
            p.frames_out.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
        }
    }

    /// a binary frame to a receiver: a datagram is dropped while the receiver's queue is long (`roam_queue`,
    /// `shed_queue`), a stream segment never is (see `stream_queue`: the receiver or the client flooding it goes
    /// instead)
    fn send_frame(&self, from: &Arc<Peer>, p: &Arc<Peer>, data: &Bytes, dst: u32) -> bool {
        if data[0] == KIND_STREAM {
            return self.send_stream(from, p, data, dst);
        }
        // a player behind on its path gets only its share of free roam's snapshots (lag.rs), one not driving its own
        // (away.rs)
        if data[0] == KIND_UDP {
            let share = p.share.load(Relaxed);
            if share < SHARE_FULL && lag::is_snap(data) && !lag::pick(share) {
                self.stats.thinned.inc();
                return false;
            }
            if p.away.load(Relaxed) && self.slow.is_some() && lag::is_snap(data) && !lag::pick(away::SHARE) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        let q = &p.conn.out;
        let limit = if data[0] == KIND_UDP { self.o.roam_queue } else { self.o.shed_queue };
        if q.buffered() + q.dgram() > limit {
            self.stats.shed.inc();
            return false;
        }
        self.post(p, data, from.vip, dst)
    }

    /// a datagram to p, into its bundle when it takes them, else as it is.  Free roam's wait for the bundle clock's
    /// next tick; LAN play's for LAN play's short one (`lan_ms`, with whatever else is queued): a race's creator sends
    /// each joiner a datagram a frame (60 a second at 60 fps) and the joiners' own come in between, each a message of
    /// its own to the page until 2026-10-31, while a tick's wait of up to 25 ms, at random, made the other cars wobble
    fn post(&self, p: &Arc<Peer>, data: &Bytes, src: u32, dst: u32) -> bool {
        if !p.takes_bundles() {
            return self.send(p, Out::Frame { data: data.clone(), src, dst });
        }
        if !self.room(p, Cut::Slow) {
            self.stats.dropped.inc();
            return false;
        }
        let clock = if (KIND_LAN_UDP..=KIND_LAN_ICMP).contains(&data[0]) {
            self.lan_clock.as_deref()
        } else if p.away.load(Relaxed) && data[1] == compact::ROAM_OK && Some(src) != self.roam_vip && self.slow.is_some() {
            // free roam from another player to one who is not driving: the slow clock's tick, or sooner with whatever
            // else goes to it (away.rs)
            self.slow.as_deref()
        } else {
            self.clock.as_deref()
        };
        p.conn.push_dgram(data.clone(), src, dst, clock);
        true
    }

    /// a stream segment (kind 4) to p: past the receiver's share for one client (or its whole queue), whose fault it
    /// is decides who goes: a receiver that stopped reading, or the client with the most queued there (all of its
    /// connections)
    fn send_stream(&self, from: &Arc<Peer>, p: &Arc<Peer>, data: &Bytes, dst: u32) -> bool {
        let g = &from.group.id;
        let len = cost(data);
        let now = mono_ms();
        let mut guard = self.streams.lock();
        // a receiver that left after deliver_now looked: its close logic let go of its queue here (under this lock,
        // after the connection ended), and it must not come back, for good
        if !p.open() {
            return false;
        }
        let st: &mut Streams = &mut guard;
        let s = st.by_conn.entry(p.conn.id).or_default();
        let mine = s.mine(g).map_or(0, |i| s.queued[i].n);
        if mine + len > self.o.stream_share || s.total + len > self.o.stream_queue {
            if self.stalled(s, now) {
                self.cut(p, Cut::Stall);
                return false;
            }
            // the receiver reads, and more comes than it takes: the client with the most queued there goes
            let mut top = g.clone();
            let mut most = mine;
            for q in &s.queued {
                if q.n > most {
                    most = q.n;
                    top = q.group.clone();
                }
            }
            self.cut_group(st, &top, Cut::Hog);
            if top == *g {
                return false;
            }
        }
        if !self.room(p, Cut::Slow) {
            self.stats.dropped.inc();
            return false;
        }
        let s = st.by_conn.entry(p.conn.id).or_default();
        // straight to the connection while it has little queued; behind the switch's own queue otherwise, so that
        // what the receiver takes is seen segment by segment
        if s.sq.is_empty() && p.conn.out.buffered() <= STREAM_LOW {
            p.conn.push(Out::Frame { data: data.clone(), src: from.vip, dst });
            return true;
        }
        if s.sq.is_empty() {
            s.since = now;
            s.out = now;
        }
        let era = match s.mine(g) {
            Some(i) => {
                s.queued[i].n += len;
                s.queued[i].era
            }
            None => {
                st.era += 1;
                s.queued.push(Queued { group: g.clone(), era: st.era, n: len });
                st.era
            }
        };
        s.total += len;
        s.sq.push_back(Segment { data: data.clone(), src: from.vip, dst, group: g.clone(), era });
        // (SeqCst: see OutQueue::buffered_synced)
        p.conn.streaming.store(true, SeqCst);
        Self::pump_one(&p.conn, s);
        true
    }

    /// p has stream segments waiting and none of them got out for `stall_ms`: it stopped reading
    fn stalled(&self, s: &StreamQueue, now: f64) -> bool {
        let ms = self.o.stall_ms;
        !s.sq.is_empty() && now - s.since > ms && now - s.out > ms
    }

    /// every connection of one client goes, and the stream segments of it still waiting at the others
    fn cut_group(&self, st: &mut Streams, id: &Arc<str>, why: Cut) {
        for q in self.all.load().iter() {
            if q.group.id == *id && q.open() {
                self.cut(q, why);
            }
            let Some(s) = st.by_conn.get_mut(&q.conn.id) else { continue };
            let Some(i) = s.mine(id) else { continue };
            let e = s.queued.remove(i);
            s.total -= e.n;
            s.sq.retain(|x| !(x.era == e.era && x.group == e.group));
        }
    }

    /// p's queued stream segments into its connection, as far as it has taken the ones before (after each write of
    /// its writer)
    pub(crate) fn pump(&self, conn: &Arc<Conn>) {
        let mut st = self.streams.lock();
        match st.by_conn.get_mut(&conn.id) {
            Some(s) => Self::pump_one(conn, s),
            None => conn.streaming.store(false, Relaxed),
        }
    }

    fn pump_one(conn: &Arc<Conn>, s: &mut StreamQueue) {
        if !conn.open() {
            s.sq.clear();
        }
        while !s.sq.is_empty() && conn.out.buffered_synced() <= STREAM_LOW {
            let x = s.sq.pop_front().expect("not empty");
            let len = cost(&x.data);
            if let Some(i) = s.queued.iter().position(|q| q.era == x.era && q.group == x.group) {
                s.queued[i].n -= len.min(s.queued[i].n);
                if s.queued[i].n == 0 {
                    s.queued.remove(i);
                }
            }
            s.total -= len.min(s.total);
            s.out = mono_ms();
            conn.push(Out::Frame { data: x.data, src: x.src, dst: x.dst });
        }
        conn.streaming.store(!s.sq.is_empty(), SeqCst);
    }
}

/// the frame as sent to a host (or the trace): its own copy, with its source and destination written in
fn own(data: &Bytes, src: u32, dst: u32) -> Bytes {
    let mut b = BytesMut::with_capacity(data.len());
    b.put_slice(&data[..4]);
    b.put_u32(src);
    b.put_u32(dst);
    b.put_slice(&data[12..]);
    b.freeze()
}

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::{AttachCtx, LanOptions};
    use crate::{BASE, UDP_SET};

    /// a peer on the switch without a socket: its connection's queue only fills
    pub(crate) fn peer(sw: &Arc<LanSwitch>, group: &str) -> (Arc<Conn>, Arc<AttachCtx>, Arc<Peer>) {
        let conn = Arc::new(Conn::new(sw.conn_ids.fetch_add(1, Relaxed)));
        let ctx = Arc::new(AttachCtx {
            resume: false,
            queue: false,
            group: sw.join_group(false, Some(group)),
            site: None,
            on_join: None,
            on_leave: None,
            ident: None,
            on_hello: None,
            on_claim: None,
            country: 0,
        });
        let p = sw.admit(&conn, &ctx, None).expect("admitted");
        (conn, ctx, p)
    }

    pub(crate) fn frame(kind: u8, dst: u32) -> Bytes {
        let mut f = vec![0u8; 40];
        f[0] = kind;
        f[8..12].copy_from_slice(&dst.to_be_bytes());
        Bytes::from(f)
    }

    /// The buckets charged once for a bundle entry's destinations come to what charging them one destination after
    /// the other comes to: the same destinations paid for (the first that does not fit ends the bundle) and the same
    /// frames and bytes left in each bucket, to the bit.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn charging_a_list_at_once_is_charging_it_one_by_one() {
        let sw = LanSwitch::new(LanOptions::default(), "", None, None, None, None);
        let mut x: u64 = 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15;
        let mut rnd = move |m: u64| {
            x ^= x << 13;
            x ^= x >> 7;
            x ^= x << 17;
            x % m
        };
        let peers: Vec<_> = (0..50).map(|i| peer(&sw, &format!("g{i}"))).collect();
        let (mut cut_short, mut whole) = (0, 0);
        for case in 0..20_000 {
            let p = &peers[case % peers.len()].2;
            // mostly free roam's snapshots, now and then up to `max_frame`
            let n = (12 + if rnd(4) == 0 { rnd(8180) } else { rnd(200) }) as f64;
            // levels anywhere from empty to full, with fractions (a refill leaves them), and a debt (the Online host's)
            let mut set = |pair: &mut crate::Pair| {
                for b in [&mut pair.frames, &mut pair.bytes] {
                    b.v = (rnd(1_000_000) as f64 / 1_000_000.0) * b.cap * 1.1 - b.cap * 0.1;
                    b.t = 1e12;
                }
            };
            set(&mut p.buckets.lock());
            set(&mut p.group.buckets.lock());
            // 1 to 255 destinations, now and then a broadcast's count among them
            let costs: Vec<usize> = (0..1 + rnd(255)).map(|_| if rnd(20) == 0 { 1 + rnd(3000) as usize } else { 1 }).collect();
            let mut want = (p.buckets.lock().clone(), p.group.buckets.lock().clone());
            let mut paid_want = 0;
            for &k in &costs {
                let k = k as f64;
                let ok = [&mut want.0, &mut want.1].iter_mut().all(|q| q.frames.has_at(1e12, k) && q.bytes.has_at(1e12, n * k));
                if !ok {
                    break;
                }
                for q in [&mut want.0, &mut want.1] {
                    q.frames.take_at(1e12, k);
                    q.bytes.take_at(1e12, n * k);
                }
                paid_want += 1;
            }
            let (paid, all) = sw.charge(p, 1e12, n, costs.iter().copied());
            assert_eq!((paid, all), (paid_want, paid_want == costs.len()), "case {case}");
            let (a, b) = (p.buckets.lock().clone(), p.group.buckets.lock().clone());
            for (got, want) in [(&a, &want.0), (&b, &want.1)] {
                assert_eq!(got.frames.v.to_bits(), want.frames.v.to_bits(), "case {case}: frames left");
                assert_eq!(got.bytes.v.to_bits(), want.bytes.v.to_bits(), "case {case}: bytes left");
            }
            if all { whole += 1 } else { cut_short += 1 }
        }
        assert!(cut_short > 1000 && whole > 1000, "both cases came up ({cut_short} cut short, {whole} whole)");
        sw.stop();
    }

    /// The second security audit: a bundle entry of 255 broadcasts, refused by the budgets, walked every peer 255
    /// times before the refusal (2000 such messages here: 2 billion looks at a peer, seconds; without a walk, well
    /// under a millisecond).
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_broadcast_refused_walks_no_peer() {
        let sw = LanSwitch::new(LanOptions { max_peers: 24000, ..LanOptions::default() }, "", None, None, None, None);
        let peers: Vec<_> = (0..24000).map(|i| peer(&sw, &format!("g{i}"))).collect();
        let p = &peers[0].2;
        for b in [&mut *p.buckets.lock(), &mut *p.group.buckets.lock()] {
            b.frames.v = 0.0;
            b.frames.t = 1e15;
        }
        let f = frame(KIND_UDP, BROADCAST);
        let t = std::time::Instant::now();
        for _ in 0..2000 {
            assert!(!sw.route(p, &f, std::iter::repeat_n(BROADCAST, 255)));
        }
        let ms = t.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 1000.0;
        assert!(ms < 500.0, "2000 refused messages of 255 broadcasts at 24000 players took {ms:.0} ms");
        assert!(peers.iter().all(|(c, ..)| c.out.q.lock().len() <= 1), "nothing sent (a welcome at most)");
        sw.stop();
    }

    /// LAN play's broadcasts go to the list of those with LAN play open: a page that said nothing (no hello yet, or
    /// none of LAN play in it) and one that shut LAN play are not on it, and one that left or was replaced is gone
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn the_list_of_lan_play_follows_hellos_lan_messages_and_closes() {
        let sw = LanSwitch::new(LanOptions::default(), "", None, None, None, None);
        let (_ac, _actx, a) = peer(&sw, "a");
        let (bc, bctx, b) = peer(&sw, "b");
        let on = |sw: &LanSwitch| {
            let mut v: Vec<u32> = sw.lan_all.load().iter().map(|p| p.vip).collect();
            v.sort();
            v
        };
        assert_eq!(on(&sw), [0u32; 0], "no hello yet: none of them");
        let hello = |lan: u8| match crate::text::parse_json(format!(r#"{{"t":"hello","name":"x","lan":{lan}}}"#).as_bytes()) {
            Some(serde_json::Value::Object(m)) => m,
            _ => unreachable!(),
        };
        sw.hello(&a, &hello(1));
        assert_eq!(on(&sw), [a.vip]);
        sw.hello(&b, &hello(0));
        assert_eq!(on(&sw), [a.vip]);
        sw.set_lan(&b, true);
        assert_eq!(on(&sw), [a.vip, b.vip]);
        sw.set_lan(&a, true);
        sw.set_lan(&b, false);
        assert_eq!(on(&sw), [a.vip]);
        // a LAN broadcast from a reaches nobody: b's LAN play is shut
        assert!(sw.route(&a, &frame(KIND_LAN_UDP, BROADCAST), std::iter::once(BROADCAST)));
        assert!(b.conn.out.q.lock().iter().all(|o| !matches!(o, Out::Frame { .. })));
        sw.set_lan(&b, true);
        assert!(sw.route(&a, &frame(KIND_LAN_UDP, BROADCAST), std::iter::once(BROADCAST)));
        assert_eq!(b.conn.out.q.lock().iter().filter(|o| matches!(o, Out::Frame { .. })).count(), 1);
        bc.terminate();
        sw.closed(&bc, &bctx);
        assert_eq!(on(&sw), [a.vip], "gone with its connection");
        sw.stop();
    }

    /// A LAN broadcast goes only to the pages with a socket on its port as their "udp" says (server.dll's advert on
    /// 9999: a joiner closed the server list's socket, the Online screens never had one), and to every page that does
    /// not say (an older page or module); one that sends its ports with {"t":"lan"} changes where they go
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_lan_broadcast_goes_only_where_a_socket_takes_its_port() {
        let sw = LanSwitch::new(LanOptions::default(), "", None, None, None, None);
        let (_ac, _actx, a) = peer(&sw, "a");
        let (_bc, _bctx, b) = peer(&sw, "b");
        let (_cc, _cctx, c) = peer(&sw, "c");
        let (_dc, _dctx, d) = peer(&sw, "d");
        let hello = |udp: &str| match crate::text::parse_json(format!(r#"{{"t":"hello","name":"x","lan":1{udp}}}"#).as_bytes()) {
            Some(serde_json::Value::Object(m)) => m,
            _ => unreachable!(),
        };
        let bit = |port: u32| 1u32 << (port % 31);
        sw.hello(&a, &hello(""));
        sw.hello(&b, &hello(&format!(r#","udp":{}"#, UDP_SET | bit(9999) | bit(3658))));
        sw.hello(&c, &hello(&format!(r#","udp":{}"#, UDP_SET | bit(3658))));
        sw.hello(&d, &hello(""));
        let advert = |port: u16| {
            let mut f = frame(KIND_LAN_UDP, BROADCAST).to_vec();
            f[12..14].copy_from_slice(&port.to_be_bytes());
            f[14..16].copy_from_slice(&port.to_be_bytes());
            Bytes::from(f)
        };
        let got = |p: &Peer| p.conn.out.q.lock().iter().filter(|o| matches!(o, Out::Frame { .. })).count();
        assert!(sw.route(&a, &advert(9999), std::iter::once(BROADCAST)));
        assert_eq!((got(&b), got(&c), got(&d)), (1, 0, 1), "b has 9999, c only 3658, d does not say");
        assert_eq!(sw.stats.bcast_skipped.get(), 1);
        assert_eq!(sw.stats.bcast_skipped_bytes.get(), 40);
        // the same bit (3658 + 31 x 1): it goes, as a port with a socket would
        assert!(sw.route(&a, &advert(3658 + 31), std::iter::once(BROADCAST)));
        assert_eq!((got(&b), got(&c), got(&d)), (2, 1, 2));
        // c's server list opens (9999 bound): {"t":"lan"} with its ports; a mask without UDP_SET, or none, says nothing
        c.udp.store(crate::udp_of(Some(&serde_json::json!(UDP_SET | bit(9999)))), Relaxed);
        b.udp.store(crate::udp_of(Some(&serde_json::json!(bit(5)))), Relaxed);
        assert!(sw.route(&a, &advert(9999), std::iter::once(BROADCAST)));
        assert_eq!((got(&b), got(&c), got(&d)), (3, 2, 3));
        // not LAN play's UDP (its ICMP, kind 5): every page with LAN play open, whatever its ports
        c.udp.store(UDP_SET, Relaxed);
        assert!(sw.route(&a, &frame(KIND_LAN_ICMP, BROADCAST), std::iter::once(BROADCAST)));
        assert_eq!(got(&c), 3);
        assert_eq!(sw.stats.bcast_skipped.get(), 1);
        sw.stop();
    }

    /// the free-roam hub for these tests: only its address (10.77.0.253)
    struct Hub;
    impl nfsu2_util::Host for Hub {
        fn vip(&self) -> u32 {
            BASE | 0xFD
        }
        fn name(&self) -> &str {
            ""
        }
        fn listed(&self) -> bool {
            false
        }
        fn frame(&self, _from: u32, _data: Bytes, _ctx: FrameCtx) {}
        fn peer_gone(&self, _vip: u32) {}
        fn info(&self) -> tokio::sync::oneshot::Receiver<serde_json::Value> {
            tokio::sync::oneshot::channel().1
        }
        fn vips(&self) -> tokio::sync::oneshot::Receiver<std::collections::HashSet<u32>> {
            tokio::sync::oneshot::channel().1
        }
        fn stop(&self) {}
    }

    /// The hub's lists, map and lobbies (`send_to` from 10.77.0.253) to a page that takes bundles go in its next
    /// bundle, marked for the compact form; to one that does not, a message of their own as before, and so does any
    /// other host's frame (the Online host's TCP segments)
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn the_hubs_frames_go_in_a_bundle_to_a_page_that_takes_them() {
        let sw = LanSwitch::new(LanOptions::default(), "", None, Some(Arc::new(Hub)), None, None);
        let (_ac, _actx, a) = peer(&sw, "a");
        let (_bc, _bctx, b) = peer(&sw, "b");
        let hello = |bundle: u8| match crate::text::parse_json(
            format!(r#"{{"t":"hello","name":"x","bundle":{bundle},"compact":{bundle}}}"#).as_bytes(),
        ) {
            Some(serde_json::Value::Object(m)) => m,
            _ => unreachable!(),
        };
        sw.hello(&a, &hello(1));
        sw.hello(&b, &hello(0));
        let from = |src: u32, to: u32, kind: u8| {
            let mut f = frame(kind, to).to_vec();
            f[4..8].copy_from_slice(&src.to_be_bytes());
            Bytes::from(f)
        };
        let hub = BASE | 0xFD;
        assert!(matches!(sw.send_to(a.vip, from(hub, a.vip, KIND_UDP), None), nfsu2_util::SendResult::Sent));
        assert!(matches!(sw.send_to(b.vip, from(hub, b.vip, KIND_UDP), None), nfsu2_util::SendResult::Sent));
        assert!(matches!(sw.send_to(a.vip, from(BASE | 1, a.vip, KIND_STREAM), None), nfsu2_util::SendResult::Sent));
        let kinds = |p: &Peer| {
            p.conn
                .out
                .q
                .lock()
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|o| match o {
                    Out::Dgram { src, dst, .. } => Some(format!("dgram {src:x}>{dst:x}")),
                    Out::Raw(f) => Some(format!("raw {:x}", u32::from_be_bytes([f[4], f[5], f[6], f[7]]))),
                    _ => None,
                })
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        };
        assert_eq!(kinds(&a), [format!("dgram {hub:x}>{:x}", a.vip), format!("raw {:x}", BASE | 1)]);
        assert_eq!(kinds(&b), [format!("raw {hub:x}")]);
        assert!(a.conn.out.dgram() > 0, "counted as a bundle's entry");
        sw.stop();
    }

    /// A frame waiting in a receiver's queue has bytes of its own: not the block the sender's reader read it into,
    /// which a frame of a few bytes kept whole (the second security audit)
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_queued_frame_holds_its_own_bytes_not_the_senders_block() {
        let sw = LanSwitch::new(LanOptions::default(), "", None, None, None, None);
        let (_ac, _actx, a) = peer(&sw, "a");
        let (_bc, _bctx, b) = peer(&sw, "b");
        for kind in [KIND_UDP, KIND_LAN_UDP, KIND_STREAM] {
            let mut block = vec![0u8; 64 << 10];
            block[100..140].copy_from_slice(&frame(kind, b.vip));
            let block = Bytes::from(block);
            assert!(sw.route(&a, &block.slice(100..140), std::iter::once(b.vip)));
            let q = b.conn.out.q.lock();
            let Some(Out::Frame { data, .. }) = q.iter().rev().find(|o| matches!(o, Out::Frame { .. })) else {
                panic!("kind {kind}: queued")
            };
            let at = data.as_ptr() as usize;
            let range = block.as_ptr() as usize..block.as_ptr() as usize + block.len();
            assert!(!range.contains(&at), "kind {kind}: the queued frame is a slice of the sender's block");
            assert_eq!(&data[..], &block[100..140]);
        }
        sw.stop();
    }

    /// A stream segment whose receiver closed between the sender's look at it and the streams' lock: nothing of it
    /// stays at the switch (the receiver's queue was let go with its connection, and must not come back).
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_segment_to_a_receiver_that_just_left_leaves_nothing_behind() {
        let sw = LanSwitch::new(LanOptions::default(), "", None, None, None, None);
        let (_ac, _actx, a) = peer(&sw, "a");
        let (bc, bctx, b) = peer(&sw, "b");
        // the sender saw b open (deliver_now); b's connection ends and its close logic runs; then the segment
        bc.terminate();
        sw.closed(&bc, &bctx);
        assert!(!sw.send_stream(&a, &b, &frame(KIND_STREAM, b.vip), b.vip));
        assert!(sw.streams.lock().by_conn.is_empty(), "no stream queue for a connection that is gone");
        sw.stop();
    }
}

//! The state folder's lan-addresses.json (the switch's store): `[{"v":"10.77.0.2","h":"<base64url of the token's
//! SHA-256>"},...]`, the addresses held and then the ones reserved, so that the players come back to the same
//! addresses after a restart.  Written whole to a temporary file (mode 0600), then renamed over the old one
//! (`nfsu2_util::atomic_file`), not synced: it is written again half a second after any change while players come
//! and go, and a file cut short by a power cut only means new addresses for the players.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use parking_lot::Mutex;
use serde_json::Value;

use nfsu2_util::atomic_file::Options;

use crate::text::js_string;

pub(crate) struct Store {
    path: PathBuf,
    /// the newest list written (saves run on blocking threads: an older one never overwrites a newer one)
    written: Mutex<u64>,
}

impl Store {
    pub(crate) fn new(path: PathBuf) -> Self {
        Store { path, written: Mutex::new(0) }
    }

    /// what the switch starts with: the addresses and their hashes (none when the file is missing or broken; an entry
    /// that is not an address the switch hands out with a hash of 32 bytes is skipped)
    pub(crate) fn load(&self) -> Vec<(u32, [u8; 32])> {
        let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(&self.path) else { return Vec::new() };
        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes);
        let Ok(Value::Array(list)) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&text) else { return Vec::new() };
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for e in &list {
            let Value::Object(e) = e else { continue };
            let v = crate::vip_num(&js_string(e.get("v")));
            let Some(Value::String(h)) = e.get("h") else { continue };
            let h = nfsu2_util::js::from_base64url(h);
            if v != 0 && h.len() == 32 {
                let mut hash = [0u8; 32];
                hash.copy_from_slice(&h);
                out.push((v, hash));
            }
        }
        out
    }

    /// the list as it was at `seq` (the next change tries again when this fails)
    pub(crate) fn save(&self, seq: u64, json: &str) {
        let mut written = self.written.lock();
        if seq <= *written {
            return;
        }
        if Options::new().no_sync().write(&self.path, json.as_bytes()).is_ok() {
            *written = seq;
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn reads_what_it_wrote_and_skips_what_is_broken() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let s = Store::new(dir.path().join("lan-addresses.json"));
        assert!(s.load().is_empty());
        let h = nfsu2_util::js::base64url(&[7u8; 32]);
        let json = format!(
            r#"[{{"v":"10.77.0.2","h":"{h}"}},{{"v":"10.77.0.1","h":"{h}"}},{{"v":"10.77.1.2","h":"short"}},7,null,{{"v":["10.77.2.2"],"h":"{h}"}}]"#
        );
        s.save(1, &json);
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join("lan-addresses.json")).unwrap(), json);
        assert_eq!(s.load(), vec![(0x0A4D_0002, [7u8; 32]), (0x0A4D_0202, [7u8; 32])]);
        // an older list never overwrites a newer one
        s.save(1, "[]");
        assert_eq!(s.load().len(), 2);
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
            let mode = std::fs::metadata(dir.path().join("lan-addresses.json")).unwrap().permissions().mode();
            assert_eq!(mode & 0o777, 0o600);
        }
        std::fs::write(dir.path().join("lan-addresses.json"), "{not json").unwrap();
        assert!(s.load().is_empty());
    }
}
