// Seven tests of the page (web/src/net/index.ts, bundled as the app bundles it) against the Rust switch, started by
// tests/page.rs, which passes its ports.  What they read of the switch's insides (its peers, info(), reserved) comes
// from the harness's GET /state.
//   node page.mjs <case> <port> [<port> ...]
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import path from 'node:path';
import zlib from 'node:zlib';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { WebSocket } from 'ws';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import * as esbuild from 'esbuild';
import * as P from '../../../../src/net/proto.ts';
import { sourceKeys } from '../../../../tools/i18n-keys.mjs';

const HERE = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const WEB = path.join(HERE, '../../../..');
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms));
/** the page's own texts (web/src/net/index.ts's English, the keys the page translates): a notice is checked as one of
 *  them, so new wording needs no change here */
const TEXTS = new Set(sourceKeys(fs.readFileSync(path.join(WEB, 'src/net/index.ts'), 'utf8')).keys.map(k => k.key));
const ipStr = (v) => [v >>> 24, (v >>> 16) & 255, (v >>> 8) & 255, v & 255].join('.');

/** the switch's insides, as these tests read them: { peers: [{ vip, name, hello, lan }], info, reserved } */
const state = async (port) => (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/state`)).json();
/** until f() says yes (5 s at most), its condition read from the switch (async) */
const until = async (f, ms = 5000) => { const t0 = Date.now(); while (!(await f())) { if (Date.now() - t0 > ms) throw new Error('timed out'); await sleep(20); } };

// a fake browser on the switch's WebSocket (what these tests need of one)
class Client {
  constructor(port, name, query = '', resume = null, { deltas = false, lan, bundle = false } = {}) {
    this.name = name; this.frames = []; this.ctl = []; this.waiters = []; this.resume = resume; this.deltas = deltas;
    this.extra = { ...(deltas ? { deltas: 1 } : {}), ...(lan !== undefined ? { lan } : {}), ...(bundle ? { bundle: 1 } : {}) };
    this.view = null; this.ctlBytes = 0;
    const q = resume ? (query ? query + '&resume' : '?resume') : query;
    this.ws = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan${q}`);
    this.ws.binaryType = 'nodebuffer';
    this.ws.on('message', (d, bin) => {
      if (bin) this.frames.push({ buf: Buffer.from(d), t: performance.now() });
      else {
        const m = JSON.parse(String(d));
        this.ctl.push(m); this.ctlBytes += d.length;
        if (m.t === 'peers') this.view = new Map(m.peers.map(p => [p.vip >>> 0, p]));
        if (m.t === 'delta' && this.view) { for (const v of m.gone) this.view.delete(v >>> 0); for (const p of m.peers) this.view.set(p.vip >>> 0, p); }
      }
      for (const w of this.waiters.splice(0)) w();
    });
    this.closed = new Promise(r => this.ws.on('close', r));
  }
  async welcome() {
    const m = await this.until(() => this.ctl.find(m => m.t === 'welcome'));
    this.vip = m.vip >>> 0; this.token = m.token;
    if (!this.resume) this.ws.send(JSON.stringify({ t: 'hello', name: this.name, ...this.extra }));
    return m;
  }
  until(f, ms = 2000) {
    return new Promise((res, rej) => {
      const t = setTimeout(() => rej(new Error(`${this.name}: timed out`)), ms);
      const check = () => { const v = f(); if (v) { clearTimeout(t); res(v); } else this.waiters.push(check); };
      check();
    });
  }
  sendBundle(entries) { this.ws.send(bundleOf(entries)); }
  dgrams() {
    const out = [];
    this.frames.forEach(({ buf }, msg) => {
      const one = b => out.push({ buf: b, msg, kind: b[0], src: b.readUInt32BE(4), dst: b.readUInt32BE(8), data: b.subarray(16).toString() });
      if (buf[0] !== 32) return one(buf);
      for (let at = 4; at + 4 <= buf.length;) { const f = at + 4 + 4 * buf[at], end = f + buf.readUInt16BE(at + 2); one(buf.subarray(f, end)); at = end; }
    });
    return out;
  }
  close() { this.ws.close(); return this.closed; }
}
function frameOf(dst, data, kind = 1, sport = 9999, dport = 9999) {
  const f = Buffer.alloc(16 + Buffer.byteLength(data));
  f[0] = kind; f.writeUInt32BE(dst >>> 0, 8); f.writeUInt16BE(sport, 12); f.writeUInt16BE(dport, 14); Buffer.from(data).copy(f, 16);
  return f;
}
function bundleOf(entries) {
  const parts = [Buffer.from([32, 0, 0, 0])];
  for (const { f, to = [] } of entries) {
    const h = Buffer.alloc(4 + 4 * to.length);
    h[0] = to.length; h.writeUInt16BE(f.length, 2); to.forEach((v, j) => h.writeUInt32BE(v >>> 0, 4 + 4 * j));
    parts.push(h, f);
  }
  return Buffer.concat(parts);
}

// the page (web/src/net/index.ts), bundled as the app bundles it, against a switch on port
let pageJs = null;
async function pageNet(port) {
  pageJs ??= (await esbuild.build({ entryPoints: [path.join(WEB, 'src/net/index.ts')], bundle: true, write: false, format: 'esm', platform: 'neutral' })).outputFiles[0].text;
  globalThis.location ??= new URL(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/`);
  return import('data:text/javascript;base64,' + Buffer.from(pageJs).toString('base64'));
}
function mailbox(memory, ptr) {
  const hdr = P.NET_HDR_BYTES, w = new Int32Array(memory.buffer, ptr, hdr / 4);
  w[P.W_MAGIC] = P.NET_MAGIC; w[P.W_VERSION] = P.NET_VERSION; w[P.W_HDR_BYTES] = hdr; w[P.W_SLOT_BYTES] = P.NET_SLOT_BYTES;
  w[P.W_TX_SLOTS] = P.NET_TX_SLOTS; w[P.W_RX_SLOTS] = P.NET_RX_SLOTS;
  w[P.W_TX_OFF] = hdr; w[P.W_RX_OFF] = hdr + P.NET_TX_SLOTS * P.NET_SLOT_BYTES;
  return { w, ptr, size: P.NET_MAILBOX_BYTES };
}
function want(mb, on) { Atomics.store(mb.w, P.W_WANT, on); Atomics.add(mb.w, P.W_TX_BELL, 1); Atomics.notify(mb.w, P.W_TX_BELL); }
const fakeGame = (memory, boxes) => ({ memory, ctl: new Int32Array(1), exited: new Promise(() => {}),
  registered: k => boxes[k] ? Promise.resolve({ ptr: boxes[k].ptr, size: boxes[k].size }) : new Promise(() => {}) });
function txPush(memory, mb, { kind = 1, dst, sport = 47210, dport = 47210, data }) {
  const w = mb.w, dv = new DataView(memory.buffer), head = Atomics.load(w, P.W_TX_HEAD);
  const s = mb.ptr + w[P.W_TX_OFF] + ((head >>> 0) % P.NET_TX_SLOTS) * P.NET_SLOT_BYTES, d = Buffer.from(data);
  dv.setUint32(s + P.S_LEN, d.length, true); dv.setUint32(s + P.S_KIND, kind, true); dv.setUint32(s + P.S_DST_IP, dst >>> 0, true);
  dv.setUint16(s + P.S_SRC_PORT, sport, true); dv.setUint16(s + P.S_DST_PORT, dport, true);
  dv.setFloat64(s + P.S_T_MS, performance.timeOrigin + performance.now(), true);
  new Uint8Array(memory.buffer).set(d, s + P.S_DATA);
  Atomics.store(w, P.W_TX_HEAD, (head + 1) | 0);
}
const txBell = mb => { Atomics.add(mb.w, P.W_TX_BELL, 1); Atomics.notify(mb.w, P.W_TX_BELL); };
function rxTake(memory, mb) {
  const w = mb.w, dv = new DataView(memory.buffer), out = [];
  let tail = Atomics.load(w, P.W_RX_TAIL);
  for (const head = Atomics.load(w, P.W_RX_HEAD); tail !== head; tail = (tail + 1) | 0) {
    const s = mb.ptr + w[P.W_RX_OFF] + ((tail >>> 0) % P.NET_RX_SLOTS) * P.NET_SLOT_BYTES;
    out.push({ src: dv.getUint32(s + P.S_SRC_IP, true), dst: dv.getUint32(s + P.S_DST_IP, true),
      data: Buffer.from(new Uint8Array(memory.buffer, s + P.S_DATA, dv.getUint32(s + P.S_LEN, true))).toString() });
  }
  Atomics.store(w, P.W_RX_TAIL, tail);
  return out;
}
/** the same with each datagram's bytes and ports, as the game reads them */
function rxTakeRaw(memory, mb) {
  const w = mb.w, dv = new DataView(memory.buffer), out = [];
  let tail = Atomics.load(w, P.W_RX_TAIL);
  for (const head = Atomics.load(w, P.W_RX_HEAD); tail !== head; tail = (tail + 1) | 0) {
    const s = mb.ptr + w[P.W_RX_OFF] + ((tail >>> 0) % P.NET_RX_SLOTS) * P.NET_SLOT_BYTES;
    out.push({ src: dv.getUint32(s + P.S_SRC_IP, true), dst: dv.getUint32(s + P.S_DST_IP, true),
      sport: dv.getUint16(s + P.S_SRC_PORT, true), dport: dv.getUint16(s + P.S_DST_PORT, true),
      data: Buffer.from(new Uint8Array(memory.buffer, s + P.S_DATA, dv.getUint32(s + P.S_LEN, true))) });
  }
  Atomics.store(w, P.W_RX_TAIL, tail);
  return out;
}
/** a free-roam datagram as runtime/roam_core.c rc_encode makes it: "N2FR", version 1, a type, its length and CRC */
function roamDatagram(type, n) {
  const d = Buffer.alloc(16 + n + 4);
  d.write('N2FR', 0, 'latin1'); d[4] = 1; d[5] = type; d.writeUInt16LE(d.length, 6); d.writeUInt32LE(0x12345678, 8); d[12] = 7;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) d[16 + i] = (i * 37 + 11) & 255;
  d.writeUInt32LE(zlib.crc32(d.subarray(0, d.length - 4)), d.length - 4);
  return d;
}

/** a SNAP of one state as roam_core.c rc_encode makes it (its fields from k, so that each differs), with an extension
 *  of x bytes when x is given */
function snapDatagram({ sender = 0xABCD0001, seq, t, p, v, k, x }) {
  const b = 8, d = Buffer.alloc(b + 66 + (x !== undefined ? 1 + x : 0) + 4);
  d.write('N2FR', 0, 'latin1'); d[4] = 1; d[5] = 3; d.writeUInt16LE(d.length, 6);
  d.writeUInt32LE(sender, b); d.writeUInt16LE(seq & 0xffff, b + 4); d.writeUInt16LE((x !== undefined ? 0x40 : 0) | 0x20, b + 6);
  d[b + 8] = 2; d[b + 9] = 7; d.writeUInt16LE(0x0102, b + 10); d[b + 12] = 1; d[b + 13] = 3;
  d.writeUInt32LE(t >>> 0, b + 14);
  p.forEach((f, i) => d.writeFloatLE(f, b + 18 + 4 * i)); v.forEach((f, i) => d.writeFloatLE(f, b + 30 + 4 * i));
  [100 + k, -200, 30000 - k, 5].forEach((q, i) => d.writeInt16LE(q, b + 42 + 2 * i));
  [3 * k, -k, 7].forEach((w, i) => d.writeInt16LE(w, b + 50 + 2 * i));
  d.writeInt16LE((k * 101) << 16 >> 16, b + 56); d[b + 58] = 200; d[b + 59] = k % 3; d.writeUInt16LE((3000 + 7 * k) & 0xffff, b + 60);
  d.writeInt16LE(1500 + k, b + 62); d[b + 64] = 4; d[b + 65] = 0x10;
  if (x !== undefined) {
    d[b + 66] = x;
    if (x > 0) {
      for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) d.writeInt16LE(-300 + k + i, b + 67 + 2 * i);
      let o = b + 76;
      if (x >= 11) { d[o] = 1; d[o + 1] = 2; o += 2; }
      if (x >= 23) { for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) d[o + i] = (i * 9 + k) & 255; o += 12; }
      if (x === 16 || x === 28) { d.writeUInt16LE(4000 + k, o); d[o + 2] = 10; d[o + 3] = 20; d[o + 4] = 30; }
    }
  }
  d.writeUInt32LE(zlib.crc32(d.subarray(0, d.length - 4)), d.length - 4);
  return d;
}
/** the same as the game gets it through the fields (nfsu2-lan fpred.rs): the time to 256 us, the position to 1 mm, the
 *  velocity to 1 cm/s (rounded half away from zero, as Rust's round), and the CRC made again */
function roundedDatagram(d) {
  const r = Buffer.from(d), b = 8, away = x => Math.sign(x) * Math.round(Math.abs(x)) + 0;
  r.writeUInt32LE((Math.floor((r.readUInt32LE(b + 14) + 128) / 256) % 2 ** 24) * 256, b + 14);
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    r.writeFloatLE(away(r.readFloatLE(b + 18 + 4 * i) * 1000) / 1000, b + 18 + 4 * i);
    r.writeFloatLE(away(r.readFloatLE(b + 30 + 4 * i) * 100) / 100, b + 30 + 4 * i);
  }
  r.writeUInt32LE(zlib.crc32(r.subarray(0, r.length - 4)), r.length - 4);
  return r;
}

const cases = {
  // the page: in line when the switch is full (where it is; no notice: the line over the game says it), its place kept
  // across a dropped link, in when a place frees up, with a notice once (a switch with room for one)
  async full([port]) {
    const { attachNet } = await pageNet(port);
    const game = (name, notices, line) => {
      const memory = new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 10, maximum: 10, shared: true }), mb = mailbox(memory, 0);
      want(mb, 1);
      return attachNet(fakeGame(memory, { 4: mb }), { url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan`, name, onNotice: t => notices.push(t),
        onQueue: q => line.push(q), pingMs: 60_000 });
    };
    const na = [], nb = [], qa = [], qb = [];
    const a = game('A', na, qa);
    try {
      await a.online;
      const b = game('B', nb, qb);
      try {
        await until(() => qb.length === 1);
        assert.deepEqual(qb[0], { pos: 1, of: 1 });
        assert.equal(b.state, 'queued');
        assert.deepEqual(nb, [], 'no notice in line: the line over the game says it');
        assert.equal((await state(port)).info.waiting, 1);
        // its link drops: back to the same place, with no notice
        b['ws'].close(4000, 'dropped');
        await until(async () => (await state(port)).info.rejoined === 1);
        await until(() => qb.length === 2 && b.state === 'queued');
        assert.deepEqual(qb[1], { pos: 1, of: 1 });
        assert.deepEqual(nb, []);
        assert.equal((await state(port)).info.waiting, 1);
        a.close();
        assert.match(await b.online, /^10\.77\.([0-9]|1[0-9])\.\d+$/);
        await until(() => nb.length === 1);
        assert.ok(TEXTS.has(nb[0]) && /freed up/.test(nb[0]), `a notice once in: ${nb[0]}`);
        assert.equal(qb.at(-1), null, 'out of line');
        assert.deepEqual([na, qa], [[], []], 'the first game heard nothing');
        // a third waits in line, then stops waiting (the page menu's Play offline): out of line for good
        const nc = [], qc = [], c = game('C', nc, qc);
        try {
          await until(() => qc.length === 1 && c.state === 'queued');
          c.goOffline();
          await until(async () => (await state(port)).info.lineLeft === 1);
          assert.deepEqual([c.state, qc.at(-1), (await state(port)).info.waiting], ['away', null, 0]);
          c.setAway(false); await sleep(600);
          assert.deepEqual([c.state, (await state(port)).info.queued], ['away', 2], 'nothing takes the switch again');
        } finally { c.close(); }
      } finally { b.close(); }
    } finally { a.close(); }
  },

  // the page: the switch let go when no mailbox wants it, taken again when one does; LAN play open or not
  async mailboxes([port]) {
    const { attachNet } = await pageNet(port);
    const pages = Math.ceil(2 * P.NET_MAILBOX_BYTES / 65536);
    const memory = new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: pages, maximum: pages, shared: true });
    const roam = mailbox(memory, 0), lanMb = mailbox(memory, P.NET_MAILBOX_BYTES);
    const logs = [];
    const link = attachNet(fakeGame(memory, { 4: roam, 7: lanMb }), { url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan`, name: 'P', pingMs: 60_000, idleMs: 300, log: l => logs.push(l) });
    const peers = async () => (await state(port)).peers;
    try {
      await sleep(300);
      assert.equal((await peers()).length, 0, 'nothing wants the switch yet: no connection');
      want(lanMb, 1);                                                        // the game's WSAStartup
      const v1 = await link.online;
      await until(async () => { const p = await peers(); return p.length === 1 && p[0].hello; });
      assert.equal((await peers())[0].lan, true, 'LAN play open: said in the hello');
      assert.equal(Atomics.load(lanMb.w, P.W_PAGE_STATE), P.NET_PAGE_ONLINE);
      want(roam, 1); want(lanMb, 0);                                         // free roam on, LAN screens left
      await until(async () => (await peers())[0]?.lan === false);
      await sleep(600);
      assert.equal((await peers()).length, 1, 'free roam still wants it');
      want(roam, 0);                                                         // free roam off too
      await sleep(100);
      assert.equal((await peers()).length, 1, 'kept for idleMs');
      await until(async () => (await peers()).length === 0);
      assert.equal(link.state, 'idle');
      const s = await state(port);
      assert.equal(s.info.released, 1, 'its address freed at once');
      assert.equal(s.reserved, 0);
      for (const mb of [roam, lanMb]) assert.equal(Atomics.load(mb.w, P.W_PAGE_STATE), P.NET_PAGE_IDLE);
      // a want back within idleMs keeps the place; after it, the page connects again
      want(lanMb, 1);
      await until(async () => (await peers()).length === 1 && Atomics.load(lanMb.w, P.W_PAGE_STATE) === P.NET_PAGE_ONLINE);
      await until(async () => (await peers())[0]?.lan === true);
      const v2 = P.ipStr(Atomics.load(lanMb.w, P.W_VIP) >>> 0);
      assert.notEqual(v2, v1, 'a new address (the old one went back)');
      want(lanMb, 0); await sleep(100); want(lanMb, 1); await sleep(500);
      assert.equal((await peers()).length, 1); assert.equal((await state(port)).info.released, 1, 'a short break keeps the place');
      // peer bits: one bit per host of the /17 up to the module's 2048 (a peer in another /24 has its own bit; the
      // third lands in 10.77.4.x, past a /22); the seventh lands in 10.77.8.x, past the /21 and the bitmap: no bit
      // (the module asks that host itself, runtime/web/net_lan.c), and nothing written past the bitmap (its header's
      // padding)
      const others = Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, i) => new Client(port, `O${i + 1}`));
      for (const o of others) await o.welcome();
      const hs = others.map(o => (o.vip & 0x7fff) >>> 0), low = hs.filter(h => h < P.NET_PEER_BITS);
      assert.ok(low.some(h => h >= 1024), `a host past the /22 (${hs.map(h => h.toString(16))})`);
      assert.ok(low.length < hs.length, `a host past the /21 (${hs.map(h => h.toString(16))})`);
      for (const h of low) await until(() => (Atomics.load(lanMb.w, P.W_PEER_BITS + (h >>> 5)) >>> (h & 31)) & 1);
      for (let i = P.NET_PEER_BITS / 32; P.W_PEER_BITS + i < P.NET_HDR_BYTES / 4; i++) assert.equal(Atomics.load(lanMb.w, P.W_PEER_BITS + i), 0, `word ${i} untouched`);
      for (const o of others) await o.close();
      assert.ok(logs.some(l => /goes back/.test(l)), 'the console says why it let go');
    } finally { link.close(); }
  },

  // the page: away, the place goes back while the game wants it and stays free; back, it is taken again
  async away([port]) {
    const { attachNet } = await pageNet(port);
    const memory = new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 10, maximum: 10, shared: true }), roam = mailbox(memory, 0);
    const logs = [];
    const link = attachNet(fakeGame(memory, { 4: roam }), { url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan`, name: 'P', pingMs: 60_000, idleMs: 100, log: l => logs.push(l) });
    const size = async () => (await state(port)).peers.length;
    try {
      want(roam, 1);                                                         // free roam runs
      const v1 = await link.online;
      await until(async () => (await size()) === 1);
      link.setAway(true);
      assert.equal(link.state, 'away');
      assert.equal(Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_PAGE_STATE), P.NET_PAGE_IDLE, 'C hears that the page let go');
      await until(async () => (await size()) === 0);
      const s = await state(port);
      assert.equal(s.info.released, 1, 'its address freed at once');
      assert.equal(s.reserved, 0);
      want(roam, 0); want(roam, 1); await sleep(300);                        // the game wants it again, and again
      assert.equal(await size(), 0, 'nothing connects while away');
      want(roam, 0); await sleep(300);
      assert.equal(link.state, 'away', 'the idle timer does not end away');
      link.setAway(false);
      assert.equal(link.state, 'idle', 'back, with nothing that wants the switch: no connection');
      await sleep(200);
      assert.equal(await size(), 0);
      link.setAway(true); want(roam, 1); link.setAway(false);                // back while free roam runs
      await until(async () => (await size()) === 1 && Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_PAGE_STATE) === P.NET_PAGE_ONLINE);
      assert.notEqual(P.ipStr(Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_VIP) >>> 0), v1, 'a new address');
      assert.ok(logs.some(l => /the player is away/.test(l)) && logs.some(l => /here again/.test(l)), 'the console says so');
    } finally { link.close(); }
  },

  // the page: kicked, it tells the game and stays off the switch for the rest of the game, whatever wants it; a page
  // whose id is banned is turned away at its hello the same way
  async removed([port]) {
    const { attachNet } = await pageNet(port);
    const memory = new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 10, maximum: 10, shared: true }), roam = mailbox(memory, 0);
    const mem2 = new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 10, maximum: 10, shared: true }), roam2 = mailbox(mem2, 0);
    const logs = [], told = [];
    const size = async () => (await state(port)).peers.length;
    const link = attachNet(fakeGame(memory, { 4: roam }), { url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan`, name: 'P', id: 'page-p', pingMs: 60_000, idleMs: 100,
      log: l => logs.push(l), onRemoved: r => told.push(r) });
    const banned = attachNet(fakeGame(mem2, { 4: roam2 }), { url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan?gate=page-b`, name: 'B', id: 'page-b', pingMs: 60_000,
      onRemoved: r => told.push(r) });
    try {
      want(roam, 1);
      const vip = P.ipNum(await link.online);
      await until(async () => (await size()) === 1);
      assert.equal((await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/expel?vip=${vip}&code=4001&msg=Stop`)).status, 200);
      await until(() => told.length === 1);
      assert.deepEqual(told[0], { ban: false, msg: 'Stop' });
      assert.equal(link.state, 'away');
      assert.equal(Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_PAGE_STATE), P.NET_PAGE_IDLE, 'C hears that the page let go');
      await until(async () => (await size()) === 0);
      assert.equal((await state(port)).reserved, 0, 'its address free at once');
      want(roam, 0); want(roam, 1); link.setAway(true); link.setAway(false); await sleep(300);
      assert.equal(await size(), 0, 'nothing connects again: not a want, not the away check');
      assert.ok(logs.some(l => /the operator kicked this player \("Stop"\): no switch for the rest of this game/.test(l)), logs.join('\n'));
      // its id banned: told at its hello, and off
      want(roam2, 1);
      await until(() => told.length === 2);
      assert.deepEqual(told[1], { ban: true, msg: 'page-b' });
      assert.equal(banned.state, 'away');
      await sleep(300);
      assert.equal(await size(), 0);
    } finally { link.close(); banned.close(); }
  },

  // the page: its hello names the players it blocks (NetOptions.block): page.rs reads what the hub was told
  async block([port]) {
    const { attachNet } = await pageNet(port);
    const memory = new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 10, maximum: 10, shared: true }), roam = mailbox(memory, 0);
    const link = attachNet(fakeGame(memory, { 4: roam }), { url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan`, name: 'P', block: ['Bob', 'carl'], pingMs: 60_000 });
    try {
      want(roam, 1);
      await link.online;
      await until(async () => (await state(port)).peers.some(p => p.hello));
    } finally { link.close(); }
  },

  // the page: what C queued at once goes as one bundle, a snapshot to several friends once; bundles from the switch are
  // taken apart in order
  async bundles([port]) {
    const { attachNet } = await pageNet(port);
    const memory = new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 10, maximum: 10, shared: true }), roam = mailbox(memory, 0);
    want(roam, 1); Atomics.store(roam.w, P.W_MODE, P.NET_MODE_VLAN);
    const link = attachNet(fakeGame(memory, { 4: roam }), { url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan`, name: 'P', pingMs: 60_000 });
    try {
      const me = P.ipNum(await link.online);
      const b = new Client(port, 'B'), c = new Client(port, 'C', '', null, { bundle: true });
      await b.welcome(); await c.welcome(); await sleep(100);
      // a tick of free roam: the same snapshot to B and C, another frame to B, the snapshot to the hub's address
      txPush(memory, roam, { dst: b.vip, data: 'snap' }); txPush(memory, roam, { dst: c.vip, data: 'snap' });
      txPush(memory, roam, { dst: b.vip, data: 'more' }); txPush(memory, roam, { dst: P.NET_ROAM_HUB, data: 'snap' });
      txBell(roam);
      await b.until(() => b.dgrams().length >= 2); await c.until(() => c.dgrams().length >= 1);
      assert.deepEqual(b.dgrams().map(g => [g.data, g.src === me, g.dst === b.vip]), [['snap', true, true], ['more', true, true]]);
      assert.deepEqual(c.dgrams().map(g => [g.data, g.src === me, g.dst === c.vip]), [['snap', true, true]]);
      assert.equal((await state(port)).info.bundlesIn, 1, 'the four went as one message');
      // three from C at once (one bundle): the switch sends them to the page as one message, and C hears them in order
      c.sendBundle([{ f: frameOf(me, 'r1', 1, 47210, 47210) }, { f: frameOf(me, 'r2', 1, 47210, 47210) }, { f: frameOf(me, 'r3', 1, 47210, 47210) }]);
      await until(() => Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_RX_HEAD) - Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_RX_TAIL) >= 3);
      assert.deepEqual(rxTake(memory, roam).map(r => [r.data, r.src === c.vip, r.dst === me]), [['r1', true, true], ['r2', true, true], ['r3', true, true]]);
      assert.ok((await state(port)).info.bundlesOut >= 1, 'to the page as a bundle');
      const s = link.stats();
      assert.equal(s.framesOut, 4); assert.equal(s.framesIn, 3, 'frames counted one by one');
      // its hello took compact bundles (nfsu2-lan compact.rs): free roam's datagrams come without their magic,
      // version, length and CRC, and the game still reads them byte for byte, as it does a broadcast, other ports,
      // a broken CRC and LAN play's UDP
      const snap = roamDatagram(3, 70), hello = roamDatagram(1, 40), broken = roamDatagram(3, 70);
      broken[broken.length - 1] ^= 0x55;
      const sent = [{ f: frameOf(me, snap, 1, 47210, 47210), dst: me, sport: 47210, dport: 47210, data: snap },
        { f: frameOf(P.NET_BROADCAST, hello, 1, 47210, 47210), dst: P.NET_BROADCAST, sport: 47210, dport: 47210, data: hello },
        { f: frameOf(me, snap, 1, 47211, 47300), dst: me, sport: 47211, dport: 47300, data: snap },
        { f: frameOf(me, broken, 1, 47210, 47210), dst: me, sport: 47210, dport: 47210, data: broken }];
      c.sendBundle(sent.map(({ f }) => ({ f })));
      await until(() => Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_RX_HEAD) - Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_RX_TAIL) >= sent.length);
      const got = rxTakeRaw(memory, roam);
      assert.deepEqual(got.map(g => [g.src === c.vip, g.dst >>> 0, g.sport, g.dport, g.data.toString('hex')]),
        sent.map(x => [true, x.dst >>> 0, x.sport, x.dport, x.data.toString('hex')]), 'byte for byte');
      assert.equal(link.stats().framesIn, 3 + sent.length);
      assert.ok(link.stats().compactIn >= 2, 'as compact bundles');
      // its hello took deltas too: a friend's snapshots, a few bytes new each time and now and then longer, come as
      // what changed (nfsu2-lan compact.rs Refs, proto.ts unpackCompact) and still reach the game byte for byte
      const seq = [];
      let snapNow = Buffer.from(roamDatagram(3, 70));
      for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) {
        const body = Buffer.from(snapNow.subarray(16, snapNow.length - 4));
        body[(i * 7) % body.length] = i; body[(i * 13 + 3) % body.length] ^= 0x5a;
        const d = Buffer.alloc(16 + body.length + (i === 30 ? 1 : 0) + 4);
        snapNow.copy(d, 0, 0, 16); body.copy(d, 16);
        d.writeUInt16LE(d.length, 6); d.writeUInt32LE(zlib.crc32(d.subarray(0, d.length - 4)), d.length - 4);
        seq.push(d); snapNow = d;
      }
      for (let i = 0; i < seq.length; i += 6) {
        c.sendBundle(seq.slice(i, i + 6).map(d => ({ f: frameOf(me, d, 1, 47210, 47210) })));
        await until(() => Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_RX_HEAD) - Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_RX_TAIL) >= Math.min(6, seq.length - i));
        assert.deepEqual(rxTakeRaw(memory, roam).map(g => g.data.toString('hex')), seq.slice(i, i + 6).map(d => d.toString('hex')), `snapshots ${i} on`);
      }
      assert.ok(link.stats().deltaIn >= 50, `as deltas (${link.stats().deltaIn} of ${seq.length})`);
      // free roam's own datagrams (a ping, a pong) wait for the next car state to a friend, at most TX_HOLD_MS (50)
      // after the page's last send, and go with it as one message; one long after the last send goes at once
      const ping = roamDatagram(6, 8), pong = roamDatagram(7, 16), carState = roamDatagram(3, 70);
      const ins = async () => (await state(port)).info.bundlesIn, in0 = await ins(), nb = b.dgrams().length, nc = c.dgrams().length;
      await sleep(80);
      txPush(memory, roam, { dst: b.vip, data: ping }); txBell(roam);
      await b.until(() => b.dgrams().length >= nb + 1);
      txPush(memory, roam, { dst: b.vip, data: pong }); txBell(roam);
      await sleep(15);
      assert.equal(b.dgrams().length, nb + 1, 'a pong right after a send waits');
      txPush(memory, roam, { dst: c.vip, data: carState }); txBell(roam);
      await b.until(() => b.dgrams().length >= nb + 2); await c.until(() => c.dgrams().length >= nc + 1);
      assert.equal(await ins(), in0 + 1, 'the ping alone (a frame), then the pong with the car state (a bundle)');
      txPush(memory, roam, { dst: b.vip, data: carState }); txBell(roam);
      await b.until(() => b.dgrams().length >= nb + 3);
      const t0 = performance.now();
      txPush(memory, roam, { dst: b.vip, data: ping }); txBell(roam);
      await b.until(() => b.dgrams().length >= nb + 4);
      const held = performance.now() - t0;
      assert.ok(held >= 25, `without a car state it waits until 50 ms after the last send (${held.toFixed(0)} ms)`);
      // a game not driving (its HELLO says a race): its own wait until 500 ms after the last send (TX_HOLD_AWAY_MS; the
      // switch holds what its friends send it as long, nfsu2-lan away.rs), and a HELLO that says it drives again goes
      // at once, with what waited
      const helloSt = st => {
        const d = roamDatagram(1, 40);
        d[19] = st; d.writeUInt32LE(zlib.crc32(d.subarray(0, d.length - 4)), d.length - 4);
        return d;
      };
      txPush(memory, roam, { dst: b.vip, data: helloSt(3) }); txBell(roam);
      await b.until(() => b.dgrams().length >= nb + 5);
      let t1 = performance.now();
      txPush(memory, roam, { dst: b.vip, data: ping }); txBell(roam);
      await b.until(() => b.dgrams().length >= nb + 6);
      const away = performance.now() - t1;
      assert.ok(away >= 300, `not driving, it waits until 500 ms after the last send (${away.toFixed(0)} ms)`);
      await sleep(30);
      t1 = performance.now();
      txPush(memory, roam, { dst: b.vip, data: ping }); txPush(memory, roam, { dst: b.vip, data: helloSt(2) }); txBell(roam);
      await b.until(() => b.dgrams().length >= nb + 8);
      const back = performance.now() - t1;
      assert.ok(back < 200, `driving again: at once (${back.toFixed(0)} ms)`);
      await b.close(); await c.close();
    } finally { link.close(); }
  },

  // its hello took every other datagram as what changed too ("ldelta":1, nfsu2-lan compact.rs Refs::other): a race's
  // LAN UDP from two rivals, a few bytes new each time, now and then of another length or on other ports, with a LAN
  // broadcast and the race horn's UDP among them, reaches the game byte for byte, most of it as deltas
  async races([port]) {
    const { attachNet } = await pageNet(port);
    const memory = new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 10, maximum: 10, shared: true }), lanMb = mailbox(memory, 0);
    want(lanMb, 1); Atomics.store(lanMb.w, P.W_MODE, P.NET_MODE_LAN);
    const link = attachNet(fakeGame(memory, { 7: lanMb }), { url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan`, name: 'P', pingMs: 60_000 });
    try {
      const me = P.ipNum(await link.online);
      const r1 = new Client(port, 'R1', '', null, { bundle: true }), r2 = new Client(port, 'R2', '', null, { bundle: true });
      await r1.welcome(); await r2.welcome(); await sleep(100);
      const pk = [Buffer.alloc(140), Buffer.alloc(140)];
      pk.forEach((b, j) => { for (let i = 0; i < b.length; i++) b[i] = (i * 31 + 7 * j) & 255; });
      const sent = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < 90; i++) {
        const j = i % 2, c = j ? r2 : r1;
        let b = pk[j];
        b[(i * 7) % b.length] = i; b[(i * 13 + 5) % b.length] ^= 0x5a; b.writeFloatLE(i * 1.5, 20);
        if (i % 20 === 10) pk[j] = b = Buffer.concat([b, Buffer.from([i])]);
        if (i % 20 === 15) pk[j] = b = b.subarray(0, b.length - 3);
        const data = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0, 64, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]), b]);
        const dport = i === 41 ? 6114 : 6113;
        sent.push({ c, kind: 3, dst: me, sport: 6112, dport, data, f: frameOf(me, data, 3, 6112, dport) });
        if (i % 9 === 4) {
          const bc = Buffer.from([0, 64, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, i]);
          sent.push({ c, kind: 3, dst: P.NET_BROADCAST, sport: 6112, dport: 6112, data: bc, f: frameOf(P.NET_BROADCAST, bc, 3, 6112, 6112) });
        }
      }
      for (let i = 0; i < sent.length; i += 6) {
        const part = sent.slice(i, i + 6);
        for (const c of [r1, r2]) { const mine = part.filter(x => x.c === c); if (mine.length) c.sendBundle(mine.map(({ f }) => ({ f }))); }
        await until(() => Atomics.load(lanMb.w, P.W_RX_HEAD) - Atomics.load(lanMb.w, P.W_RX_TAIL) >= part.length);
        const got = rxTakeRaw(memory, lanMb);
        const key = g => `${g.src >>> 0}/${g.dst >>> 0}/${g.sport}/${g.dport}/${g.data.toString('hex')}`;
        // (the two rivals' bundles may come in either order: each one's own in order)
        for (const c of [r1, r2])
          assert.deepEqual(got.filter(g => g.src >>> 0 === c.vip).map(key), part.filter(x => x.c === c).map(x => key({ ...x, src: c.vip })), `datagrams ${i} on`);
      }
      assert.ok(link.stats().deltaIn >= 70, `as deltas (${link.stats().deltaIn} of ${sent.length})`);
      const mix = (await state(port)).info.mix;
      console.log(`race datagrams: ${mix['LAN UDP'][1]}, ${(mix['LAN UDP'][0] / mix['LAN UDP'][1]).toFixed(1)} bytes each (plain ${5 + 4 + 8 + 141})`);
      assert.ok(mix['LAN UDP'][0] / mix['LAN UDP'][1] < 60, `${(mix['LAN UDP'][0] / mix['LAN UDP'][1]).toFixed(1)} bytes a race datagram`);
      // the game's own of one frame (a race's creator sends each joiner one, one after the other) go in one message:
      // the page waits TX_HOLD_LAN_MS (1) after the first before it sends (it sent at once, so the rest of the frame
      // went in messages of their own)
      const in0 = (await state(port)).info.bundlesIn, n1 = r1.dgrams().length, n2 = r2.dgrams().length;
      for (const [c, j] of [[r1, 0], [r2, 1], [r1, 2]]) {
        txPush(memory, lanMb, { kind: 3, dst: c.vip, sport: 6112, dport: 6112, data: Buffer.from([0, 64, 0, 0, j, 0, 0, 0, 9, 9]) });
        txBell(lanMb);
      }
      await r1.until(() => r1.dgrams().length >= n1 + 2); await r2.until(() => r2.dgrams().length >= n2 + 1);
      assert.equal((await state(port)).info.bundlesIn, in0 + 1, "a frame's three datagrams, one message");
      assert.ok(link.stats().txWaitMeanMs >= 0.9, `they waited ${link.stats().txWaitMeanMs.toFixed(2)} ms for the rest of the frame`);
      await r1.close(); await r2.close();
    } finally { link.close(); }
  },

  // its hello took friends' car states by their fields (nfsu2-lan fpred.rs, proto.ts fpredTake): each reaches the game
  // rounded, as the switch rounded it, with a CRC that checks out; one of a layout that does not go so (three states)
  // and a HELLO reach it as they were
  async fpred([port]) {
    const { attachNet } = await pageNet(port);
    const memory = new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 10, maximum: 10, shared: true }), roam = mailbox(memory, 0);
    want(roam, 1); Atomics.store(roam.w, P.W_MODE, P.NET_MODE_VLAN);
    const link = attachNet(fakeGame(memory, { 4: roam }), { url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan`, name: 'P', pingMs: 60_000 });
    try {
      const me = P.ipNum(await link.online);
      const c = new Client(port, 'C', '', null, { bundle: true });
      await c.welcome(); await sleep(100);
      const sent = [];
      let t = 4_294_000_000;
      for (let k = 0; k < 120; k++) {
        t = (t + 50_000 + (k % 7 === 0 ? 16_667 : 0)) >>> 0;
        const a = k * 0.05, moving = k < 90;
        const p = moving ? [1695.123 + 40 * Math.cos(a), -884.5 + 40 * Math.sin(a), 24.25 + 0.01 * k] : [1700.5, -880.25, 25.125];
        const v = moving ? [-40 * Math.sin(a), 40 * Math.cos(a), 0.2] : [0, 0, 0];
        sent.push(snapDatagram({ seq: k, t, p, v, k: moving ? k : 90, x: k % 10 === 5 ? 28 : k === 40 ? 0 : 16 }));
        if (k === 60) {
          const three = snapDatagram({ seq: k, t, p, v, k, x: 16 });
          three[8 + 12] = 3;
          three.writeUInt32LE(zlib.crc32(three.subarray(0, three.length - 4)), three.length - 4);
          sent.push(three, roamDatagram(1, 40));
        }
      }
      const expect = sent.map(d => d[5] === 3 && d[8 + 12] === 1 ? roundedDatagram(d) : d);
      for (let i = 0; i < sent.length; i += 6) {
        const part = sent.slice(i, i + 6);
        c.sendBundle(part.map(d => ({ f: frameOf(me, d, 1, 47210, 47210) })));
        await until(() => Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_RX_HEAD) - Atomics.load(roam.w, P.W_RX_TAIL) >= part.length);
        const got = rxTakeRaw(memory, roam);
        assert.deepEqual(got.map(g => [g.src === c.vip, g.sport, g.dport, g.data.toString('hex')]),
          expect.slice(i, i + 6).map(d => [true, 47210, 47210, d.toString('hex')]), `datagrams ${i} on`);
        for (const g of got) assert.equal(g.data.readUInt32LE(g.data.length - 4), zlib.crc32(g.data.subarray(0, g.data.length - 4)), 'a CRC that checks out');
      }
      const info = (await state(port)).info;
      assert.ok(info.fpredEntries >= 115 && info.fpredEntries <= info.snapEntries, `by their fields: ${info.fpredEntries} of ${info.snapEntries}`);
      assert.ok(info.snapBytes / info.snapEntries < 40, `${(info.snapBytes / info.snapEntries).toFixed(1)} bytes a car state`);
      await c.close();
    } finally { link.close(); }
  },

  // a page driving in free roam: the switch times its round trip by stamping its compact bundles (probe_ms 100 here),
  // which the page echoes in its next bundle or alone (ECHO_WAIT_MS), not by pinging it; every car state still comes
  async echo([port]) {
    const { attachNet } = await pageNet(port);
    const memory = new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 10, maximum: 10, shared: true }), roam = mailbox(memory, 0);
    want(roam, 1); Atomics.store(roam.w, P.W_MODE, P.NET_MODE_VLAN);
    const link = attachNet(fakeGame(memory, { 4: roam }), { url: `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/lan`, name: 'P', pingMs: 60_000 });
    try {
      const me = P.ipNum(await link.online);
      const c = new Client(port, 'C', '', null, { bundle: true });
      await c.welcome(); await sleep(100);
      // the page's game drives: a car state of its own to C now and then (the switch reads that it drives from it)
      let k = 0;
      const mine = () => { txPush(memory, roam, { dst: c.vip, data: snapDatagram({ sender: 0x1111, seq: k, t: 1_000_000 + 50_000 * k, p: [1, 2, 3], v: [0, 0, 0], k: k++ }) }); txBell(roam); };
      mine();
      let got = 0;
      for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
        c.sendBundle([{ f: frameOf(me, snapDatagram({ seq: i, t: 2_000_000 + 50_000 * i, p: [10 + i, 2, 3], v: [1, 0, 0], k: i }), 1, 47210, 47210) }]);
        if (i % 4 === 0) mine();
        await sleep(50);
        got += rxTakeRaw(memory, roam).length;
      }
      await sleep(200);
      got += rxTakeRaw(memory, roam).length;
      assert.equal(got, 40, 'every car state, through stamped bundles too');
      const st = await state(port);
      const p = st.peers.find(x => x.vip >>> 0 === me);
      assert.ok(st.info.echoes >= 5, `stamps echoed: ${st.info.echoes}`);
      assert.ok(p.rtt !== null && p.rtt >= 0 && p.rtt < 100, `the page's round trip: ${p.rtt} ms`);
      await c.close();
    } finally { link.close(); }
  },
};

const [name, ...ports] = process.argv.slice(2);
try {
  await cases[name](ports.map(Number));
  console.log(`page ${name}: ok`);
  process.exit(0);
} catch (e) {
  console.error(`page ${name}: ${e.stack ?? e}`);
  process.exit(1);
}

//! Seven tests of the page (web/src/net/index.ts): the page's own code, bundled as the app bundles it, run in node
//! (tests/page.mjs) against this switch.  Skipped (with a message) without node.

mod harness;

use harness::*;
use nfsu2_lan::LanOptions;

/// page.mjs's case against the switches on these ports
async fn page(case: &str, ports: &[u16]) {
    let script = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("tests/page.mjs");
    let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new("node");
    cmd.arg(script).arg(case).args(ports.iter().map(u16::to_string)).current_dir(web_dir());
    let out = tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(90), cmd.output()).await.expect("page.mjs in time").expect("node");
    print!("{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout));
    eprint!("{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr));
    assert!(out.status.success(), "page.mjs {case} failed");
}

fn no_node() -> bool {
    if node().is_none() {
        println!("skipped: no node");
        return true;
    }
    false
}

// on a switch with room for one: the second game waits in line (told where, and "the server is full" once), keeps
// its place when its link drops, and hears "a place freed up" when the first leaves and it gets on

//! Free roam's license plates through the switch (src/plates.rs): a HELLO whose plate is broken or reads as a slur
//! goes on without it (a `[plate]` line for the slur), so the player is still heard; a new plate goes once per 10 s at
//! most (the HELLO goes on with the last one meanwhile), the same one always; and a HELLO without one is not looked at.
mod harness;
use harness::*;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

/// a HELLO of core 17 from "Ann": its header's flags, then (`ext`) the crews' count, the links, the outrun's player and
/// the flag's length, 0 each, and with `plate` its length and bytes; CRC and length right
fn datagram(flags: u16, ext: bool, plate: Option<&[u8]>) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut d = vec![0u8; 29];
    d[..4].copy_from_slice(b"N2FR");
    d[4] = 1;
    d[5] = 1;
    d[14..16].copy_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
    d[16] = 17;
    d[19] = 2;
    d[28] = 3;
    d.extend_from_slice(b"Ann");
    d.push(0); // the ids it hears
    if ext {
        d.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]); // crews, links, outrun, flag
    }
    if let Some(t) = plate {
        d.push(t.len() as u8);
        d.extend_from_slice(t);
    }
    let n = (d.len() + 4) as u16;
    d[6..8].copy_from_slice(&n.to_le_bytes());
    let crc = crc32fast::hash(&d);
    d.extend_from_slice(&crc.to_le_bytes());
    d
}
/// the HELLO a game sends with plate `text` ("" none: no flag, no plate)
fn hello(text: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    if text.is_empty() { datagram(0x0200, false, None) } else { datagram(0x8200, true, Some(text)) }
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn broken_plates_and_slurs_go_on_without_their_plate_a_new_plate_once_per_ten_seconds() {
    let _guard = serial().await;
    let sw = start(opts()).await;
    let lines = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::<String>::new()));
    let l2 = lines.clone();
    sw.lan.on_line(Box::new(move |s: &str| l2.lock().unwrap().push(s.to_string())));
    let mut a = Client::connect(sw.port, "Ann").await;
    a.welcome().await;
    let mut b = Client::connect(sw.port, "Bob").await;
    b.welcome().await;
    let send = |d: &[u8]| a.udp(b.vip, 47210, 47210, d, 1, 0);
    let broken = [&b"123456789"[..], b"bad", b"A B", b"A\0B", "\u{c9}".as_bytes()];
    let slurs = [&b"N1GGER"[..], b"N1GGER", b"1488"];
    for t in broken.iter().chain(slurs.iter()) {
        send(&hello(t));
    }
    // a good one, the same one again, another within 10 s, one without a plate; and one whose CRC is wrong
    send(&hello(b"AB123456"));
    send(&hello(b"AB123456"));
    send(&hello(b"XYZ789"));
    send(&hello(b""));
    let mut bad = hello(b"N1GGER");
    *bad.last_mut().unwrap() ^= 1;
    send(&bad);
    let mut want: Vec<Vec<u8>> = broken.iter().map(|t| datagram(0x0200, true, Some(t))).collect(); // the flag off, the rest as it came
    want.extend(slurs.iter().map(|_| datagram(0x0200, true, None))); // the plate taken out
    want.extend([hello(b"AB123456"), hello(b"AB123456"), hello(b"AB123456"), hello(b""), bad.clone()]);
    b.until_true(|g| g.frames.len() >= want.len()).await;
    tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
    let got: Vec<Vec<u8>> = b.got().frames.iter().map(|(f, _)| f[16..].to_vec()).collect();
    assert_eq!(got, want, "what came");
    let l = lines.lock().unwrap().clone();
    assert_eq!(l.len(), 3, "{l:?}");
    assert!(
        l[0].starts_with("[plate] ") && l[0].ends_with("\"Ann\" N1GGER: reads as a slur, dropped (its HELLOs go on without it)"),
        "{l:?}"
    );
    assert!(l[1].ends_with("\"Ann\" 1488: reads as a slur, dropped (its HELLOs go on without it)"), "{l:?}");
    assert!(l[2].ends_with("\"Ann\" AB123456"), "{l:?}");
    a.close().await;
    b.close().await;
    sw.close().await;
}

//! The line (queue.rs): pages that can wait (?queue) wait for a place in their order when every place is taken, a page
//! of before still gets "LAN full", a page that lets go leaves its place in line, one that dropped keeps it for its
//! ticket, newcomers never pass the line, a dropped player's token still gets its address back at once.

mod harness;

use harness::*;
use nfsu2_lan::LanOptions;
use serde_json::{Value, json};

/// a page that can wait: /lan?queue (with ?resume and its ticket when it comes back), its hello at once as the page sends it
async fn waiter(port: u16, name: &str, ticket: Option<&str>) -> Client {
    let q = if ticket.is_some() { "?queue&resume" } else { "?queue" };
    let c = Client::with(port, name, q, Opts::default()).await;
    let mut h = json!({ "t": "hello", "name": name, "lan": 1 });
    if let Some(t) = ticket {
        h["ticket"] = t.into();
    }
    c.text(&h.to_string());
    c
}

/// its newest {"t":"queue"} once it says pos (2 s at most)
async fn told(c: &Client, pos: u64) -> Value {
    c.until(|g| g.ctl.iter().rev().find(|m| m["t"] == "queue").filter(|m| m["pos"] == pos).cloned()).await
}

fn line_opts(max_peers: usize) -> LanOptions {
    LanOptions { max_peers, line_tell_ms: 100, ..opts() }
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn the_line_lets_them_in_first_come_first_served() {
    let _s = serial().await;
    let sw = start(line_opts(2)).await;
    let mut a = Client::connect(sw.port, "Alice").await;
    a.welcome().await;
    let mut b = Client::connect(sw.port, "Bob").await;
    b.welcome().await;
    assert!(sw.lan.full(), "two places, two players");
    assert_eq!(sw.lan.waiting(), 0);
    // full: the ones that can wait are told their place (the first time with a ticket), a page of before is refused
    let mut c = waiter(sw.port, "Carol", None).await;
    let m = told(&c, 1).await;
    assert_eq!(m["of"], 1);
    assert!(m["ticket"].as_str().is_some_and(|t| t.len() >= 20), "a ticket: {m}");
    assert!(m.get("eta").is_none(), "no pace yet: {m}");
    let mut d = waiter(sw.port, "Dave", None).await;
    assert_eq!(told(&d, 2).await["of"], 2);
    let e = Client::connect(sw.port, "Eve").await;
    assert_eq!(e.closed().await, (1013, "LAN full".into()), "a page that cannot wait");
    assert!(sw.lan.full());
    assert_eq!(sw.lan.waiting(), 2);
    assert!(c.got().ctl.iter().all(|m| m["t"] != "welcome") && sw.peer_named("Carol").is_none(), "nobody waiting is on the switch");
    // a waiting page's ping is answered
    c.text(r#"{"t":"ping","id":7}"#);
    c.until(|g| g.ctl.iter().find(|m| m["t"] == "pong" && m["id"] == 7).cloned()).await;
    // a place frees up (the page let go): the first in line takes it, with the hello it sent while it waited
    a.close_with(1000, "idle");
    let w = c.welcome().await;
    assert!(w["vip"].is_u64());
    wait_for(2000, || sw.peer_named("Carol").is_some_and(|p| p.hello)).await;
    c.until_true(|g| g.names() == "Bob,Carol").await;
    // the next one moves up, and goes in when the next place frees up
    assert_eq!(told(&d, 1).await["of"], 1);
    b.close_with(1000, "closed");
    d.welcome().await;
    assert_eq!(sw.lan.waiting(), 0);
    let i = sw.info().await;
    assert_eq!((i["queued"].as_u64(), i["lineIn"].as_u64(), i["waiting"].as_u64()), (Some(2), Some(2), Some(0)));
    // the line is empty: a newcomer gets a place at once again (once one is free: the switch has let Carol go)
    c.close_with(1000, "idle");
    wait_for(2000, || !sw.lan.full()).await;
    let mut f = waiter(sw.port, "Fay", None).await;
    f.welcome().await;
    assert_eq!(f.got().count("queue"), 0);
    sw.close().await;
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn a_dropped_page_keeps_its_place_for_its_ticket_one_that_lets_go_leaves() {
    let _s = serial().await;
    let sw = start(line_opts(1)).await;
    let mut a = Client::connect(sw.port, "Alice").await;
    a.welcome().await;
    let c = waiter(sw.port, "Carol", None).await;
    let ticket = told(&c, 1).await["ticket"].as_str().unwrap().to_string();
    let mut d = waiter(sw.port, "Dave", None).await;
    told(&d, 2).await;
    let g = waiter(sw.port, "Gina", None).await;
    told(&g, 3).await;
    // Carol's link drops (no close frame): her place is kept; Gina lets go: hers goes at once
    c.terminate();
    g.close_with(1000, "idle");
    wait_for(2000, || sw.lan.waiting() == 2).await;
    // a place frees up: Carol is away, so Dave (next) takes it, and Carol keeps the first place
    a.close_with(1000, "idle");
    d.welcome().await;
    assert_eq!(sw.lan.waiting(), 1, "Carol's place kept");
    // Carol is back with her ticket: her place again, first
    let mut c2 = waiter(sw.port, "Carol", Some(&ticket)).await;
    let m = told(&c2, 1).await;
    assert!(m.get("ticket").is_none(), "her ticket stays the one she has");
    let mut h = waiter(sw.port, "Hank", None).await;
    told(&h, 2).await;
    d.close_with(1000, "idle");
    c2.welcome().await;
    wait_for(2000, || sw.peer_named("Carol").is_some()).await;
    assert_eq!(told(&h, 1).await["of"], 1);
    // a ticket nobody holds is a newcomer's place, at the back
    let x = waiter(sw.port, "Xena", Some("no-such-ticket-0000000000")).await;
    assert_eq!(told(&x, 2).await["of"], 2);
    let i = sw.info().await;
    assert_eq!(i["rejoined"], 1);
    assert_eq!(i["lineLeft"], 1, "Gina");
    c2.close_with(1000, "idle");
    h.welcome().await;
    sw.close().await;
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]

    assert_eq!(a2.welcome().await["vip"], wa["vip"]);

    b.close_with(1000, "idle");
    c.welcome().await;

    sw.close().await;
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn a_full_line_refuses_and_the_pace_gives_a_wait() {

    }

//! A player under a race ban (the crate doc's Kicks and bans) stays on the switch, but no frame that races another
//! player goes from it or to it: LAN play, free roam's outrun and lobby messages (in a bundle too); its other free-roam
//! datagrams pass.  A hello under a name taken away is turned away with `CLOSE_RENAME`.

mod harness;

use bytes::Bytes;
use harness::*;
use nfsu2_lan::CLOSE_RENAME;
use serde_json::json;

const ROAM_PORT: u16 = 47210;

/// a free-roam datagram of type t (runtime/roam_core.h: "N2FR", version 1, type, then the rest of its header)
fn roam(t: u8) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut d = b"N2FR".to_vec();
    d.extend([1, t]);
    d.extend([0u8; 26]);
    d
}

/// what c got from `from` (sorted: LAN play's datagrams and stream segments wait for clocks of their own): LAN play's
/// kinds, and free roam's datagram types
fn got_from(c: &Client, from: u32) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut v: Vec<String> = c
        .got()
        .dgrams()
        .iter()
        .filter(|d| d.src == from)
        .map(|d| if d.kind == 1 && d.buf.len() > 21 { format!("roam {}", d.buf[21]) } else { format!("kind {}", d.kind) })
        .collect();
    v.sort();
    v
}

/// a sends b LAN play's UDP and TCP, an outrun's, a lobby's and a PING's datagram, and an outrun's in a bundle
fn send_all(a: &Client, b: &Client) {
    a.udp(b.vip, 9999, 9999, b"lan", 3, 0);
    a.udp(b.vip, 50000, 9900, b"seg", 4, 0);
    for t in [9, 12, 6] {
        a.udp(b.vip, ROAM_PORT, ROAM_PORT, &roam(t), 1, 0);
    }
    a.send_bundle(&[(frame_of(b.vip, &roam(9), 1, ROAM_PORT, ROAM_PORT), vec![])]);
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn a_race_banned_player_races_nobody_and_drives_on() {
    let _s = serial().await;
    let sw = start(opts()).await;
    let mut a = Client::with(sw.port, "Ann", "?norace=pa", Opts { id: Some("pa"), ..lan(1) }).await;
    a.welcome().await;
    let mut b = Client::with(sw.port, "Bob", "?norace=pa", Opts { id: Some("pb"), ..lan(1) }).await;
    b.welcome().await;
    a.until(|g| g.ctl.iter().find(|m| m["t"] == "races").cloned()).await;
    wait_for(2000, || sw.peer_named("Bob").is_some_and(|p| p.hello)).await;
    assert!(b.got().ctl.iter().all(|m| m["t"] != "races"));
    // either way: only the PING
    send_all(&a, &b);
    send_all(&b, &a);
    sleep(300).await;
    assert_eq!(got_from(&b, a.vip), vec!["roam 6"]);
    assert_eq!(got_from(&a, b.vip), vec!["roam 6"]);
    assert!(a.is_open() && b.is_open());

    // the operator lifts it while Ann plays: everything goes; and puts one on Bob
    assert!(sw.lan.set_races(a.vip, false, Bytes::from(json!({ "t": "races", "lifted": true }).to_string())));
    a.until(|g| g.ctl.iter().find(|m| m["lifted"] == true).cloned()).await;
    send_all(&a, &b);
    sleep(300).await;
    assert_eq!(got_from(&b, a.vip), vec!["kind 3", "kind 4", "roam 12", "roam 6", "roam 6", "roam 9", "roam 9"]);
    assert!(sw.lan.set_races(b.vip, true, Bytes::from(json!({ "t": "races", "msg": "x" }).to_string())));
    send_all(&a, &b);
    sleep(300).await;
    assert_eq!(got_from(&b, a.vip).len(), 8, "one more: the PING");
    assert!(!sw.lan.set_races(0x0A4D_1717, true, Bytes::from_static(b"{}")), "nobody there");
    sw.close().await;
}

//! names.mjs itself, under node, against this port: the same answer for every name of a corpus (names.test.mjs's
//! names, near misses, made-up names from a fixed seed, ASCII and Unicode, and every code point of Unicode's planes
//! in use in a few places of a name), the same lists and the same lookalikes.  Skipped (with a message) where there
//! is no node.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Command;

use super::tests::{ALLOWED, BLOCKED, UNICODE};
use super::*;

/// SplitMix64: the same names on every run
struct Rnd(u64);

impl Rnd {
    fn next(&mut self, n: usize) -> usize {
        self.0 = self.0.wrapping_add(0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15);
        let mut z = self.0;
        z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xbf58_476d_1ce4_e5b9);
        z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94d0_49bb_1331_11eb);
        ((z ^ (z >> 31)) % n as u64) as usize
    }

    fn pick<'a, T>(&mut self, a: &'a [T]) -> &'a T {
        &a[self.next(a.len())]
    }
}

/// the characters of these ranges of code points
fn chars(ranges: &[(u32, u32)]) -> Vec<char> {
    ranges.iter().flat_map(|&(a, b)| a..=b).filter_map(char::from_u32).collect()
}

/// Marks: accents of every script, variation selectors, the keycap, and some that Unicode added after 16.0 (marks
/// with a combining class in unicode-normalization's tables, nothing yet for Node's ICU).
fn marks() -> Vec<char> {
    chars(&[
        (0x300, 0x36f),
        (0x483, 0x489),
        (0x591, 0x5bd),
        (0x64b, 0x65f),
        (0x900, 0x903),
        (0x93a, 0x94f),
        (0x1ab0, 0x1ace),
        (0x1dc0, 0x1dff),
        (0x20d0, 0x20f0),
        (0xfe00, 0xfe0f),
        (0xfe20, 0xfe2f),
        (0x1d165, 0x1d169),
        (0x1d16d, 0x1d172),
        (0xe0100, 0xe0110),
        (0x10ef5, 0x10efb),
        (0x1e6e3, 0x1e6ef),
    ])
}

/// Spaces, separators and signs that stand for no letter, the format characters (zero-width, bidi, tags) among them.
fn separators() -> Vec<char> {
    let mut v: Vec<char> = " _-.,;:/\\*#~^`'\"?=<>()[]{}%&2\t\n".chars().collect();
    v.extend(chars(&[
        (0xa0, 0xa0),
        (0xad, 0xad),
        (0xb7, 0xb7),
        (0x61c, 0x61c),
        (0x85, 0x85),
        (0x1680, 0x1680),
        (0x180e, 0x180e),
        (0x2000, 0x200f),
        (0x2022, 0x2022),
        (0x2028, 0x202f),
        (0x205f, 0x2064),
        (0x2066, 0x2069),
        (0x3000, 0x3000),
        (0xfeff, 0xfeff),
        (0xe0001, 0xe0001),
        (0xe0020, 0xe007f),
    ]));
    v
}

/// Emoji (with a skin tone, a joiner, a variation selector), other scripts, digits of other scripts, signs that

/// The code points this port reads as one ASCII character, by that character: styled letters and digits
/// (fullwidth, mathematical, circled, squared, super- and subscript), accented letters, ligature-free letterlike
/// signs, and the lookalikes of other scripts.  That names.mjs reads them so too is what the answers show.
fn alternatives() -> HashMap<char, Vec<char>> {
    let mut alts: HashMap<char, Vec<char>> = HashMap::new();
    let ranges = [
        (0xa0, 0x2ff),
        (0x370, 0x52f),
        (0x1d00, 0x1dbf),
        (0x1e00, 0x1eff),
        (0x2070, 0x20c0),
        (0x2100, 0x218f),
        (0x2460, 0x24ff),
        (0xff00, 0xff5e),
        (0x1d400, 0x1d7ff),
        (0x1f100, 0x1f1ff),
    ];
    for ch in chars(&ranges) {
        match read(&ch.to_string())[..] {
            [r] if r.is_ascii_graphic() => alts.entry(r).or_default().push(ch),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    alts
}

/// pieces of the made-up names: the lists' words, the near misses, the names this server sees most, digits
fn pieces() -> Vec<&'static str> {
    let mut p: Vec<&str> = ANYWHERE
        .iter()
        .chain(WHOLE)
        .chain(EDGE)
        .chain(EDGE_OK_START)
        .chain(EDGE_OK_END)
        .chain(WHOLE_OK)
        .chain(PID_STEMS)
        .copied()
        .collect();
    p.extend(NEAR);
    p.extend([
        "mustafa", "gs", "raccoon", "spice", "spicy", "niger", "pakize", "pakistan", "xx", "gamer", "a", "g", "dani", "hakan", "van",
        "tycoon", "trigger", "ibrahim", "99", "1995", "69", "42",
    ]);
    // the neo-Nazi code and other numbers, names with the new words' letters in them
    p.extend(["1488", "88", "14", "1_4", "8-8", "spider", "shinigami", "zuniga", "adolf"]);
    // a lone n before digits, the "pid" words' surroundings, Nigeria
    p.extend(["n", "1663", "pid", "topi", "drift", "nigeria"]);
    // the hate phrases' words, and a word that starts as their group does
    p.extend(HATE_VERBS.iter().chain(HATE_BETWEEN).chain(HATE_GROUPS));
    p.push("jewel");
    p
}

/// the digits and signs that stand for a letter (names.mjs FROM and TO, the other way round)
fn swap(ch: char) -> &'static [char] {
    match ch.to_ascii_lowercase() {
        'o' => &['0'],
        'i' => &['1', '!', '|', 'l'],
        'e' => &['3'],
        'a' => &['4', '@'],
        's' => &['5', '$'],
        't' => &['7', '+'],
        'g' => &['6', '9', 'q'],
        'b' => &['8'],
        _ => &[],
    }
}

/// names of names.test.mjs's generator (web/test/names.test.mjs, its 20,000 for names.h): the pieces with digits and
/// signs for letters, capitals, doubled letters, separators, a number at the end; then plain ASCII noise
fn ascii_names(r: &mut Rnd, pieces: &[&str], names: &mut Vec<String>) {
    for _ in 0..20_000 {
        let mut n = String::new();
        for _ in 0..1 + r.next(3) {
            for ch in r.pick(pieces).chars() {
                match r.next(10) {
                    0 if !swap(ch).is_empty() => n.push(*r.pick(swap(ch))),
                    1 => n.push(ch.to_ascii_uppercase()),
                    2 => n.extend([ch, ch]),
                    _ => n.push(ch),
                }
                if r.next(12) == 0 {
                    n.push(*r.pick(&[' ', '_', '-', '.', '2']));
                }
            }
            if r.next(3) == 0 {
                n.push_str(r.pick(&["", " ", "_", "42"]));
            }
            if r.next(4) == 0 {
                push_number(r, &mut n, None);
            }
        }
        n.truncate(24);
        names.push(n);
    }
    for _ in 0..5_000 {
        names.push((0..r.next(25)).map(|_| char::from(32 + r.next(95) as u8)).collect());
    }
}

/// a number of 1 to 4 digits, ASCII or (with alts) now and then styled ones
fn push_number(r: &mut Rnd, n: &mut String, alts: Option<&HashMap<char, Vec<char>>>) {
    for _ in 0..1 + r.next(4) {
        let d = char::from(b'0' + r.next(10) as u8);
        match alts.and_then(|a| a.get(&d)) {
            Some(styled) if r.next(3) == 0 => n.push(*r.pick(styled)),
            _ => n.push(d),
        }
    }
}

/// The pieces again, through other scripts and styles: letters as their lookalikes, styled or accented, marks after
/// them, separators and format characters between them, emoji and other characters, runs, capitals, numbers.
fn unicode_names(r: &mut Rnd, pieces: &[&str], names: &mut Vec<String>) {
    let (alts, marks, separators, others) = (alternatives(), marks(), separators(), others());
    let alt = |r: &mut Rnd, ch: char| alts.get(&ch).map(|a| *r.pick(a));
    for _ in 0..30_000 {
        let mut n = String::new();
        for _ in 0..1 + r.next(3) {
            for ch in r.pick(pieces).chars() {
                let ch = if r.next(5) == 0 { ch.to_ascii_uppercase() } else { ch };
                match r.next(10) {
                    0..4 => n.push(alt(r, ch).unwrap_or(ch)),
                    4 if !swap(ch).is_empty() => {
                        let sign = *r.pick(swap(ch));
                        n.push(alt(r, sign).filter(|_| r.next(2) == 0).unwrap_or(sign));
                    }
                    5 => n.extend([ch, alt(r, ch).unwrap_or(ch)]),
                    _ => n.push(ch),
                }
                match r.next(25) {
                    0 | 1 => n.push(*r.pick(&marks)),
                    2 => n.push(*r.pick(&separators)),
                    3 => n.push(*r.pick(&others)),
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
            match r.next(4) {
                0 => n.push(*r.pick(&separators)),
                1 => push_number(r, &mut n, Some(&alts)),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        if r.next(10) == 0 {
            n.insert(0, *r.pick(&others));
        }
        names.push(n);
    }
    // plain noise of all those
    let all: Vec<char> = alts.values().flatten().chain(&marks).chain(&separators).chain(&others).copied().collect();
    for _ in 0..3_000 {
        names.push((0..r.next(30)).map(|_| *r.pick(&all)).collect());
    }
}

/// Names longer than the 255 letters names.mjs reads, a word of the lists somewhere in them.
fn long_names(r: &mut Rnd, pieces: &[&str], names: &mut Vec<String>) {
    for _ in 0..2_000 {
        let mut n: String = (0..240 + r.next(40)).map(|_| *r.pick(&['x', 'y', 'X', ' ', '_', '4'])).collect();
        let at = r.next(n.len() + 1);
        n.insert_str(at, r.pick(pieces));
        names.push(n);
    }
}

/// Every code point of the planes in use (and every 97th of the rest) in a few places of a name, so that NFKD, the
/// marks and the lookalikes are the same for all of them: one that is gone, one that is no letter, a small letter
/// and a capital each answer otherwise for "Dani?99GS", "x?Fag" and "f?g"; one this port reads with letters or
/// digits in also stands for each letter of the lists' words.
fn sweep(names: &mut Vec<String>) {
    let words: &[&str] = &[
        "f?g",
        "i?ne",
        "?oon",
        "?yke",
        "ibn?",
        "?ag",
        "fa?",
        "c?ink",
        "k?ke",
        "?igaboo",
        "?ike",
        "porch?onkey",
        "chi?k",
        "g?ok",
        "s?ic",
        "ni?q",
        "?etard",
        "?pic",
        "?ranny",
        "j?nglebunny",
        "?etback",
        "d?ke",
    ];
    for cp in 0x80..=0x10ffff_u32 {
        let in_use = cp <= 0x3_ffff || (0xe_0000..=0xe_ffff).contains(&cp);
        let Some(ch) = char::from_u32(cp).filter(|_| in_use || cp % 97 == 0) else { continue };
        let c = ch.to_string();
        for t in ["Dani?99GS", "x?Fag", "f?g"] {
            names.push(t.replace('?', &c));
        }
        if read(&c).iter().any(|&x| letter(x).is_some() || x.is_ascii_digit()) {
            names.extend(words.iter().map(|t| t.replace('?', &c)));
        }
    }
}

fn corpus() -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names: Vec<String> =
        ANYWHERE.iter().chain(WHOLE).chain(BLOCKED).chain(UNICODE).chain(ALLOWED).chain(NEAR).map(|n| n.to_string()).collect();
    names.extend(["xfagx", "x_fag_x", "xFagX"].map(String::from));
    let (mut r, pieces) = (Rnd(7), pieces());
    ascii_names(&mut r, &pieces, &mut names);
    unicode_names(&mut r, &pieces, &mut names);
    long_names(&mut r, &pieces, &mut names);
    sweep(&mut names);
    names
}

/// the node script: blockedName of each name of the corpus, names.mjs's lists, and its lookalikes (not exported:
/// read from its source)
const SCRIPT: &str = r#"
import fs from 'node:fs';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
const [names, corpus] = process.argv.slice(2);
const { SLURS, EDGE_OK, WHOLE_OK, PID_STEMS, HATE, blockedName } = await import(pathToFileURL(names).href);
let blocked = '';
for (const n of JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(corpus, 'utf8'))) blocked += blockedName(n) ? '1' : '0';
const m = /const LOOKALIKE = (\{[\s\S]*?\});/.exec(fs.readFileSync(names, 'utf8'));
const lookalike = m && Object.entries(Function(`return (${m[1]})`)()).map(([k, v]) => [k.codePointAt(0), v.codePointAt(0)]);
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ blocked, slurs: SLURS, edgeOk: EDGE_OK, wholeOk: WHOLE_OK, stems: PID_STEMS, hate: HATE, lookalike }));
"#;

/// a folder of its own under the system's temp, gone with it
struct TempDir(PathBuf);

impl Drop for TempDir {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
    }
}

fn strings(v: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<&str> {
    v.as_array().expect("an array").iter().map(|s| s.as_str().expect("a string")).collect()
}

#[test]
fn answers_as_names_mjs() {
    let names_mjs = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../../src/app/names.mjs");
    assert!(names_mjs.exists(), "no {}", names_mjs.display());
    let nanos = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default().as_nanos();
    let dir = TempDir(std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("nfsu2-names-{}-{nanos}", std::process::id())));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir.0).expect("a temp folder");
    let names = corpus();
    let (script, input) = (dir.0.join("check.mjs"), dir.0.join("names.json"));
    std::fs::write(&script, SCRIPT).expect("the script");
    std::fs::write(&input, serde_json::to_string(&names).expect("JSON")).expect("the corpus");
    let out = match Command::new("node").arg(&script).arg(&names_mjs).arg(&input).output() {
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
            eprintln!("answers_as_names_mjs skipped: no node ({e})");
            return;
        }
        r => r.expect("node runs"),
    };
    assert!(out.status.success(), "node failed: {}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr));
    let js: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&out.stdout).expect("node's JSON");

    assert_eq!(strings(&js["slurs"]["anywhere"]), ANYWHERE, "the anywhere list");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["slurs"]["whole"]), WHOLE, "the whole list");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["slurs"]["edge"]), EDGE, "the edge list");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["edgeOk"]["start"]), EDGE_OK_START, "the edge list's words a part may start with");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["edgeOk"]["end"]), EDGE_OK_END, "the edge list's words a part may end with");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["wholeOk"]), WHOLE_OK, "the names a part may be that read as a word of the whole list");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["stems"]), PID_STEMS, "the English words' starts before a pid word");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["hate"]["verbs"]), HATE_VERBS, "the hate phrases' verbs");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["hate"]["between"]), HATE_BETWEEN, "the words between in a hate phrase");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["hate"]["groups"]), HATE_GROUPS, "the hate phrases' groups");

    let pairs = js["lookalike"].as_array().expect("names.mjs's LOOKALIKE table, read from its source");
    let char_of = |v: &serde_json::Value| v.as_u64().and_then(|c| char::from_u32(c as u32)).expect("a code point");
    for pair in pairs {
        let (k, v) = (char_of(&pair[0]), char_of(&pair[1]));
        assert_eq!(lookalike(k), v, "the lookalike of U+{:04X}", k as u32);
    }
    let ours = (0..=0x10ffff).filter_map(char::from_u32).filter(|&c| lookalike(c) != c).count();
    assert_eq!(ours, pairs.len(), "lookalikes names.mjs does not have");

    let answers = js["blocked"].as_str().expect("the answers").as_bytes();
    assert_eq!(answers.len(), names.len());
    let (mut blocked, mut unicode, mut diff) = (0, 0, Vec::new());
    for (name, &a) in names.iter().zip(answers) {
        let ours = blocked_name(name);
        blocked += usize::from(ours);
        unicode += usize::from(!name.is_ascii());
        if ours != (a == b'1') {
            let cps: Vec<String> = name.chars().map(|c| format!("{:x}", c as u32)).collect();
            diff.push(format!("{name:?} [{}]: names.mjs {}, here {ours}", cps.join(" "), a == b'1'));
        }
    }
    eprintln!("{} names ({unicode} past ASCII), {blocked} blocked, {} answered otherwise", names.len(), diff.len());
    assert!(diff.is_empty(), "names the two read differently:\n{}", diff[..diff.len().min(40)].join("\n"));
    assert!(blocked > 10_000 && blocked < names.len() - 10_000, "both answers among the names ({blocked} blocked)");
}

/// Plates for [`blocked_plate`]: every plate of up to 3 capitals and digits, then plates of the plate lists' pieces (and
/// the name lists' short words, numbers, near misses) with digits for letters, cut to 8, and plain capitals and digits
/// up to 8; a few that are no plate (small letters, a space, longer than 8: read as names)
fn plates() -> Vec<String> {
    const AZ09: &[u8] = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789";
    let mut plates: Vec<String> = vec![String::new()];
    for n in 1..=3u32 {
        for k in 0..AZ09.len().pow(n) {
            plates.push((0..n).map(|d| char::from(AZ09[k / AZ09.len().pow(d) % AZ09.len()])).collect());
        }
    }
    let mut pieces: Vec<String> = PLATE_EDGE
        .iter()
        .chain(PLATE_END_OK)
        .chain(PLATE_RESTS)
        .chain(PLATE_ANYWHERE)
        .chain(PLATE_ANYWHERE_OK)
        .chain(PLATE_ALONE)
        .chain(PLATE_MARKS)
        .chain(PLATE_NUMBERS)
        .chain(WHOLE)
        .chain(EDGE)
        .map(|w| w.to_ascii_uppercase())
        .collect();
    pieces.extend(
        [
            "big", "lil", "x", "s", "kkkk", "night", "mustafa", "nigga", "1488", "88", "14", "6", "9", "0", "1", "3", "4", "8", "42",
            "123", "1995",
        ]
        .map(|w| w.to_ascii_uppercase()),
    );
    let mut r = Rnd(11);
    for _ in 0..30_000 {
        let mut n = String::new();
        for _ in 0..1 + r.next(3) {
            for ch in r.pick(&pieces).clone().chars() {
                // a digit for a letter now and then (only those of a plate: no signs, no small l)
                let digits: Vec<char> = swap(ch).iter().copied().filter(char::is_ascii_digit).collect();
                n.push(if r.next(8) == 0 && !digits.is_empty() { *r.pick(&digits) } else { ch });
            }
        }
        plates.push(n.chars().take(8).collect());
    }
    for _ in 0..10_000 {
        plates.push((0..r.next(9)).map(|_| char::from(*r.pick(AZ09))).collect());
    }
    plates.extend(["bigfag", "BIG FAG", "BIGFAGBIGFAG", "Fag", "KKK_88"].map(String::from));
    plates
}

/// the node script: blockedPlate of each plate, and names.mjs's PLATE lists
const PLATE_SCRIPT: &str = r#"
import fs from 'node:fs';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
const [names, corpus] = process.argv.slice(2);
const { PLATE, blockedPlate } = await import(pathToFileURL(names).href);
let blocked = '';
for (const n of JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(corpus, 'utf8'))) blocked += blockedPlate(n) ? '1' : '0';
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ blocked, plate: PLATE }));
"#;

#[test]
fn plates_answer_as_names_mjs() {
    let names_mjs = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../../src/app/names.mjs");
    assert!(names_mjs.exists(), "no {}", names_mjs.display());
    let nanos = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default().as_nanos();
    let dir = TempDir(std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("nfsu2-plates-{}-{nanos}", std::process::id())));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir.0).expect("a temp folder");
    let plates = plates();
    let (script, input) = (dir.0.join("check.mjs"), dir.0.join("plates.json"));
    std::fs::write(&script, PLATE_SCRIPT).expect("the script");
    std::fs::write(&input, serde_json::to_string(&plates).expect("JSON")).expect("the corpus");
    let out = match Command::new("node").arg(&script).arg(&names_mjs).arg(&input).output() {
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
            eprintln!("plates_answer_as_names_mjs skipped: no node ({e})");
            return;
        }
        r => r.expect("node runs"),
    };
    assert!(out.status.success(), "node failed: {}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr));
    let js: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&out.stdout).expect("node's JSON");

    assert_eq!(strings(&js["plate"]["edge"]), PLATE_EDGE, "the plate's edge words");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["plate"]["endOk"]), PLATE_END_OK, "the words a plate may end with");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["plate"]["rests"]), PLATE_RESTS, "the words after an edge word that starts a plate");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["plate"]["anywhere"]), PLATE_ANYWHERE, "the plate's anywhere words");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["plate"]["anywhereOk"]), PLATE_ANYWHERE_OK, "the words that hold a plate's anywhere word");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["plate"]["alone"]), PLATE_ALONE, "the plate's parts on their own");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["plate"]["marks"]), PLATE_MARKS, "the codes' letters");
    assert_eq!(strings(&js["plate"]["numbers"]), PLATE_NUMBERS, "the codes' numbers");

    let answers = js["blocked"].as_str().expect("the answers").as_bytes();
    assert_eq!(answers.len(), plates.len());
    let diff: Vec<String> = plates
        .iter()
        .zip(answers)
        .filter(|(p, a)| blocked_plate(p) != (**a == b'1'))
        .map(|(p, a)| format!("{p:?}: names.mjs {}", *a == b'1'))
        .collect();
    let blocked = answers.iter().filter(|&&a| a == b'1').count();
    eprintln!("{} plates, {blocked} blocked, {} answered otherwise", plates.len(), diff.len());
    assert!(diff.is_empty(), "plates the two read differently:\n{}", diff[..diff.len().min(40)].join("\n"));
    assert!(blocked > 1_000 && blocked < plates.len() - 1_000, "both answers among the plates ({blocked} blocked)");
}

//! A player's name that reads as a slur: the rules of web/src/app/names.mjs (the page's), ported.  The server refuses
//! one for the Online mode (an account or persona; the Online results drop the ones kept under one) and the switch's
//! peer list shows "player" for one (nfsu2-lan's `clean_name`); the page's settings refuse one as "Your name".
//! runtime/names.h is the same lists and the same matching for the game (the names over the cars in free roam).
//!
//! A name is read as letters only: a to z in lower case, the digits and signs that stand for letters as those
//! (0 o, 1 ! | l i, 3 e, 4 @ a, 5 $ s, 7 + t, 6 9 g, 8 b), anything else left out: "N1-g g@" reads "nigga".  Digits
//! that make a number are left out too: three or more in a row, or two that end a part ("Hakan1995", "Dani99",
//! "Dani99GS" are no slur; "ni99a" is one); but not right after a part that is a lone n (or ni) so far, with a letter
//! after them ("N1663r", "BigN199a"; "N1995" stays a letter and a year).
//! Before that (here only: the game's names are ASCII) accents, fullwidth and styled letters go (NFKD) and the
//! Cyrillic and Greek letters that look like Latin ones read as those.  A word matches where each of its letters
//! comes at least as many times in a row as in the word ("niiiggga"; one g is not the two of "nigger").
//!  - anywhere: a word long enough that no other word has it inside it; "niger" not where "nigeri" is (Nigeria)
//!  - whole: a short one that other words have inside them ("Mustafa GS", "raccoon", "spicy", "Pakize"), only as a
//!    part of the name on its own, and plural: the parts are split where a character is no letter and where a
//!    capital follows a small letter, digits and signs read as letters between them or not ("f4g_42", "XxCoonXx",
//!    "Big1Fag"); the name's letters together count as one too ("F A G").  "Dyke" after "Van" is the surname; a name
//!    of [`WHOLE_OK`] is none ("Nazli").
//!  - edge: a word that starts or ends a part (or the name's letters together), plural too ("nigabro", "biggniga"),
//!    but not where a part starts or ends with a word of [`EDGE_OK_START`] or [`EDGE_OK_END`] there ("Nigar",
//!    "Zuniga", "Hooniga")
//!
//! The other offensive names go the same way (picked from the live server's names, 2026-10-26, 11-02, 11-05 and
//! 11-07): Nazi ones and their nicknames, hate aimed at a group, terror, sexual violence; and a name with 1488 in it
//! (the neo-Nazi code), spaces, _ or - between its digits or not ("14_88"); and hate aimed at a group as a phrase
//! ([`HATE_VERBS`]: a verb, a word between or none, the group).  A swear
//! word is no such name.  A "pid" word (pidor, pidar, pidr) right after the start of an English word
//! that ends in "pid" (rapid, cupid, stupid), or after a vowel when it runs into the next part ("TopiDrift"), is no
//! slur ("RapidRacer"; "dapidor", "YaPidor" are).
//!
//! The Online lobby's chat is read with the same lists, a word at a time ([`chat_slur`]); here only.

use unicode_general_category::{GeneralCategory, get_general_category};
