const CODE: &[char] = &['1', '4', '8', '8'];

/// The digits and signs that stand for letters, and those letters, by position.
const FROM: &[u8; 15] = b"01!|l34@5$7+698";
const TO: &[u8; 15] = b"oiiiieaassttggb";

/// names.mjs `letter(ch)` for every ASCII character, worked out once: the letter it reads as, 0 for none.  No other
/// character reads as a letter.
const LETTERS: [u8; 128] = {
    let mut table = [0; 128];
    let mut ch = 0;
    while ch < 128 {
        let low = (ch as u8).to_ascii_lowercase();
        let mut letter = if low.is_ascii_lowercase() { low } else { 0 };
        let mut i = 0;
        while i < FROM.len() {
            if FROM[i] == low {
                letter = TO[i];
            }
            i += 1;
        }
        table[ch] = letter;
        ch += 1;
    }
    table
};

/// ch as a letter (above), else None
fn letter(ch: char) -> Option<u8> {
    let c = *LETTERS.get(ch as usize)?;
    (c != 0).then_some(c)
}

/// A word of the lists as the letters a name is read as (`word` in names.mjs: "l" reads "i", so "junglebunny" is
/// looked for as "jungiebunny"), worked out at compile time.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Word {
    letters: [u8; 16],
    len: usize,
}

impl Word {
    const fn new(w: &str) -> Word {
        let (bytes, mut letters, mut len, mut i) = (w.as_bytes(), [0; 16], 0, 0);
        while i < bytes.len() {
            // the lists are ASCII; a byte of a longer UTF-8 character reads as no letter, as that character would
            let c = if bytes[i] < 128 { LETTERS[bytes[i] as usize] } else { 0 };
            if c != 0 {
                letters[len] = c;
                len += 1;
            }
            i += 1;
        }
        Word { letters, len }
    }

    fn letters(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.letters[..self.len]
    }
}

const fn words<const N: usize>(list: &[&str]) -> [Word; N] {
    let mut out = [Word { letters: [0; 16], len: 0 }; N];
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < N {
        out[i] = Word::new(list[i]);
        i += 1;
    }
    out
}

const ANYWHERE_WORDS: [Word; ANYWHERE.len()] = words(ANYWHERE);
const WHOLE_WORDS: [Word; WHOLE.len()] = words(WHOLE);
const EDGE_WORDS: [Word; EDGE.len()] = words(EDGE);
const OK_START_WORDS: [Word; EDGE_OK_START.len()] = words(EDGE_OK_START);
const OK_END_WORDS: [Word; EDGE_OK_END.len()] = words(EDGE_OK_END);
const OK_WHOLE_WORDS: [Word; WHOLE_OK.len()] = words(WHOLE_OK);
const STEM_WORDS: [Word; PID_STEMS.len()] = words(PID_STEMS);

const VERB_WORDS: [Word; HATE_VERBS.len()] = words(HATE_VERBS);
const BETWEEN_WORDS: [Word; HATE_BETWEEN.len()] = words(HATE_BETWEEN);

/// The anywhere words by their first letter (a to z), as bits of their index (the first 128 words in [0], the rest in
/// [1]): a word is at s[i] only when s[i] is its first letter, so only those are looked for there (the lobby's chat
/// reads every line).
const ANYWHERE_FIRST: [[u128; 2]; 26] = {
    assert!(ANYWHERE.len() <= 256);
    let mut t = [[0; 2]; 26];
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < ANYWHERE_WORDS.len() {
        t[(ANYWHERE_WORDS[i].letters[0] - b'a') as usize][i / 128] |= 1 << (i % 128);
        i += 1;
    }
    t
};

/// The Cyrillic and Greek letters that look like Latin ones read as those, and a few Latin ones NFKD keeps (dotless
/// i, L, O and D with a stroke, eng, script g), the inverted exclamation mark and the euro sign.
fn lookalike(ch: char) -> char {
    match ch {
        // Cyrillic А, Greek Α
        '\u{0410}' | '\u{0391}' => 'A',
        // Cyrillic В, Greek Β
        '\u{0412}' | '\u{0392}' => 'B',
        // Cyrillic С, Greek lunate sigma Ϲ
        '\u{0421}' | '\u{03F9}' => 'C',
        // Cyrillic Komi Ԁ, Latin Đ
        '\u{0500}' | '\u{0110}' => 'D',
        // Cyrillic Е, Greek Ε
        '\u{0415}' | '\u{0395}' => 'E',
        // Cyrillic Н, Greek Η
        '\u{041D}' | '\u{0397}' => 'H',
        // Cyrillic І, Greek Ι
        '\u{0406}' | '\u{0399}' => 'I',
        // Cyrillic Ј
        '\u{0408}' => 'J',
        // Cyrillic К, Greek Κ
        '\u{041A}' | '\u{039A}' => 'K',
        // Latin Ł
        '\u{0141}' => 'L',
        // Cyrillic М, Greek Μ
        '\u{041C}' | '\u{039C}' => 'M',
        // Greek Ν
        '\u{039D}' => 'N',
        // Cyrillic О, Greek Ο, Latin Ø
        '\u{041E}' | '\u{039F}' | '\u{00D8}' => 'O',
        // Cyrillic Р, Greek Ρ
        '\u{0420}' | '\u{03A1}' => 'P',
        // Cyrillic Ѕ
        '\u{0405}' => 'S',
        // Cyrillic Т, Greek Τ
        '\u{0422}' | '\u{03A4}' => 'T',
        // Cyrillic Х, Greek Χ
        '\u{0425}' | '\u{03A7}' => 'X',
        // Cyrillic У, Greek Υ
        '\u{0423}' | '\u{03A5}' => 'Y',
        // Greek Ζ
        '\u{0396}' => 'Z',
        // Cyrillic а, Greek α
        '\u{0430}' | '\u{03B1}' => 'a',
        // Cyrillic в, Ь, ь, Greek β
        '\u{0432}' | '\u{042C}' | '\u{044C}' | '\u{03B2}' => 'b',
        // Cyrillic с, Greek lunate sigma ϲ
        '\u{0441}' | '\u{03F2}' => 'c',
        // Cyrillic Komi ԁ, Latin đ
        '\u{0501}' | '\u{0111}' => 'd',
        // Cyrillic е, Greek ε, the euro sign
        '\u{0435}' | '\u{03B5}' | '\u{20AC}' => 'e',
        // Latin script ɡ
        '\u{0261}' => 'g',
        // Cyrillic н
        '\u{043D}' => 'h',
        // Cyrillic і, Greek ι, Latin dotless ı, the inverted exclamation mark
        '\u{0456}' | '\u{03B9}' | '\u{0131}' | '\u{00A1}' => 'i',
        // Cyrillic ј
        '\u{0458}' => 'j',
        // Cyrillic к, Greek κ
        '\u{043A}' | '\u{03BA}' => 'k',
        // Latin ł
        '\u{0142}' => 'l',
        // Cyrillic м
        '\u{043C}' => 'm',
        // Cyrillic п, Greek η, Latin ŋ
        '\u{043F}' | '\u{03B7}' | '\u{014B}' => 'n',
        // Cyrillic о, Greek ο, Latin ø
        '\u{043E}' | '\u{03BF}' | '\u{00F8}' => 'o',
        // Cyrillic р, Greek ρ
        '\u{0440}' | '\u{03C1}' => 'p',
        // Cyrillic Kurdish ԛ
        '\u{051B}' => 'q',
        // Cyrillic ѕ
        '\u{0455}' => 's',
        // Cyrillic т, Greek τ
        '\u{0442}' | '\u{03C4}' => 't',
        // Greek υ
        '\u{03C5}' => 'u',
        // Greek ν
        '\u{03BD}' => 'v',
        // Cyrillic х, Greek χ
        '\u{0445}' | '\u{03C7}' => 'x',
        // Cyrillic у
        '\u{0443}' => 'y',
        _ => ch,
    }
}

/// `\p{M}`: a mark (Mn, Mc, Me)
fn is_mark(ch: char) -> bool {
    matches!(get_general_category(ch), GeneralCategory::NonspacingMark | GeneralCategory::SpacingMark | GeneralCategory::EnclosingMark)
}

/// A character the mark table's Unicode has not assigned yet.  unicode-normalization's tables can be newer than
/// that (and than Node's ICU, which is the same Unicode, 16.0 as this is written): ICU leaves a character it does
/// not know as it is, with no decomposition and combining class 0, so it also ends a run of marks to reorder.
fn unknown(ch: char) -> bool {
    !ch.is_ascii() && get_general_category(ch) == GeneralCategory::Unassigned
}

/// The name's characters as names.mjs reads them, `[...name.normalize('NFKD').replace(/\p{M}/gu, '')]` with the
/// lookalikes as their Latin letters.
fn read(name: &str) -> Vec<char> {
    // NFKD, the marks and the lookalikes change no ASCII character
    if name.is_ascii() {
        return name.bytes().map(char::from).collect();
    }
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(name.len());
    for piece in name.split_inclusive(unknown) {
        let (known, new) = match piece.chars().next_back() {
            Some(ch) if unknown(ch) => (&piece[..piece.len() - ch.len_utf8()], Some(ch)),
            _ => (piece, None),
        };
        out.extend(known.nfkd().filter(|&ch| !is_mark(ch)).map(lookalike));
        out.extend(new);
    }
    out
}

/// The run of n digits at str[i] is a number, not letters: three or more, or two with no letter after them or a
/// capital after a small letter before them.
fn number(str: &[char], i: usize, n: usize) -> bool {
    if n != 2 {
        return n > 2;
    }
    let before = i.checked_sub(1).and_then(|b| str.get(b));
    match str.get(i + 2) {
        None => true,
        Some(&after) => letter(after).is_none() || (after.is_ascii_uppercase() && before.is_some_and(|b| b.is_ascii_lowercase())),
    }
}

/// The end of word w (its letters) at s[i], each letter at least as many times in a row as in w (the name's run of
/// it is taken whole); None if it is not there.
fn at(s: &[u8], mut i: usize, w: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    let run = |from: &[u8], c: u8| from.iter().take_while(|&&x| x == c).count();
    let mut j = 0;
    while let Some(&c) = w.get(j) {
        let m = run(&w[j..], c);
        let k = run(s.get(i..).unwrap_or_default(), c);
        if k < m {
            return None;
        }
        i += k;
        j += m;
    }
    Some(i)
}

/// t is all one of words, or its plural
fn whole(t: &[u8], words: &[Word]) -> bool {
    words.iter().any(|w| at(t, 0, w.letters()).is_some_and(|e| t[e..].iter().all(|&c| c == b's')))
}

/// t is a word of [`WHOLE`] (or its plural), and no name of [`WHOLE_OK`]
fn whole_word(t: &[u8]) -> bool {
    whole(t, &WHOLE_WORDS) && !OK_WHOLE_WORDS.iter().any(|x| x.letters() == t)
}

/// t starts with word w (its letters)
fn starts_with(t: &[u8], w: &Word) -> bool {
    at(t, 0, w.letters()).is_some()
}

/// t ends with word w (its letters), or its plural
fn ends_with(t: &[u8], w: &Word) -> bool {
    (0..t.len()).any(|i| at(t, i, w.letters()).is_some_and(|e| t[e..].iter().all(|&c| c == b's')))
}

/// t starts or ends with a word of the edge list, and not with a word of [`EDGE_OK_START`] or [`EDGE_OK_END`] there
fn edge(t: &[u8]) -> bool {
    EDGE_WORDS.iter().any(|w| {
        (starts_with(t, w) && !OK_START_WORDS.iter().any(|x| starts_with(t, x)))
            || (ends_with(t, w) && !OK_END_WORDS.iter().any(|x| ends_with(t, x)))
    })
}

/// The JS keeps at most 255 letters of a name, and of a part of it: the rest of a longer one is not read.
const CAP: usize = 255;

/// Letters read so far, at most [`CAP`] of them, and whether a part of the name starts at each.
struct Letters {
    buf: [u8; CAP],
    starts: [bool; CAP],
    len: usize,
}

impl Letters {
    fn new() -> Letters {
        Letters { buf: [0; CAP], starts: [false; CAP], len: 0 }
    }

    /// c, the first letter of a part or not
    fn push(&mut self, c: u8, start: bool) {
        if self.len < CAP {
            self.buf[self.len] = c;
            self.starts[self.len] = start;
            self.len += 1;
        }
    }

    fn get(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.buf[..self.len]
    }

    fn starts(&self) -> &[bool] {
        &self.starts[..self.len]
    }
}

/// A "pid" word of the anywhere list (pidor, pidar, pidr) at s[i] is the end of an English word: not at the start of
/// a part (starts[j]: a part starts at s[j]), and right after the start of one of those words ("RapidRacer",
/// "Stupidrift"), or after a vowel and into the next part ("TopiDrift"); "vladpidr", "dapidor", "YaPidor" are slurs.
fn english_pid(s: &[u8], i: usize, w: &[u8], starts: &[bool]) -> bool {
    if !w.starts_with(b"pid") || starts[i] {
        return false;
    }
    if STEM_WORDS.iter().any(|st| s[..i].ends_with(st.letters())) {
        return true;
    }
    let end = at(s, i, w).unwrap_or(i + 1);
    i > 0 && b"aeiouy".contains(&s[i - 1]) && starts[i + 1..end].contains(&true)
}

/// "nigeri", where "niger" is no slur (Nigeria)
const NIGERIA: &[u8] = b"nigeri";

/// a hate phrase (a verb, a word between or none, a group: "gasthejews") at s[i]
fn hate(s: &[u8], i: usize) -> bool {
    VERB_WORDS.iter().filter(|v| at(s, i, v.letters()).is_some()).any(|v| {
        // no word between, or one of them
        let between = std::iter::once(&[][..]).chain(BETWEEN_WORDS.iter().map(Word::letters));
        let mut phrases = between.flat_map(|b| GROUP_WORDS.iter().map(move |g| [v.letters(), b, g.letters()].concat()));
        phrases.any(|w| at(s, i, &w).is_some())
    })
}

/// a word of the anywhere list or a hate phrase is in s (letters; starts[j]: a part starts at s[j]), and no English
/// "pid" word or Nigeria
fn anywhere(s: &[u8], starts: &[bool]) -> bool {
    (0..s.len()).any(|i| {
        if hate(s, i) {
            return true;
        }
        ANYWHERE_FIRST[(s[i] - b'a') as usize].iter().enumerate().any(|(half, &bits)| {
            let mut m = bits;
            while m != 0 {
                let w = ANYWHERE_WORDS[half * 128 + m.trailing_zeros() as usize].letters();
                let nigeria = w == b"niger" && s[i..].starts_with(NIGERIA);
                if at(s, i, w).is_some() && !english_pid(s, i, w, starts) && !nigeria {
                    return true;
                }
                m &= m - 1;
            }
            false
        })
    })
}

/// A name read: its letters, and whether each of its parts is one letter ("F A G", "f.a.g")
struct Scan {
    s: Letters,
    single: bool,
}

/// The name's letters, None when 1488 or a part of its own that is a word of the whole list (or starts or ends with a
/// word of the edge list) is in it
fn scan(name: &str) -> Option<Scan> {
    let str = read(name);
    // spaces, _ or - between its digits or not ("14_88"; not "1:48.8", a lap time)
    let code: Vec<char> = str.iter().copied().filter(|c| !matches!(c, ' ' | '_' | '-')).collect();
    if code.windows(CODE.len()).any(|w| w == CODE) {
        return None;
    }
    // s: all the name's letters; t: the part being read
    let (mut s, mut t) = (Letters::new(), Letters::new());
    // the part before was "van"; the last letter (not a digit or sign read as one) was a small one
    let (mut after_van, mut low, mut single) = (false, false, true);
    let mut i = 0;
    while i <= str.len() {
        let ch = str.get(i).copied();
        let r = str[i..].iter().take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).count();
        // after a lone n (or ni) and before a letter, digits are letters: "N1663r"
        let lone_n = matches!(t.get(), b"n" | b"ni") && str.get(i + r).is_some_and(|&a| letter(a).is_some());
        let num = r > 0 && number(&str, i, r) && !lone_n;
        let c = if num { None } else { ch.and_then(letter) };
        if (c.is_none() || (low && ch.is_some_and(|ch| ch.is_ascii_uppercase()))) && t.len > 0 {
            if (whole_word(t.get()) && !(after_van && whole(t.get(), &DYKE))) || edge(t.get()) {
                return None;
            }
            after_van = t.get() == b"van";
            single &= t.len == 1;
            t.len = 0;
        }
        match (c, ch) {
            (Some(c), Some(ch)) => {
                s.push(c, t.len == 0);
                t.push(c, false);
                if ch.is_ascii_alphabetic() {
                    low = ch.is_ascii_lowercase();
                }
            }
            _ => low = false,
        }
        i += if num { r } else { 1 };
    }
    Some(Scan { s, single })
}

/// names.mjs `blockedName(name)`: the name reads as a slur (above)
pub fn blocked_name(name: &str) -> bool {
    scan(name).is_none_or(|n| anywhere(n.s.get(), n.s.starts()) || whole_word(n.s.get()) || edge(n.s.get()))
}

/// word x holds s[i..e): it is there from s[j], j <= i, to e or past it
fn held(s: &[u8], i: usize, e: usize, x: &[u8]) -> bool {
    (i.saturating_sub(x.len())..=i).any(|j| at(s, j, x).is_some_and(|f| f >= e))
}

/// names.mjs `blockedPlate(plate)`: a license plate (capitals and digits, at most 8; anything else is read as a name
/// only) reads as a slur, as a name or as a plate.  A plate has no small letters to split its parts by ("BIGFAG" is
/// "BigFag") and its words run into each other, so:
///  - a word of [`PLATE_EDGE`] that ends the plate's letters, plural too ("BIGFAG", "KILLFAGS"), unless they end with
///    a word of [`PLATE_END_OK`] ("RACCOON"), or that starts them with a word of [`PLATE_RESTS`] after it, plural or
///    not ("FAGBOY")
///  - a word of [`PLATE_ANYWHERE`] anywhere in its letters, unless a word of [`PLATE_ANYWHERE_OK`] holds it
///  - its letters as a name's, but a lone digit at its end is a number ("MUSTAFA6", "HUZAIFA9")
///  - codes: a part (letters or digits in a row) of [`PLATE_ALONE`], or one of [`PLATE_MARKS`] next to one of
///    [`PLATE_NUMBERS`] ("HH88", "88SS")
pub fn blocked_plate(plate: &str) -> bool {
    if blocked_name(plate) {
        return true;
    }
    let p = plate.as_bytes();
    if p.len() > 8 || !p.iter().all(|b| b.is_ascii_uppercase() || b.is_ascii_digit()) {
        return false;
    }
    let parts: Vec<&[u8]> = p.chunk_by(|a, b| a.is_ascii_digit() == b.is_ascii_digit()).collect();
    let is = |x: &[u8], list: &[&str]| list.iter().any(|w| w.as_bytes() == x);
    for (k, x) in parts.iter().enumerate() {
        let marked = (k > 0 && is(parts[k - 1], PLATE_MARKS)) || parts.get(k + 1).is_some_and(|y| is(y, PLATE_MARKS));
        if is(x, PLATE_ALONE) || (is(x, PLATE_NUMBERS) && marked) {
            return true;
        }
    }
    // its letters as a name's, a lone digit at its end left out
    let q: Vec<char> = match p {
        [.., a, d] if a.is_ascii_uppercase() && d.is_ascii_digit() => &p[..p.len() - 1],
        _ => p,
    }
    .iter()
    .map(|&b| char::from(b))
    .collect();
    let mut s = Vec::with_capacity(q.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < q.len() {
        let r = q[i..].iter().take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).count();
        if r > 0 && number(&q, i, r) {
            i += r;
            continue;
        }
        s.extend(letter(q[i]));
        i += 1;
    }
    let edge = P_EDGE_WORDS.iter().any(|w| {
        (ends_with(&s, w) && !P_END_OK_WORDS.iter().any(|x| ends_with(&s, x)))
            || at(&s, 0, w.letters()).is_some_and(|e| {
                let (rest, bare) = (&s[e..], &s[e + s[e..].iter().take_while(|&&c| c == b's').count()..]);
                P_REST_WORDS.iter().any(|r| whole(rest, std::slice::from_ref(r)) || whole(bare, std::slice::from_ref(r)))
            })
    });
    edge || P_ANY_WORDS
        .iter()
        .any(|w| (0..s.len()).any(|i| at(&s, i, w.letters()).is_some_and(|e| !P_ANY_OK_WORDS.iter().any(|x| held(&s, i, e, x.letters())))))
}

/// The most one-letter words in a row read as a word of the whole list ("f a g s")
const WHOLE_RUN: usize = 8;

/// A chat line's words that read as a slur (the Online lobby's chat, nfsu2-online): the first such span of the
/// line, None for none.  The line is no name: its letters all together would read words across its words ("rapid
/// race" has "pidr" in it, "go ok" is "gook"), so it is read a word (between spaces, without the ! at its end) at a
/// time:
///  - a word as a name: 1488 or a part of the whole list in it, a word of the anywhere list in its letters; its
///    letters together only when each part is one letter ("f.a.g", not "go,ok"); "Dyke" after "van" is the surname
///  - two words in a row: a word of the anywhere list across them ("nig ger", "sieg heil", "nate higgers")
///  - three or four words in a row: a hate phrase from the first one's start ("gas the jews", not "vegas the jewel")
///  - one-letter words in a row: their letters, for the anywhere list ("n i g g a"), and three to eight of them for
///    the whole list ("F A G", "u r a f a g")
pub fn chat_slur(line: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    let mut words: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
    let mut from = None;
    for (i, ch) in line.char_indices().chain([(line.len(), ' ')]) {
        match (ch.is_whitespace(), from) {
            (true, Some(f)) => {
                // the ! at a word's end is punctuation, not an i
                let e = f + line[f..i].trim_end_matches('!').len();
                if e > f {
                    words.push((f, e));
                }
                from = None;
            }
            (false, None) => from = Some(i),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    // each word's letters, and where its parts start
    let mut letters: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::with_capacity(words.len());
    let mut starts: Vec<Vec<bool>> = Vec::with_capacity(words.len());
    for (k, &(a, b)) in words.iter().enumerate() {
        // a word after "van" is read with it, as the name "van ..." ("van Dyke")
        let after_van = k > 0 && letters[k - 1] == b"van";
        let (n, skip) = match scan(&line[a..b]) {
            None if after_van => (scan(&line[words[k - 1].0..b]), 3),
            n => (n, 0),
        };
        let (s, st) = match n {
            Some(n) if !anywhere(n.s.get(), n.s.starts()) && !(n.single && (whole_word(n.s.get()) || edge(n.s.get()))) => {
                (n.s.get()[skip..].to_vec(), n.s.starts()[skip..].to_vec())
            }
            _ => return Some(&line[a..b]),
        };
        if k > 0 && anywhere(&[letters[k - 1].as_slice(), &s].concat(), &[starts[k - 1].as_slice(), &st].concat()) {
            return Some(&line[words[k - 1].0..b]);
        }
        // three or four words in a row, a hate phrase from the first one's start ("gas the jews")
        for j in k.saturating_sub(3)..k.saturating_sub(1) {
            if hate(&[letters[j..].concat(), s.clone()].concat(), 0) {
                return Some(&line[words[j].0..b]);
            }
        }
        letters.push(s);
        starts.push(st);
    }
    // the one-letter words in a row
    let mut k = 0;
    while k < words.len() {
        let n = letters[k..].iter().take_while(|s| s.len() == 1).count();
        if n >= 3 {
            let s: Vec<u8> = letters[k..k + n].iter().map(|s| s[0]).collect();
            let span = |i: usize, j: usize| &line[words[k + i].0..words[k + j - 1].1];
            if anywhere(&s, &vec![true; n]) {
                return Some(span(0, n));
            }
            for i in 0..n {
                for j in i + 3..=(i + WHOLE_RUN).min(n) {
                    if whole_word(&s[i..j]) {
                        return Some(span(i, j));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        k += n.max(1);
    }
    None
}

/// A name's letters as the lists read it (above: the digits and signs that stand for letters as those, numbers and
/// everything else left out): what names that read the same have in common ("B4d_Name", "bad name", "BadName99").
/// The names the operator took away ([`Deny`]) are compared by it.
pub fn letters(name: &str) -> String {
    let str = read(name);
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(str.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < str.len() {
        let r = str[i..].iter().take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).count();
        if r > 0 && number(&str, i, r) {
            i += r;
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(c) = letter(str[i]) {
            out.push(char::from(c));
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    out
}

/// The names the server's operator took away (nfsu2-bans: `rename`), by their [`letters`]: nobody plays under one, or
/// under a name that reads the same.  The switch's hello, the Online lobby and free roam's hub look a name up here;
/// the bans write it (`set`), and each change moves `generation` on (the hub looks at a player's name again then).
#[derive(Default, Debug)]
pub struct Deny {
    set: std::sync::RwLock<std::collections::HashSet<String>>,
    generation: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64,
}

impl Deny {
    /// the names taken away now (as they were typed, or their letters already: the same)
    pub fn set(&self, names: impl IntoIterator<Item = String>) {
        let set = names.into_iter().map(|n| letters(&n)).filter(|l| !l.is_empty()).collect();
        *self.set.write().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = set;
        self.generation.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
    /// whether `name` reads as one of them
    pub fn has(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        let set = self.set.read().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
        !set.is_empty() && {
            let l = letters(name);
            !l.is_empty() && set.contains(&l)
        }
    }
    /// moves on with each `set`
    pub fn generation(&self) -> u64 {
        self.generation.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)
    }
}

// names.mjs: the lists' words, the ways round them, and not the other words
#[test]
fn lists_ways_round_and_other_words() {
    for w in ANYWHERE.iter().chain(WHOLE).chain(EDGE) {
        assert!(blocked_name(w), "{w}");
    }
    for v in HATE_VERBS {
        for b in [""].iter().chain(HATE_BETWEEN) {
            for g in HATE_GROUPS {
                assert!(blocked_name(&format!("{v}{b}{g}")), "{v}{b}{g}");
            }
        }
    }
    for n in BLOCKED.iter().chain(UNICODE) {
        assert!(blocked_name(n), "{n}");
    }
    for n in ALLOWED {
        assert!(!blocked_name(n), "{n}");
    }
    // a word of the whole list only as a part on its own
    assert!(!blocked_name("xfagx") && blocked_name("x_fag_x") && blocked_name("xFagX"));
}

// not in names.test.mjs: the pieces on their own

#[test]
fn letters_as_the_js_reads_them() {
    for (ch, c) in [('a', Some(b'a')), ('Z', Some(b'z')), ('L', Some(b'i')), ('l', Some(b'i')), ('|', Some(b'i'))] {
        assert_eq!(letter(ch), c, "{ch}");
    }
    for (ch, c) in [('0', b'o'), ('1', b'i'), ('!', b'i'), ('3', b'e'), ('4', b'a'), ('@', b'a'), ('5', b's')] {
        assert_eq!(letter(ch), Some(c), "{ch}");
    }
    for (ch, c) in [('$', b's'), ('7', b't'), ('+', b't'), ('6', b'g'), ('9', b'g'), ('8', b'b')] {
        assert_eq!(letter(ch), Some(c), "{ch}");
    }
    for ch in ['2', ' ', '_', '-', '.', '\u{e9}', '\u{430}', '\u{ff41}', '\u{1f600}'] {
        assert_eq!(letter(ch), None, "{ch}");
    }
    assert_eq!(WHOLE_WORDS[0].letters(), b"fag");
    assert_eq!(ANYWHERE_WORDS[14].letters(), b"jungiebunny");
    assert_eq!(ANYWHERE_WORDS[11].letters(), b"chingchong");
}

#[test]
fn read_as_nfkd_without_marks_and_lookalikes() {
    let text = |s: &str| read(s).into_iter().collect::<String>();
    assert_eq!(text("Mustafa GS"), "Mustafa GS");
    assert_eq!(text("\u{f1}i\u{332}"), "ni");
    assert_eq!(text("\u{ff4e}\u{1d41a}\u{24d0}"), "naa");
    assert_eq!(text("\u{39d}\u{430}\u{20ac}"), "Nae");
    // a keycap: the digit stays, the variation selector and the enclosing keycap are marks
    assert_eq!(text("1\u{fe0f}\u{20e3}"), "1");
    // the ligature and the fraction come apart, the emoji and the zero-width joiner stay
    assert_eq!(text("\u{fb00}\u{bd}\u{1f600}\u{200d}"), "ff1\u{2044}2\u{1f600}\u{200d}");
    // a character newer than the mark table's Unicode (16.0) stays as it is, the text around it read as always
    assert_eq!(text("\u{e9}\u{1dfd5}\u{e9}"), "e\u{1dfd5}e");
}

#[test]
fn numbers_and_letters() {
    // three or more digits are a number, and a split (but after a lone n or ni: digits_after_a_lone_n)
    assert!(blocked_name("fag123") && !blocked_name("xni999a") && !blocked_name("xni9999a") && blocked_name("ni999a"));
    // two that end a part, or before a capital after a small letter, are a number; between small letters, letters
    assert!(!blocked_name("Dani99") && !blocked_name("Dani99GS") && blocked_name("ni99a"));
    assert!(!blocked_name("Xni99A") && blocked_name("XNI99A") && blocked_name("Ni99A"));
    // one digit is always read as a letter, or for 2 as none: a split, the name's letters still read together
    assert!(blocked_name("f4g") && blocked_name("f2ag") && blocked_name("fa2g2") && !blocked_name("fa2g2x"));
    // 1488 anywhere, in any run of digits, past the 255 letters too, spaces, _ or - between its digits or not; not
    // other signs between them (a lap time, a price) or other digits
    assert!(blocked_name("x1488x") && blocked_name("2281488") && blocked_name(&("x".repeat(300) + "1488")));
    assert!(blocked_name("14 88") && blocked_name("14_88") && blocked_name("1-4-8-8") && blocked_name("x_14__88_"));
    assert!(!blocked_name("1448") && !blocked_name("1:48.8") && !blocked_name("14.88") && !blocked_name("14x88"));
}

#[test]
fn parts_and_runs() {
    assert!(blocked_name("niiiiggggaaaa") && blocked_name("Niger") && !blocked_name("Nigeria") && !blocked_name("nige"));
    assert!(blocked_name("XxCoonXx") && !blocked_name("xxcoonxx") && blocked_name("xx_coon_xx"));
    assert!(blocked_name("F A G") && blocked_name("f.a.g.s") && !blocked_name("f a g x"));
    assert!(!blocked_name("Van Dyke") && !blocked_name("VanDyke") && blocked_name("Dyke") && blocked_name("X Dyke"));
    assert!(blocked_name("Van Fag") && blocked_name("Vanfag Dyke"));
}

#[test]
fn a_pid_word_after_an_english_start_is_english() {
    assert!(!blocked_name("RapidRacer") && !blocked_name("xStupidorx") && !blocked_name("Insipidar"));
    assert!(blocked_name("vladpidr") && blocked_name("Pidr228") && blocked_name("xpidrx") && blocked_name("rapid_pidr"));
    // after a vowel only into the next part, never at a part's start
    assert!(!blocked_name("TopiDrift") && !blocked_name("topi drift") && blocked_name("dapidor"));
    assert!(blocked_name("YaPidor") && blocked_name("ya_pidor") && blocked_name("LilP1dr"));
}

#[test]
fn edge_words_start_or_end_a_part() {
    assert!(blocked_name("nigabro") && blocked_name("x_nigabro") && blocked_name("bignigas") && blocked_name("Big_Niga"));
    // the letters together count too, and only an edge: not inside a part
    assert!(blocked_name("n.i.g.a.b.r.o") && !blocked_name("xnigabrox") && !blocked_name("Hoonigan"));
    // the words of the ok lists, there and only there
    assert!(!blocked_name("Nigar") && !blocked_name("Zuniga") && !blocked_name("Kniga_x") && !blocked_name("Minigas"));
    assert!(blocked_name("Nigar_niga") && blocked_name("Kniga_bigniga") && blocked_name("xZunigaX_niga"));
}

#[test]
fn digits_after_a_lone_n() {
    // before a letter they are letters
    assert!(blocked_name("N1663r") && blocked_name("BigN199a") && blocked_name("Nl99A") && blocked_name("n111gg3er"));
    // at the end, or after more than an n (or ni), a number
    assert!(!blocked_name("N1995") && !blocked_name("N1663") && !blocked_name("Kaan1998GS") && !blocked_name("Doran1994TR"));
    assert!(!blocked_name("N_1663r") && !blocked_name("Nas1663r"));
}

// the lobby's chat: a word at a time, two words together for the anywhere list, one-letter words in a row
#[test]
fn chat_lines() {
    let slur = |l: &str| chat_slur(l).map(str::to_string);
    for (line, span) in [
        ("you nigger", "nigger"),
        ("Kestrel> nate higgers", "higgers"),
        ("nig ger lol", "nig"),
        ("nibb a", "nibb a"),
        ("SIEG HEIL", "SIEG HEIL"),
        ("n i g g e r", "n i g g e r"),
        ("so F A G", "F A G"),
        ("u r a f a g", "f a g"),
        ("f.a.g.s", "f.a.g.s"),
        ("ur a fag!!", "fag"),
        ("you n!gger", "n!gger"),
        ("N1GG4 pls", "N1GG4"),
        ("go 1488", "1488"),
        ("porch monkey", "porch monkey"),
        ("van Dyke_fag", "Dyke_fag"),
        ("van dyke-nigger", "dyke-nigger"),
        ("lol niger", "niger"),
        ("ya pidor", "pidor"),
        ("big nigabro", "nigabro"),
        ("austrian artist", "austrian artist"),
        ("lets gasthejews", "gasthejews"),
        ("gas thejews", "gas thejews"),
        ("gas the jews", "gas the jews"),
        ("KILL ALL THE J3WS now", "KILL ALL THE J3WS"),
        ("we kill all the jews", "kill all the jews"),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(slur(line).as_deref(), Some(span), "{line}");
    }
    // swearing stays, and so do the words across words that the letters all together would read
    for line in [
        "merci kurwa",
        "SEN? MERC? AMK",
        "KUZO> DOM TORETTO H?S FATHER",
        "rapid race",
        "stupid race",
        "go ok",
        "go,ok",
        "fa g",
        "Van Dyke",
        "a b c d e",
        "the spice must flow",
        "hi! I'm Nigel from Nigeria",
        "topi drift",
        "Zuniga and Nigar",
        "lap 1:48.8",
        "las vegas the jewel",
        "kill all the bots then the jews",
        "",
        "   ",
    ] {
        assert_eq!(slur(line), None, "{line}");
    }
    // the span is the line's own text
    let line = "a\u{a0}porch  monkey b";
    assert_eq!(chat_slur(line), Some("porch  monkey"));
}

#[test]
fn letters_past_255_are_not_read() {
    let x = |n: usize| "x".repeat(n);
    assert!(blocked_name(&(x(250) + "nigga")));
    assert!(!blocked_name(&(x(252) + "nigga")));
    // a part of its own is read from its start, whatever came before
    assert!(blocked_name(&(x(300) + "_fag")) && blocked_name(&(x(300) + " " + &x(300) + "_fag")));
    assert!(!blocked_name(&(x(300) + "fag")));
}

// the operator's names taken away: a name that reads the same is taken away with it, another is not
#[test]
fn names_taken_away_by_their_letters() {
    assert_eq!(letters("B4d_N4me"), "badname");
    assert_eq!(letters("Bad Name 1995"), "badname");
    assert_eq!(letters("Dani99GS"), "danigs");
    assert_eq!(letters("1234"), "");
    let d = Deny::default();
    assert!(!d.has("BadName"));
    let g = d.generation();
    d.set(["Bad_Name".to_string(), "4444".to_string()]);
    assert!(d.generation() > g);
    for same in ["BadName", "b4d n4me", "BADNAME", "Bad.Name.2000", "8adName"] {
        assert!(d.has(same), "{same}");
    }
    for other in ["BadNames", "Bad", "GoodName", "", "1234"] {
        assert!(!d.has(other), "{other}");
    }
    d.set([]);
    assert!(!d.has("BadName"));
}

{"id": "AT001599", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/server-rs/crates/online/src/aries.rs", "originalBytes": 19551, "originalSha256": "152ef3f75b544e7e022fd55e3b9e796a5c58be21f077b5fe87655489105a0ab1", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 19551, "utf8TotalBytes": 19551}

//! The lobby protocol's framing (EA DirtySock "ProtoAries", as SPEED2.EXE's lobby client and EA's server.dll speak
//! it):
//!
//! - `[0..3]` kind: four ASCII characters ("auth", "+rom", "@dir", ...)
//! - `[4..7]` code: four bytes; 0 in a request and in a reply that succeeded, an error tag ("imst", "pass", ...)
//!   or a subkind ("new7") otherwise; "filt" in a game list search made with the Filter the player set (the runtime's
//!   own, runtime/olfilter.c)
//! - `[8..11]` u32 big-endian: the whole message's length, these 12 bytes included
//! - `[12..]` the body: KEY=VALUE fields, NUL-terminated
//!
//! The body is DirtySock's "TagField" text.  The client finds a field by its key (case-insensitive) after any byte
//! <= 0x20 (so tabs, newlines and spaces all separate fields) and writes a value (0x741A50) with every byte below
//! 0x20, 0x7F and = " : % ^ as %xx (lowercase hex), in double quotes when the value has a space.  This module
//! writes exactly that and reads both that and plain values.
//!
//! Secrets: the login messages carry PASS (the account password, XOR-masked or encrypted, both reversible: as good
//! as plain text), REGKEY (the CD key) and PSES (a checksum of the player's game files).  [`parse_fields`] takes a
//! test of keys to skip, and the lobby skips [`SECRET_KEYS`] for every message: their values are never decoded, so
//! nothing after the parser can keep or log one.  The one exception is PASS in gcre and gjoi, which is a game's own
//! password there (the lobby keeps only a digest of it).  [`redact_body`] is for the dev-only frame trace (trace.rs).

use std::borrow::Cow;

use indexmap::IndexMap;
use nfsu2_util::{js, json};

use crate::jsx;

/// keys whose values the server never reads: the account password, the CD key, the file checksum (but PASS in gcre
/// and gjoi: a game's password)
pub const SECRET_KEYS: [&str; 3] = ["PASS", "REGKEY", "PSES"];

pub const HDR: usize = 12;
/// the client's receive buffer is 0x8000 bytes; nothing it sends or needs is near this
pub const MAX_FRAME: usize = 8192;

/// a field's value: a string, a number (written as JavaScript writes one: `js::number_to_string`), or nothing (the
/// field is left out)
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum V {
    S(String),
    N(f64),
    Null,
}

impl From<&str> for V {
    fn from(s: &str) -> V {
        V::S(s.to_string())
    }
}
impl From<String> for V {
    fn from(s: String) -> V {
        V::S(s)
    }
}
impl From<&String> for V {
    fn from(s: &String) -> V {
        V::S(s.clone())
    }
}
impl From<Option<String>> for V {
    fn from(s: Option<String>) -> V {
        s.map_or(V::Null, V::S)
    }
}
impl From<Option<&str>> for V {
    fn from(s: Option<&str>) -> V {
        s.map_or(V::Null, |s| V::S(s.to_string()))
    }
}
impl From<&Option<String>> for V {
    fn from(s: &Option<String>) -> V {
        s.as_ref().map_or(V::Null, |s| V::S(s.clone()))
    }
}
macro_rules! v_num {
    ($($t:ty),*) => { $(impl From<$t> for V { fn from(x: $t) -> V { V::N(x as f64) } })* };
}
v_num!(f64, i64, u64, i32, u32, u16, usize);

/// a body's fields: (key, value), in order
pub type Fields = Vec<(Cow<'static, str>, V)>;

/// `fields![(k, v), ...]`: a [`Fields`] (a Vec: most are sent as they are, some grow)
macro_rules! fields {
    ($(($k:expr, $v:expr)),* $(,)?) => {{
        #[allow(clippy::useless_vec)]
        let f: $crate::aries::Fields = vec![$((::std::borrow::Cow::from($k), $crate::aries::V::from($v))),*];
        f
    }};
}

const HEXD: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";

fn special(c: u8) -> bool {
    matches!(c, 0x3d | 0x22 | 0x3a | 0x25 | 0x5e | 0x7f)
}

/// a value as the client writes one (latin1 bytes)
pub fn encode_value(v: &V, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
    let mut b = Vec::new();
    match v {
        V::S(s) => jsx::latin1_encode(s, &mut b),
        V::N(x) => b.extend_from_slice(js::number_to_string(*x).as_bytes()),
        V::Null => b.extend_from_slice(b"null"),
    }
    let quote = b.contains(&0x20);
    if quote {
        out.push(b'"');
    }
    for c in b {
        if c < 0x20 || special(c) {
            out.extend_from_slice(&[b'%', HEXD[(c >> 4) as usize], HEXD[(c & 15) as usize]]);
        } else {
            out.push(c);
        }
    }
    if quote {
        out.push(b'"');
    }
}

/// `/^[A-Za-z0-9_+@$~]{1,32}$/`
fn good_key(k: &str) -> bool {
    (1..=32).contains(&k.len()) && k.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"_+@$~".contains(&b))
}

/// a body: "K=V<sep>K=V<sep>" (no NUL), as latin1 bytes; a field name that is not one (`good_key`) is an error
pub fn encode_fields(fields: &[(Cow<'static, str>, V)], sep: u8) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(16 * fields.len());
    encode_fields_into(fields, sep, &mut out)?;
    Ok(out)
}

fn encode_fields_into(fields: &[(Cow<'static, str>, V)], sep: u8, out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), String> {
    for (k, v) in fields {
        if *v == V::Null {
            continue;
        }
        if !good_key(k) {
            let mut q = String::new();
            json::write_str(&mut q, k);
            return Err(format!("bad field name {q}"));
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(k.as_bytes());
        out.push(b'=');
        encode_value(v, out);
        out.push(sep);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// a 4-character kind or code ("" for 0), padded with NULs
fn tag4(t: &str, what: &str, out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut b = Vec::with_capacity(4);
    jsx::latin1_encode(t, &mut b);
    if b.len() > 4 {
        let mut q = String::new();
        json::write_str(&mut q, t);
        return Err(format!("{what} {q} is longer than 4 characters"));
    }
    b.resize(4, 0);
    out.extend_from_slice(&b);
    Ok(())
}

/// one message (code "" = 0, success), fields separated by newlines
pub fn encode_frame(kind: &str, code: &str, fields: &[(Cow<'static, str>, V)]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    encode_frame_sep(kind, code, fields, b'\n')
}

/// one message, fields separated by `sep` (the fields are checked first, then the kind, then the code: the error is
/// the first one's)
pub fn encode_frame_sep(kind: &str, code: &str, fields: &[(Cow<'static, str>, V)], sep: u8) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let mut f = Vec::with_capacity(HDR + 24 * fields.len() + 1);
    f.extend_from_slice(&[0; HDR]);
    encode_fields_into(fields, sep, &mut f)?;
    f.push(0);
    let mut tags = Vec::with_capacity(8);
    tag4(kind, "kind", &mut tags)?;
    tag4(code, "code", &mut tags)?;
    f[..8].copy_from_slice(&tags);
    let n = f.len() as u32;
    f[8..12].copy_from_slice(&n.to_be_bytes());
    Ok(f)
}

/// one message of a ready body (latin1 text, without its NUL)
#[cfg(test)]
pub fn encode_frame_text(kind: &str, code: &str, text: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let mut f = Vec::with_capacity(HDR + text.len() + 1);
    tag4(kind, "kind", &mut f)?;
    tag4(code, "code", &mut f)?;
    f.extend_from_slice(&[0; 4]);
    jsx::latin1_encode(text, &mut f);
    f.push(0);
    let n = f.len() as u32;
    f[8..12].copy_from_slice(&n.to_be_bytes());
    Ok(f)
}

/// a 4-byte tag as text: printable characters kept, NULs dropped, anything else as \xNN
pub fn tag_text(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut s = String::with_capacity(4);
    for &c in b {
        if c == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        if (0x20..0x7f).contains(&c) {
            s.push(c as char);
        } else {
            s.push_str("\\x");
            s.push(HEXD[(c >> 4) as usize] as char);
            s.push(HEXD[(c & 15) as usize] as char);
        }
    }
    s
}

/// one message of a stream: kind and code as text, the body (the bytes after the header, NUL included)
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Msg {
    pub kind: String,
    pub code: String,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
}

/// The messages in a byte stream.  `push` returns the complete messages so far; a length
/// below 12 or above `max` makes the stream bad (`error` set, nothing more is returned: the caller drops the
/// connection).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct FrameReader {
    max: usize,
    buf: Vec<u8>,
    pub error: Option<String>,
}

impl Default for FrameReader {
    fn default() -> Self {
        FrameReader::new(MAX_FRAME)
    }
}

impl FrameReader {
    pub fn new(max: usize) -> Self {
        FrameReader { max, buf: Vec::new(), error: None }
    }
    pub fn push(&mut self, chunk: &[u8]) -> Vec<Msg> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        if self.error.is_some() {
            return out;
        }
        self.buf.extend_from_slice(chunk);
        let mut pos = 0;
        while self.buf.len() - pos >= HDR {
            let b = &self.buf[pos..];
            let n = u32::from_be_bytes([b[8], b[9], b[10], b[11]]) as usize;
            if n < HDR || n > self.max {
                self.error = Some(format!("a message of {n} bytes (at most {})", self.max));
                self.buf = Vec::new();
                return out;
            }
            if b.len() < n {
                break;
            }
            out.push(Msg { kind: tag_text(&b[0..4]), code: tag_text(&b[4..8]), body: b[HDR..n].to_vec() });
            pos += n;
        }
        if pos == self.buf.len() {
            self.buf.clear();
        } else if pos > 0 {
            self.buf.drain(..pos);
        }
        out
    }
    /// bytes waiting for the rest of a message
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn pending(&self) -> usize {
        self.buf.len()
    }
}

/// each %xx (two hex digits, either case) as the character xx; any other % stays
fn unescape(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut s = String::with_capacity(b.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < b.len() {
        if b[i] == b'%'
            && i + 2 < b.len()
            && let (Some(h), Some(l)) = ((b[i + 1] as char).to_digit(16), (b[i + 2] as char).to_digit(16))
        {
            s.push(char::from((h * 16 + l) as u8));
            i += 3;
            continue;
        }
        s.push(b[i] as char);
        i += 1;
    }
    s
}

/// The fields of a body, in order, keys upper-cased; a key `skip` says yes to is
/// passed over without its value being decoded (it appears with the value None, so a caller can tell that one
/// was sent).  Text after the first NUL is ignored.
pub fn parse_fields(b: &[u8], skip: impl Fn(&str) -> bool) -> Vec<(String, Option<String>)> {
    let end = memchr_nul(b);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < end {
        while i < end && b[i] <= 0x20 {
            i += 1;
        }
        if i >= end {
            break;
        }
        let mut k = i;
        while k < end && b[k] > 0x20 && b[k] != 0x3d {
            k += 1;
        }
        // a word without "=": not a field
        if k >= end || b[k] != 0x3d {
            i = k;
            continue;
        }
        let key = jsx::latin1_decode(&b[i..k]).to_uppercase();
        let j = k + 1;
        let raw;
        if j < end && b[j] == 0x22 {
            // "quoted value"
            let mut q = j + 1;
            while q < end && b[q] != 0x22 {
                q += 1;
            }
            raw = if skip(&key) { None } else { Some(&b[j + 1..q]) };
            i = q + 1;
        } else {
            let mut q = j;
            while q < end && b[q] > 0x20 {
                q += 1;
            }
            raw = if skip(&key) { None } else { Some(&b[j..q]) };
            i = q;
        }
        out.push((key, raw.map(unescape)));
    }
    out
}

fn memchr_nul(b: &[u8]) -> usize {
    b.iter().position(|&c| c == 0).unwrap_or(b.len())
}

/// the lobby's skip: SECRET_KEYS
pub fn is_secret(k: &str) -> bool {
    SECRET_KEYS.contains(&k)
}

/// [`parse_fields`] as a map (the first of a repeated key wins, as the client's own search finds the first), in the
/// order the keys came
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct FieldMap(pub IndexMap<String, Option<String>>);

impl FieldMap {
    /// a body's fields ([`SECRET_KEYS`] skipped)
    pub fn parse(body: &[u8]) -> FieldMap {
        Self::parse_with(body, is_secret)
    }
    pub fn parse_with(body: &[u8], skip: impl Fn(&str) -> bool) -> FieldMap {
        let mut m = IndexMap::new();
        for (k, v) in parse_fields(body, skip) {
            m.entry(k).or_insert(v);
        }
        FieldMap(m)
    }
    /// a field's value: None when the field is missing or was skipped
    pub fn get(&self, k: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.0.get(k).and_then(|v| v.as_deref())
    }
    /// the field was sent (a skipped one too)
    pub fn has(&self, k: &str) -> bool {
        self.0.contains_key(k)
    }
    /// a field's value, "" when the field is missing or was skipped
    pub fn str(&self, k: &str) -> &str {
        self.get(k).unwrap_or("")
    }
    /// a field's number (as `jsx::to_number` reads its text), `def` when the field is missing
    pub fn num(&self, k: &str, def: f64) -> f64 {
        match self.0.get(k) {
            Some(Some(v)) => jsx::to_number(v),
            // a skipped field's number is 0 (the lobby never asks for one)
            Some(None) => 0.0,
            None => def,
        }
    }
}

/// keys a trace must not show (the secrets, a game's own password, and the key of a persona's Messenger login):
/// `/^(PASS\w*|REGKEY|PSES|LKEY)$/i` on the upper-cased key
fn redacted(k: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(k, "REGKEY" | "PSES" | "LKEY")
        || k.strip_prefix("PASS").is_some_and(|r| r.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'_'))
}

/// a body as one printable line for the dev-only trace, every secret replaced
pub fn redact_body(body: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut s = String::new();
    for (i, (k, v)) in parse_fields(body, redacted).into_iter().enumerate() {
        if i > 0 {
            s.push(' ');
        }
        s.push_str(&k);
        s.push('=');
        match v {
            None => s.push_str("<redacted>"),
            Some(v) => json::write_str(&mut s, &v),
        }
    }
    s
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn latin1(b: &[u8]) -> String {
        jsx::latin1_decode(b)
    }

    // header: kind, code, big-endian length with the NUL-terminated body
    #[test]
    fn header() {
        let f = encode_frame("auth", "", &fields![("NAME", "Bob"), ("ADDR", "10.77.0.3")]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&f[0..4], b"auth");
        assert_eq!(&f[4..8], &[0, 0, 0, 0]);
        assert_eq!(u32::from_be_bytes([f[8], f[9], f[10], f[11]]) as usize, f.len());
        assert_eq!(latin1(&f[HDR..]), "NAME=Bob\nADDR=10.77.0.3\n\0");
        let e = encode_frame("auth", "pass", &[]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(&e[4..8], b"pass");
        assert_eq!(e.len(), HDR + 1);
        assert_eq!(&encode_frame_text("news", "new7", "X=1").unwrap()[4..8], b"new7");
        assert!(encode_frame("toolong", "", &[]).is_err());
        assert!(encode_fields(&fields![("BAD KEY", 1)], b'\n').is_err());
    }

    // values as the game writes them
    #[test]
    fn values() {
        let ev = |v: V| {
            let mut o = Vec::new();
            encode_value(&v, &mut o);
            latin1(&o)
        };
        assert_eq!(ev("plain".into()), "plain");
        assert_eq!(ev("two words".into()), "\"two words\"");
        assert_eq!(ev("a=b".into()), "a%3db");
        assert_eq!(ev("q\"u:o%t^e".into()), "q%22u%3ao%25t%5ee");
        assert_eq!(ev("tab\there\nnl".into()), "tab%09here%0anl");
        assert_eq!(ev("\x7f".into()), "%7f");
        assert_eq!(ev(1234.into()), "1234");
        // latin1 bytes >= 0x80 stay as they are
        assert_eq!(ev("\u{c4}".into()), "\u{c4}");
    }

    // round trip through the reader, both separators, quotes, escapes
    #[test]
    fn round_trip() {
        let fields = fields![("NAME", "two words"), ("TEXT", "hi = \"you\": 100% ^^"), ("N", "7"), ("EMPTY", "")];
        let want: Vec<(String, Option<String>)> = fields
            .iter()
            .map(|(k, v)| {
                (
                    k.to_string(),
                    Some(match v {
                        V::S(s) => s.clone(),
                        _ => unreachable!(),
                    }),
                )
            })
            .collect();
        for sep in *b"\n\t" {
            let f = encode_frame_sep("mesg", "", &fields, sep).unwrap();
            let m = FrameReader::default().push(&f);
            assert_eq!(m[0].kind, "mesg");
            assert_eq!(m[0].code, "");
            assert_eq!(parse_fields(&m[0].body, is_secret), want);
        }
        // what the client itself sends: spaces between fields, a word without "=" skipped, text after the NUL ignored
        let body = b"NAME=x  junk PERS=\"a b\"\tLKEY=k\0NAME=after";
        let got = parse_fields(body, is_secret);
        let s = |a: &str, b: &str| (a.to_string(), Some(b.to_string()));
        assert_eq!(got, vec![s("NAME", "x"), s("PERS", "a b"), s("LKEY", "k")]);
        // keys are found case-insensitively, the first one wins (as the client's own search)
        let m = FieldMap::parse(b"name=a\nNAME=b\n\0");
        assert_eq!(m.get("NAME"), Some("a"));
    }

    // stream: split and packed messages, the size limit
    #[test]
    fn stream() {
        let a = encode_frame("addr", "", &fields![("ADDR", "10.77.0.5"), ("PORT", "50000")]).unwrap();
        let b = encode_frame("skey", "", &fields![("SKEY", "$37940faf2a8d1381a3b7d0d2f570e6a7")]).unwrap();
        let all = [a.clone(), b].concat();
        let mut cut = 1;
        while cut < all.len() {
            let mut r = FrameReader::default();
            let mut got = r.push(&all[..cut]);
            got.extend(r.push(&all[cut..]));
            assert_eq!(got.iter().map(|m| m.kind.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), ["addr", "skey"], "cut at {cut}");
            assert_eq!(r.pending(), 0);
            cut += 3;
        }
        let mut r = FrameReader::new(64);
        let big = encode_frame("mesg", "", &fields![("TEXT", "x".repeat(100))]).unwrap();
        assert!(r.push(&big).is_empty());
        assert!(r.error.as_deref().unwrap().contains("at most 64"));
        assert!(r.push(&a).is_empty(), "nothing after a bad length");
        let mut tiny = vec![0u8; 12];
        tiny[..4].copy_from_slice(b"xxxx");
        tiny[8..12].copy_from_slice(&4u32.to_be_bytes());
        let mut r2 = FrameReader::default();
        r2.push(&tiny);
        assert!(r2.error.is_some());
    }

    // secrets: never decoded, never in the trace
    #[test]
    fn secrets() {
        let pw = "CANARY-PASSWORD-123";
        let mut body = encode_fields(
            &fields![("NAME", "Bob"), ("PASS", pw), ("TOS", "1"), ("REGKEY", "ABCD-EFGH"), ("PSES", "0123abcd"), ("PASSWORD", "gamepw")],
            b'\n',
        )
        .unwrap();
        body.push(0);
        let f = parse_fields(&body, is_secret);
        assert_eq!(f.iter().map(|(k, _)| k.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), ["NAME", "PASS", "TOS", "REGKEY", "PSES", "PASSWORD"]);
        for (k, v) in &f {
            if SECRET_KEYS.contains(&k.as_str()) {
                assert_eq!(*v, None, "{k}");
            }
        }
        assert!(FieldMap::parse(&body).has("PASS") && FieldMap::parse(&body).get("PASS").is_none());
        let quoted = format!("NAME=a PASS=\"{pw} x\" REGKEY={pw}\0");
        assert!(parse_fields(quoted.as_bytes(), is_secret).iter().all(|(k, v)| k == "NAME" || v.is_none()));
        let line = redact_body(&body);
        assert!(!line.contains(pw) && !line.contains("ABCD") && !line.contains("0123abcd") && !line.contains("gamepw"), "{line}");
        assert!(line.contains("PASS=<redacted>") && line.contains("NAME=\"Bob\""));
    }
}
